mr president juncker, mr prime minister renzi, the italian presidency will be remembered for a number of initiatives, notably with regard to the bank resolution fund or money laundering, but it will be remembered above all for having had the courage and the intelligence to put on the political agenda some of the issues essential for the survival of the euro and the european project. the need to reconcile public accounting discipline with the survival of the economy and employment, or the need not to kill strategic investment simply because public spending must be contained, may seem trivial, but they are not. the italian presidency has taken these issues seriously as subjects for discussion on the fundamental policies of europe. the european commission is new, the parliament has changed, but europe remains mired in stagnation with deflationary risks, with frightening unemployment and with the loss of citizens' confidence in the european project. it is true that the italian presidency has not yet brought the shock of energy and vitality that europe urgently needs, but perhaps that would be impossible. but after years of dogmatism, of blind and impoverishing austerity without hope, the new juncker commission and the italian presidency have begun to open up the issues that matter and to point in the right direction. nothing is done, but the door has been opened to the work we have to do, certainly at national level, but certainly also at collective level, now that the limits and gaps in the european architecture and, above all, the single currency are evident. the reflection must continue. i hope that the latvian presidency will not lose sight of the moment, but i hope that italy, once in the council, will not lose sight of the way. europe needs italy, and the citizens represented here in this house need to rediscover hope and, above all, the soul of europe. thanks to the italian presidency, a ray of hope is now shining before us.
the italian presidency of the european union has created high expectations. the inspiring speech by mateo renzi in the european parliament and the priorities set - europe for jobs and economic growth, a europe closer to the citizens: an area for democracy, rights and freedoms and a new impetus for the european union's external policy - generated a hope that was only partially met. if, in the field of external relations, the european union's efforts to play a greater role in the many economic and military conflicts that are raging in the world were notable, in the field of growth and employment the italian presidency was unable to turn words into deeds, certainly not for lack of effort, but because in europe a punitive hegemony of some countries over others continued to prevail, instead of having evolved towards a level of cooperation and solidarity that would benefit everyone.
in writing. the agreement reached on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory provides a clearer framework and more flexibility as to the reasons for such a refusal. at the same time, it must be said that this agreement leaves many of us dissatisfied, both those who are strongly opposed to the cultivation of gmos in the european union because of the environmental risks that exist, which science cannot exclude, and those who believe that the scientific evidence available on the health effects of gmos is irrefutable and that the obstacles to this technology are helping to kill science and the small european companies in the sector. i would like to conclude by saying that i believe this agreement represents a small but important step, as it preserves the robust scientific evaluation process by the european food safety authority and reserves the possibility for member states to act in defence of the will of their citizens, according to a number of pre-established criteria.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i would ask you to calm the mood of that bench, please. first of all, i would like to point out that our group has proposed a debate on fisheries at this part-session, a debate which would include the debate on this report on the fisheries agreement between the european union and são tomé and príncipe. we regret that all the other groups have refused to take part in this debate. it is incomprehensible, especially since you cannot claim that we have a full agenda, that yesterday was without any debate. as regards this agreement, it is important to remember that this parliament can only approve or reject the proposals negotiated by the european commission and cannot amend them. if we were able to make these amendments, the proposal which is being discussed and voted on here would certainly be very different from the one we have, because a profound change in the philosophy, objectives and results of these agreements is needed. it is important to approve this agreement, it is important for são tomé and príncipe and for the member states of the european union, but it does not erase, it cannot erase the overall negative balance of what has been left behind, nor does it erase the need for profound changes. among other aspects, improvements in the quantity and reliability of information on catches and, in general, on the state of conservation of fisheries resources, more and better support for the training of observers and the development of monitoring capacity by são tomé and príncipe, more and better sectoral cooperation, changing the course of the last three decades of life that this agreement, in various forms, already has, in respect for the sovereignty and the legitimate choices and priorities of são tomé and príncipe. these are requirements for a fair agreement that truly promotes sustainable development and fisheries, and the european commission should take them into account in the coming years.
in writing. the conclusion of this protocol between the european union and são tomé and príncipe is very important not only for the development of the african nation but also from the european point of view as it will allow our vessels to expand their fishing area while allowing better control in terms of environment and sustainability. it is also an important way of strengthening the european union's relations with a country which has had a strong link with portugal for a long time and with which we have every interest in cooperating. my vote in favour of this report is a wish that it be put into practice as soon as possible and that parliament be kept informed of developments in this process.

in writing. the previous protocol, which was in force from 13 may 2011 to 12 may 2014, allowed 40 eu tuna vessels to operate: 28 purse seiners and 12 surface longliners. the financial contribution was eur 682 500 per year, of which about 35% was earmarked for supporting the santomense sectoral policy. the new protocol to the eu-são tomé and príncipe fisheries agreement will allow 34 vessels from spain, france and portugal to fish in são tomé and príncipe's waters. the protocol also aims to promote a sustainable fisheries policy and to support the sectoral policy of santo domingo. the overall financial contribution is eur 2 805 000 over four years. i also think it is important that the european commission should take the necessary steps, including the possible revision and increase of the sectoral support component of the agreement, to ensure an effective reversal of the path followed over the last twenty years.
in writing. the eu-são tomé and príncipe fisheries agreement is part of the network of tuna fisheries agreements in west africa. the first fisheries agreement between the eec and são tomé and príncipe was concluded in 1984. since then, eight protocols have been implemented, two of which are under the fisheries partnership agreement. however, the results achieved so far in the field of sectoral cooperation are very limited. this is a reality that needs to change. this agreement, in conjunction with other development support instruments such as the european development fund, should promote the effective sustainable development of the santoméan fisheries sector and related industries and activities, increasing the added value that is left in the country as a result of the exploitation of its natural resources. the european commission should take the necessary steps including the possible revision and increase of the sectoral support component of the agreement to ensure an effective reversal of the path followed over the last twenty years.

in writing. i would vote in favour of this recommendation on the conclusion, on behalf of the eu, of the new four-year protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe, as it will enable eu vessels to fish in são tomé and príncipe's waters through an annual financial contribution which will allow a significant amount to be channelled to support são tomé and príncipe's sectoral policy. however, i would like to stress, as the rapporteur has done, that it is imperative to adopt a more integrated approach to sectoral cooperation with this country, which will allow, in particular, greater information to the santoméan authorities on the catch index, conservation of fishery resources, increased training of observers and the capacity to monitor the santoméan eez, as well as support for the development of fishing infrastructure that will allow the export of fishery products to the european union, among others. it is therefore not enough to allocate financial compensation. it is imperative that these are accompanied by credible sectoral policies that allow the development of the santo domingo fishing sector, in respect of the sovereignty and legitimate aspirations and objectives of the country in this sector.
in writing. like the mep and rapporteur joão ferreira, i, as the s&d shadow rapporteur, have assessed this agreement positively. i have to make some comments, however, which i regard as opportunities for improvement in future fisheries agreements with the european union. the agreement lacks references to target species, protected species such as sea turtles, marine mammals and seabirds, and no mention is made of mitigation or control measures for sharks. one of the biggest threats to sea turtle populations is industrial fishing. são tomé and príncipe until recently used sea turtles for both food and local crafts, but since a few years both government authorities and local communities associated with ngos have been implementing programs to protect sea turtles, including their nesting sites. the european union must be united in this effort to protect the environment and this should have been reflected in this fisheries agreement. finally, i would point out that it is important that the activity includes the inclusion of independent observers, whose costs are borne financially by the shipowners. this should be the case in all fisheries agreements.

the first fisheries agreement between the eec and são tomé and príncipe was concluded in 1984. since then, eight protocols have been implemented, two of them under the fisheries partnership agreement. however, the results achieved so far in the field of sectoral cooperation are very limited. this is a reality that must be changed urgently. this agreement, in conjunction with other development support instruments such as the european development fund, should promote the effective sustainable development of the santoméan fisheries sector and related industries and activities, increasing the added value that is left in the country as a result of the exploitation of its natural resources. the european commission should take the necessary steps including the possible revision and increase of the sectoral support component of the agreement to ensure an effective reversal of the path followed over the last twenty years.
relations between the european union and the republic of seychelles in the fisheries sector are governed by a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement. this is the union's most important agreement in the indian ocean region, making the seychelles its main partner in that area. this agreement is an access agreement concerning access for fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to the waters and biological resources of mayotte. before the change in the status of mayotte, due to the geographical proximity between mayotte and seychelles, relations between european and seychelles fishing vessels on the one hand and mayotte on the other were governed by a private agreement. this access agreement is the first of its kind and is exceptional in that it allows vessels flying the flag of a third country to fish in european territorial waters. the agreement provides for eight tuna vessels and two replenishment vessels flying the seychelles flag to be allowed access to the 24- to 100-mile zone for a renewable period of six years. the zone between 0 and 24 miles shall remain reserved for the local fishery of mayotte.
in writing. this agreement allows seychelles-flagged vessels access to mayotte waters and its resources. the territory of mayotte acquired the status of an outermost region of the eu in january 2014. as a result, the exclusive economic zone of mayotte is subject to the provisions of the eu treaties since its establishment. the conservation of the living marine resources of mayotte, within the framework of the common fisheries policy, is an exclusive competence of the eu. for this reason, the existing bilateral agreement between mayotte and seychelles previously already existing must now be re-established by the eu. our position on the eu's powers in this area is well known. we are against it. however, this report is only intended to extend under the new conditions the same previously existing agreement, which allows a limited number of seychelles vessels to fish for migratory species in mayotte waters, offering some counterparts aimed at supporting the sustainable development of the fishing sector in mayotte which is mainly made up of small-scale fleet. which is why we have nothing to object to in this deal.
relations between the european union and the republic of seychelles in the fisheries sector are governed by a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement. the sustainable tuna fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and seychelles entered into force on 10 may 2003 and has been renewed twice since that date. this is the union's most important agreement in the indian ocean region, making the seychelles its main partner in that area. this agreement is an access agreement, initialled on 3 april 2014, between the republic of seychelles and the european union on access for fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to waters and biological resources of mayotte.
in writing. the eu-seychelles sustainable tuna fisheries partnership agreement entered into force on 10 may 2003. this agreement, initialled on 3 april 2014, concerns access for seychelles fishing vessels to mayotte waters, authorising 8 seychelles tuna vessels and 2 seychelles tankers to fish in mayotte waters within a range of 24 to 100 nautical miles. it is noted that the territory of mayotte became an eu outermost region on 1 january 2014 and its exclusive economic zone is now an integral part of eu waters. it was therefore necessary to replace the previous private agreement governing relations between seychelles fishing vessels and mayotte. in terms of financial contributions, the fees paid by seychelles vessels are identical to those paid by european vessels in seychelles waters (eur 110 per tonne of fish caught in the first year) and these fees are to be used to support local fisheries in mayotte. i voted in favour of the agreement because i consider it to be beneficial for both parties and in accordance with the terms of the common fisheries policy and the rules of the indian ocean tuna commission.
in writing. on 10 may 2003, a partnership agreement between the european union and seychelles in the field of sustainable tuna fisheries entered into force. however, as from 1 january 2014, mayotte became an outermost region of the eu and this access agreement was initialled on 3 april 2014 concerning access for fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to the waters and biological resources of mayotte, which became managed by the eu, in accordance with article 3 tfeu which establishes that the union has exclusive competence to manage the fishery resources of mayotte and to negotiate and manage the bilateral agreements relating to this territory. the new agreement will allow a limited number of vessels flying the flag of seychelles and traditionally fishing in mayotte waters to continue fishing in the octs' eez under the rules of the common fisheries policy. i voted in favour of this recommendation because i agree with the rapporteur that the conditions attached to this agreement are appropriate, proportionate and transparent, and that they bring benefits to both parties.
in writing. this is an atypical fishing agreement. contrary to what is usual, instead of obtaining access to fishing grounds in third countries, the european union is now disposing of its territory so that a third country can fish there. the european union is thus allowing the republic of seychelles to fish in mayotte, a new outermost region of europe. the financial benefits of the initiative are passed on to the maiote government. i ask to speak to justify my choice to vote in favour because i think it is crucial that it should be noted that, although it is a positive agreement, it could have gone further. future fisheries agreements will have to clearly define the target species, mention the species in those waters that are covered by international, national or regional conservation status, and indicate what measures are taken to mitigate any effect on these species.
the territory of mayotte acquired the status of an outermost region of the european union on 1 january 2014. as a result, the mayotte exclusive economic zone (eez) now belongs to eu waters. since the eu has exclusive competence for the conservation of resources (article 3 tfeu), the european union is responsible for the management of fishery resources and the negotiation and management of bilateral agreements on mayotte. in view of their proximity, mayotte and seychelles were the subject of a private agreement. this has allowed a total of some 30 vessels, including eight from seychelles, to fish for migratory species in mayotte waters, thus allowing the development of their fishing industry through the direct payment of fees by shipowners to the french authorities in mayotte. this agreement between the republic of seychelles and the european union thus allows a limited number of seychelles vessels to continue fishing in the maiote eez, taking into account the rules of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. this agreement allows seychelles-flagged vessels access to mayotte waters and its resources. the territory of mayotte acquired the status of an outermost region of the eu in january 2014. as a result, the exclusive economic zone of mayotte is subject to the provisions of the eu treaties since its establishment. the conservation of its marine living resources, under the common fisheries policy, is an exclusive competence of the eu. for this reason, the existing bilateral agreement between mayotte and seychelles must now be re-established by the eu. our position on the eu's powers in this area is well known. we are against it. as this report is only intended to extend under the new conditions the same agreement as before, allowing a limited number of seychelles vessels to fish for migratory species in mayotte waters, offering some counter-measures to support the sustainable development of the fishing industry in mayotte, which is essentially a small-scale fleet, we have nothing to oppose to this agreement.

the accession of romania and bulgaria to the eu (in 2007) required the conclusion of a protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement to extend to these two countries the scope of the creation of a free trade area. the conclusion of this protocol is not, however, a neutral act, since it broadens its scope by increasing the territory and the population covered. this agreement will have a serious impact on tunisia's ability to take measures to manage its economy independently, allowing the large economic groups on both sides freedom of establishment without additional costs, and benefiting them at the expense of smes, small and mediumsized farmers, family farming and small-scale fishing. the effects of this are well known: it increases competition and thereby puts pressure on workers to reduce wages, reduce export costs, lower prices for the final consumer in order to destroy local production, and then raise them again when production and/or trade cease to be dominant, without benefiting food quality and safety, and causing even greater environmental destruction.

in writing. the euro-mediterranean partnership between the eu and the countries of the southern mediterranean started in 1995 with the barcelona process. between 1998 and 2005, the eu concluded euro-mediterranean association agreements with seven countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean, including tunisia (decision 98/238/ec on the conclusion of the euro-mediterranean agreement establishing an association between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of tunisia, of the other part). the main objectives of these agreements are to promote regular dialogue on political and security matters, economic, commercial and financial cooperation (progressive liberalisation of trade, sustainable regional development and investment promotion), and social, cultural and educational cooperation between the parties. as bulgaria and romania have acceded to the eu with effect from 1 january 2007, it was necessary to ensure the full participation of these two member states in bilateral relations with tunisia. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the conclusion of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and tunisia to take account of the accession of bulgaria and romania to the eu.

in writing. i support the ries report as the possible compromise, although i have many doubts about the solution found. i am sensitive to the complexity of the gmo problem and to the fact that there are passionate opinions on this subject which vary from one member state to another. and i agree that there should be legal certainty when member states ban or limit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) authorised at eu level on their territories, based on environmental reasons such as the maintenance of local biodiversity, socioeconomic impacts or land use criteria, among others. but i am afraid that this will not help to strengthen the cohesion of the internal market and i am afraid of the contagion factors that can occur between neighbouring states when one authorises and the other does not, despite the fact that it has been established that member states must ensure that gm crops do not contaminate conventional and organic crops and must prevent crossborder contamination.
in writing. this directive gives member states the possibility to prohibit or limit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) authorised at eu level on their territory, based on environmental reasons such as the maintenance of local biodiversity, socioeconomic impacts or land use criteria, among others. in 2014, the area cultivated with gmos in portugal was 8542,41 hectares, according to data from the ministry of agriculture. among the grounds that member states may invoke to justify a prohibition or restriction on the cultivation of gmos are environmental criteria, criteria related to land use planning, land use, socioeconomic impacts, agricultural policy objectives and the need to avoid the presence of gmos in other products. member states should ensure that gm crops do not contaminate conventional and organic crops and prevent cross-border contamination, a request expressed by the majority of european farmers.
in writing. the good intentions of the majority in this parliament have once again been overridden by the economic interests of the biotechnology multinationals. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. the proposal would require member states to ask multinational companies which produce and market gmos for authorisation to exclude them from their geographical scope. they may accept or refuse that request. this is unacceptable. it is the total submission of political power to the interests of big capital. if there are any doubts about the majority of this parliament's approach to this issue and its implications, the mere fact that the legal basis in this text is shifting from environmental protection to the internal market reveals yet another intention of this proposal, which is inseparable from the transatlantic trade and investment partnership agreement with the us: to satisfy the commercial objectives of the big us biotechnology (gmo) companies. although the initial intention of the proposal could be seen as an advance on the present situation, negotiations with the council resulted in an unacceptable text. we voted against it.
in writing. i voted against because i consider that the cultivation of gmos poses a serious danger to health, the environment and biodiversity. the decision on this matter cannot be left to the member states, because it is a decision which has repercussions beyond the sources, not only because of the risk of contamination but also because of the distribution and sale of gmo products, even in countries where cultivation is prohibited. the return of the decision to the member states in this matter is a poisoned gift, because the rights and health of european citizens are being jeopardized under a false guise of strengthening national sovereignty. it is therefore a farce, especially when we know that this is one of the issues that will be negotiated under the transatlantic partnership agreement.
in writing. i agree that member states should have the possibility to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their territory, in accordance with this proposal which has now been adopted. i also agree with the amendments proposed by the ep which add measures to prohibit or limit the cultivation of gmos in all or part of the national territory. we should also be able to rely on local or regional environmental grounds and socioeconomic impacts to make such bans. member states should also take into account, when deciding, reasons related to socio-economic impacts, such as the unfeasibility or high cost of coexistence measures and the risk of contamination of conventional or organic farming by gmos. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the amendment to the current eu legislative framework on gmos aims to give more latitude and legal certainty to member states wishing to ban the cultivation of gmos permitted at european level in all or part of their territories. such prohibitions or limitations shall be based on grounds other than those covered by the environmental and health risk assessment that is part of the eu authorisation process. among the grounds that member states may invoke to justify a prohibition or restriction on the cultivation of gmos are environmental criteria complementing those assessed by the european food safety authority (efsa) at european level, criteria related to land use planning, land use, socio-economic impacts, agricultural policy objectives and the need to avoid the presence of gmos in other products. i believe that such a proposal will give european countries greater freedom to address specific national or local issues raised by the cultivation of gmos, and will also help to facilitate the authorization process in this area. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. following the council position adopted on 23 july 2014 by the 28 union ministers of the environment to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos in their territories, the recommendation now emerges with a view to adopting a directive aimed at extending the rights of member states in this field through a strict legal framework that will only allow gmos to be placed on the market after an authorisation based on a scientific assessment of the risks to human and animal health and the environment. as can be read in the text of the recommendation, this is in practice to amend directive 2001/18/ec on the deliberate release into the environment of gmos and the authorised cultivation of gmos under regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 on food and feed containing or produced from gmos. in view of this factual circumstantiality, i agree with the amendments to the proposal which are essentially intended to give greater latitude and legal certainty to member states wishing to ban the cultivation of gmos in all or part of their territories, thus unlocking a deadlock which had persisted since the european parliament's vote at first reading on 5 july 2011.
at the end of the process of discussing this directive, once again, the interests of multinational agribusinesses are privileged. your gmo supporters are in the majority in this parliament and, as you would expect, they approve this proposal. the protection of the public interest, public health, the environment and sustainable agriculture, especially small and medium-sized farming, but also national sovereignty, have been relegated to the background. with this directive, which runs counter to all the appeals and recommendations of the envi committee, states are put in the unacceptable position of having to ask multinationals not to market genetically modified organisms on their territory, and the multinationals can refuse this request. the legal basis is no longer the environment and public health, but the internal market. the way in which the majority of this parliament views this issue and its implications is thus revealing.
in writing. i voted in favour of the directive which gives member states more flexibility to prohibit or limit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) authorised at eu level on their territories, based on environmental grounds such as the maintenance of local biodiversity, socioeconomic impacts or on criteria related to land use, among others. the amendment to the current eu legislative framework on gmos will give greater latitude and legal certainty to member states wishing to ban the cultivation of gmos permitted at european level in all or part of their territories. european countries will now have greater freedom to address specific national or local issues raised by the cultivation of gmos.
in writing. the initial good intentions of the majority in this parliament have once again given way to the economic interests of the biotechnology multinationals, to the detriment of the defence of traditional agriculture, the environment, the interests and health of the population, as we unfortunately expected. the text adopted has removed essential points, such as the principle of coexistence and the introduction of clean zones between neighbouring countries, thus undermining and weakening the precautionary principle, and the same applies to environmental concerns and protection, which are no longer the legal basis for the precautionary principle. the text presented gives more room for large biotechnology and agribusiness companies to reject and take legal action against requests for restrictions/ban on gmos in member states that so wish. no account is taken of any liability, refund and damage protection schemes, in particular with regard to liability requirements and financial guarantees, and the rights of consumers of choice and traditional farmers not to see their crops contaminated are not guaranteed. we voted against it.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) was established by international agreement in 1949. the area covered by the agreement includes the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. the main tasks of the cgpm are to promote the development, conservation and rational management of living aquatic resources, formulate and recommend conservation measures and promote cooperation projects in the field of training. this amendment will allow for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans and the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays in the gfcm agreement area, which i support.
in writing. this agreement allows seychelles-flagged vessels access to mayotte waters and its resources. the territory of mayotte has acquired the status of an outermost region of the eu since january 2014. as a result, the exclusive economic zone of mayotte is subject to the provisions of the eu treaties since its establishment. the conservation of the living marine resources of mayotte, within the framework of the common fisheries policy, is an exclusive competence of the eu. for this reason, the existing bilateral agreement between mayotte and seychelles previously already existing must now be re-established by the eu. our position on the eu's powers in this area is well known. we are against it. however, this report is only intended to extend under the new conditions the same previously existing agreement, which allows a limited number of seychelles vessels to fish for migratory species in mayotte waters, offering some counterparts aimed at supporting the sustainable development of the fishing sector in mayotte which is mainly made up of small-scale fleet. which is why we have nothing to object to in this deal.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) was established by international agreement in 1949. the area covered by the agreement includes the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. the main tasks of the cgpm are to promote the development, conservation and rational management of living aquatic resources, formulate and recommend conservation measures and promote cooperation projects in the field of training. the contracting parties to the gfcm are the european community, albania, algeria, bulgaria, cyprus, croatia, egypt, france, japan, greece, israel, italy, lebanon, libya, malta, morocco, monaco, romania, syria, slovenia, spain, tunisia and turkey. the gfcm is to be concluded in accordance with the provisions of the agreement between the european community and the republic of turkey on trade in textile products. the provisions of the gfcm should be implemented in a manner that protects, conserves and develops living aquatic resources. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), established in 1949, covering the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters, has as its main tasks to promote the development, conservation and rational management of living aquatic resources, to design and recommend conservation measures and to promote cooperation projects in the field of training. the gfcm has adopted a set of measures aimed at ensuring, for example, the sustainable exploitation of red coral; the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans; a high level of protection of sharks and rays against fishing activities, including those involving sharks and rays listed as endangered or threatened species; and the sustainable development of small pelagic stocks in the adriatic sea. these measures go beyond the protection already ensured at union level for species by the habitats directive and other eu acts and should be incorporated into union law. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal to amend regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 which aims to transpose the recommendations of the gfcm into community law.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for an amendment to regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 of the european parliament and of the council as i consider the recommendations suggested by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) for sustainable exploitation of red coral, reduction of bycatch of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans, as well as the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays belonging to the ecosystem covered by the gfcm agreement to be relevant and justified. i welcome, as does the rapporteur, the proposal to transpose these recommendations of the gfcm into community law, as these are measures which go beyond the protection already granted to these species at european union level by the habitats directive and other union acts, and as they impose specific obligations on operators and member states to register and report relevant information on this matter. however, i share the rapporteur's concern about the transposition of these recommendations by the member states, which should not be subject to derogation.
the ec's proposal for a diploma is a smart and consistent instrument to support the management of mediterranean marine biodiversity in the context of human activities. this diploma creates specific rules to protect turtles, seabirds, monk seals, cetaceans and some species of sharks. the commission is also concerned about the introduction of rules restricting the effort involved in the capture of red coral. the proposal now approved by parliament includes the possibility of using remote-controlled vehicles for commercial exploitation in the future. however, if this is to happen, the negative implications of the technology should be taken into account, both in terms of contact damage and increased stress. we cannot allow the proposed reduction of effort at shallower depths to be transposed technologically to greater depths in a strategy of fishing down the deep. as a precautionary measure, marine protected areas, which have already brought benefits to overexploited red coral populations in europe, should be extended.
in writing. this proposal aims to transpose the recommendations of the cgpm into community law. however, the commission ignores the measures already in place in the member states which are already in line with the cgpm recommendations. member states which have already transposed the recommendations of the gfcm cannot today be required to submit to the commission the requests for derogations provided for by the gfcm. however, it should be noted that the deactivation of the derogation procedure also removes the procedure for obtaining an independent judgment to see whether member states have in fact transposed the cgpm recommendations to protect red coral. the commission proposal is in some cases more stringent than the cgpm recommendations. for example, the commission completely prohibits the use of underwater vehicles for red coral exploitation after 2014 when the relevant cgpm recommendation does not prevent it from being used in case of favourable scientific advice. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) is a regional fisheries management organisation established within the framework of fao, whose objectives are to promote the development, conservation and rational management of marine resources. this legislative proposal aims to transpose into eu law a set of measures adopted by the gfcm. technical measures are being considered to enable sustainable management of red coral, mitigation of the incidental capture of seabirds, turtles and cetaceans, and the conservation of seals, sharks and rays. the mato report generally undermines the european commission's legislative proposal, which occasionally goes beyond the cgpm's recommendations on the protection of red coral and other wildlife that may be caught accidentally; in some cases, it even seems to call into question some of the recommendations of the cgpm. that is why we are voting against it.

the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. egypt is going through a difficult and unstable process and therefore things cannot be seen in black and white. we can all identify the threats that are being posed to democratic rights in egypt, namely freedom of expression or freedom of assembly, as the vice-president herself has mentioned, but we have to learn from the lessons of the past and especially from the last four years in this region and i think that lessons must be drawn from recent events and the first of the lessons is to avoid giving lessons. we must know that the future of egypt is necessarily in the hands and decisions of the egyptian people. in this transitional process, which the european union can and must obviously support, it can support as an intermediary, as an intermediary if the parties so wish, an intermediary to try to promote the establishment of social peace. i understand that holding parliamentary elections is a positive step, but we must bear in mind that this organization is primarily the responsibility of the egyptians. we certainly have common objectives and the vice-president has mentioned them, and well, our question is how best to support and not to get into a process of interference. i think we must safeguard the right of the egyptian people to decide their own destiny. but i also want to stress, madam vice-president, in closing, your deep respect for this house, for all the hours you have spent here debating with us. it is indeed an honour to be able to count on the european commission to treat us as it is treating us here today.
after four years of illusions, with countless atrocities committed against the population, we have again at the head of the most populous arab nation those who, in practice, have never stopped ruling in egypt. the egyptian armed forces are, in fact, the most powerful institution in the country and the west knows this. it is no accident that the egyptian regime has been largely supported by the united states with an average annual subsidy of 1.8 billion dollars that has lasted for decades. only israel and colombia receive more. while the government goes shopping to supply its army, the people are hungry for bread and thirsty for democracy and social rights. our appeal is that you let those people decide their future and stop supporting local oligarchies based on the geostrategic interests of the west.
the importance of egypt makes it natural that we should follow its situation with concern. some of the problems that led to the spring revolution of january 2011 still prevail in this secular nation. indeed, high youth unemployment, unemployment of women, growing poverty, high illiteracy, religious tensions and the doubts and serious concerns expressed by the international community about the general state of democracy and the rule of law are still part of the reality of the most populous arab country. however, and despite this scenario, we look with hope to the future of egypt and the egyptians. firstly, because we are shortly to hold legislative elections, which always means opening up new windows of opportunity in a context of greater political stability. secondly, because there is evidence of an economic recovery that could lead to gdp growth of 3.5% in 2015. the egyptian authorities are now expected to respect scrupulously the universal principles to which they have committed themselves, and we naturally expect the european union, through the high representative, to keep a close eye on the electoral process and to pay greater attention to the implementation of the european neighbourhood policy.
the egyptian leadership has a choice to make: either integrate into the international community as a rule of law and a responsible actor in the middle east and north africa region or maintain an oppressive state of its people, imprisoning journalists, including those from al jazeera, political and human rights activists, homosexuals, while freeing the corrupt dictator mubarak. egypt may have a constitution today that speaks about human rights, minority rights, women's rights, but that constitution is not being implemented. these basic rights are being grossly and massively violated. justice doesn't work independently. in the mediterranean, and beyond, we would well need a strong, influential, credible egypt. but you can't do that by strangling democracy. on the contrary, each mubarak makes his own morsi and they will reappear sooner or later. the european choice is more for more. the downside is, it's less for less. we will all be lost in the mediterranean and beyond if the greatness of the pharaohs, the islamic enlightenment of al-azhar, the hope reborn in tahrir square, is little left in egypt today, gagged by general al-sisi.

on behalf of the s&d group. in october 2013 this parliament adopted a resolution, of which i was rapporteur, on the impact of corruption on human rights. in it we proposed to broaden the definition of human rights defenders in the european union guidelines to make it extended to anti-corruption activists such as aleksej navalny, who have courageously consistently exposed corruption within the highest levels of the russian state apparatus and the putin oligarchy. the conviction of the navalny brothers, part of the strategy used by the russian authorities to use laws and courts to silence opponents and civil society, reaffirms the need to support those who denounce corruption both in europe and abroad. today we are calling for a strategy by the european union and its member states to promote democratic principles and the rule of law in russia. in my view, this will have to include a magnitsky act, now extended to the conviction of the navalny brothers. a law that establishes lists of officials, prosecutors and judges, who, in violation of their constitutional obligations, fabricate charges and convict activists. this law should impose specific sanctions, such as a visa ban in the european union and the freezing of any financial assets that they or their close family members hold in european union countries.

in writing. i congratulate ms emily o'reilly on the excellent work she is doing as ombudsman and pay tribute to her predecessor who has left a very positive legacy. the number of citizens who have recourse to the ombudsman is proof that its existence is known and respected. i believe, however, that we must continue to work to make this powerful instrument for the defence of european citizens more visible. i recognise that the european commission is the institution most closely scrutinized by citizens, but it cannot be overlooked that more than half of the cases that reach the ombudsman relate to this institution alone. i also agree with mrs o'reilly's reaction to the unacceptable limitation of the ombudsman's powers of inquiry at europol. i hope the ombudsman will not resign himself to the idea that the treaties can be revised or amended by means of international agreements.
in writing. 23 245 citizens sought help from the ombudsman's services in 2013, 19 418 citizens received advice through the interactive guide on the ombudsman's website, while 1407 requests consisted of requests for information, were registered as complaints 2420 requests (2442 in 2012) and 2354 actions were taken by the ombudsman in relation to complaints received in 2013. considers it important that the ombudsman provides more detailed information on the types of complaint format, so as to make it possible to make comparisons over the years between complaints received in electronic format via the ombudsman's interactive website and complaints received offline; i therefore congratulate emily o'reilly on her first annual report as ombudsman and welcome her approach to maintaining a positive cooperation and working relationship with parliament, in particular with its committee on petitions.
in writing. in 2013, the ombudsman recorded 23 245 contacts made by citizens who used his services through the ombudsman's portal. the vast majority (19 418) received online support through the interactive guide available on the ombudsman's website. the remaining contacts concerned requests for information (1 407) which the ombudsman's services replied to or complaints (2 420). in presenting his annual report to the committee on petitions, the ombudsman outlined his new strategy, towards 2019. this strategy is based on three main concepts: impact, relevance and visibility. based on these concepts, the ombudsman intends to carry out more strategic investigations into systemic problems (impact), to strengthen the ombudsman's role by contributing to key eu debates (relevance) and to increase the visibility of the institution itself by promoting its intervention with stakeholders and by drawing attention to important cases (visibility). in order to promote transparency, it is recommended that investigations of significant public interest be initiated. a close observation of the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership would therefore strengthen the ombudsman's role as the guardian of eu transparency.
this own-initiative report is an analysis of the work carried out by the european ombudsman in 2013. as the current ombudsman emily o'reilly only took office on 30 september 2014, this document focuses on the work of her predecessor nikiforos diamandouros. the european parliament considers it important that the annual reports drawn up by the ombudsman express concrete figures of citizens' requests, whether they relate to contacts only, or to requests for support and/or complaints. under articles 20, 24 and 228 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the european ombudsman is competent to receive complaints about possible maladministration in the activities of the institutions and bodies of the european union, acting on his own initiative or on the basis of complaints lodged by eu citizens. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report because i support the new strategy towards 2019, based on these three premises: impact, relevance and visibility.
in writing. the european ombudsman has presented to parliament, in accordance with rule 220 of parliament's rules of procedure, the report on his activities in 2013. i note that transparency issues once again top the list of cases handled in 2013, alongside issues of ethics, citizens' participation in the union's decision-making process, fundamental rights and the culture of service. i welcome the new strategy presented by the ombudsman, road to 2019, which is based on three main concepts: impact, relevance and visibility and the publication of a new version of the european code of good administrative behaviour and i also welcome the opening of the inquiry into the lack of transparency in the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) as well as emily o'reilly's aspiration to make the institution of the ombudsman as accessible as possible. i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the presentation of the european ombudsman's annual report for 2013 and congratulate emily o'reilly on her approach to maintaining a positive working relationship and cooperation with parliament. i also pay tribute to professor nikiforos diamandouros, who retired in 2013, for the legacy he left as european ombudsman. i believe that the noble role of the ombudsman should be to support the strengthening of structures and institutions for accountability and transparency at european level, promoting the good administration and quality of democracy that european citizens deserve, because it is to them that his work is directed. a final word of appreciation for the ombudsman's new strategy towards 2019, based on three main pillars aimed at solving systemic problems, under the triad of impact, relevance and visibility; finally, i would just like to welcome the importance of the european citizens' initiative, which will bring about greater direct involvement of citizens in the decision-making process related to the preparation of european legislation.

in writing. the ombudsman opened 350 inquiries, 341 of which were based on complaints and 9 on his own initiative. the vast majority (64,3%) concerns the european commission (a significant increase from 52,7% in 2012). the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet and to use it for their own purposes. although transparency, openness, access to information, respect for citizens' rights and high ethical values are considered essential to generate and maintain trust between citizens and residents and institutions, there is a legalistic approach that covers up the action of institutions such as the european commission (and the policy it carries out in the framework of the troika) or frontex, which daily infringes the rights of migrants and refugees by deporting them to their countries of origin, policies that are at the heart of the action of these institutions and that do not happen for accidental reasons. we still voted in favour.

libya continues to be embroiled in internal political struggles that have turned into a violent power struggle between two rival seats of government and numerous competing factions of nationalist, islamist, tribal and regional forces, resulting in increased suffering of the civilian population, deaths, mass displacement and a widespread humanitarian crisis. the latest wave of clashes has caused the internal displacement of at least 400 000 libyans, forcing another 150 000 people, including many migrant workers, to leave the country, and it is estimated that over a million libyans are already in tunisia. i condemn this escalation of violence in libya, particularly against civilians, and support the un-mediated talks. it is essential that all parties to violent acts commit to an unconditional ceasefire and refrain from further divisive actions.

in writing. on the night of 15 february 2012, an indian fishing vessel approached an italian merchant ship sailing off the coast of kerala state, india. on board were six italian marines whose mission was to protect the ship from possible pirate attacks. during the approach and in fear of an attack, warning shots were fired at the indian vessel, with two indian fishermen fatally wounded. following this incident, the indian authorities detained two marines who were identified as being responsible for opening fire on the fishing vessel. the case has caused diplomatic tensions, and it is particularly worrying that after three years, the indian authorities are still holding the italian marines without any charges being laid. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the parties to make every effort to reach a reasonable and mutually acceptable solution as a matter of urgency, ensuring full respect for the human and legal rights of those allegedly involved.

the proposal for a european fund for strategic investments is bold, innovative, will create jobs, help businesses and encourage entrepreneurship. it is an ambitious investment plan which will have positive side effects in widening and strengthening the internal market. it will remove obstacles to the further development of this market. it will foster interconnectivity and network interconnections, in particular in the energy and digital sectors. it will help to strengthen our competitiveness and, for example, to increase our energy independence. for the success of this fund we need legitimacy and transparency. projects should seek the participation and inclusion of all member states concerned and the european parliament should be fully involved in this plan. the juncker plan, as it is known, must also have an internal solidarity component, a territorial cohesion component.
this european fund for strategic investments responds to an urgent need to combat the economic anaemia in which europe finds itself. the reality of unemployment, the lack of growth prospects and the risks of deflation are there to justify this need. the means, unfortunately, do not correspond at all to the needs. the fund is scarce and very much dependent on the response of private investors. this model has failed in the past and will continue to fail, because it is based on building public-private partnerships where the public deals with the cost and the private deals with the profit. we've seen this in health care, in communications infrastructure, and even in education. failure, because the problem is not just a lack of funding, there is also a lack of investor confidence, fuelled by austerity policies that continue to promote wealth concentration and depress aggregate consumption. europe needs a public investment project with public funding, which contributes to the social and economic cohesion of the european area.
the launch of the european fund for strategic investments is a quantum leap in european crisis management policy. it means acknowledging the failure of the impoverishment model as a path to sustainability of public accounts. the new fund has weaknesses, but it opens up a new conceptual stage. on the one hand, there are explicit strategic options and, on the other hand, the capitalisation of the fund will not be accounted for public deficit purposes. the next step will be to extend this exception to all strategic investment. this is the way to a future of sustainable growth for europe.
in writing. this investment plan will only be positive if it is no longer a programme for granting public guarantees to private investments. the nature of the investments involved - large infrastructure projects - makes it easy to conclude that we are talking about public-private partnerships, where the profit is on the private side and the risk is on the public side. moreover, if investments are not based on the creation of safe, stable and entitled jobs, the jobs that will be created will be ephemeral, poorly paid and will not solve, in the medium and long term, any of the problems that it claims to be solving.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, copyright is protected for as long as the author lives. the seventy-year period for the protection of the patrimonial dimension of copyright in an intellectual creation after the death of the author is an aberration from a legal and economic point of view. moreover, it is an inadmissible privilege in these times without any acceptable justification. this long period of time does not protect the authors but rather the people who have no legitimate connection to the act of creation. it prolongs, after the death of the author, an illegitimate situation of exclusive monopoly which, while understandable during the life of the creator, becomes unacceptable after his death, since it prevents, or at least restricts, the enjoyment of the work by the general public. this privilege is more appropriate to the privateist conceptions of the time of napoleon's civil code than to a time like the present, in which the democratization of access to culture and the widespread enjoyment of works of art is sought. the present legal system prolongs for too long a situation of exclusive monopoly in favour of the heirs of the intellectual creator, so that only they, or those they appoint, can disseminate the work. at the very least, they can prevent its publication, that is, they can prevent its publication or public knowledge for seventy years after the author's death. let us see if this system applied, for example, to patents on medicines, where the medicine could be protected for seventy years after the death of the author. the commission's proposal is to reduce the time limit from 70 years to 20 or 30 years. the end of protectionism, but the freedom to enjoy intellectual creations and works of art.

the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a fundamental instrument in the context of judicial cooperation between contracting states in resolving cases of international child abduction. the convention aims to harmonize the different legal systems of the states which normally both declare themselves competent to hear and determine the action and declare the custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent, and to adopt the criterion of the state of residence of the child. since this matter is currently the exclusive external competence of the union, a council decision calling for the acceptance by member states of the accession of third countries to the hague convention is necessary. i support the hautala report in this respect and congratulate the gabonese state on its accession to the convention, thus taking a step forward in protecting its children against abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. this type of situation occurs very often when a couple separates. as the parents are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between those states in order to obtain custody of the children. in these cases, the main problem lies in the nationalist tendencies of the legal systems of each state. it is common for the courts of the countries concerned to declare that they have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. i voted in favour of accepting gabon's accession to the hague convention in the best interests of minors who have links with the gabonese community and who will thus be protected against abduction.
the hague convention establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states aimed at finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. this type of situation occurs very frequently when a couple separates, and the convention addresses this type of situation at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children.
in writing. child abduction occurs quite frequently when a couple with members from different states separates. without going into some of the considerations made during this debate, concerning the legal systems of each state, it is common for the courts of the respective countries to declare themselves both competent and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the national parent of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level. its objectives are to ensure the prompt return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any contracting state and to ensure that rights of custody and access existing in a contracting state are effectively respected in other contracting states. they are fair and relevant objectives. gabon has deposited its instrument of accession to the convention. the eu now has competences in the field of the convention, in accordance with the decision 1/13 of the court of justice of the eu. however, the 1980 hague convention does not recognise the participation of international organisations such as the eu. for this reason, the council had to take a successive decision to approve the application for accession by gabon, andorra, the seychelles, russia, albania, singapore, morocco and armenia. we voted in favour.
in writing. with gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, the eu takes another step towards achieving one of its priorities, which is the protection and promotion of the rights of the child. this is how children of gabonese origin residing in the eu are protected from abduction.
in writing. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all eu member states, with a total of 86 signatory states. the convention aims to protect the child at international level from the effects of wrongful removal or retention and to lay down the procedures for ensuring the child's immediate return to the state of his or her habitual residence and for ensuring the protection of the right of access. most often, the problem arises when separated parents with different nationalities try to secure custody of their children by taking advantage of the lack of cooperation between the competent authorities, in this case the courts. the courts of both states generally claim to be the only competent authority to clarify these situations. this convention, for its part, will establish that the competent authorities and the laws to be applied are those of the state where the child resides. because of the importance of this convention for the protection of children, i am voting in favour of gabon's accession to it.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction, ratified by all eu member states, establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction, which very often occur as a result of divorces and separations of parents from different states. more specifically, the convention, seeking to counteract the nationalistic tendency of the legal systems of each state, provides that such cases must be tried by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the state of residence of the child and also provides for a system ensuring the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. although this is currently a matter of exclusive external competence of the eu, the truth is that the convention does not provide for independent intervention by international organisations. to this end, and in order to ensure the protection of minors with links to the gabonese community, the acceptance by the member states of gabon's accession is necessary. the present proposal for a council decision calls for such acceptance. i voted in favour.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is an important instrument with regard to the civil aspects of international child abduction. the fact that it is a system of cooperation between the different states makes it easier to find solutions to a problem which persists to this day. the strengthening of legislative systems must be an imperative and gabon's accession to the hague convention should be welcomed.
in writing. in this report too, we are faced with a proposal to resolve conflicts of territorial jurisdiction in the matter of international child abduction, allowing member states to accept gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention. since the conditions are the same as those already mentioned for other contracting states, i consider it essential that the member states accept their accession, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. the main purpose of this convention is to ensure the prompt return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any contracting state and to ensure that rights of custody and access in a contracting state are effectively respected in other contracting states. the following countries have deposited their instruments of accession to the convention: albania, andorra, armenia, gabon, morocco, singapore, seychelles, russia. the european union now has competence in the field of the convention, in accordance with the decision 1/13 of the court of justice of the european union. however, although member states no longer have this competence, the 1980 hague convention does not recognise participation in international organisations such as the european union. the council has therefore taken a successive decision to approve the application for accession by gabon, andorra, the seychelles, russia, albania, singapore, morocco and armenia.
in writing. the objective of the convention in question is to ensure the prompt return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any contracting state and to ensure that rights of custody and access existing in a contracting state are effectively respected in other contracting states. child abduction often occurs when a couple separates and the parents are from different states. the rapporteur believes that the main problem is the nationalist tendencies in the legal systems of each member state. it is common for the courts of the respective countries to declare that they both have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. gabon has deposited its instrument of accession and we have voted in favour of it, since this agreement is contrary to the interests of minors.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a fundamental instrument in the context of judicial cooperation between contracting states in resolving cases of international child abduction. the convention aims to harmonize the different legal systems of the states which normally both declare themselves competent to adjudicate the action and declare the custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent, by adopting the criterion of the state of residence of the child. since this matter is currently the exclusive external competence of the union, a council decision calling for the acceptance by member states of the accession of third countries to the hague convention is necessary. i support the hautala report in this respect and congratulate andorra on its accession to the convention, thus taking a step forward in protecting its children against abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. this type of situation occurs very often when a couple separates. as the parents are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between those states in order to obtain custody of the children. in these cases, the main problem lies in the nationalist tendencies of the legal systems of each state. it is common for the courts of the countries concerned to declare that they have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. i voted in favour of accepting andorra's accession to the hague convention in the best interests of minors who have ties to the andorran community and who will thus be protected against abduction.

in writing. in order to ensure that this convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is applied uniformly and consistently in the union, since all member states are signatories, and considering that the union has exclusive competence in matters of international child abduction, the european commission, in the interest of the union, adopted in december 2011 eight proposals concerning the declarations of acceptance by member states of the accession of eight third states to the 1980 hague convention. following the opinion of the court of justice of the union, which upheld exclusive external competence, contrary to the council's opinion, the commission presented these accession proposals to parliament and the council. given the importance of this convention, i consider it extremely important that russia should vote in favour of its accession, which would oblige it to respect the agreement at international level.

in writing. considering that the hague convention of 25 october 1980 establishes a fundamental instrument of cooperation between contracting states with regard to international child abduction, i voted in favour of this report, with the aim of promoting concerted and rapid solutions to help solve these crimes on an increasingly global scale. as albania is a neighbour of the european union, with many citizens residing in european countries and where such conflicts may arise, it is essential that the member states accept albania's accession to the convention as a means of protecting children against abduction throughout the european union.

in writing. the objective of the convention in question is to ensure the prompt return of children unlawfully transferred to or wrongfully retained in any contracting state and to ensure that rights of custody and access existing in a contracting state are effectively respected in other contracting states. the situation of child abduction occurs very frequently when a couple separates and when the parents are from different states. the rapporteur believes that the main problem is the nationalist tendencies in the legal systems of each member state. it is common for the courts of the respective countries to declare that they both have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. albania has deposited its instrument of accession and we have voted in favour of it, since this agreement is contrary to the interests of minors.
the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a fundamental instrument in the context of judicial cooperation between contracting states in resolving cases of international child abduction. the convention aims to harmonize the different legal systems of the states which normally both declare themselves competent to adjudicate the action and declare the custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent, by adopting the criterion of the state of residence of the child. since this matter is currently the exclusive external competence of the union, a council decision calling for the acceptance by member states of the accession of third countries to the hague convention is necessary. i support the hautala report in this respect and congratulate singapore on its accession to the convention, thus taking a step forward in protecting its children against abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. this type of situation occurs very often when a couple separates. as the parents are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between those states in order to obtain custody of the children. in these cases, the main problem lies in the nationalist tendencies of the legal systems of each state. it is common for the courts of the countries concerned to declare that they have jurisdiction and for the courts to grant custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state they represent. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by providing that cases are heard by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the child's state of residence. i voted in favour of accepting singapore's accession to the hague convention in the best interests of minors who have links with the singaporean community and who will thus be protected against abduction.

in writing. as i have shown my vote in favour of the accession process to the 1980 hague convention for gabon, andorra, the seychelles, russia, albania, morocco and armenia, i consider it important that singapore is one of the contracting countries, so that this same convention has an increasing number of countries, which will give it more strength on the international scene.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction, ratified by all eu member states, establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to find a solution to cases of international child abduction, which very often occur as a result of divorces and separations of parents from different states. more specifically, the convention, seeking to counteract the nationalistic tendency of the legal systems of each state, provides that such cases must be tried by the competent courts and in accordance with the applicable law of the state of residence of the child and also provides for a system ensuring the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. although this is currently a matter of exclusive external competence of the eu, the truth is that the convention does not provide for independent intervention by international organisations. to this end, and in order to ensure the protection of minors with links to the singaporean community, acceptance by the member states of singapore's accession is necessary. the present proposal for a council decision calls for such acceptance. i voted in favour.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is an important instrument with regard to the civil aspects of international child abduction. the fact that it is a system of cooperation between the different states makes it easier to find solutions to a problem which persists to this day. the strengthening of legislative systems must be an imperative and singapore's accession to the hague convention should be welcomed.
