in writing. all member states have to indicate the names of the candidates elected to the european parliament and to examine complaints about the validity of the election of certain members. at this stage there are still delays or the failure to communicate the names of the elected candidates, as well as unresolved cases. for the smooth functioning of the european institutions, in particular parliament, and for the member states to communicate swiftly to the european parliament not only the names of all the elected candidates but also the list of any substitutes and to conclude without delay the examination of the disputes submitted to them and to inform parliament of the results.
in writing. the committee on legal affairs has competence to verify the credentials of members. this report, which includes the list of elected members, reports on the results of the direct elections to the european parliament which took place from 22 to 25 may 2014, on the basis of official communications from all member states on the final results of those elections. the rapporteur highlights several important aspects, such as the fact that some nationals of certain member states who have resided in another country for a certain period of time may have been deprived of the right to vote in their home member state, which in some cases may also imply the deprivation of the right to stand as a candidate. the rapporteur rightly believes that depriving citizens who have exercised their right to free movement within the eu of the right to vote and to stand as a candidate in the member state of residence amounts to a punishment and violates the principle of direct universal suffrage. it calls on the commission to ensure that no member state provides for such a possibility. it also calls on the member states to simplify the registration formalities for the participation of nationals of other member states in european elections, both as voters and as candidates, in particular by removing unnecessary administrative barriers. we voted in favour.
in writing. this formal act validates the names of all the meps elected in the 28 member states in the elections of 22-25 may 2014, thus concluding this process. i wish all members the very best of luck in carrying out their mandates.
in writing. the european act concerning the election of the representatives of the european parliament by direct universal suffrage was published on 20 september 1976. in 1976, the posts which are incompatible with the office of member of the european parliament were defined and the professional activities they hold, as well as any other paid functions or activities, were identified. i am in favour of this report which criticises the fact that some individuals from certain member states who have resided in another country for a certain period of time have been deprived of the right to vote and stand as a candidate in their home member state, as has happened in the united kingdom. i also believe that all member states should send the list of members elected to the european parliament as quickly as possible, together with the names of all the substitutes, should it become necessary to replace the elected members.
in writing. this decision concerns the verification of the credentials of the members of the european parliament elected from 22 to 25 may 2014. under article 12 of the act of 20 september 1976 and article 3 (3) and (4) of the rules of procedure, the european parliament is to verify the credentials of its members by recording the results officially proclaimed by the member states and by deciding on any complaints made on the basis of the act, with the exception of those based on national electoral laws. however, given that all members have submitted declarations of incompatible duties and declarations of financial interests and that no complaints have been lodged under the 1976 act to date, the committee on legal affairs, which is responsible for this matter, proposes that, subject to any decisions by the competent authorities of the member states in which the election results have been contested, the mandates of the members listed in the annex be declared valid. i voted in favour, also joining the concerns expressed about the deprivation of the right to vote and the simplification of registration formalities for the participation of nationals of other member states in european elections.
in writing. the transparency effort should be inherent in the european parliament and the role of mep. the proposal is precisely a constant check to identify those aspects which need to be corrected or simplified as quickly as possible, such as those relating to the deprivation of the right to vote and the exercise of the right to vote of citizens in their member state of residence after they have exercised their right to free movement within the eu.
in writing. i support this report by the committee on legal affairs on the verification of the credentials of the members of the european parliament elected between 22 and 25 may, in so far as it is based on the legal framework for the election of members of the european parliament. the final step in this legislative framework, which began with the formal submission of applications and culminated in the european parliament's own verification of credentials, is thus completed.
in writing. the report calls on the member states to simplify registration formalities for the participation of nationals of other member states in european elections, both as voters and as candidates, in particular by removing unnecessary administrative barriers, and asks the commission to ensure that member states' practices are in line with eu law. in this connection, it declares valid, subject to any decisions adopted by the competent authorities of the member states in which the election results have been contested, the mandate of members of the european parliament whose election has been notified by the competent national authorities. we have nothing to object to or comment on.
in writing. pursuant to point 10 of section xvi of annex vi to the rules of procedure, the committee on legal affairs has jurisdiction to scrutinise the credentials of members. this report, which includes the list of elected members, reports on the results of the direct elections to the european parliament which took place from 22 to 25 may 2014, on the basis of official communications from all member states on the final results of those elections. we voted in favour of this report which includes precise information on some worrying irregularities in the electoral process which need to be resolved in the near future: nationals of certain member states who have resided in another country for a certain period of time may have been deprived of the right to vote in their member state of origin; the commission has also proposed that the united kingdom should be allowed to take part in the european elections. the rapporteur advocates simplifying the registration formalities for the participation of nationals of other member states in european elections, both as voters and as candidates, in particular by removing unnecessary administrative barriers, which could help to avoid the problem.
in writing. with the report by mrs ayala sender we are facilitating the crossborder enforcement of road safety legislation. it is crucial to speed up the exchange of information on infringements and to ensure a high level of protection for eu drivers. i am convinced that this legislation will help to reduce the number of offences committed by drivers from other member states and will create a strong deterrent for these drivers, since an offence committed in another member state can be charged to the driver in the member state of residence. the directive 2011/82/ec on the cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences, adopted on 25 october 2011, which had been declared invalid by the court of justice of the eu on legal grounds, is thus re-adopted. the new text respects the court's judgment by introducing a new legal basis, namely transport safety, and adds the territorial scope of application to denmark, the united kingdom and ireland.
in writing. this directive aims to ensure a high level of protection for all road users on the union road network by facilitating the cross-border exchange of information on road safety related traffic offences and, consequently, the application of penalties where such offences are committed with a vehicle registered in a member state other than that in which the offence was committed. i voted in favour of this proposal which aims to reduce the number of road accidents which cause the death and temporary or permanent disability of thousands of european and national citizens every year.
in writing. the court of justice of the eu had ruled that transport safety is the appropriate legal basis. the content of the provisions of the directive demonstrated that the system of exchange of information between the competent authorities of the member states, on which the directive was based, was the means and not the objective of the directive, which was simply to improve road safety. although it declared the directive invalid, the court recognised its relevance and stated that, in order to avoid a legal vacuum, the provisions of the annulled directive should be maintained for 12 months. the commission has therefore put forward a new proposal for a directive, which deserves my agreement, although it was responsible for promoting the request for annulment, since it was the first to show interest in presenting to parliament, as soon as possible, a new text to replace the text of the directive only in the points relating to the legal basis and the territorial scope of application. this directive should be adopted before 6 may 2015 in order to avoid a legal limbo in almost all member states that have already incorporated the provisions of the repealed directive into their national law. i voted in favour, recalling that we have always considered it a priority to ensure maximum road safety.
in writing. this directive aims to ensure greater protection for all road users in the various member states by facilitating the cross-border exchange of information on road safety related traffic offences and, consequently, the application of penalties where such offences are committed with a vehicle registered in a member state other than that in which the offence was committed. the offences covered by the directive are speeding, failure to use a seat belt, failure to stop at a red traffic light, driving under the influence of alcohol, driving under the influence of psychotropic substances, failure to wear a safety helmet, driving in a restricted lane and the unlawful use of a mobile phone or other communication device while driving. the amendment proposed by the european commission aims to amend the legal basis, following the decision of the european court of justice, while maintaining the existing level of protection. these are relevant and justified amendments. the amendments introduced by the report are designed to ensure that the processing of vehicle registration data containing personal data is subject to specific data protection provisions. we voted in favour.
in writing. this proposal takes over the text of directive 2011/82/eu on the cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences, adopted by a large majority in the european parliament and unanimously in the council in 2011, with the exception of two qualitatively significant amendments. on the one hand, the change in the legal basis and subsequent technical amendments and, on the other hand, because of this new legal basis for transport, the extension of the scope to the three member states which were excluded from the previous directive.
in writing. the court of justice of the european union has upheld the european commission's request to challenge the legal basis of directive 2011/82/eu, which was approved by the european parliament and the council. the directive was repealed but its effects remained in force, within a reasonable period which could not exceed 12 months, until a new directive was adopted on the basis of article 91 (1) (c) tfeu on road safety. the content of the directive is only subject to technical amendments, in particular with regard to data protection. the commission has thus identified eight infringements of the traffic rules which may lead to crossborder exchange of information, in particular when the infringement is committed by a vehicle registered in a member state other than that in which the infringement was committed. countries such as the united kingdom, ireland and denmark will have a transitional period for applying it, as they were not covered under the previous legal basis. this approval is the right decision for a concrete policy on road safety. i believe that when it is revised in 2016, it would be important to consider the possibility of including new infringements, in particular toll non-payment.
in writing. directive 2011/82/eu on the cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences aimed to end impunity for foreign vehicles on union roads and ensure road safety in the eu. foreign drivers enjoyed a certain impunity for crossborder offences, as the competent authorities did not know the address of the owner of the vehicle. in 2014, the court of justice found that that directive had been adopted on the basis of an incorrect legal basis and declared it invalid. it nevertheless acknowledged its relevance, stating that the provisions of the directive would remain in place for 12 months in order to avoid a legal vacuum and allow the legislator to adopt a new text. the commission therefore proposed a new text to adapt the judgment: it introduces transport safety as a legal basis, adds denmark, the united kingdom and ireland to the territorial scope of application and provides for adjustments as regards the implementing rules on data protection. i think it is essential to avoid a legal vacuum in a priority area such as road safety, so i voted in favour.
in writing. all measures aimed at improving road safety are welcome, especially when they aim to fill a legal gap related to the end of impunity for foreign vehicles on union roads, allowing all europeans to be treated equally. however, as the rapporteur has pointed out, special attention should be paid to the necessary protection of personal data.
in writing. following the judgment of the court of justice of the eu of 6/05/2014 in case c-43/12, which found that directive 2011/82/eu was adopted on the basis of an incorrect legal basis - that concerning police cooperation, the cjeu decided that transport safety should be the appropriate legal basis. the present proposal, which aims at creating a new directive amending directive 2011/82/eu on the cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences, is based on two fundamental changes to the previous text: on the one hand, the creation of a new legal basis for the field of transport safety and, on the other hand, the extension of the scope to the three member states that had decided not to accede to the previous directive - denmark, the united kingdom and ireland. the commission is therefore proposing to adopt a proposal on traffic offences which aims to avoid a legal vacuum in almost all the member states which have already incorporated the provisions of the repealed directive into their national law. i therefore considered it appropriate, necessary and urgent to vote in favour of this report on one of the areas considered to be one of the political priorities of the union: road safety.
in writing. this discussion arises from confusion about the legal basis of the directive which was consensual and necessary. with this revision, we have noted as positive its updating with the introduction of new types of infringements and greater guarantees in terms of data protection. the directive will certainly put an end to a certain feeling of impunity, but it will certainly not work miracles. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem, including the introduction of a new system of road safety inspections. in this respect, we are very concerned about the public-private partnership model which dominates road construction in europe and particularly in portugal. the result is high-priced toll roads that push much of the population onto secondary roads of poor quality and at great cost to the safety of the towns. this is just one example. palliative care is necessary, but it does not eliminate the need for background treatment.
the fisheries agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal was terminated in 2006, which resulted in a drastic reduction in the number of eu tuna trawlers in senegalese waters. in this context, the european commission negotiated a renewal of the agreement between the republic of senegal and the european union on sustainable fisheries. one of the principles of the agreement is to ensure a level playing field for eu fleets by not granting more favourable conditions to fleets other than those set out in the agreement, provided that the vessels have the same characteristics and catch the same species. in addition, the satellite monitoring system and the cooperation established between the eu and the republic of senegal on vessel monitoring and tracking in senegalese waters will help the local authorities to step up their fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. i voted in favour of this agreement because it provides for adequate support for the fisheries sector at local level, defines the exploitation of fisheries resources in accordance with the principles of sustainable fishing and constitutes an economic opportunity for the union's fisheries sector.
the fisheries sector accounts for only 1.3% of senegal's real gdp and eur 136 million of total exports, which are estimated at eur 1.7 billion. the report estimates that in 2011 the total exports of senegalese fishery products to the eu (mostly frozen) was approximately 40 000 tonnes. senegal also plays a key role in the landing of products from both artisanal and industrial fisheries, with some 400 000 tonnes of products landed, of which 90% come from artisanal fisheries and less than 50 000 tonnes from industrial fisheries. the reports concluded that the conclusion of a new partnership could be beneficial to both parties, helping both the republic of senegal and the european union to create jobs. the eu commits itself to ensuring that at least 20% of the seamen on board its vessels fishing in senegalese waters are from senegal or an acp country. the total amount of the financial contribution provided is eur 13 930 000.
in writing. this is another agreement in the west african tuna fisheries agreement network. the first fisheries agreement concluded between the eu and senegal dates from 2002 and expired in 2006. the new protocol has a duration of five years. the financial contribution provided for is eur 13 930 000, of which eur 5 240 000 is paid by the shipowners for access to fishing authorisations and eur 8 690 000 for compensation for access to resources and sectoral support. the licences will be distributed in full to the spanish and french fleets (36 tuna vessels and 2 trawlers), as no other member states (such as portugal) have expressed an interest in the fishing opportunities created by this agreement. despite the ill-conceived agreement on the problems and limitations common to other fisheries agreements, particularly as regards the effectiveness and efficiency of sectoral support, we consider it acceptable for both parties to conclude it. the fisheries control measures provided for in senegalese waters under this agreement to combat illegal, unregulated and unreported (iuu) fishing shall be positively registered.
in writing. the republic of senegal is a coastal state in west africa sharing its maritime borders with the republic of guinea-bissau, the republic of the gambia, the cape verde archipelago and the islamic republic of mauritania. with the exception of the borders with mauritania to the north and guinea-bissau to the south, the maritime borders of the republic of senegal are defined and recognised by mutual agreement. the total amount of the financial contribution provided for in this agreement is eur 13 930 000. this amount shall be distributed as follows: (a) eur 8 690 000 in the form of financial compensation for the annual financial compensation (based on a reference tonnage of 14 000 tonnes per year for highly migratory species) and for support for the development of senegal's sectoral fisheries policy; (b) eur 5 240 000, corresponding to the estimated amount of fees payable by shipowners for fishing licences. this agreement will be beneficial to both parties and will enable senegal's economic development, helping its people to live better and have better living conditions.
in writing. the european commission negotiated the renewal of the agreement between the government of the republic of senegal and the european union on fishing off the coast of senegal, thereby fixing fishing opportunities for european vessels against financial compensation. the agreement provides for 28 tuna seiners, 8 reelers and 2 trawlers (directed fishing for blackfish, a deep-sea species) to be allowed to fish in the waters of the republic of senegal in return for financial compensation of eur 1 808 000 in the first year, eur 1 738 000 in the second, third and fourth years and eur 1 668 000 in the fifth year. i am in favour of this agreement which allows the capture of 14 000 tonnes of tuna and an authorized catch of 2 000 tonnes for the blackfish.
in writing. the renewal of the eu-senegal sustainable fisheries partnership agreement aims to establish a new framework for cooperation, ensuring a level playing field for the union fleets. the protocol will be in force for five years and three categories of vessels will be authorized to fish in senegalese waters: 28 tuna seiners, 8 reed-fishing vessels and 2 trawlers (targeted for bluefin tuna). the financial contribution provided for is eur 13 930 000, of which eur 8 690 000 will be used for the annual financial compensation and support for the development of senegal's fisheries sector policy. given the opportunities for senegal's economy to prosper through better exploitation of existing fisheries resources, in accordance with the principles of sustainable fisheries and good practice in the sector, i believe that the new agreement and the new protocol are beneficial to both parties. i therefore voted in favour.
the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal is an asset for both parties, and in particular for the european union, as it has the potential to increase its economic activity in the region. satellite monitoring is also important in helping local authorities to step up their fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. this recommendation on the conclusion, on behalf of the eu, of a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal and its implementation protocol, which will be in force for five years, deserves my vote in favour, as it will allow the renewal of an agreement which expired in 2006, following the first agreement which had entered into force as early as 1981. the termination of the agreement in 2006 resulted in a drastic reduction in the number of tuna seiners in senegalese waters: of the 18 eu-flagged tuna vessels operating there, only two were able to continue their activities and a new agreement was therefore urgently needed. the conclusion of this agreement will ensure a level playing field for the union fleets by preserving, conserving and exploiting the fisheries resources of the region in a sustainable manner and will guarantee the conditions for supporting senegal's sectoral fisheries policy (1,3% of gdp), in particular through the financial contribution of eur 13 930 000, granted in respect of the country's sovereignty and legitimate aspirations and objectives in this sector.
in writing. the european union's fisheries agreements with third countries provide opportunities to provide, in a fair and clear way, sites with resources that can be exploited sustainably, to promote good use of the sea by providing third countries with the tools to combat illegal, irregular or unreported fishing, and to contribute to the development of third countries by providing fair payment for the use of their endogenous resources. the fisheries agreement with senegal is part of this. unlike other fisheries agreements, this one defines target species and some of the protected species. these facts are welcome. however, the agreement lacks mention of many of the protected species, including whales, dolphins, turtles and seabirds, and methodologies to avoid their disturbance. it is also noted that appendix 4 on protected areas does not yet contain information. it would be appropriate that this information should be available at this time and without prejudice to future changes. finally, it is noted that the fishing observation system, although controlled by the third country, is not entirely borne by the shipowners. a quarterly contribution of eur 100 as provided for in the agreement seems insufficient for this purpose.
the first agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal in the fisheries sector entered into force on 1 june 1981. the protocol expired in 2006. there was then a drastic reduction in the number of tuna-fishing vessels in senegalese waters. in this context, the council authorised the european commission to negotiate a renewal of the agreement between the republic of senegal and the european economic community, giving rise to a proposal for the conclusion of a new partnership agreement in the field of sustainable fisheries. this is an economically reasonable agreement, taking into account the fishing opportunities available, and ensuring the basis for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of the fisheries resources concerned. it also provides for fair support and sufficient conditions for the local fisheries sector.

the eu has always developed internal security and counter-terrorism policies based on police and judicial cooperation and the promotion of the sharing of security information, respecting fundamental rights and the rule of law. relations between the eu and the us are based on a strong partnership and cooperation in a number of areas, based on common and shared values of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the effectiveness of counter-terrorism measures and respect for human rights are not contradictory but rather complementary and mutually reinforcing objectives. however, respect for fundamental rights is an indispensable component of the success of counter-terrorism policies. therefore, member states conducting independent and effective investigations into human rights violations related to the cia programme need to base their investigations on sound forensic evidence and respect for national judicial systems, eu and international law, the primacy of national security and the sensitive aspects of any ongoing criminal investigations.

in writing. established in 2006, the internet governance forum (igf) has the primary role and function of discussing a wide range of issues related to internet governance and making recommendations to the international community, if necessary. the internet is a key pillar of the digital single market, promoting innovation, growth, trade, cultural diversity and human rights. we must therefore be concerned with expanding access to the internet worldwide, keeping the internet an open and shared resource, rejecting the idea of a state-controlled internet, and recognizing that our fundamental freedoms and human rights are not negotiable and must be protected online. by renewing the igf's mandate, strengthening its resources and maintaining the multilateral model of internet governance, we are contributing to ensuring an open and independent internet in the future, non-discriminatory access to knowledge, the stimulation of growth and employment, the promotion and protection of cultural and linguistic diversity and the legal protection of internet neutrality, which is an indispensable prerequisite for safeguarding freedom of expression.

in writing. the igf is tasked with discussing a wide range of issues related to internet governance and, if necessary, making recommendations to the international community. the european union's priorities in this area are to expand access to the internet worldwide, to maintain the internet as a global, open and shared resource, to ensure non-discriminatory access to knowledge, to increase the accountability and transparency of the multilateral model of internet governance, to reject the idea of a state-controlled internet, and to recognise that our fundamental freedoms and human rights are not negotiable and must be protected online. for all these reasons, i agree with the renewal of the igf's mandate and the strengthening of its resources, increasing the inclusive participation of all stakeholders.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) as a contribution to a democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue that broadens the range of internet governance issues. the resolution aims to put pressure on the un general assembly to renew the igf's mandate, strengthen its resources and maintain the multilateral model of internet governance. it is also proposed that the eu institutions concerned maintain financial support to the secretariat, to ensure the development of an efficient, independent organisation and thus contribute to the democratisation, openness and neutrality of the internet. these are goals that we feel are appropriate and fair. the internet should be a global resource of wide access to knowledge and information, communication, cultural diversity and freedom of expression. in line with the need to improve secure access, doubts and reservations remain as to the mechanisms and organisations that hold the power to ensure such security. we do not support attempts to push the provision of some services to the private sector, alienating the public service which, in this matter, is the guarantor of social prices for the populations and a secure and universal internet.
the internet is now a global instrument and its management should therefore be guided by the common interest. the internet is today one of the main means of spreading democratic values in the world, and is an indispensable instrument for promoting all kinds of initiatives, political debate and the dissemination of knowledge. the development of the internet is therefore essential if it is to be more equally accessible to all in the eu. it is also essential that it is safe for all its users, in particular for children who are less able to defend themselves against the potential dangers of its use. we must therefore prevent the governance of the internet from being dominated by any single entity or group of entities, so that it maintains its status as a global public good. hence my vote.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forums (igfs) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) with regard to the organisation of forums for democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue. the aim is to discuss various issues related to internet governance and to make recommendations to the international community. i am in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that the united nations general assembly should continue to support this forum and the european union should take advantage of this process to hold more public debates with the main stakeholders at european level. i also believe that internet access should be improved worldwide, provided that the security and stability of computer services are guaranteed. this access reinforces the maxim, which i also subscribe to, that there should be no barriers to free knowledge by citizens.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forums (igfs) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) with regard to the organisation of forums for democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue. the primary role and function of the igf is to discuss a wide range of issues related to internet governance, making recommendations to the international community in this regard, if necessary. the ad hoc delegations sent by the european parliament played a key role in promoting european values and interacting with civil society organisations and representatives of national parliaments present at these events, in collaboration with the member states and the commission. however, considering that the internet is a fundamental pillar of the single market, promoting innovation, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights, and that growth related to the internet economy is expected to reach almost 11% in the eu, i think it is very important to promote this multilateral model of internet governance and to continue the fruitful exchanges carried out in the context of the igf. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the united nations general assembly to renew the mandate of the igf.
in writing. nowadays, the internet is a key pillar of the digital market. increasingly, the internet promotes growth, innovation, trade, cultural diversity and even human rights. the multilateral model of internet governance is an asset and should be supported. to this end, it is important that the member states, and in particular the commission, reinforce the sustainability of this model. however, it is important that efforts are made to ensure the neutrality and legal protection of the internet in order to safeguard the freedom of expression and information, which is so threatened today.
in writing. this proposal builds on the importance of the internet governance forum (igf) for democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue, the purpose of which is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society, which ends this year. the report, as the text of the report states, calls for an open and independent internet as a common global resource, along with non-discriminatory access to knowledge, and stresses that it is essential to continue efforts to ensure the legal protection of its neutrality, which is an indispensable prerequisite for safeguarding freedom of information and expression, stimulating growth and employment by developing innovation and business opportunities related to the internet, and promoting and protecting cultural and linguistic diversity. the eu is also calling for the creation of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the internet. at eu level, it is important to stress the need to support this process through exchanges and policy discussions, as well as financial support to enable the forum to develop as an efficient and independent organisation.
in writing. this proposal aims at renewing the mandate of the internet governance forum (igf), which is a multilateral working platform with the primary function of discussing a wide range of issues related to internet governance, and may even make recommendations to the international community aimed, inter alia, at promoting the expansion of internet access worldwide, ensuring its maintenance as a global resource of broad access to knowledge and information, as well as communication, cultural diversity and freedom of expression. the internet is also a key pillar promoting innovation and growth of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in various sectors of economic activity. notwithstanding issues relating to access to a secure internet and the guarantee of the protection of users' personal data, it is essential to continue the work, thus contributing to its development and deepening, in a multilateral platform that ensures its democratic character and safeguards the interests of the peoples and member states of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum because it addresses the need to improve access to the internet and stresses that the igf should remain as comprehensive as possible. calling for further efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality, which is an indispensable prerequisite for safeguarding freedom of information and expression, for stimulating growth and employment by developing internet-related innovation and business opportunities, and for promoting and protecting cultural and linguistic diversity. on the other hand, in considering that fundamental freedoms and human rights are non-negotiable and must be protected, in deploring that some states, citing security concerns, are trying to reduce the worldwide connectivity of their citizens and in rejecting an internet controlled and monitored by states, the text is in line with my convictions. furthermore, by urging the un to renew the igf's mandate, strengthen its resources and maintain the multilateral model of its governance, the resolution embodies a free and democratic vision of internet use by all.
in writing. this resolution aims to press the un general assembly to renew the mandate of the internet governance forum, to strengthen its resources and to maintain the multilateral model of internet governance. it is also proposed that the eu institutions concerned maintain financial support to the secretariat, to ensure the development of an efficient, independent organisation and thus contribute to the democratisation, openness and neutrality of the internet. in line with the need to improve secure access, doubts and reservations remain as to the mechanisms and organisations that hold the power to ensure such security. we do not support attempts to push the provision of some services to the private sector, alienating the public service which in this matter is the guarantor of social prices for the populations and a secure and universal internet.
the labelling of meat and meat products as to country of origin or place of provenance is a major concern for european consumers, especially following a number of food scandals that have become public in recent years. despite the current requirement of mandatory information on unprocessed beef and voluntary information in other cases, fraudulent traceability and information systems in the food chain have not been avoided. in matters of public health and food safety, i believe that a compulsory regime is the most appropriate, contributing on the one hand to a more rigorous system of traceability of products along the food chain and on the other hand to a more informed and transparent choice by the consumer, influencing his behaviour at the time of the choice. such a measure should always take into account the principle of proportionality in the administrative burden for operators in the sector and the competent supervisory authorities, while seeking to minimise its effects on price increases, supply disruptions and food waste.
in writing. according to a study by the european commission, 90% of consumers want to know the origin of the meat used in processed foods. in the wake of the horse meat scandal, the need to provide clear information to consumers and to increase transparency and accountability throughout the food chain has become even more pressing. i voted in favour of this resolution, reflecting the concern of european citizens and calling on the commission to come forward with proposals for the mandatory labelling of the origin of meat in processed foods. at the same time, a level playing field for economic operators in the sector, in particular smes, must be ensured and the necessary measures taken to combat fraud by strengthening controls.
in writing. it is estimated that 30-50% of the total volume of slaughtered meat is processed into meat ingredients for foodstuffs, mainly minced meat, meat preparations and meat products. the consumer should therefore be informed of the country of origin or place of provenance of such meat. indication of origin is mandatory in the eu for unprocessed beef and beef products and this measure should be extended to meat in processed foods. we cannot forget the impact that food fraud can have on food security, consumer health, consumer confidence, the functioning of the food chain and the stability of agricultural prices. the fight against fraud must be given priority.
in writing. from april this year, the indication of the country of origin will be mandatory for unprocessed meat from pigs, goats, sheep and poultry, and has been mandatory since the bse crisis for both processed and unprocessed beef. the resolution proposes making it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat in processed foods. measures are needed to avoid excessive and unjustified administrative burden that the change may impose on the rank and the need to provide for control mechanisms that allow the authorities to ensure the effective implementation of these standards. the aim is greater transparency along the food chain, along with better information for the consumer. if this instrument contributes to more stable relations between suppliers and meat processors and to greater care in the choice of suppliers and products by operators in this sector, favouring proximity, which can result in the enhancement of national production, then it will be positive. we supported this resolution, although we have some doubts about the practical implementation of the measure, which we have already expressed in the debate and in written questions to the european commission. we reserve a final position for the time when the legislative proposals in question are examined.
in writing. this report is positive because it aims to indicate the origin of meat in processed foods on labels in order to ensure greater transparency throughout the food chain and to better inform european consumers, while taking into account their impact assessments and avoiding excessive costs and administrative burdens. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. this resolution calls on the commission to submit legislative proposals to determine the origin of meat in processed foods such as lasagna. it should be mandatory to indicate this on the label of these products in order to better inform consumers and ensure greater transparency throughout the food chain, while avoiding excessive financial and administrative burdens. i have voted against this proposal, however, because i believe that such a requirement will bring unbearable costs to the manufacturing industries, which will not translate into benefits for consumers. the labelling is now voluntary and has been sufficient for consumers to be informed and, if they so wish, to consume only food with the appropriate indication of origin. at a time when it is necessary to give a positive boost to european industry, i do not think it is appropriate to burden it with additional costs by adding information which already exists on a voluntary basis.
in writing. this motion for a resolution identifies some pertinent issues with regard to the labelling issue. the indication on the label of the origin of meat in processed foods, as indicated in the impact study presented by the ec, will lead to an increase in production costs. given that 90% of the companies in the sector are smes, they will have an increased administrative burden. however, labelling of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat or meat products does not in itself prevent fraud, but a rigorous system will allow infringements to be detected and timely dealt with. a better traceability system along the food supply chain will help to make the relationships between suppliers and meat processors more stable and healthy and will allow consumers to make more confident choices. i voted in favour of this proposal for the reasons mentioned above, considering that the european union should reflect on a labelling system that ensures greater traceability and better food safety.
in writing. within the eu, depending on the member state, an estimated 30 to 50% of the total volume of slaughtered meat is processed into meat ingredients for foodstuffs, mainly minced meat, meat preparations and meat products. because indication of origin is already mandatory in the eu for unprocessed beef and beef products, expectations have been created among consumers regarding information on the origin of other types of fresh meat and meat used as an ingredient in processed foods. in fact, a consumer survey carried out in 2013 by the food chain assessment consortium revealed that more than 90% of consumers consider it important that the label indicates the origin. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that greater transparency throughout the food chain will have a positive impact on health and consumer confidence, and will also make it possible to detect fraud.
in writing. the recent developments in some eu member states concerning the sale of processed meat and food are of great concern. the labelling and the mandatory identification of the country of origin of the foodstuffs purchased is an added value for consumers. european consumers must have confidence in the food they eat. the successive food fraud cases which have occurred in recent times and in several member states are worrying. it is essential that consumer information labelling requirements are met, as is the existence of effective legislation to monitor the established parameters and fines for institutions that do not comply with them.
in writing. the present motion for a resolution (non-legislative) concerns the need to indicate on the labelling of products the origin of meat in processed foods in order to ensure greater transparency throughout the food chain. i consider it necessary, in the interests of public health and information for european consumers, that all processed food should include on the label the indication of the origin of the meat used as an ingredient, as it seems to me that this simple fact will ensure better traceability along the food supply chain, more stable relations between suppliers and meat processors and greater diligence in the choice of their suppliers. as regards the impact of this measure on prices, i welcome the fact that the report recommends that the commission submit legislative proposals which avoid excessive financial and administrative burdens. finally, i would also stress the need to encourage the commission to adopt measures to prevent and combat fraud in the food sector. unfortunately, this proposal was not voted for by my group, which wanted these measures to be adopted voluntarily, and only 60 members of the epp voted in favour of this proposal, including myself.
in writing. in theory, we think it is a good thing that information on the origin of the meat used in processed foods can be visible on the label. we could even extend this standard to all the ingredients in these products. we have, however, doubts about the operability of this standard. this issue, as is invariably the case in the european union, is the result of a scandal which has had an impact on the media and which has led the institutions to legislate without a mature reflection on the problems. it's one thing to adulterate a product with the illegal incorporation of horse meat. it is quite another to impose the labelling of the geographical origin of portions of meat incorporated into a processed food without looking at the costs this entails for the rank and file and without looking at whether there are control mechanisms which enable the authorities to ensure that these standards are actually met. in the absence of a closed position on this subject, these are questions that it would be important to discuss without rushing into a rule that will always have a strong impact, especially at the level of small and medium-sized enterprises in the sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods because the initiative is balanced, proportionate, ensures greater transparency, reflects a commitment to safe and high quality food and is appropriate for the defence of european consumers. following the bse crisis in europe, the horse meat crisis in the uk and, more recently, the minced meat crisis in portugal, all the necessary measures should be taken to prevent and combat fraud in the food sector, which is an integral part of eu policy, in order to address the structural weaknesses of the food chain by increasing and strengthening its control. the industry is not harmed in that the mandatory labelling requirements must take account of the principle of proportionality and the administrative burden will be shared between food business operators and the responsible authorities, while consumers clearly benefit from having relevant information concerning the entire food chain of the product they will eat.
in writing. from april this year, the indication of the country of origin will be mandatory for unprocessed meat from pigs, goats, sheep and poultry, and has been mandatory since the bse crisis for both processed and unprocessed beef. the resolution proposes making it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat in processed foods. we have supported this resolution, although we have some doubts about the practical implementation of the measure. we reserve a final position for the time when the legislative proposals in question are examined.

the purpose of the establishment of this special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect, which will consist of 45 members, is not only to examine the application by a member state or the commission of state aid law and union tax law in relation to tax rulings, but also to propose appropriate measures for the proper functioning of the internal market and to verify that aid granted by a state or through state resources is compatible with the internal market and is not being misused. the committee will also analyse and assess the impact of aggressive tax planning by companies established or incorporated in the member states and the exchange of information in this field.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument that provides support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns and aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant as soon as possible. this was the case for the chemical company pl/zachem, which saw its share of the eu's global chemicals market fall dramatically from 35,2% in 1992 to 17,8% in 2012. at the same time, there was a migration of the chemical industry to asia, where there was a very sharp increase in the manufacture of chemicals, from a share of 8,7% in 2002 to 30,5% in 2012. the difficulties in that company are related to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation and the conditions for the application to be eligible for support from the egf have been verified. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to improve the employability of all workers through adapted training and the recognition of qualifications and skills acquired throughout their working lives. this support should be complementary to the liability of the company under national law.
‒ the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. the polish authorities submitted application egf/2013/009 pl/zachem following 615 redundancies in zaklady chemiczne zachem and two suppliers, related to the suspension of production and the reorganisation of zachem. i voted in favour.
in writing. established more than 50 years ago, zachem s.a. was one of the most important chemical companies in poland and one of the largest companies in the north-western part of the country. from 1989 onwards, with the argument of greater efficiency and flexibility to survive in the new competitive environment, several changes were made both in the management and in the division of the company. in 2006, warsaw-based ciech increased its chemicals portfolio when it acquired zachem and organika sarzyna. with the increase of competition on the asian market, the sole producer in poland saw its market share decrease dramatically from 30,5% in 2002 to 17,8% in 2012. following the sale of tdi assets to basf, ciech, with the consent of the polish government, decided to discontinue the main activities of zachem and to dispose of or liquidate all remaining assets. some 615 workers lost their jobs in the region with the highest unemployment rate in the country. we agree to the rapid mobilisation of this aid to support the main targets with the consequences of the liberalisation of world trade, and we reiterate our criticism of the lack of measures to halt the course of the neoliberal policies which have once again led to this outcome.
‒ the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to poland, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf under the application egf/2013/009 pl/zachem following 615 redundancies in zaklady chemiczne zachem and two suppliers, related to the cessation of production and reorganisation of zachem, operating in nace rev. 2 division 20 (manufacture of chemicals) in the province of kujawsko-pomorskie at nuts ii level.

‒ the application to which this report refers concerns 708 redundancies in the duferconlmk companies. using the argument of serious economic disturbances, with a decrease in market share and a decrease in production to justify the option of using mass redundancies, the application submitted by belgium to the european globalisation adjustment fund seeks to mobilise the amount of eur 981 956. although the belgian authorities have guaranteed that the financial contribution will in no way replace the actions and responsibilities of the companies under national law or collective agreements, which is an attempt to ensure that the funding is not used to promote redundancies, what is needed is the restoration of the lost jobs and compensation for the damage caused to the lives of these 708 workers and their families.
