in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative proposal which aims, on the one hand, to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions from road vehicles and, on the other, to adapt the legislation to the technological requirements of electric mobility without affecting the load capacity of vehicles. this will help to speed up the introduction of more aerodynamic or hybrid vehicles. the proposal also aims to improve the intermodality of freight transport and to take measures to improve road safety.
‒ the proposed amendments bring improvements not only to new truck models but also to the safety of truck drivers and road users. member states should, for example, take specific measures to identify vehicles likely to exceed the relevant weight limits and implement appropriate national provisions within two years of the entry into force of the revision of the directive. it was also decided that the commission should review the directive three years after the national provisions enter into force, taking into account certain market segments, in particular that of light commercial vehicles.
the report also calls for the introduction of a european standardisation system for the safety of vehicles in road traffic. it is important to know at the outset whether the circulation of vehicles of these dimensions and weights is compatible with the road network of each member state, in particular as regards road endurance, maintenance and safety. the prerogatives given to member states in deciding on the type of vehicles that can be used on their road network are fundamental. it is recognised that certain technical aspects will result in improvements in the mechanical and energy performance, comfort, safety and reduction of polluting gases, including greenhouse gases, of vehicles. for these reasons, we voted in favour.
‒ i consider it essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in particular carbon dioxide (co2) emissions, to improve road safety, to adapt the applicable legislation to technological developments and to evolving market needs and to facilitate intermodal transport operations, while ensuring undistorted competition and protecting road infrastructure. i therefore vote in favour of this document on second reading.
‒ this proposal for a directive contains a set of important measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, increase road safety and adapt the sector to technological and market developments. since it improves the aerodynamics of the cabin of motor vehicles, with energy efficiency advantages, it also allows an increase in the load capacity of vehicles and maximum lengths. from now on, three- and/or two-axle vehicles with two- and/or three-axle semi-trailers up to a total weight of 44 and/42 tonnes are allowed to circulate. in order to ensure the application of this directive, member states should carry out annual checks on the weight of vehicles and the weighing devices used on board or otherwise should also be made available to the driver. the exchange of information between member states on their own infringements and controls should also be extended. i am in favour of adopting this document because it allows for the harmonization of the rules on road transport, removing obstacles to its development and obstructions to the internal market.
‒ technological developments make it possible to install retractable or retractable aerodynamic devices at the rear of vehicles. similarly, the use of alternative powertrains, which will draw energy from consumable fuels and/or a battery, allows pollution to be reduced. however, greenhouse gas emissions need to be reduced in order to improve road safety, to adapt the applicable legislation to technological developments and to evolving market needs and to facilitate intermodal transport operations, while ensuring undistorted competition and protecting road infrastructure. however, the installation of such devices would exceed the maximum authorised lengths and weights under council directive 96/53/ec. it is therefore appropriate to provide for a derogation from the maximum authorised weights and dimensions of vehicles and vehicle combinations laid down in directive 96/53/ec. the aim is to enable manufacturers to introduce new truck models that exceed current weight and size limits in order to improve the overall safety of the vehicle, its energy efficiency and its environmental performance. this proposal for a directive is aimed at making these changes. i voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve road safety, adapt the legislation applicable to technological and market developments, protecting road infrastructure and ensuring at the same time undistorted competition. technological developments have made it possible to install retractable or retractable aerodynamic devices at the rear of vehicles, thereby reducing their strength and, consequently, their consumption. the installation of these devices will cause vehicles to exceed the length limits, and therefore derogation from the regulation setting these limits is necessary. a new cab profile would help to improve road safety by reducing the blind spots for drivers, saving many lives. a new cabin profile would also allow for the installation of collision energy absorption structures.
‒ the amendment of the maximum authorised dimensions in national and international traffic, as well as the maximum weights of certain vehicles on the same routes, is essential given the constant flow of transport and loads in the member states of the european union. however, it is important and appropriate to monitor compliance with the standards set and the proposed amendment to the previous legislation on this matter.
‒ this document proposes a set of derogations from directive 96/53/ec, with the aim of fixing new maximum dimensions and new maximum weights, in national and international traffic, for certain road vehicles circulating in the european union. it is necessary to know in advance whether the circulation of vehicles of these dimensions and weights is compatible with the road network of each member state of the european union, in particular as regards road endurance, maintenance and safety. certain technical aspects of the diploma may result in improvements in the mechanical and energy performance, comfort, safety and emission reduction of vehicles. that is why we are voting in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of this regulation, as it is a regulation that leads to increased long-term european investment in the real economy, and this funding is 'a key tool to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth' (§1). the amount of assigned revenue in accordance with article 21 (3) of the financial regulation is estimated at eur 100000.
‒ long-term financing is a key tool to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, high employment and competitiveness for building a future economy, in a way that is less prone to systemic risks and more resilient. the european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing for various infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or long-lived listed small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) that issue equity or debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. by providing funding for these projects, eltifs contribute to the financing of the union's real economy and the implementation of its policies. financing for projects such as transport infrastructure, sustainable energy production or distribution, social infrastructure (housing or hospitals), implementation of new technologies and systems that reduce resource and energy consumption, or continued growth of smes may be scarce. eltifs can play a key role in this regard and can also raise capital by attracting investors from third countries.
the rhetoric of smart or not smart growth, innovation and investment does not hide the eu's persistence in a set of policies that block the realisation of any of these factors. the crisis of capitalism and its expression in the eu marked by over-accumulation of capital and the confirmation of the law of the tendency of the rate of profit to fall are still developing and deepening. in this particular case, if the market is not working, if the players are not investing, then we should not expect market instruments to solve the problem. the results of the ecb's longterm refinancing operations on banks are shown. this instrument is more of the same. it doesn't even innovate. it does not even contain a clause guaranteeing the social and labour rights of the jobs to be financed. it contains no environmental guarantee. as history teaches us, the recessionary cycle will only be broken by new policies based on an ambitious public investment programme that will restore the states to their leading role in the economy and in the construction of growth and development strategies.
‒ long-term financing is a key tool to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, high employment and competitiveness for building a future economy in a way that is less prone to systemic risks and more resilient. the european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing for various infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or long-lived listed small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) that issue equity or debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. by providing funding for these projects, eltifs contribute to the financing of the union's real economy and the implementation of its policies. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the european commission has focused its policy activity on fostering economic growth as well as job creation, implementing concrete measures aimed at boosting investment in the european union. i am voting in favour of this report, which aims to boost the long-term investments that must be made at european level, particularly those which make a decisive contribution to deepening the european single market and the transeuropean energy, transport and telecommunications networks. i also believe that the european union should make available a wider range of investment funds to support start-ups, thus diversifying their funding opportunities, which should be more in the form of venture capital companies rather than traditional bank loans granted by entities in the financial system.
‒ long-term financing is a key tool to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and to promote high employment and competitiveness. the european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing for various infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or long-lived listed small and medium-sized enterprises that issue equity or debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. eltifs thus contribute to the financing of the union's real economy and the implementation of its policies. as the financial crisis has shown, to tackle the lack of financing, it is important to complement bank financing with a wide range of sources of financing that better mobilise capital markets. eltifs can play a key role in this respect by channelling private savings into the european economy and attracting investors from third countries. i therefore voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the draft regulation to lay down rules for a clear identification of the categories of assets eligible for investment by eltifs.
‒ i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that long-term financing is a key tool to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the eu2020 strategy, generating jobs and competitiveness, but in a regulated and transparent way. the european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing for a range of projects and infrastructure, unlisted companies or listed small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), complementing bank financing in order to address possible financing shortfalls, mobilising capital and attracting investors from third countries. i also consider that it is necessary to regulate the rules for eltifs in order to avoid market distortions.
‒ long-term financing is a key tool to move away from austerity and to enable the european economy to enter a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy. these funds provide financing for various infrastructure projects, as well as for unlisted companies or small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), increasing employment and competitiveness.
‒ i voted in favour of this supplementary report on the proposal for a regulation on european long-term investment funds, precisely because i consider it to be an essential instrument for moving towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in line with the europe 2020 strategy. this financial mechanism will be the starting point for the creation of an integrated internal market for raising capital, which can and should be channelled into long-term investment in the european economy. for this reason, and like the rapporteur, i think it is essential that the commission should be able to identify the main obstacles to the crossborder mobilisation of these funds and their tax treatment, so that the objectives set out in the regulation can ensure the standardisation of investment requirements and ensure the conditions for the activity of these funds throughout the union.
we have a serious problem in the eu which arises from the expectations of economic operators who do not see any prospects for growth at eu level. we can talk about innovation, we can talk about smart growth, we can use whatever rhetoric we want. we might even think that economic agents are blind. but you only need to look at the world to understand that neoliberal policies based on free trade and non-intervention by the state in the economy to understand the reluctance of the agents to invest. and if the market doesn't work, if the players don't invest, then we shouldn't expect market instruments to solve the problem. see the results of the ecb's longterm refinancing operations on banks. this instrument is more of the same. it doesn't even innovate. they do not even contain a clause guaranteeing the social and labour rights of the jobs to be financed. they contain no environmental guarantees. as history teaches us, the recessionary cycle will only be broken by new policies based on an ambitious public investment programme that restores the central role of the states in building growth and development strategies.
‒ one of the major challenges facing the european union is to combat the fragmentation of the internal market in a number of areas, in particular the obstacles to the smooth functioning of the integrated electronic payments market. i support the bidegain report because i believe that this new regulation prevents excessive levels of fees from becoming widespread and promotes the creation of a genuine european-wide payments market by setting a maximum interchange fee of 0.2% of the transaction value for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards, whether they are cross-border or national. the establishment of a secure, efficient and competitive electronic payment system benefits consumers, traders and businesses, and the savings from this new regulation should be reflected in lower retail prices.
‒ this was an important vote of the strasbourg session in march 2015. in order to combat the fragmentation of the internal market caused by direct and indirect obstacles to the smooth functioning of an integrated electronic payments market, i voted in favour of european legislation to address the distinctions between national and international payments, making the european electronic payments market a reality, and to provide rules to make electronic payments effectively 'safer, more efficient, more competitive and more innovative' (§6), which is 'crucial for consumers, traders and businesses to be able to fully benefit from the advantages of the single market, especially as the world moves towards electronic commerce' (§6).
‒ payment transactions associated with debit and credit cards will be subject to a maximum eu interchange rate within six months. the idea is to prevent excessive levels from becoming widespread and to promote the creation of an eu-wide payments market. currently, in most eu countries, interchange fees paid by merchants to banks for the use of debit and credit cards are not subject to any legislation but to decisions by national authorities and vary widely between member states, creating barriers between national payment markets. the new regulation aims to prevent excessive levels of these fees from becoming widespread, to increase their transparency, to ensure a level playing field and to promote the creation of an eu-wide payments market. the ceilings are set at 0.3% of the transaction value for credit cards and 0.2% for debit cards, which i think is fair.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns a proposal to regulate, directly and indirectly, the exchange rates applied by companies and banks that issue and market debit and credit cards. the report comes out of the trilogue procedure with positive aspects. among them is the fact that payment and service providers cannot propose or require interchange fees for each bank transaction exceeding 0.2% of the value of the transaction, when it comes to debit cards. in national operations, member states may set a lower rate ceiling than that provided for and impose a fixed amount for the maximum rate as a limit on the amount of the resulting rate. they may also authorise payment service providers to apply interchange fees per transaction of up to eur 0,05 revised every five years. as regards credit cards, fees at european level are limited to levels not exceeding 0.3% of the transaction value. in this case, member states may also set lower thresholds for national operations. each member state should lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this regulation. we voted in favour.
‒ the fragmentation of the internal market is detrimental to competitiveness, growth and job creation in the union. with a view to the proper functioning of the internal market, it is necessary to remove direct and indirect obstacles to the proper functioning and completion of an integrated electronic payments market, without distinguishing between national and cross-border payments. i agree with the aims of this proposal, hence my vote in favour.
‒ some member states have adopted or are developing legislation to regulate interchange fees directly or indirectly, covering areas such as interchange fee caps, merchant service fees or the acceptance of all cards by the service provider. i am in favour of the establishment of uniform technical and commercial requirements for payment transactions, so that there is no differentiation within the european union. i am therefore in favour of the new rules which are due to come into force in six months' time, stipulating that a maximum amount for bank charges should not exceed 0.3% of the transaction value in the case of credit card payments and 0.2% when the debit card is the chosen payment method.
‒ the fragmentation of the internal market is detrimental to competitiveness, growth and job creation in the union. it is therefore necessary to remove direct and indirect obstacles to the smooth functioning of an integrated market for secure and efficient electronic payments, without distinguishing between national and cross-border payments, in order to enable consumers, traders and businesses to fully benefit from the advantages of the single market, especially as the world moves towards electronic commerce. logically, obstacles to the efficient functioning of the card market, including in the area of card payments and payments via the internet and mobile devices associated with card transactions, must be removed. card-based payment transactions, rather than cash payments, could be advantageous for merchants and consumers, provided that the charges for the use of card-based payment systems are set at a cost-efficient level, while contributing to fair competition, innovation and the entry of new market entrants. in view of this framework, this proposal for a regulation subjects payment transactions associated with debit and credit cards to a maximum interchange fee. i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that all payment transactions associated with debit and credit cards should, at most, be subject to an exchange rate with a defined limit. the information from the assessments on this issue indicates that the prohibition of interchange fees for debit card transactions will be beneficial for the widespread acceptance and use of cards, for the development of the single market and will generate further benefits for merchants and consumers. i therefore believe that, in view of the current situation, a single maximum level of interchange fees should be imposed for both national and crossborder card transactions.
‒ at a time when we are moving globally towards e-commerce, the existence of secure, efficient, competitive and innovative electronic payments is crucial if consumers, traders and businesses are to benefit fully from the advantages of the single market. the creation of uniform rules on electronic payment methods is a useful tool in removing any obstacle to the freedom to provide services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a ceiling for interchange fees for card-based payment transactions within the european union. within six months, 0.2% will be the rate fixed for debit card payments and 0.3% the rate for credit card payments, subject to the five-year transition period for national payment transactions. until now, exchange rates have been the responsibility of the national authorities, creating a marked disparity across the member states. the aim of this regulation was not only to prevent excessive levels of these charges from becoming widespread, but also to increase transparency, ensure fair conditions of competition and promote the creation of a european-wide payments market which benefits. this measure directly benefits traders, who thereby reflect in their prices the reduction in fees payable to banks, and indirectly consumers, who benefit from the price reduction in the goods and services they purchase.
‒ after having been presented to the european parliament at first reading, this report comes back after the trilogue with positive aspects. among them is the fact that payment and service providers cannot propose or require interchange fees for each bank transaction exceeding 0.2% of the value of the transaction when it comes to debit cards. in national operations, member states may set a lower ceiling for the percentage rates than provided for and impose a fixed amount for the maximum rate as a limit on the amount of the resulting rate. they may also authorise payment service providers to apply interchange fees per transaction of up to eur 0,05 revised every five years. as regards credit cards, fees at european level are limited to levels not exceeding 0.3% of the transaction value. in this case, member states may also set lower thresholds for national operations. in the case of universal cards, the rule for debit card transactions is followed. each member state should lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this regulation. in defence of consumers, the burden of such charges, which represent a more easy profit for banks and financial companies, is unacceptable.
‒ this report concerns a proposal to regulate, directly and indirectly, the exchange rates applied by companies and banks issuing and marketing debit and credit cards. after having been presented to the european parliament at first reading, this report comes back after the trilogue with positive aspects. among them is the fact that payment and service providers cannot propose or require interchange fees for each bank transaction exceeding 0.2% of the value of the transaction when it comes to debit cards. in defence of consumers, with regard to e-commerce, online sales and payments with such cards, the burden of such fees, which are nothing but more easy profit for banks and financial companies, is unacceptable.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument that provides support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns and aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant. this is the case of saint-gobain sekurit, which manufactures safety glass for the automotive industry. the company's activities were closely linked to the production trends in the automotive industry, which between 2007 and 2012 decreased from 21,9 to 19,5 million units, while in the rest of the world it increased from 47,5 to 60,6 million units. the difficulties of that company in europe are linked to globalisation and the conditions for the application to be eligible for egf support have been verified. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to improve the employability of all workers through appropriate training and the recognition of qualifications and skills acquired throughout their working lives, on equal terms. this support should be complementary to the liability of the company under national law and not superimposed on other types of union financial support.
in january 2015, the decision was adopted on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in favour of belgium, amounting to eur 1 339 928, due to the dismissal of 257 workers between august and december 2013 at saint-gobain sekurit. a significant decrease in production between 2007 and 2012 at sgs benelux, driven by a significant increase in production in the rest of the world, led to a loss of around eur 20 million at this company. however, in the same group, profits were recorded in other companies on more profitable terms, leading the group to the option of a layoff of 257 workers. the use of this funding, the report says, is aimed at providing individual assistance in job search, case management and general information services, training and retraining. it is shameful that the eu is sympathetic to the bedouin strategy of multinational companies, which set up camp in a given place in exchange for large amounts of community funds and, when it suits them, for the sake of maximising profits, set up camp and move on to other places, often with the generous support of the very same eu funds.
‒ the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and should now be granted to belgium, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf in the form of egf/2013/011 be/saint-gobain sekurit following 257 redundancies linked to the closure of a production unit of the saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) group in auvelais, which produced safety glass for the automotive industry.
in writing. ‒ belgium has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following the closure of a production unit of the saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) group producing safety glass for the automotive industry, which resulted in 257 redundancies during the period from 31 august to 31 december 2013. according to the commission, this application fulfils the eligibility criteria provided for in the egf regulation, as it is found, on the one hand, that the redundancies in question are related to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as the automotive safety glass manufacturing sector has suffered from severe economic disruption as a result of various factors such as declining production, increasing market shares of third country competitors and increasing imports of these products, and, on the other hand, that the redundancies occurred in a difficult socioeconomic context, characterised by a relatively high level of structural and long-term unemployment and low levels of skills and competences. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for belgium.
‒ i voted in favour of this application as it meets the requirements. this decision concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 339 928 from the egf in order to mitigate the effects of the redundancies caused by the lay-offs of 257 people in the period from 31 august 2013 to 31 december 2013 in the sector of safety glass manufacturing for the automotive industry. this sector has suffered from severe economic disturbances due to various factors, leading to a decrease in the union production of automotive safety glass caused by an increase in the market shares of third country competitors and an increase in imports of these products. in addition, there has been a general trend among manufacturers and suppliers of the automotive industry to shift production from western europe (particularly france, belgium and spain) to eastern europe. in addition, the coordinated package of personalised services to be co-financed includes the following measures for the reintegration into the labour market of 257 dismissed workers: individual assistance in job search, case management and general information services; training and retraining; promotion of entrepreneurship.
‒ the creation of legislative and budgetary instruments to provide complementary support to the most diverse sectors has proved to be a positive measure in the transition and adjustment of the member states to the era of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important instrument in that it can serve to reintegrate people and businesses into the global market. in this case, and in the light of the situation presented, the aid granted to belgium is relevant.

‒ equality between men and women must be seen as one of the pillars of our society, which is why the issues raised in this own-initiative report of the european parliament are central to europe. the work carried out by my colleague marc tarabella calls for the european union and the member states to take gender into account in the europe 2020 strategy as well as the development of a plan for investment in social infrastructure, as this is estimated to have a positive effect on the growth of gross domestic product. because of these and other issues raised in the report, such as the prevention of violence against women and the call to resume negotiations on the maternity directive, i shall vote in favour of this text.
‒ i voted in favour of this report, firstly because of the need to give due weight to the role of women in the framework of the new policies for economic revitalization, ensuring that the gains from these policies are effectively reverted to greater empowerment of women. and there is evidence of the need for this procedure: the increase in the employment rate for women has been rather slow, from 58.1% to 62.8% over the last 10 years, which is obviously a weak and disappointing development. if the current trend continues, the europe 2020 target will not be reached until 2038. it is therefore essential and urgent to promote the participation of women in the labour market. secondly, we see the persistence of the gender pay gap: "if current trends continue, it will be necessary to wait until 2084 for women and men to have equal pay". it is therefore important to act on this matter in order to speed up the reduction of this gap. finally, they add to these reasons the need for a concerted eu response to poverty among older women (10% more than men) and the need for a strong political signal on the reform of the maternity leave directive.
in writing. ‒ as the report points out, it is regrettable and we must step up action to eradicate the fact that women do not receive the same pay as men when they perform the same or equally valuable functions. the reduction of the gender pay gap by one percentage point will lead to an increase in economic growth of 0,1%, which makes the reduction of the gender pay gap crucial in the current economic downturn. equal participation of men and women in the labour market could significantly increase the eu's economic potential. more women than men live in poverty and social exclusion, especially older women, whose pension is on average 39% lower than that of men. the council must urgently take a position on the maternity leave directive because the current directive does not reflect the evolution of society. a comprehensive policy framework on gender-based violence should focus on prevention, prosecution of offenders, protection of victims, education for equality, and sanctions for violent or discriminatory behaviour against women.
in writing. ‒ this report makes a reasonable diagnosis of the setbacks that women's rights have had in recent years, particularly in the last decade, although we do not agree with some statements, when it is tried to make believe that the european semester can meet social objectives, which is impossible because it is contradictory. the report also does not hold the eu or governments responsible for policies which have led to the destruction of the social functions of states, unemployment, lower incomes, and pushed women into poverty and exploitation. we have proposed several amendments in this respect, all of which were rejected by the majority of parliament, which says a lot about your position on this matter. in fact, there is no desire to identify the real causes of these setbacks. the balance between personal and professional life has also deteriorated: the european union has a long history of working towards a common european policy on health and safety at work. we also welcome the fact that this report addresses sexual and reproductive rights from a fundamental human rights perspective and recommends easier access to contraception and abortion, although we recognise that it is up to the member states to define health policies. we voted in favour.
‒ this report addresses important issues such as the pay gap, women's participation in the labour market, the impact of the crisis, poverty, the proposal for a directive on maternity leave, currently blocked by the member states, and thus makes a good diagnosis of the hard work still to be done in relation to women's rights. i would stress and deplore the fact that women are not paid the same when they perform the same or equivalent functions as men. in the eu, the gender pay gap is 16.4%. we must hold to account the policies of various governments that have reduced wages and withdrawn social rights and that lead so many women to live in a situation of poverty and social exclusion . it is also urgent to find effective measures to prevent and punish violence against women.

in writing. this proposal is to examine the progress made in the european union with regard to gender equality, and some proposals have been put forward with which i do not agree. in this respect, i voted against the adoption of 'systems of parity and gender quotas introduced in some member states' because i believe that all people should be in public or private positions by competence and recognition of their work, to the detriment of gender quotas. i also voted against the proposal for 'easier access to abortion' because i believe that preventive measures, family planning and the availability of contraceptive methods to prevent pregnancy should be adopted first, thus protecting the safeguarding of human rights. finally, i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is essential to continue to work actively to improve gender equality not only in the european union but also worldwide. the report focuses on this important subject and not on divisive issues which have unfortunately been brought into the european debate and are strictly a matter for the member states.
‒ equality between women and men is a fundamental principle of the eu, enshrined in the treaties since the treaty of rome in 1957 and in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. this resolution takes stock of the progress made in 2013 towards full gender equality. it stresses, first of all, that the increase in the employment rate of women is still quite slow. since 2002, it has increased from 58,1% to 62,8% and has been affected by the crisis. the fiscal consolidation policies have affected the public sector, where women are more represented, and have led to an increase in precarious employment (32% for women compared with 8.2% for men). these short-term factors are accompanied by structural problems, notably the gender pay gap. it should be noted that according to an oecd study of december 2012, the eu could see its gdp increase by 12% if there was true equality between men and women in the labour market. so, although i disagree with some of the points raised in the report, particularly the defence of easier access to abortion, i voted in favour, given the importance of this issue.
‒ i voted in favour of this report as a whole because it is very balanced in expressing the concerns for a society with true equality between men and women at a time when europe is showing very strong signs of economic recovery and therefore of emerging from the crisis, leading to the fulfilment of the europe 2020 strategy. in order to achieve this, it is essential to improve the quality of work and to combat gender inequalities, in particular in factors such as the wage gap for the performance of the same tasks, inequalities in access to the labour market, among others. at the same time, i also believe that it is urgent to introduce measures to promote the reconciliation of private and professional life in order to combat the persistence of stereotypes.

‒ a sound european union competition policy is of paramount importance in our times. only through an innovative competition policy and an open market will we overcome the current financial crisis. eu competition policy has brought numerous benefits in terms of consumer welfare and has been an essential tool in removing obstacles to the free movement of people, services, goods and capital and in preserving a competitive single market. i particularly welcome the adoption of the directive on antitrust actions and the ecj ruling on anti-competitive fees for the use of credit cards. despite the successes achieved, i reiterate the need to continue to identify possible imbalances between member states which could distort competition and to pay attention to the phenomena of social dumping and the misuse of structural funds which are incorrectly used to indirectly shift services and production to other member states.
‒ the framework of a competitive europe, centred on clear competition rules, is the only one that allows a positive and constructive way out of the crisis. i believe that the fight against cartels, the abuse of a dominant market position or certain state aids are elements which distort the internal market and therefore require close supervision by the commission, especially in the context of ex post bailouts of financial institutions by states and the growing need for a transparent policy of harmonising tax provisions throughout the eu. at the same time, i support the appointment of the rapporteur for the creation and implementation of legislation promoting competition in the energy, digital, financial, industrial and transport sectors. if we want to give credibility to the portuguese and european economy and turn the page to a new era of prosperity, we must closely monitor the competition dossier, which is why i voted in favour of the rapporteur messerschmidt's suggestions in this particular case.
‒ a competition policy based on a fair business plan in all sectors is an essential instrument for ensuring the proper functioning of a dynamic, sustainable and innovative internal market, for economic growth and job creation, and for being competitive on the global stage. the report finds that competition does not operate equally well in all member states. it should be noted that the cartels have resulted in losses of between eur 181 and 320 billion. tax evasion, tax fraud and tax havens cost eu taxpayers around €1 trillion a year in lost revenue, distorting competition in the single market between companies that pay taxes and those that do not. competition drives innovation, productivity, job creation and investment by all actors across the single market and across all business models, including smes, while fully respecting national diversities. for all these reasons, i consider it important that the commission applies the rules on antitrust, state aid and merger control in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and social progress.
‒ this report analyses eu competition policy. as always, he laments the single market, the open market and the sacrosanct free competition. although it is punctuated here and there with aspects which we support and which cannot be denied or hidden, such as criticism of state aid to the banking sector, tax fraud in the eu and its component in competition policy, the recognition of the existence of cartels and the need to combat them, the fact is that it insists on the continuation of eu competition policy and its consequences. the report calls for the eu to pursue these policies further, in particular by calling for the liberalisation of sectors such as transport, health, industry and energy, and for a chapter on competition rules in ttip, the digital single market, etc. more liberalization is called for in more public and strategic sectors of the economy. without addressing the consequences, such as creating difficulties for state intervention, and serious obstacles to competition in other eu policy areas, such as the cap in agriculture, where entire crops are being wiped out. the defence of the role of competition policy as an instrument for preserving european democracy speaks volumes about the concept of democracy that prevails here.
‒ the report includes some positive points concerning the violation of eu competition policies, such as: criticism of state aid to the banking sector; the google case and its lack of resolution and the scale of tax fraud competition in the eu. the report also calls for the eu to take a more active role in the fight against terrorism and to promote the development of a european security and defence policy. for these reasons i abstained.
‒ it should be clear to everyone that competition policy and competitiveness in general are vital to the health and success of the eu as a whole and therefore of its citizens. it is by fostering an innovative competitive culture that we may be able to finally emerge from the financial crisis. through an effective competition policy, we can consolidate and strengthen the eu's importance in the world. therefore, as we embark on a new political mandate, the term 'competitiveness' must be at the top of our political agenda. this report shows that much remains to be done to improve eu competition policy. let us all work together to achieve the goals we have set.
‒ some sectors of the single market remain divided by national borders and artificial barriers, and there is sometimes an abuse of structural funds or tax aid that causes difficulties for the european union's competition policy. i believe that competition policy is an instrument for preserving european economic democracy, in that it prevents excessive concentration of economic and financial power in a few hands and allows the competitiveness of the various european sectors to be increased. in this sense, and because i believe that it is essential to improve the single market in the area of competition policy, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ in the single market, some sectors remain divided by national borders and artificial barriers. on the other hand, we are witnessing practices such as social dumping and the misuse of structural funds, which raise difficulties which also need to be addressed in the framework of eu competition policy. competition policy is an instrument for preserving european democracy in that it prevents excessive concentration of economic and financial power in a few hands, which puts at risk the independence of european political power vis-à-vis the large industrial and banking groups. the report also stresses that competition policy is a cornerstone of the european social market economy, ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market, the development of smes and the protection of consumer interests. in this respect, it is worth noting the commitment shown by the new commission to effectively apply competition rules in the areas of antitrust and cartels, mergers and state aid, to align competition instruments with market developments, and to promote an innovative competition culture both in the eu and globally. i voted in favour.
in the case of the european union, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's internal market is not distorted. practices that devalue labour, state aid that favours companies in favour of others, unlawful competition practices, the negative impact of cartels and the monopolization of certain sectors make it difficult or even impossible to maintain the healthy competitiveness that is essential for economic growth and job creation. it also calls into question the eu's free market principle. i also agree that the need to ensure a level playing field for businesses in the internal market also implies the fight against dumping and the implementation of social and environmental legislation at european level.
‒ i believe that competition policy and competitiveness in general are vital to the health and success of the eu and should be at the top of our political agenda. however, we must always bear in mind that this must never override the rights of workers and the fundamental guarantees of every citizen.
‒ it is a well-established fact that we need to promote healthy, sustainable and effective competition in order to pursue the ambitious objectives of the union in terms of jobs, growth, innovation, productivity and investment, with a view to a more globally competitive european economy. overall, i agree with the proposals made in this resolution concerning the annual report on eu competition policy and therefore voted in favour of it. i would also stress that the adoption of these proposals would be extremely beneficial for the completion of the single market, especially those relating to greater protection of the rights and interests of consumers and to ensuring greater competitiveness for our common competition policy.
‒ it was in the name of free competition that liberalizations and privatizations of strategic sectors of the economy and the advance of the market on growing spheres of social life were justified. the result was catastrophic. public monopolies have been replaced by private monopolies or oligopolies. the promises of more competition, better quality and lower prices are now a mirage. in the electricity sector, liberalisation and the end of vertical integration of generation and distribution in publicly owned companies have led to increases in energy bills for businesses and households. as monopoly profits and rents have risen. in transport the picture is similar, with the same public revenues guaranteeing private profits. we therefore condemn this false argument of competition, which has only served to weaken the national states and to line the pockets of the same old ones.
‒ this annual report lauds the single market, the open market and free competition. although it is punctuated here and there with aspects which we support and which cannot be denied or hidden, such as criticism of state aid to the banking sector, tax fraud in the eu and its component in competition policy, the recognition of the existence of cartels and the need to combat them, the fact is that it insists on the pursuit of eu competition policy with all its consequences. the report calls for the eu to deepen these policies, in particular by calling for the liberalisation of sectors such as transport, health, industry and energy, and advocating the existence of a chapter on competition rules in ttip in the digital single market. we voted against it.

‒ the report on the activity of the european central bank in 2013 is conclusive proof of the complete failure of the ecb's monetary policy. he failed to forecast economic growth and inflation. it has failed in all measures to control inflation and inject liquidity into the economy, whether in setting interest rates or in the various refinancing operations of the banks. nothing is said about the ecb's growing power. no suggestion is made to question the legitimacy of this institution. we strongly disagree with the report's praise of the ecb's policy and particularly of the banking union, which represents a further step in the amputation of fundamental parts of the sovereignty of the states and the concentration of power in the hands of big financial capital, through the institutions at its service, such as the ecb, which at the same time manages and supervises the financial sector in the eu. we continue to advocate a fundamental change in the ecb's statutes, which guarantees its political control by the states and their presence, on an equal footing, in its management. in the name of a supposed independence, what is being said is that the ecb is totally dependent on financial capital.

‒ this report aims to reform a set of regulations in the commercial field (omnibus i and omnibus ii). the majority of these are technical corrections, which aim to define safeguard and surveillance instruments that can be applied to imports of products, including coal and steel, and to update the annex. however, it is worth recalling our opposition to the omnibus i and omnibus ii regulations. following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty in 2009, the common commercial policy becomes an exclusive competence of the eu, with states losing the power to conclude, in accordance with their specific interests, bilateral trade agreements with other countries or regional blocs. limiting the sovereignty of states in the field of their trade policies. decisions on trade agreements are now being made in the interests of the major european powers. although this is an eminently technical report, our vote is inseparable from the above-mentioned position of principle.
‒ this is a purely technical matter. this proposal concerns the codification and recasting of regulation (ec) no 625/2009 on common rules for imports from certain third countries. that is why i am voting in favour.

‒ the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation whose objective is to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. this decision was voted in favour by me in favour of the enhancement of the efficiency of the agreement, which was considered in 2011 to be achieved through a process of amending the agreement. one of the most important changes introduced in the new agreement is a 'clear overall objective of biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources' consistent with my conviction, as a permanent member of the envi commission, of the need to preserve marine ecosystems. secondly, the new version of the agreement establishes 'common management of fisheries through multiannual management plans, the establishment of restricted fishing zones and the collection and dissemination of data', together with the fight against illegal fishing, the pursuit of maximum sustainable yield, blue growth and an approach to fisheries that takes into account the ecosystem perspective, including, in my view, the need to introduce sanctions and dispute settlement mechanisms.
‒ the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) whose objective is to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. in 2013, a process of amending the gfcm agreement was initiated, which revised the structure and content of the current gfcm agreement in order to bring it into line with the modern instruments of the gfcm. the main changes introduced are a clearer explanation of the objectives and principles underlying the gfcm agreement; a better definition of the gfcm's functions, namely the promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fishing restricted areas and the collection and dissemination of data; sanctions in cases of non-compliance by members and non-members and the resolution of disputes.
‒ the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), established within the framework of the fao in 1949, entered into force in 1952. the european community became part of the gfcm in 1998. the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation whose objective is to promote the conservation, rational management and best use of living marine resources. the gfcm contracting parties have agreed to amendments to the agreement, which are basically aimed at bringing it into line with the latest developments in the general framework of regional fisheries management organisations. the main changes introduced are:- a clearer explicit statement of the objectives of the gfcm (biological, economic, social, environmental) and of terms which are necessary for a correct interpretation of the agreement;- a clearer definition of the functions of the gfcm, which includes the promotion of common management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fishing restricted areas, the collection and dissemination of data;- the establishment of sanctions in cases of non-compliance with the agreement;- the establishment of dispute settlement mechanisms for disputes that may arise between the contracting parties. the rapporteur proposes that parliament should approve these amendments. we voted in favour.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, in that i support the establishment of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), as it is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) whose purpose is to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. the amendment to the agreement now proposed has been negotiated with the contracting parties in the gfcm and the council has authorised the commission to negotiate on behalf of the union on matters falling within the union's competence. i agree with the need to revise the structure and content of the current agreement to bring it into line with the modern instruments of the rfmo, including a clearer explanation of the objectives and principles underlying the gfcm agreement, a better definition of the functions of the gfcm, provisions on sanctions and dispute settlement.

‒ i welcome and vote in favour of this recommendation on the acceptance, on behalf of the european union, of the amendment to the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, as it introduces clarifying amendments to its objectives and principles relating to the sustainability of marine resources. the amendments also included a better definition of the scope of the gfcm's functions, sanctioning provisions for cases of non-compliance and a mechanism to facilitate dispute settlement. like the rapporteur, i believe that these amendments will achieve the objective of improving the sustainable use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea, and will also ensure the conservation and protection of marine ecosystems.
‒ the proposal for a council decision is an important document because it clarifies the general principles underlying the general fisheries commission agreement for the mediterranean, integrating the pillars of sustainable development into the marine environment. the new agreement promotes the common management of fisheries through coordinated plans aimed at the principle of precautionary management based on ecosystems, reducing landings, combating illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing and creating marine protected areas. i shall, however, dwell on one concept, so that it can be properly applied in the operationalization of this document. maximum sustainable income is not a goal, but a limit. in this respect, the new common fisheries policy states that catch levels must be maintained to ensure that the water resources are above the level that promotes maximum sustainable yield. in other words, fishing effort will have to be conservative, i.e. less than what promotes maximum sustainable yield.
‒ the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), in accordance with the provisions of article xiv of the fao constitution, was approved by the fao conference in 1949 and entered into force in 1952. the european community acceded to the gfcm on 16 june 1998 by decision 98/416/ec. the mediterranean and black sea states which are members of the eu are also parties to the agreement. in view of the mutual interest in the development and proper use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea, and in view of the guarantees regarding the conservation and sustainable use of living marine resources in the application area and the protection of marine ecosystems, we have nothing to object to.
‒ this item is concerned with the waiver of the immunity of theodoros zagorakis, mep, at the request of the deputy prosecutor of the supreme court of justice of greece and communicated in plenary on 28 january 2015, in the context of the ongoing e2010/3844 procedure before the criminal court of thessaloniki. taking into account the relevant legal provisions, case law and the report of the committee on legal affairs, i voted in favour of the waiver of the immunity of this member, in agreement with the majority of members of the european parliament, considering that theodoros zagorakis is accused of a breach of his physical integrity and of failing to comply with safety standards at the workplace as president of paok football club, and considering that there is no reason to assume that the legal proceedings are aimed at prejudicing the political activity of the member, given that they were initiated several years before the start of the member's term of office, in line with the recitals of the european parliament's decision of 11 march 2015.
the european parliament has called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european parliament is given the necessary powers to deal with the matter. the member is accused of violating the physical integrity and not complying with the safety standards at the workplace. the legal action relates to the work accident suffered in may 2010 by an employee of paok football club at the club's stadium in thessaloniki. theodoros zagorakis is the defendant in his capacity as president and legal representative of the club. the alleged infringement has no apparent connection with the status of theodoros zagorakis as a member of the european parliament, but only with his duties as president of paok football club. consequently, the action does not concern any opinion or vote expressed in the exercise of his mandate as a member of the european parliament within the meaning of article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union. it is therefore considered that there is no reason to assume that the judicial action is aimed at prejudicing the political activity of the member, given that it was initiated several years before the start of the member's term of office and therefore the parliamentary immunity should be lifted. we voted in favour.
‒ the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and that independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. this request is made by the deputy prosecutor of the supreme court of justice of greece, who has requested the waiver of the immunity of theodoros zagorakis, member of the european parliament, in the context of a possible conviction for an alleged infringement. theodoros zagorakis is charged with assault and breach of the safety regulations at the workplace. the charge in question is related to the work accident suffered on 13 may 2010 by an employee of paok football club at the club's stadium in thessaloniki and is directed against theodoros zagorakis in his capacity as president and legal representative of the club. since the alleged infringement has no obvious connection with the situation of theodoros zagorakis as a member of the european parliament, i have therefore voted in favour of the waiver of parliamentary immunity.

in writing. ‒ employment, enterprises and entrepreneurship to promote growth and economic, social and territorial cohesion are priority issues. both the eu budget and the juncker plan should help to revive the economy and boost job creation. the existence of a favourable business environment and the development of an entrepreneurial culture, including decent jobs, can restore the role of the more than 20 million smes, representing 99% of all enterprises in the union, as the main job creators. eu cohesion policy has been useful in supporting public investment in vital economic areas. the community budget must continue to play a crucial role in reducing disparities between europe's regions by ensuring investment in the areas where it is most needed. this internal solidarity must also be accompanied by external solidarity, based on the promotion of european values and respect for the commitments made. the commission should present a payment plan to address the recurring problem of outstanding invoices, which at the end of 2014 reached an unprecedented amount of eur 24,7 billion.
‒ the eu budget process is marked by a complex framework, in which the voluntarism of the speeches with selfless references to employment, investment, growth does not find the right match at the level of the eu budget. more specifically, regarding the 2016 budget and what this report tells us (or doesn't tell us) about it: - the cuts to the horizon 2020 framework programme are unacceptable, after all the propaganda around science and research; - the scenario is still that of 'business as usual'; a budget geared to fuelling the eu's neoliberal and militarist policies. we are in favour of a clear reorientation of expenditure towards policies of economic, social and territorial cohesion. policies to combat poverty and social exclusion. a genuine public investment programme, with resources amounting to at least 1% of eu gdp. a commitment to employment, social progress, environmental protection. a specific programme to compensate countries that have been victims of troika policies. a programme to frame a prepared exit from the euro, from countries whose existence has become unsustainable. these are some of the amendments we proposed to the report which were rejected by the majority. we voted against it.
‒ economic growth, internal and external solidarity and respect for commitments should guide the draft eu budget for 2016. i agree with the priorities outlined in this document which gives the guidelines for the 2016 eu budget. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the eu budget is predominantly an investment budget, with a strong leverage effect and is a catalyst for growth, competitiveness and employment, and is crucial for the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the union. this resolution sets out the political priorities for the 2016 budget. it therefore considered it imperative that all commitments in the multiannual financial framework (mff) be fully respected, and that the eu budget should present a balance between revenue and expenditure and definitively resolve certain problems, notably the invoices to be settled at the end of the year, the budgeting of the special mff instruments and the delay in implementing the new operational programmes under cohesion policy. it also stresses the support that must be given to smes and calls for legislative simplification, a reduction in bureaucracy and the use of the available financial instruments. finally, it reaffirmed the need to reform the eu's own resources system, the current inadequacies of which are causing serious deadlock in the budgetary negotiations, and to make every effort to create synergies not only between the investment plan and the eu budget but also with national budgets. i voted in favour.

‒ the protection of the eu's financial interests and the principle of sound financial management are basic and fundamental corollaries of a serious and responsible organisation of states. i believe that any misuse or fraudulent use of community taxpayers' money is detrimental to the interests of both the member states and the union as a whole. although the figures are not alarming from a statistical point of view for a union of this size, increased efforts are needed to combat fraud and corruption or any other type of activity detrimental to the financial interests of the union, whether in the collection of traditional own resources, the detection and reporting of irregularities, the control of expenditure and the application of sanctions. policy zero should be the guiding line! i would like to highlight the first eu anti-corruption report of 2014, which is a special tool for assessing and monitoring the fight against corruption, the role of olaf in monitoring irregular acts and the need for enhanced cooperation between member states and the commission in the adoption of measures and means to combat fraud.
‒ each member state contributes proportionally to the eu budget, thus representing an expression of unity and deepening european integration. the protection of financial interests and the principle of good administration increase citizens' confidence by ensuring that their money is used in a transparent manner. this report presents two proposals to strengthen existing measures to combat fraud, corruption, money laundering and other illicit activities affecting the financial interests of the union. this is where the commission and the member states must make every effort. the report notes that in 2013, 15 779 irregularities were notified to the commission, of which 14 170 were non-fraudulent and 1609 were fraudulent, involving a total amount of eur 2,14 billion, and 98% of the traditional own resources were collected without significant problems, with fraudulent irregularities representing 0,29% of the gross amount of the established octs (worth eur 61 million) and non-fraudulent irregularities representing 1,57% of the octs (worth eur 327,4 million).
‒ every year, the commission draws up a report on the protection of the european union's financial interests, including the latest information on irregularities and suspected fraud reported by the member states. this report focuses on the detection and reporting of non-fraudulent and fraudulent irregularities in relation to expenditure and revenue (traditional own resources) of the eu budget. we agree that there is a need to establish a framework for cooperation between the different member states, with the aim of sharing experience and best practice. this can be an added value for the fight against corruption at the level of each country. however, we consider it negative that such a measure is seen as an embryo, serves to promote or falls within the broader objective of developing the so-called 'area of freedom, security and justice', in particular with a view to harmonising justice at eu level. we therefore reaffirm our reservations about the creation of the european public prosecutor's office, based on europol, eurojust and olaf.
‒ the fight against fraud, corruption and any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the union is essential if the eu's policies and financial interests are to be safeguarded. only close cooperation and coordination between the commission and the member states will be able to ensure effective protection of the financial interests of the union, and it is therefore imperative to strengthen such cooperation and coordination and to make them as effective as possible. the protection of the financial interests of the union requires the same level of vigilance in respect of both resources and expenditure. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ in 2006 montenegro declared its independence from the state of serbia and in 2008 it applied for membership of the union. four years later the council approved the opening of negotiations, granting montenegro the status of candidate country. the copenhagen criteria have been implemented by the montenegrin authorities, in particular in their political, economic and social dimension and the application of the community acquis. the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in the european union. the chapter on science, education, culture and research is now closed. despite the progress made in the negotiations, there is concern that political instability could affect the actual implementation of the reforms. i would also like to stress that the conditions for freedom of expression and information for the media must be guaranteed, since this is a basic pillar of the rule of law. for the above reasons, i vote in favour of the efforts made by montenegro, its entities and citizens.

in the light of the above, the commission proposes to extend the scope of the european semester to include the following areas: only then can sustainable growth be ensured, so that better job opportunities are passed on to the next generation instead of a heavy inheritance, by holding them accountable for debts they did not commit. it is important to remember that only by promoting reproductive investments will we be stimulating sustainable job creation, which will enable real investment in human capital, professional mobility, research and innovation, which are essential to expanding the eu's economic potential and thus bringing prosperity to the people of europe. europe is a europe of regions, and the european project must leave no one behind. we must therefore continue to pay special attention to the outermost regions, the less developed regions, if we are to have real social and territorial cohesion in a europe at one speed. member states also have to do their part by eliminating unnecessary administrative burdens and red tape that discourage entrepreneurship, self-employment, the creation of 'start-ups', micro, smes that are the catalysts of economic growth, innovation, employment and social inclusion.
‒ the report on the european semester for economic policy coordination shows that the euro area is still struggling with the consequences of the economic slowdown that began in 2008. the commission must ensure that investment in economically less favoured regions is guaranteed. investment should be directed towards training and education, the fight against poverty, job creation and the fight against unemployment, support for smes and research.
in writing. ‒ we consider that the economic and social context in the eu remains bleak and that, according to the commission's autumn 2014 economic forecast, the economic recovery remains fragile. growth rates have been negative in the euro area for the past two years. we regret that the european semester has no social and employment objectives and is not in line with the social principles enshrined in the treaties. we see no more determined efforts to guide and coordinate eu policies to foster growth and better job creation. so without new policies, the burden will continue to fall on families and workers.
‒ strengthening the governance of the single market is inseparable from the practical possibility of establishing a specific pillar of the european semester dedicated to it. the coordination of economic and employment policies must be complemented by a core part covering all possible levers to stimulate the real economy which might otherwise fall outside the overall coordination of the european semester. i believe that priority areas such as the free movement of goods, services, public procurement and concessions, the digital agenda, consumer protection, energy and transport should be coordinated at the highest level within the annual governance cycle. leaving them out of the european semester would be a gross mistake in the eu's economic growth policy, obliterating the untapped potential of this market rather than using it as a catalyst for economic recovery and sustainable growth while attracting investment and promoting social cohesion. only by deepening and paying particular attention to the internal market in the context of the european semester, exploiting its potential for growth and jobs, will the european commission be able to achieve the priorities it has set for 2015 and the member states overcome the challenges posed by globalisation and the crisis.

in writing. ‒ like the rapporteur, i consider the completion of the single market, comprising more than 500 million europeans, a key instrument for the relaunch of more equitable economic growth and quality jobs in the eu, as outlined in the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to create the conditions for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. to this end, there must be a concerted effort between the eu and the member states to promote cross-border trade in services, a good and proper application and enforcement of single market rules as there are improvements to be made, in particular, in the transposition into national legislation, understanding of the legislative framework and duration of infringement proceedings. in this respect, i agree with the general guidelines set out in this report in the context of the european semester as a horizontal priority of the different union policies, preserving the balance between the economic, social and environmental dimensions and improving the quality of transposition, application, enforcement and monitoring of the rules of the single market, guaranteeing businesses access to an internal market capable of attracting investment and ensuring the necessary competitiveness for the eu to improve its economic model and assert itself as an effective global economic power.
