‒ the report recognises that the rise in unemployment and the growth in poverty and social exclusion is due to the impact of budgetary consolidation. however, in the proposals it continues to advocate measures which have been integrated into the policy of budgetary consolidation and structural reforms, which have led precisely to the problems which the report itself identifies. these are the measures which have led to the reduction of wages, the lay-offs, the cuts in public investment which are contrary to economic growth and therefore responsible for the increase in the unemployment rate. the report recommends, for example, continued fiscal consolidation and structural reforms, flexicurity, the alignment of wages with productivity and the raising of the retirement age, and the promotion of mobility as a way of reducing unemployment in some countries. we voted against it.
‒ this resolution focuses on one of the most pressing problems of the new virtual world and which - despite the efforts that have already been made - continues unfortunately to happen and to put our children at risk. it is therefore crucial to respond to the dangers that still abound on the internet and to ensure that authorities have effective monitoring and prevention capabilities. equally important, the union and the member states should also direct their efforts towards improving the awareness of educators, families and children themselves. but it is still up to the member states to implement the community framework on this matter quickly, ensuring concerted action on this phenomenon which knows no borders. in this context, the in-depth analysis to be carried out by the libe committee on this matter is of particular importance and i will put my full effort into it to better protect our children throughout the union. for all these reasons, i could not but vote in favour of this resolution and contribute to the broad consensus it has managed to achieve.
‒ the european parliament aims to combat sexual exploitation of children through this diploma by cracking down on criminals, increasing the protection of child victims of crime and focusing on preventing the phenomenon. the wording of this resolution had already been agreed with the different political groups in the ep, demonstrating the urgency and relevance of the subject. there is indeed convergence on the need for measures to manage child pornography on the internet, the existence of sufficient legal instruments to investigate and prosecute criminals, child education in ways that children can easily understand, measures to protect their personal data online, european cooperation and the establishment of best practices. the proposal also aims to cover a new dimension of the phenomenon, namely its expansion through the 'deep web', and urges representatives of alternative payment systems (e.g. bitcoin) to join the fight against child abuse, while strengthening the competence of judicial and police units in the field of high technology to face the challenge of analysing the large volume of child pornography images or materials.
‒ more efforts are needed to investigate child sexual abuse on the internet, prosecute the perpetrators, protect children and remove illegal content online. more than 80% of children who are victims of sexual abuse on the internet are under the age of ten. the sexual exploitation of children and images of abuse need to be addressed in a comprehensive manner, covering the investigation of these crimes, the prosecution of the perpetrators, the protection of children and the prevention of this phenomenon. i agree that illegal content must be immediately removed and reported to the police authorities, and that europol and national police authorities must be provided with the funding, human resources, investigative powers and technical capabilities they need to effectively investigate and prosecute criminals. eu countries that have not yet transposed the 2011 directive on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography into national law should do so.
‒ we share the general concerns expressed in this resolution. the internet can expose children to specific risks. measures are necessary to ensure its defence. the resolution does not, however, avoid mixing up just concepts and concerns with intentions likely to undermine fundamental rights and freedoms. the restrictions on widespread access to information technology, mobile communications and the internet are obvious dangers. it is necessary to ensure that, under the uncrc, the child has the right to freedom of expression, which includes the freedom to seek, receive and impart information, and that children are recognised as having the right to access information and material from a variety of national and international sources. it is also the responsibility of states and the companies providing these services to provide information to children and young people so that they can effectively manage risks and know where to turn for help. states must have sufficient resources to prevent cyber predatory and cyber harassment content on the internet and policies that have led to underfunding of educational programmes for children and parents must be reversed in order to protect children from these risks.
‒ more efforts are needed to investigate child sexual abuse on the internet, prosecute offenders, protect children and remove illegal content online. the resolution stresses that the reform of data protection rules currently under way will bring important changes to better protect children's rights on the internet. more than 80% of children who are victims of sexual abuse on the internet are under the age of ten. international cooperation and transnational investigations in this area need to be improved, as these crimes involve hundreds of countries, with their respective jurisdictions and police authorities. in this regard, the joint initiative of the eu and 55 countries from around the world, brought together in the global alliance against the sexual abuse of children on the internet, which aims to save more victims, ensure more effective repression, increase awareness and achieve a general reduction in child pornography material available online, is very important. that is why i am voting in favour.

mr president, the commercial fisheries in portugal show relative stability in the discharge of wild sea bass from year to year and this fish retains a good commercial value. the stability of the volume of fish caught could be an indication of its sustainability, but as in other regions of europe, there is no scientific knowledge to certify the state of the portuguese watershed and the amounts of annual fisheries are not even measured in terms of catches per unit of effort, but as an overall value. the opinions of the scientific bodies point to the need for specific management objectives, based on the best science, and are supported by the regional fisheries advisory councils. recent decoding of the robal genome has made it possible to identify two distinct populations of robal in the atlantic and the mediterranean. the complexity of the situation and the need to maintain sustainable water sources accessible to two distinct and sometimes competing fishing activities, commercial fishing and recreational fishing, therefore require comprehensive, pan-european and integrative regulation.

‒ this diploma sets out measures to maintain stocks above minimum conservation levels for the species. robalo is a noble species, highly sought after by the fishing industry because of its important economic value, but it is also of late maturity and slow growth, so the situation of the stocks is, according to some studies, 'concerned'. the resolution therefore calls on the member states to assess the state of the stock of sea bass by using the european maritime and fisheries fund, which provides for considerable funding for the collection of scientific data. finally, the fixing of total allowable catches, always taking into account mitigating factors and the historical fishing quotas of each country, should be introduced in order to achieve the maximum possible fishing yield within a sustainable framework.
‒ scientific information on the state of the stock of robalo is insufficient, in particular data are not available on its precise demarcation, migration routes and breeding sites, and there are several studies demonstrating that the state of the stock of robalo is worrying. mortality is still very high and robalo is a late-maturing, slow-growing species. recovery of this population unit requires a long period of time. i agree that the status of the stock of redfish and its demarcation, the migration of the species and the exact breeding sites should be assessed and that measures should be suggested for the management of the redfish fishery at european level in order to safeguard this species.
‒ fisheries management measures are often implemented in a top-down approach, supported by a lack of scientific knowledge, distanced from regional specificities, indifferent to the involvement of the sector and communities, their contributions and, as such, the impacts that these measures may have. this is an approach which we have distanced ourselves from and which we cannot but criticise, as we have always done. we appreciate that the resolution recognises the need for proper resource assessment, filling in the knowledge gaps on european robalo populations. we also welcome other aspects of this resolution, such as the reference to the importance of local government, which takes account of the diversity of situations at regional level, especially as a result of the amendments we have tabled. however, the resolution ends up being somewhat contradictory, recommending the imposition of transversal management measures at european level. these measures are contrary to the principle of regionalisation and ignore the diversity of situations. we regret that the amendments which we tabled were not accepted in plenary and which sought to address these concerns by removing the obvious contradictions and favouring management measures adapted to each specific situation.
in writing. ‒ the commission and the member states should assess the status of the robalo stock and its demarcation, the migration of the species and the exact breeding sites. the commission and the member states should build on the european maritime and fisheries fund, which provides for considerable funding for the collection of scientific data. we must impose management measures at european level for the fishing of sea bass in order to safeguard this species. these measures should take due account of scientific knowledge, promote local management and also take into account the principle of regionalisation. only then will sustainable and profitable exploitation of this important fishery be possible.
‒ scientific information on the status of the robalo stocks is insufficient, in particular the data available on their precise demarcation, migration routes and breeding sites. however, several studies have shown that the situation of the robalo stocks is worrying. mortality is very high and the robalo is a late-maturing and slow-growing species, and recovery of this population unit requires a long period of time. this resolution therefore calls on the commission and the member states to assess the status of the robalo stock and its demarcation, the migration of the species and the exact breeding sites. it also considered that management measures at european level for the fishing of sea bass were necessary to safeguard the species, which included the establishment of a multiannual sea bass management plan to restore the stock to a level above the maximum sustainable yield. i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ this resolution takes note of the lack of scientific information on robalo and calls on the commission and the member states to carry out an assessment of the resource. we also appreciate other positive aspects of this resolution, such as the reference to the importance of local management, which takes account of the diversity of situations at regional level. but despite this, general considerations are being advanced and, as of now, management measures at european level are apparently contradictory to these principles and seem to ignore the diversity of existing situations. the amendments which we have tabled here - and which we hope will be supported by you - seek to eliminate these apparent contradictions by favouring management measures which are undoubtedly necessary but which are adapted to each specific situation.

mr president, the results of the liberalization of the energy sector are in sight. the miraculous promises are confronted by the harsh reality. the natural monopolies of energy production and distribution were first broken up and then privatized. now, with the so-called energy union and the internal energy market, the conditions are being created for the further development of monopoly concentration on a european scale. this is the hard and pure objective, however much they try to envelop and adorn it with a rhetoric that is nothing more than that, the rhetoric of environmental efficiency and sustainability. however, while the new private monopolies are boasting fabulous profits, in portugal edp last year again generated over a billion euros in profits. families, businesses are choking on an energy bill that's never been higher. but the same policies will not produce different results. both the dynamisation of the economy and the sustainability of the energy model they require are to be achieved by restoring democratic public control over this strategic sector.
in its conclusions, the european council held an exchange of views on the economic situation in europe and the implementation of the fundamental structural reforms undertaken by the member states. the european council reiterates the three main pillars of the annual growth survey (investment, structural reforms and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation) and calls on the member states to reflect these priorities in their forthcoming national reform programmes and stability or convergence programmes. this shows that governments are still blind to the social and political reality of europe, dominated by unemployment, widespread poverty and the absence of prospects for growth. we need a europe which is geared to the people, not a europe which is tied to the interests of large multinational companies and the financial sector.
commissioner, in my country, portugal, as in many other countries, a small company that has managed to survive the crisis, besides having difficulty obtaining credit, has to pay 23% tax on its profits. at the same time, several large multinational companies, such as amazon, starbucks or ikea, are allegedly able to pay taxes of just over 1% by playing on the tax differences between eu states. second example, if my country cannot raise enough tax revenues to cover essential expenditure on education, health or support for the elderly, it risks paying a fine of up to 0.5% of gdp for not complying with economic governance rules. however, 19 of the 20 largest portuguese companies, which could most contribute with their tax contributions to balance these public accounts, chose to move their headquarters to the netherlands or luxembourg in order to benefit from the tax advantages offered to them. this practice of tax dumping between countries sharing the same market and the same currency becomes unbearable to citizens. the recent proposal of the european commission makes it compulsory to exchange information between the countries of the european union on tax optimisation practices. it is a step in the right direction which i acknowledge and thank commissioner moscovici for, but it is still insufficient. there are a number of measures that need to be taken to combat tax havens, to harmonize the tax base for companies, to report from one country to another. and the effort required of citizens also requires that we be determined to take these matters forward. the european parliament is fully committed to contributing to this new tax treatment and we sincerely hope, in addition to the support of civil society, in addition to the support of the commission, that we will have the same spirit of convergence from the council. that is what the citizens are demanding and that is the answer we have to give today.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, the least we can say about tax policy today is that it is inefficient and unfair. what we have seen in recent years, particularly in the crisis years, and this becomes more shocking associated with austerity, was in the name of competitiveness a huge fall in the rate of capital, both in profits and in revenues. in the name of so-called fiscal consolidation, we have seen an incredible increase in the taxation of both labour and consumption, which, combined with austerity and recession, has only had very devastating consequences for the periphery of the euro area. and the result is that in terms of the distribution of income and wealth, we're becoming more and more unequal. we've also seen aggressive tax practices, we've seen scandals associated with tax evasion and tax avoidance, as well as tax evasion, and we've seen that lux leaks is just the tip of the iceberg. the european commission's data show that european citizens lose one trillion euros a year as a result of tax evasion. as we have seen, every year there is also a permanent injustice. nineteen of the 20 largest companies in portugal have moved their headquarters to the netherlands or luxembourg to avoid paying so much tax. we are indeed witnessing tax dumping. the package on tax transparency which the commission is now proposing is nothing new. these are measures which have been in place since 1977 and which the commission has not put into practice. and calling the exchange of information between tax authorities transparent is at the very least an exaggeration. transparency was being public.
this debate is a hymn to hypocrisy. governments like president juncker have for decades coexisted with tax evasion, even encouraged it, and are now suddenly very concerned about tax justice. this report is nothing more than a list of pious intentions that binds nothing and no one. it points to scandals, but uses innocuous and inconsequential wording that does not point to the real problem. and the problem goes back to the 1980s, to the neoliberal revolution, to the privatization of key sectors of our economy, creating empires that rule our governments and our institutions. the reduction of the corporate tax base, the free movement of capital, tax havens, fraud and tax evasion are all the children of the same disease, which is the subordination of political power to economic power, that is, either we change this or everything stays the same.
the european single market is an imperfect market, limited by physical and legal barriers to the movement of goods and services, but also by practices such as tax avoidance and evasion and aggressive tax competition between member states. these practices undermine the confidence of european citizens in the single market. we must combat quickly phenomena such as lux leaks or the encouragement given by some countries to companies from other european countries to transfer tax obligations outside their territory of operation. the tax package presented by the european commission, focused on transparency, responds to a need but is clearly insufficient. the action plan on corporate taxation announced for the summer, together with the report being prepared in the european parliament, must give a clear signal of tax harmonization. transparency is not enough. active cooperation and a determined elimination of harmful tax practices in the eu context are needed.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is obvious that the question of the minimum wage we are discussing here is part of a wider discussion on what the real obstacles to the development of a barrier-free road market are and clearly has serious consequences, especially for the peripheral countries, as is the case not only in portugal but also elsewhere, and we must not forget that these issues affect economic growth and, ultimately, also affect export growth. i think that legal clarity for carriers is essential, but also a simplification of the regulatory framework. there are two basic issues here. on the one hand, there is a lack of effective control of cabotage operations and, on the other, there are differences in the application of certain provisions, such as the ban on regular weekly rest periods on board vehicles, as in france and belgium. we therefore need to review the establishment requirements, avoiding the transfer of activities to other member states with the deliberate aim of avoiding taxation and labour taxation. the commissioner has spoken here of fair working conditions and i think she has done very well, because i think it is important to safeguard the social and employment situation of european workers in this respect, especially by respecting the principle of subsidiarity. i would therefore like to ask the commission whether it is really prepared, and when, to initiate an effective reform of the road transport market in the union, so that all companies can compete on equal terms and so that their workers have access to fair conditions not only in countries such as portugal but also in other countries.

during the second world war, the roma community was the target of what can be called the 'forgotten holocaust'. roma were persecuted, captured, subjected to forced labour and murdered in germany, in the occupied territories and in countries that cooperated with the nazi regime. despite all the atrocities committed against the roma community, it was not until 1982 that the government of the federal republic of germany recognised the persecution and genocide of the roma. thirty years after the war, many of the victims did not live long enough to receive recognition and reparation for the crimes they were targeted for. sadly, there was not even possible justice for tens of thousands of human beings. the establishment of the day in remembrance of the genocide of the roma during the second world war is a long overdue gesture that is vital to restoring some justice and dignity to the roma community. i fully support the initiative and hope that this is the first of many steps in building a different narrative for rome and in recognising its integral role in european and world culture, past, present and future.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 5 046,000 for greece to support the 928 workers made redundant in 16 companies involved in radio and television programming.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument that provides support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns and aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant. in the case of attica broadcasting, and considering that the application meets the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, the aid package i voted for consists of vocational guidance, training, retraining and vocational training and grants for self-employment, job search and mobility, with a view to improving the employability of all workers. this support should be complementary to the liability of the company under national law and not superimposed on other types of union financial support. according to the data provided by the greek authorities, the greek economy is in deep recession for the sixth consecutive year (2008-2013). according to elstat, the greek statistical authority, since 2008, greek gdp has decreased by 25,7 percentage points, public consumption by 21 percentage points and private consumption by 32,3 percentage points, while unemployment has increased by 20,6 percentage points. this support concerns 928 redundancies in the reference period from 12 september 2013 to 12 june 2014.
‒ the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to obtain reimbursement of their costs from the eu when their applications are approved. the greek authorities submitted an application for redundancies in 16 companies operating in the radio and television programming activities in the attica region, corresponding to a financial contribution of more than eur 5 million. i voted in favour.
‒ the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to greece, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf in the form of the egf/2014/018 gr/attica broadcasting following 928 redundancies in 16 enterprises operating in the nace rev. 2 division 60 (radio and television programming activities) in the nuts 2 region of attica (el 30) in greece.
in writing. regulation no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. this report concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 5 046 000 from the egf for greece. it concerns 928 redundancies in the reference period from 12 september 2013 to 12 june 2014. these redundancies were due to a reduction in household disposable income and an increase in unemployment, which resulted in a huge fall in purchasing power and the need to set priorities in terms of expenditure, significantly limiting the money devoted to daily information, as happened with attica broadcasting. the coordinated package of personalised services to be co-financed consists of vocational guidance, training, retraining and vocational training and grants for self-employment, job search, training and mobility.
in writing. ‒ greece has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following 928 redundancies in 16 enterprises operating in the nace revision 2 division 60 (radio and television programme activities) in the region of attica during the period from 12 september 2013 to 12 june 2014. according to the commission, this application fulfils the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, as it is established, on the one hand, that the redundancies in question are linked to the global economic and financial crisis, as household disposable income has decreased, resulting in a huge fall in purchasing power and the need to set priorities in terms of expenditure, significantly limiting the funds devoted to daily information and drastically reducing loans to companies and individuals due to the lack of liquidity of greek banks, and, on the other hand, that the redundancies will have a very negative impact on the attica region, which already has the highest number of unemployed in greece compared to the other 12 regions. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for greece.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is a financial assistance mechanism designed to provide additional support to workers affected by the relocations that have occurred in the globalised world in which we live. greece has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf in order to cover the 928 redundancies in 16 enterprises in the audiovisual sector in the region of attica. it should be noted that this is the first application in this sector. since the dismissal of this number of workers will have a negative impact on this greek region, which has the highest unemployment rate of all the 12 regions, i consider this proposal to be important in that it provides a financial contribution to greece of €5 046 000, especially since most of these funds will be channelled to supporting the creation of businesses and investing in vocational training.
‒ due to the global financial and economic crisis which has deeply affected the greek economy, greece requested assistance from the egf following the redundancies in the media sector, in this case 928 workers in 16 companies in the area of programming and broadcasting. in this context, media companies experienced a decline in their revenues, as spending on advertising, one of their basic sources of revenue, fell dramatically by about 57%. the redundancies covered by this egf application are concentrated in attica, a region with an unemployment rate of 28% and where there are few job vacancies compared to the high number of jobseekers. as a consequence, more than 70% of the unemployed have been out of the labour market for more than 12 months. the measures co-financed by the egf helped workers to find new jobs by providing them with training, specific advice on entrepreneurship and assistance in setting up businesses. all redundant workers are eligible to participate in the measures. while we underline this support, we reiterate our criticism of the lack of measures to halt the course of the neoliberal policies which have once again led to this outcome.

in writing. ‒ mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2014/016 ie/lufthansa technik) is also requested. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's commitments under the paris agreement. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to assist their reintegration into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 2 490 758 for ireland to support the 424 workers made redundant at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and two of its supplier companies in ireland.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument that provides support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns and aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant. in the case of lufthansa technik, redundancies in the 'repair, maintenance and installation of machinery and equipment' sector in the southern and eastern regions of ireland are linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, which has led to the worldwide relocation of aircraft production. considering that the application meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, the aid package i voted for consists of vocational guidance and planning measures, egf training grants, training and upper secondary education programmes, higher education programmes, support for enterprises and self-employment, as well as income support, including the egf scheme of contributions to training costs. this support should be complementary to the liability of the company under national law and not superimposed on other types of union financial support. this support concerns 424 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd and two of its supplier companies in ireland.
‒ the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. the irish authorities submitted an application for redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd and two supplier companies in ireland for a financial contribution of eur 2 490 758. i voted in favour.
‒ the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to ireland, which submitted an application egf/2014/016 ie/lufthansa technik for a financial contribution from the egf following 424 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and two of its supplier companies in ireland.
in writing. ‒ the regulation (ec) no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. this is the tenth application to be examined under the 2015 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 2 490 758 from the egf for ireland. the irish authorities argue that the closure of ltai is the result of a profound change in trade in goods and services in the eu due to a technological shift towards the production of next generation aircraft and their components. the application thus concerns the dismissal of 149 persons in the reference period from 1 march 2014 to 30 june 2014. i therefore support this report which aims to mobilise a significant financial allocation to support people who have lost their jobs by providing them with new vocational guidance training, so that they have new tools and better skills to return to the labour market.
in writing. ‒ ireland has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following 424 redundancies in lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and two of its suppliers during the period from 1 march 2014 to 30 june 2014. according to the commission, the exceptional circumstances presented by the irish authorities justify a derogation from the intervention criteria of the egf regulation, on the one hand, as the redundancies in the 'repair, maintenance and installation of machinery and equipment' sector in the southern and eastern regions of ireland are linked to major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, as the closure of ltai is the result of a profound change in trade in goods and services in the union, which has changed the global location of aircraft production, and on the other hand, as these redundancies are expected to have a major negative impact on the already heavily disadvantaged southern and eastern regions of ireland, as demonstrated by certain socioeconomic indicators such as the low level of education and vocational training. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for ireland.
‒ the repair, maintenance and installation of machinery and equipment, as well as aircraft production in europe, has been suffering the effects of globalisation with the relocation of these services to china and south east asia. in the present case, the parent company lufthansa technik decided to base its airbus a330/340 mro operations in a subsidiary company located in the philippines. this has resulted in the dismissal of 250 workers in a very sensitive sector which has had a very negative impact on the southern and eastern regions of ireland where education and lack of vocational qualifications are a fact of life. in the light of the foregoing, i am therefore in favour of the mobilisation of this fund, amounting to € 2 490 758, in favour of ireland, as it meets the exceptional circumstances provided for in article 4 (2) of the egf regulation.
‒ lufthansa technik was split from the parent group in 1994. in 1999, lufthansa technik became fully owned by aer lingus, which in 1980 set up 'airmotive ireland', aircraft maintenance and general repair and overhaul in dublin. a profound change in trade in goods and services in the union, mainly due to globalisation and relocations, has had an impact on the business models underlying lufthansa technik, leading to the closure of lufthansa technik ireland. this is the tenth transfer proposal for mobilising the egf transmitted to the budgetary authority to date in 2015. this time it is ireland's application to the european globalisation adjustment fund to support 149 of the 424 workers made redundant by lufthansa technik in their reintegration into the labour market. once again, it is the regions with the highest unemployment rates that are hit hardest by the consequences of deregulation and liberalization of world trade and the eu's neoliberal policies.
‒ a profound change in trade in goods and services in the european union, resulting from a technological shift in the production of new generation aircraft and their components, coupled with the global offshoring of aircraft production, the fact that western european and us carriers have a habit of sending their large aircraft to china for heavy maintenance, and the offshoring of parent company lufthansa technik, which decided to base its airbus a330/340 mro operations in the subsidiary lufthansa technik philipines in the philippines, have impacted fundamental aspects of the market and the underlying business model of lufthansa technik ireland, leading to the closure of lufthansa technik ireland. this is the tenth transfer proposal for mobilising the egf transmitted to the budgetary authority so far in 2015. this time it is ireland's application to the european globalisation adjustment fund to support 149 workers out of a total of 424 workers made redundant by lufthansa technik. in addition to the many redundancies in companies in this sector over the past few years, it is even more difficult for these workers, with very specific skills in this sector, to find a new job.

in writing. ‒ a former member of the european parliament, gabriele albertini, applied for the defence of his parliamentary immunity on 16 september 2014 in the criminal action pending before the court of brescia (italy) and, in addition, requested a re-examination of the application for the defence of his parliamentary immunity in the civil action pending before the same court. according to the report of the committee on legal affairs, the supporting documents submitted by gabriele albertini did not make clear the relationship between his statements and his duties as a member of the european parliament, and in making the statements in question he was not acting in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. in the light of that report, i voted in favour of this decision, which maintains the decisions of the european parliament of 21 may 2013 and 24 february 2014 not to uphold the immunities and privileges of gabriele albertini and not to act on his request for review of the civil action brought against him.
‒ as regards the request for defence of privileges and immunities submitted by mr gabriele albertini, which has been reviewed, i agree with the consistent line of argument of the committee on legal affairs to reject this claim. as has been shown, the facts are not subject to any of the legal provisions of the protocol and the rules of procedure on this matter and there is no direct and obvious causal link between the statements he made and his performance as a member of the european parliament. as such, i find it untenable to accept his claim to the privileges and immunities of the defendant.

‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the annual report on taxation, which identifies areas of action for a fairer, more transparent and more effective tax policy. the report stresses the need to adopt fiscal policy measures that eliminate legislative discrepancies and administrative barriers between the different member states, boosting the single market. on the other hand, i agree that it is important to maintain the fiscal sustainability of states by ensuring their tax revenues by taking immediate and coordinated action, both in the eu and in the international context, to combat tax evasion and tax fraud, as well as to fight aggressive tax planning and tax havens. in this context, it is important to condemn and prevent the conclusion of secret agreements on tax exemptions for large companies and to stress the importance of measures for the automatic exchange of information and the adoption of general principles requiring the payment of taxes in the countries where services are consumed.
‒ €1 trillion of potential tax revenues are lost every year in the eu due to tax fraud and tax evasion, posing a major risk to the efficiency and fairness of eu tax systems, as it increases the tax burden on all bona fide businesses and citizens. this loss results in less public money being available for investment, which consequently translates into less capacity to encourage further private investment. companies take advantage of the complexity of tax rules and the lack of cooperation between member states to off-load profits and minimise their taxes. enhanced transparency and cooperation are therefore vital in the fight against aggressive tax planning and abusive tax practices. the tax transparency package which i voted for aims, among other things, to ensure that member states have the information they need to protect their taxable items and to effectively identify companies that try to avoid paying their fair share of tax.
‒ taking due account of the development of a tax system adapted to the specific characteristics of the economies of all member states, as provided for in the treaties, the report proposes a holistic approach to tax policy, which may prove to be an important instrument for fostering growth and deepening emu. good tax control is essential to reduce tax evasion and thus channel more revenue to member states. good taxation is therefore essential to strengthening the single market, to achieving economic growth and reducing unemployment. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ an estimated €1 trillion of potential tax revenues is lost every year in the eu due to tax fraud and evasion, so the existence of an automatic exchange of information between member states and the definitive abolition of bank secrecy in the eu as of june 2015 is key to increasing transparency in banking operations. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there are potential benefits of the internal market through tax policy and i am in favour of putting forward concrete proposals on how to tackle the obstacles which hinder the crossborder activity of individuals and businesses in the single market. finally, i would stress that the stabilisation of a fiscal policy is of strategic importance in promoting economic growth in the medium and long term, since transparent and stable taxation can help to increase investor interest.
‒ this resolution addresses the issues of taxation in the eu in 2014 and proposes a holistic approach to tax policy, identifying three main priority areas which are complementary to each other. first, it calls for specific tax policy measures to reduce the administrative burden on businesses and tax authorities by eliminating artificial barriers and discrepancies between national laws. it identifies initiatives that can ensure legal certainty, enhance cross-border trade, and promote the full potential of the single market, thereby boosting growth and jobs. secondly, it considers that fiscal policy is an important part of fiscal sustainability, as it ensures revenue. it therefore reiterates the need for immediate, coordinated and comprehensive action at eu level to combat tax evasion, tax fraud and tax avoidance, as well as aggressive tax planning and tax havens. thirdly, fiscal coordination through well-defined structural reforms in the context of the european semester is identified as the main instrument for developing fiscal policies that stimulate growth, employment and investment in the medium and long term. i voted in favour.
‒ this is the third (own-initiative) report that the european parliament has decided to draw up on the main fiscal aspects of the year 2014. it is an analysis of the current inefficiency and inequality of the tax systems of the european union, highlighting the four main problems we are facing at this level: tax evasion, tax fraud, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. by tackling these problems and using a more efficient and effective fiscal policy, we will be ensuring the fiscal sustainability of our states and of the union itself. although we are in the field of application of the principle of subsidiarity, it is important to adopt a concerted and bold policy, which is capable of simplifying procedures, reducing administrative costs, increasing transparency, sharing information between states, preserving fair and transparent competition and promoting the conclusion of tax agreements with third countries. in order to ensure good tax governance for the completion of the single market and for economic growth in the eu, it is important to strengthen the european semester as a mechanism for coordinating member states' economic and tax policies. i voted in favour of this report, which contains a number of ideas and guidelines for a responsible, transparent and balanced tax policy.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 6 052 200 for france to support the 2513 workers made redundant by mory-ducros sas.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund provides support for workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns and aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant. in the case of the french company mory ducros, which operates in the land transport sector, the number of redundancies reached 2513 out of a total of 2804 workers. in france, bankruptcies in the road freight transport sector increased by 35% per year between 2007 and 2013, as a result of the economic crisis which has led to the decline in goods production in europe, a price war in the sector and the consequent bankruptcies of companies. considering that the application meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, the aid package i voted for consists of vocational guidance and planning measures, egf training grants, training and upper secondary education programmes, higher education programmes, support for enterprises and self-employment, as well as income support, including the egf scheme of contributions to training costs.
‒ the egf was set up to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. dismissed workers are offered measures such as support for business creation, job search assistance, vocational guidance and various types of training. in most cases, national authorities have already started to take steps to have their costs reimbursed by the eu when their applications are approved. the french authorities submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following 2513 redundancies in the company mory-ducros sas, which is active in the land transport and in the oil and gas pipeline transport sector, with 84 redundancies in the whole of metropolitan france. i voted in favour.
‒ this report concerns france's application to the european globalisation adjustment fund to support 2513 workers in a company engaged in land transport, pipeline transport of oil or gas and storage and rental of related materials, moryducros. the redundancies made by the company are located throughout metropolitan france. the largest number of workers made redundant (257) is concentrated in the île de france region. at the time of the redundancies, the company was the second largest operator of these services in france, operating some 4 500 vehicles per day. with the crisis, road freight transport in vehicles weighing more than 3,5 tonnes contracted by 13,7% in the eu and 21% in france between 2007 and 2012. we agree to the mobilization of this (knowingly insufficient) aid in a hurry, although this fund only represents limited support for those who are the main victims of the capitalist crisis. we reiterate our criticism of the lack of action to halt the course of the neoliberal policies which have once again led to this outcome.
‒ the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to france, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf under the egf/2014/017 fr/moryducros following 2513 redundancies in the company mory-ducros sas, which operates in the economic activity classified under nace rev. 2 division 49 (land transport and transport by pipeline or pipeline), with the redundancies being spread over 84 locations throughout metropolitan france.
in writing. regulation no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. the application from france for the egf concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 052 200 for 2513 workers, of whom 2804 were made redundant in the company mory-ducros. i support the mobilisation of this financial envelope to cover the shortfalls in the road freight transport sector. this situation is also due, among other things, to the global economic and financial crisis which caused road freight transport to decline in european economic activity by 13,7% and, in the particular case of france, by 21% between 2007 and 2012 (eurostat).
in writing. ‒ france has submitted an application to receive a financial contribution from the egf, following 2513 redundancies in the company mory-ducros sas, operating in the nace rev. 2 division 49 (land transport and transport by pipeline) during the period from 13 march to 13 july 2014. according to the commission, this application fulfils the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, as, on the one hand, the redundancies in question are linked to the global economic and financial crisis, as the general decline in physical production in europe, which has led to a reduction in the volumes to be transported and triggered a price war in the road freight transport sector, has led to a steady deterioration of operating margins and a series of losses for the sector in france since 2007, and, on the other hand, such redundancies will further aggravate the unemployment situation in france, with a high risk of long-term unemployment and social exclusion, given the advanced age of the workers concerned. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which approves the decision to mobilise the egf for france.

in writing. mory-ducros sas, which operates in the land transport and pipeline transport sectors, faced a sharp reduction in its turnover in europe due to a general decline in the volume of raw materials or goods transported on the european market. this situation has led to a price squabble in the road freight transport sector, reducing operating margins and leading to consecutive losses since 2007. subsequently, the company went bankrupt and sent 2,513 workers to unemployment. given that the egf was set up to provide support for workers made redundant by companies that have suffered from the structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation, and given that the application submitted by mory-ducros sas meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, i am in favour of its mobilisation for the amount of eur 6 052 200. i would also like to leave a word of hope by noting that in this case a new company was created, mory global, which took over more than 50 branches out of a total of 84 and re-employed 2107 workers out of a total of 4911.

‒ this committee, called the social protection committee, is set up in an advisory capacity with the express objective of promoting cooperation between the member states and with the commission in matters of social protection policies, in full compliance with the treaty and with due regard for the powers of the union institutions and bodies. full respect for the treaty means nothing but the subordination of social rights and protection to free competition in the single market, as evidenced by the case law of the court of justice of the eu. in other words, the secondary status of social progress in relation to the 'market economy'. this committee is set up to strengthen the social dimension of emu in order to contribute to all aspects of the european semester. that is, to legitimize all the economic policies that the european commission has imposed on countries by further cuts in spending, in the social functions of the state, by privatising public resources, by promoting redundancies and by making labour costs cheaper. these measures are totally contrary to the stated social objectives. we don't fall for the bait. we voted against it.

‒ the sustainability of social protection systems, coupled with demographic change, requires member states to present long-term, sustainable strategies, identifying problems and possible solutions. although this is a matter for the member states, the european commission has put forward a mechanism for further cooperation and strengthening on the issues of modernisation and improvement of social protection. the high level committee, which has also been approved by the council, aims to help the member states to strengthen their social systems, while taking account of the priorities of each state. because of its importance for the maintenance of the european social state, where gender equality is one of the principles to be taken into account, i am in favour of the creation of a social protection committee.
in writing. the conclusions of the lisbon european council of 23 and 24 march 2000 pointed to the importance of modernising and improving the social protection system in the eu and called for enhanced cooperation between member states to exchange experience and best practice. in the context of the overall challenge of modernising social protection systems, the commission has identified four main objectives: making work rewarding and ensuring a secure income; ensuring pension security and the sustainability of pension schemes; promoting social inclusion; and ensuring a high and sustainable level of health care. the council supported the commission's proposal to establish a mechanism for closer cooperation, through the work of a group of high-level officials, for the implementation of this action. the committee shall keep under review the social situation and the development of social protection policies in the member states and in the union, and shall prepare reports and formulate opinions in its fields of competence at the request of the council or the commission or on its own initiative. this decision establishes the social protection committee. i voted in favour.

‒ this report allows the unused portion of the structural and investment funds in 2014 to be carried over to the next years, ensuring that it is not lost. the under-utilisation of the funds is due to the late adoption of the respective regulations, which led to only a small percentage of programmes being adopted by the end of 2014. the appropriations not used in 2014 and not carried over to 2015 are very significant, amounting to 15% of the 2014 budget. hence the need for a revision of the multiannual financial framework (2014-2020) to ensure budgetary commitment and payments to the various programmes that have been delayed. in practice, this review will allow unauthorised funds to be preserved and used in 2015 and beyond. the alternative to this modification would be that these resources would not be used and would be lost to this area (operational programmes) and that the appropriations would be reduced in the member states' contributions to the eu budget for the current year, which would benefit above all the wealthier countries. we voted in favour.

‒ on 1 january 2014, new rules or programmes in shared management entered into force for the structural funds: the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development, the european maritime and fisheries fund, the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund. in this regard, the multiannual financial framework should be revised with a view to transferring appropriations not used in 2014 to subsequent years, beyond the corresponding expenditure ceilings. i therefore vote in favour of this report which aims to transfer almost all cohesion policy appropriations not used in 2014 to subheading 1b 'economic, social and territorial cohesion' for 2015, with the exception of the erdf contributions to cross-border programmes under the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa) and the european neighbourhood instrument (eni), which are transferred to 2017.
in writing. the late adoption of the cohesion policy regulations for the period 2014-2020 has made it impossible to adopt all operational programmes in time and the revision of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020 is necessary. the european structural and investment funds constitute the most important investment policy of the union and it is therefore essential that all resources are used in a timely manner and in the most effective way possible to generate growth and jobs. the new programming period has already been significantly delayed, and it is important to ensure that no further delays or losses occur. this proposal sets out the mff for the period 2014-2020 and aims to transfer almost all unused appropriations in 2014 to 2015 to subheading 1b 'economic, social and territorial cohesion'. the only exception concerns certain contributions from the erdf, which will be carried over to 2017. the transfer of appropriations is an indispensable step to complete the process of starting the new programming period of cohesion policy, in order to avoid any negative impact on regions and cities and, consequently, on european citizens. i therefore voted in favour.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, alcohol consumption is a habit rooted in european society since ancient times and, if done in moderation, is benign, both socially and economically. however, alcohol abuse is the number one risk factor for disease and premature death among 25- to 59-year-olds. its abuse also represents a negative economic impact of around eur 155 billion per year. i therefore call for the renewal of the european alcohol strategy which has proven to be very useful and results-oriented and which ended in 2012. central to the treatment of alcohol is certainly the differentiated approach between what is different, i.e. between drinking in moderation and problematic patterns of alcohol consumption, as well as the recognition of regional and sub-regional variation in patterns of consumption and consideration of the different vulnerability of different segments of the population to the harmful effects of alcohol. particular consideration should be given to young people and the age at which they begin to drink. we must give priority to the issues of drinking during pregnancy, drunk driving and adopting healthy lifestyles. consumers should be provided with the necessary information in terms of public health. there is a wide diversity of practices in the member states with regard to labelling, the lack of guidelines and some level of standardisation, which translates into unnecessary costs for businesses and barriers to the single market. another important aspect is the definition of respect for the principle of subsidiarity and a minimum age for the purchase of alcohol, since from a medical/scientific point of view brain development continues well beyond that age. we must continue to improve instruments that promote good practice, gathering better indicators to evaluate the measures taken.

already mentioned, outlining the measures some member states have taken to curb the use of lightweight plastic carrier bags, do prove that action is effective. as an example, ms auken mentioned ireland. another example is scotland where early figures from retailers show that single-use carrier bag usage has fallen by more than 80% since a charge was introduced last october. these are just a few, and not the only member states that have actually taken action. once this amendment to the packaging and packaging waste directive is adopted and has entered into force, member states will have the tools available for effective action. they are responsible for the crucial task of implementation. the first step they have to take is to choose from among the instruments available to them to reduce the use of plastic carrier bags. i would also like to add that this directive addresses a major problem at source from a preventive perspective, and i have to say that the more preventive action we take today the less remedial action we will need tomorrow – especially in terms of marine litter, as was mentioned several times by a number of the members of this parliament. as many also mentioned, marine litter is a huge environmental problem threatening mainly, but not only, our marine biodiversity. i would say that this is a global problem needing a global solution. today we are only talking about the eu consumption of plastic bags but the problem is much bigger than that. i can assure everyone here that we will continue to take this problem very seriously and monitor it accordingly. the new directive also entrusts the commission with a number of tasks, such as the development of a methodology for calculating the annual per capita consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags, the development of labels or marks to ensure union-wide recognition of biodegradable and compostable plastic carrier bags, and assessing the impact of the use of oxo-degradable plastic carrier bags on the environment. we will tackle these tasks without delay with a view to meeting the – frankly more than challenging – deadlines agreed in the compromise. the compromise reached is an important step forward in addressing the issue of plastic waste, endorsed by overwhelming public support. i think that, through this new directive, we can demonstrate that the eu is able to effectively respond to matters of concern to citizens as well.
the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner arias cañete, ladies and gentlemen, it is a pity that the council is not present in this important document. the transport sector is responsible for about a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions in the european union, second only to the energy sector. in 2012, greenhouse gas emissions in the transport sector were split between road transport with a majority of 72% of the total against 12,8% for civil aviation, less than 1% for rail transport and 13,9% for the total shipping sector. between 1990 and 2007, co2 emissions in sectors other than transport decreased, while in this sector they increased by 36%. although the economic crisis has contributed to the slowdown in greenhouse gas emissions, we are already seeing the first signs that these emissions are rising again. unlike other forms of transport, the shipping sector has remained the only one not subject to any co2-reduction measures. in view of this, the 2020 energy and climate framework provides for a review clause for the inclusion of maritime transport in the union's reduction targets in the event that an international agreement is not reached in the meantime. we will be adopting legislation at this plenary session which is a first step towards reducing these emissions, which represent around 4% of co2 emissions in the european union. contrary to the objectives of decarbonising the european economy, in the medium and long term, if nothing is done, greenhouse gas emissions from ships will increase by more than 50% by 2050. the adoption of this regulation at second reading will, in my view, meet three important policy objectives: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the maritime sector, in particular the maritime transport sector. regardless of the progress made in this forum, in terms of setting targets for emission reductions being somewhat disappointing, the truth is that cooperation with our international partners is essential in terms of climate policy and the european union is once again taking the lead in this area. we will continue our efforts and this is one of the steps towards an ambitious agreement of an international nature. secondly, this legislation will combine the monitoring of co2 emissions with energy efficiency data from ships and the transparency of this data. the european commission will make reliable information on energy consumption and efficiency of ships available to the market on an annual basis. in this way, we will be able to remove barriers to the sector adopting technical and operational measures that will translate into co2 emission reductions at lower net costs, i.e. around eur 1.2 billion per year, as well as a higher competitiveness of european maritime transport, which will benefit international trade. finally, this legislation will have the potential to create some 10 000 jobs in green technology areas linked to the maritime sector, as well as public health benefits related to lower emissions of other pollutants such as nitrogen oxides, sulphur oxides and fine particulate matter. i therefore believe, ladies and gentlemen, that a robust system of monitoring, reporting and verification of emissions is a precondition and a cornerstone for any further emission reduction measures that may be decided for this sector in the near future. finally, i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs who have worked with me on this dossier, colleagues christopher fjellner, jytte guteland, julie girling, bas eickout, josu juaristi ‒ fishing is one of the occupational sectors with the highest accident rates, with very serious consequences for the lives of fishermen and their families. an estimated 24,000 lives are taken each year in the course of the activity. the international convention on standards of training, certification and room service for seafarers on fishing vessels of the international maritime organisation aims precisely to reduce as far as possible the occurrence of these threats to the safety of workers' lives by guaranteeing to the personnel on board a set of minimum requirements and qualifications for the exercise of the sector. i support the report by mrs sofia ribeiro and i consider it essential that all the member states ratify this convention. this decision should now encourage the member states to ratify the convention as soon as possible.
‒ the proposal aims to ensure that on-board personnel have the necessary qualifications to reduce threats to the safety of persons or property at sea or to the marine environment during operations on board fishing vessels. the convention requires that personnel have a minimum level of knowledge in specific subjects and have been on board a ship for a minimum period of time. fishing is the occupation with the highest accident rate, with an estimated 24 000 lives lost each year in the course of fishing. i would like to highlight the excellent work done by my colleague, mrs sofia ribeiro.
‒ the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards for the training, certification and rooms service of seafarers on fishing vessels was adopted on 7 july 1995 at an international conference attended by 74 governments, 22 of which are currently members of the european union. the purpose of the convention is to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels have professional qualifications attested by official certification and that their fitness for work is attested by medical services. these measures are aimed at improving safety conditions for this work and minimising threats to the marine environment. for countries that are signatories to the convention, these provisions are binding only for ships with a length of at least 24 metres and a propulsion power of 750 kw. this recommendation agrees that the council may authorise member states to sign the convention if they so wish, which we consider to be a positive development. we voted yes.
‒ fishing is the occupation with the highest accident rate, with an estimated 24 000 lives lost each year in the course of fishing. the stcw-f convention contains only mandatory provisions for fishing vessels of 24 metres in length or more and of 750 kw power or more, and is limited to encouraging signatory countries to apply training standards to seamen of vessels of the same length but of lower power, and does not specify mandatory minimum knowledge for fishing vessels of less than 24 metres in length. i believe that it is appropriate to extend the scope of the stcw-f convention or at least to adopt regulatory provisions applicable to vessels of less than 24 metres at union level. hence my vote.
in writing. ‒ the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards of training, certification and room service for seafarers on fishing vessels (stcw-f convention) was adopted by the international maritime organisation on 7 july 1995 in london. the convention aims to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels have the necessary qualifications (as attested by an official certificate) and the necessary fitness for work (as attested by a medical certificate) in order to minimise potential threats to the safety of human life, property at sea or the marine environment during operations on board fishing vessels. the union cannot ratify the stcw-f convention, only member states can do so. however, in accordance with the aetr case-law of the court of justice of the eu, member states cannot ratify the stcw-f convention without the authorisation of the union, as the provisions on the recognition of regulated professions exercised by union citizens on board fishing vessels affect the exercise of the union's exclusive competence in this area. the purpose of this decision is to authorise member states to ratify the stcw-f convention in accordance with the union's exclusive competences. i voted in favour.

the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of plastic bags, which is a requirement for the member states to ensure that the level of annual consumption of plastic bags does not exceed 90 bags per person on average by 2019 and 40 bags per person by 2025, and to make it mandatory for member states by the end of 2018 by requiring that no free lightweight plastic bags are made available at points of sale. the council also proposes an annual compulsory declaration of the consumption of plastic bags by the member states, in order to assess the effectiveness of the measures taken, the obligation to identify biodegradable and compostable bags. as regards the designation of 'degradable oxo-waste' proposed mainly by the producers of plastic bags, the council proposes to carry out further studies of the environmental impact of these products.
‒ this report recommends accepting the council's position after negotiations with parliament. this directive is nothing more than the direct application of the polluter-pays principle, a view which we do not share - and the council's position makes it worse, since instead of the obligation to adopt measures to ensure that the level of annual consumption of plastic bags does not exceed on average 90 bags/person by 2019 and 40 bags/person by 2025, it intends to impose it as mandatory for member states by the end of 2018, requiring that no free lightweight plastic bags are made available at points of sale. rather, research and development of solutions that avoid the harm associated with plastic bags by replacing them in their various uses should be encouraged, and environmental awareness and awareness campaigns should be promoted and supported by encouraging the change of packaging or means of transport of goods traded by the various sectors.
‒ the maritime transport sector plays a crucial role in the european economy, accounting for a large part of international freight transport between the eu and the rest of the world, and intra-community freight transport. regulation of emissions from shipping has been identified as a need in the context of air quality and climate policy-making both at european and intercontinental level. i support the report by mr josé inácio faria because it establishes a system for monitoring, reporting and verification (mcv) of greenhouse gas emissions from the maritime sector at european union level, which will make it possible to develop policies to reduce emissions associated with the sector in line with the general policies on climate, air pollution and the protection of human health.
‒ international shipping is the only means of transport that remains outside the eu's greenhouse gas reduction commitment. emissions from this sector currently account for 4% of eu-wide emissions. this regulation introduces a european-wide system for the monitoring, reporting and verification (mrv system) of co2 emissions from maritime transport. the aim is to increase transparency on ship emissions and create an incentive to reduce them. from 1 january 2018, ship-owners will have to monitor and report co2 emissions from ships of more than 5000 gross tonnage, which represent around 55% of ships calling at eu ports and around 90% of associated emissions. the new rules apply to co2 emissions from voyages to, from and between european ports. in order to minimise the administrative burden on shipowners and operators, the reporting and publication of information should be done on an annual basis.
‒ in april 2014, parliament adopted at first reading the proposal for the introduction of a system for monitoring, reporting and verifying co2 emissions from maritime transport. after all the interinstitutional discussions between parliament and the council, this report focuses on the council's position at first reading. the council's position is in line with the objectives discussed and negotiated with parliament on the eu's commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the white paper on transport, which calls for policies to this end, given the dependence of this sector on the use of fossil fuels and the fact that its emissions also contribute to air pollution and climate change. we welcome a monitoring, reporting and verification system which serves the purpose of providing better information not only on the amount of greenhouse gases (ghgs) emitted by this sector but also on the collection of concrete data which will allow the development of concrete policies to deal with the issue of ghg emissions, which is why we voted in favour. in the debate in plenary, we advanced some concerns and ideas to be taken into account in the future.
‒ this regulation requires owners of ships entering and leaving eu ports to monitor and report carbon dioxide (co2) emissions from january 2018. the new rules apply to ships of more than 5000 gross tonnage, regardless of flag state, and represent a first step towards reducing co2 emissions from shipping. the new regulation introduces a european-wide system for monitoring, reporting and verifying (mrv system) co2 emissions from shipping. the aim is to increase transparency on ship emissions and create an incentive to reduce them. that is why i am voting in favour.
