‒ the multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks was published by the european commission in october 2014. the aim of the proposal is to establish a framework for the management of multiple species of the baltic sea cod, herring and sprat stocks, where these three species are the main target of fishing. cod, herring and sprat account for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea in recent years. the baltic sea is a nearly enclosed body of water in which these three species are omnipresent and interact continuously. it is therefore of the utmost importance to ensure that the rules allow for the interactions between the species covered to be recognised, in particular the influence of cod on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa. the plan shall provide for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of those stocks and the stability of fishing opportunities and, consequently, of the livelihoods of fishermen. at the same time, it shall ensure that management is based on the latest scientific advice on the state of the stocks concerned, interactions between species and other aspects related to ecosystems and fisheries. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the main objective of this report initiated by the committee on fisheries is to establish a multi-species fishing plan which takes into account the existing dynamics of cod, herring and sprat stocks and the species caught as by-catch in the fisheries of these stocks, namely sole, sprat, rock sole and baltic hake. i support the report in question, arguing that the multiannual plan should contribute to rebuilding, achieving and maintaining the populations of the species concerned at acceptable levels of sustainability, and to minimizing as far as possible the impact on other species such as seabirds and the marine environment in general. i also believe that the european commission should take account of the advice of the advisory councils when it comes to adopting technical measures to accompany the multiannual plan.

‒ the common fisheries policy establishes a set of rules that apply to the management of european fishing fleets and the conservation of fisheries resources. to this extent, and since stocks of fishery resources are finite and others are overexploited, measures are needed to ensure the sustainability of the resources and of the fishing industry itself. this is the aim of this plan: to establish an urgent framework for the management of multiple baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat, which account for more than 94% of catches in the baltic sea in recent years. this multi-species management approach is noticeably more effective than single-species management and takes into account inter-species interactions. i therefore agree with this plan and believe that it should provide for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of stocks, based on responsible and forward-looking management, based on up-to-date scientific advice.
‒ i congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done and on the speed with which he has done it. the european union committed itself in 2002 to maintain and restore fisheries resources to levels that can produce a maximum sustainable yield, on an urgent basis then and if possible no later than 2015. the first multiannual plan is now voted on and it is our duty to make this precedent precise and appropriate. many fish stocks need to rebuild their biomass. the fishing rate must therefore be set at a level of maximum sustainable catch mortality that ensures that current economic income does not undermine its stability for the future. to ensure that the msy is resilient, a precautionary approach should be used by keeping catches at levels 10-20% below the maximum calculated fishing mortality rate. setting a target of 80% of the expected fishing mortality to maintain maximum sustainable yield will ensure that the promise made in 2002 is delivered further. because this report safeguards these positions, i voted in favour.

in writing. – one of the central objectives of the reform of the current common fisheries policy (cfp) is the progressive elimination of discards in all european union (eu) fisheries through the introduction of a landing obligation. this is designed to make better use of the available resources, and responds to public expectation to end the practice of throwing marketable fish back into the sea. high levels of discards are identified as an important driver of the lack of environmental sustainability of the cfp in the impact assessment carried out for the proposal for the basic regulation for the cfp. the changes made by the omnibus regulation should be strictly limited to implementation of the landing obligation, and only to the fisheries concerned as from 1 january 2015 (small pelagic fisheries, large pelagic fisheries, fisheries for industrial purposes, fisheries for baltic sea salmon). the legal alignment for the fisheries subject to the landing obligation after 2015 should be performed subsequently, and in conjunction with the new technical measures framework that the commission will bring forward in the coming months. the omnibus regulation should, as a result, only be concerned with the urgent issue of the implementation of the landing obligation for the fisheries concerned in 2015.

in writing. ‒ trying to reconcile cinema as a cultural and economic good and to exploit the potential of the european film industry is an excellent idea. but this will only be possible with credible investment in the development of innovative services, new business models and distribution channels to improve the availability of european films outside the eu and allow viewers to access an even wider range of films on an increasing number of platforms. investments are needed in the promotion, distribution, digitisation of content and the creation of a film culture (in connection with schools). unfortunately, the lack of investment in the creation of a strong european film industry has tended to undermine this desire. in this respect we still have much to learn from the good business practices that come to us from the united states.

‒ the european union does not have the competence to draw up a common forestry policy, but certain union policies are likely to have an impact on national forestry policies. wood is a renewable resource that is often under-utilized in europe and the smart and sustainable use of this raw material must be ensured, in particular through the development and exchange of know-how. the forestry sector currently employs over three million european citizens and its long-term competitiveness will only be possible with a skilled workforce. given that many eu policy areas, such as energy, environmental and climate protection policy, influence forest management, i agree that a new eu forest strategy, focused on better coordination, is urgently needed so that forestry and forests are better positioned in the different european strategies and a more coherent approach can be found.

in writing. ‒ with over 3.5 million jobs and the third largest employer in europe, after the metal and food industries, the forestry sector will undoubtedly be an additional economic pillar and a good way to ensure quality of life and employment. it is important that the commission has a new eu strategy for forests, but it is also important to safeguard the sustainable and responsible management of forests, balancing their multifunctional role in economic, social and environmental terms.

‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context and after assessing the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of these decisions, which give the commission and the implementing agencies (education, audiovisual and culture executive agency, small and medium-sized enterprises executive agency, consumers, health and food executive agency, european research council executive agency, research executive agency, innovation and networks executive agency and innovation and networks executive agency) discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and regular functioning of the european institutions.

‒ despite the measures taken by the european union and the individual member states to combat youth unemployment, the figures are alarming and there is no prospect of a reduction in the short term. the youth employment initiative is one of the main instruments for combating this scourge, but its rate of use is low because of the lack of public funds for the launch of projects to offer young people a job, a traineeship or training. the member states most affected by youth unemployment are also those which have the greatest difficulty in obtaining co-financing. i support the report by mrs morin-chartier which is to unlock €1 billion under the youth employment initiative, allowing for pre-financing of operational programmes for 2015, which means that the states will receive money earlier to help young people return to work and education or to do a traineeship. the pre-financing rate of the yei is thus increased from 1% to 30%, which allows, for example, portugal to have an advance of around eur 48 million, which will cover the expenditure already incurred since september 2013.

in writing. the youth unemployment rate has been rising steadily for years. youth unemployment in the eu remains above 20% and the percentage of young people not in work, education or training is above 10% in most member states. in addition, these rates remain higher for women than for men. the european union has put at the disposal of the member states a number of instruments to combat this scourge. unfortunately, these arrangements have not been sufficiently used by the member states, mainly because of the lack of public funds for projects aimed at providing young people with a job, a traineeship or training. paradoxically, this difficulty in obtaining co-financing is particularly acute in the member states most affected by youth unemployment. i therefore welcome the european commission's decision to release this billion euro, which will enable some essential projects to be launched. tomorrow's sustainable employment depends on investment today in the education and training of young people, as well as on reforms that make it easier for learners to transition between different types and degrees of education and between education and employment.
‒ in the light of the scourge of unemployment which is cross-cutting across the union, the european commission has put forward a proposal to increase the amount of pre-financing available to member states to promote the employment of young people and to provide support for unemployed young people, education or training in the different regions of the most affected countries. in practice, the proposal provides for an increase in the pre-financing rate from 1% to 30% in the 2015 budget allocation, unlocking some eur 1 billion for this year. we note that member states have had difficulty in making the payments necessary for the implementation of actions under the youth employment initiative, with particular emphasis on countries where unemployment levels in this age group are higher, where there are greater budgetary constraints and lack of funding. in the case of portugal, for example, some eur 48 million will be allocated to cover expenditure already incurred since september 2013. i therefore fully support this proposal, as it will help to promote greater integration of young people into the labour market and thereby reduce the dramatic unemployment rate affecting the youngest population in the european union.

in writing. - i am of the opinion that the commission proposal should be made viable and approved, repealing regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on the common rules for imports of certain textile products from third countries applicable to imports of textile products from third countries with which the european community has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or other arrangements. in recent years, the european union has only maintained bilateral agreements on trade in textile products with russia and serbia. following the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, this regulation has lost its effectiveness.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eec) no 3030/93 concerns the common rules applicable to imports of certain textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded agreements, protocols or other bilateral arrangements. in recent years, the eu has only maintained bilateral agreements on trade in textile products with russia and serbia. however, with the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, this regulation has lost its main purpose. in addition, this regulation was also used to impose quantitative limits on certain textile products originating in china and, where appropriate, to use the transitional safeguard mechanism specific to china. this safeguard mechanism expired on 11 december 2013. the purpose of this report is to repeal regulation (eec) no 3030/93 because, as a result of the above, it is considered that it no longer makes sense to exist. the fact that it has become legally unnecessary or obsolete does not, however, erase the political meaning of the conditions which justified it - the need to regulate trade and safeguard production systems in the face of the wave of deregulation and liberalization.
in writing. ‒ council regulation (eec) no 3030/93 concerns imports of certain textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols and taken other steps. in recent years, the eu has only maintained bilateral textile trade agreements with russia and serbia. however, following the entry of russia into the world trade organisation (wto) in 2012 and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia in 2013, council regulation (eec) no 3030/93 lost its true function. furthermore, the quantitative limits on products originating in the people's republic of china imposed by the regulation expired on 11 december 2013 and trade has since been liberalised and managed under the wto. in these circumstances, therefore, for reasons of legal certainty, this resolution approves the repeal of the said regulation. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ having lost its main objectives (bilateral agreements on trade in textile products with russia and serbia and the transitional restriction of certain textile products from chima) and having expired on 11 december 2013, and for reasons of legal certainty, the regulation should be repealed.
‒ following the recasting of the report on the common rules for imports of certain textile products originating in third countries, it is necessary to repeal regulation (eec) no 3030/93, which applies to imports of textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or other operations. this was the case for the russian federation and serbia before russia's accession to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia on 1 september 2013. in parallel, the regulation was maintained as a means of imposing quantitative limits for certain textile products originating in the people's republic of china and to use the transitional safeguard mechanism specific to certain products for china, which expired on 11 december 2013. in view of the above, i voted in favour of repealing regulation no 3030/93.

the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (eec) no 1692/73 of 25 june 1973 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the kingdom of norway. in 1987, the commission decided to ask its services to codify all acts at the latest after 10 amendments, in order to make eu legislation more accessible and easier to understand for the ordinary citizen, which will allow him new opportunities and the possibility of benefiting from the specific rights attributed to him. this objective cannot be achieved as long as there is a dispersion of numerous provisions, amended on several occasions, often substantially, which requires a reading both of the original act and of the acts amending it. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, whilst preserving the content of the codified acts in full and introducing only the formal amendments required by the codification process itself. it is therefore a highly technical report.

in writing. ‒ in 1987, the commission decided to ask its services to codify all acts at the latest after 10 amendments, in order to make eu legislation more accessible and easier to understand for the ordinary citizen, which would give him new opportunities and the possibility to benefit from the specific rights attributed to him. in order to ensure clarity and transparency of the law, it is necessary to codify the rules which have been subject to frequent amendments. the european parliament, the council and the commission have agreed, by means of an interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994, on an accelerated procedure which can be used for the rapid adoption of consolidated acts. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in the regulation, while preserving the content of the codified acts in full and introducing only the formal changes required by the codification process itself.

‒ this report codifies the council regulation on certain procedures for applying the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of albania, of the other part. the eu signed a stabilisation and association agreement with albania in 2006, the first step towards eventual membership. the aim of this agreement is to establish a free trade area progressively. in general, the primary objective behind the conclusion of such agreements with third countries is their integration into the eu's internal market as a way of ensuring the dominance of their economies by the large transnational corporations of the eu countries, this is the real meaning of "free trade". we are in favour of deepening relations of cooperation and friendship between countries and peoples, based on meeting their real needs, which are mutually beneficial and contribute to mutual development, and we therefore reject agreements which are contrary to these principles. although the main purpose of this report is to help to organize and understand the legislation which was scattered, we are thus making clear our position in principle on the substantive issues underlying it.

‒ the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (ec) no 994/98 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid, articles relating to the general principle of the prohibition of state aid to undertakings. state aid is an important economic policy instrument to boost economic, social, environmental and regional development, in particular to enable the state to intervene in order to realise its strategic choices, to ensure the financing of public services and to compensate undertakings which provide services of general interest.' to limit the sovereignty and the capacity of the state to intervene in this area in the name of a sacrosanct 'free competition' is to amputate democracy, to distort it and to conform it to the class interests of a minority, against the interests of the majority, that is to say, it is to deny it in practice. although the function of this report is eminently technical, facilitating the organization and understanding of legislation that was scattered, we thus signal our position of principle on the substantive matter underlying it.

‒ we know that state aid is an important economic policy instrument to boost economic, social, environmental and regional development, in particular so that the state can intervene in order to realise its strategic options, ensure the financing of public services and compensate companies that promote so-called 'services of general interest'. we know that successive reforms of state aid have reduced the scope for granting such aid. this is generally contrary to public policy which sees state aid as essential to support the regional development efforts of the cohesion countries, and we have therefore voted against these reports. we do, however, think it is important that all the amendments which have been adopted in the meantime should be brought together in a single document, making the legislation easier to understand.
‒ the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid, articles relating to the general principle of the prohibition of state aid to undertakings. we know that state aid is an important economic policy instrument to boost economic, social, environmental and regional development, in particular so that the state can intervene in order to realise its strategic choices, ensure the financing of public services and compensate undertakings that promote so-called 'services of general interest'. we know that successive reforms of state aid have reduced the scope for granting such aid. this is generally contrary to public policy which sees state aid as essential to support the regional development efforts of the cohesion countries, and we have therefore voted against these reports. we abstain because in this case the aim is to bring the amendments adopted together in a single document, making the legislation easier to understand.
‒ the present proposal, which has received my vote in favour, consists of a codification of regulation (ec) no 994/98 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid. it also provides that the commission has the power to declare, by means of block exemption regulations, that certain aid is compatible with the internal market pursuant to article 107 tfeu and without being subject to the notification requirements of article 108 tfeu. these categories include aid for small and medium-sized enterprises, research, development and innovation, environmental protection, employment and training, among others. i also welcome the rapporteur's proposal on the criteria to be included in each regulation and for each category of aid, since it is essential to know, in particular, the purpose of the aid, the beneficiaries, the ceilings for exempted aid and the forms of control.
‒ since this is only a proposal which is confined to a pure and simple codification of the existing texts, without any substantive changes, it deserves my agreement.

‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which concerns the court of auditors' special reports, in the context of the discharge to the commission for the financial year 2013, as i consider that the court of auditors' observations will have the effect of improving the budgetary practices of the commission in particular and of the eu in general.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and proper functioning of the european institutions, and it is obviously here that the court of auditors' special reports should be examined.
‒ this is a formal procedure whereby it is recognised that the budget implementation of the body under review is in line with what was previously budgeted. it is therefore a question of assessing the accounting validity of a document. from this point of view we have little to comment on. as regards the political considerations underlying the role of this institution in the context of an integration process based on values which we do not share, we cannot but attach our deeply critical point of view. this process of integration, of which this body or institution is an integral part, represents today a factor of enormous social backwardness and a factor which accentuates economic, social and territorial inequalities.
‒ the specific objectives of development policy should be safeguarded by the european external action service (eeas) and the european development funds (edf), financed by the member states, are the main financial instrument for the provision of union aid in the context of development cooperation to the acp states. the commission also notes that the pre-financing instruments paid by the european commission amounted to eur 424 million and that the operating revenue amounted to eur 124 million in the financial year 2013. i therefore believe that the rationalization and approximation of edf rules will probably lead to a reduction in the risk of error and inefficiency and to an increase in the level of transparency and legal certainty.
‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context, and after assessing the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of this decision granting the commission discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2013.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and regular functioning of the european institutions.

‒ as this is a budgetary matter concerning the implementation of the budget for the european institutions and agencies for 2013, and taking into account the annual report of the court of auditors which ensures the reliability, legality and regularity of the accounts, as well as other legal provisions contained in the recitals of the draft decision, i voted in favour of discharge for the implementation of the european parliament's budget for the financial year 2013.
‒ the court of auditors' audit concluded that no serious deficiencies were identified in relation to the audited items concerning parliament. the final appropriations of parliament for 2013 thus totalled eur 1 750 463 939, reserved for the administrative expenditure of the union institutions as a whole, corresponding to an increase of 1,9% compared to the 2012 budget. of the total, 70% correspond to expenditure on members of the institution, officials and temporary staff, buildings and ancillary expenditure and expenditure relating to parliamentary assistance. of this amount, 99.02% of the appropriations entered in the budget of the european parliament were used, i.e. a cancellation rate of 0.8% was recorded, and, as in previous years, a very high level of budget implementation was achieved.
‒ this report on the discharge for the year 2013 to the european parliament is intended to certify the final accounts. there is generally sufficient assurance that the accounts reflect the financial situation of parliament, and there are no questions or reservations. for these reasons i voted in favour of this document. however, i would like to stress four elements which are present in this document. firstly, the question of the single seat which would lead to long-term savings in the union budget. secondly, i am in favour of greater transparency in the allocation of general expenditure and i therefore believe that parliament should come up with solutions. i also believe that there should be more clarity in the information concerning local assistants and apas. finally, it should be noted that the evaluations of the parliamentary work of members carried out by external organisations, based on quantitative criteria, often generate unnecessary work for purely statistical purposes, with consequences for the general budget of the union.
‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context, and after assessing the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of this decision giving the president of the european parliament discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2013.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and regular functioning of the european institutions.
‒ this is a formal procedure whereby it is recognised that the budget implementation of the body under review is in line with what was previously budgeted. it is therefore a question of assessing the accounting validity of a document. from this point of view we have little to comment on. as regards the political considerations underlying the role of this institution in the context of an integration process based on values which we do not share, we cannot but attach our deeply critical point of view. this process of integration, of which this body or institution is an integral part, represents today a factor of enormous social backwardness and a factor which accentuates economic, social and territorial inequalities.
‒ as this is a budgetary matter concerning the implementation of the budget for the european institutions and agencies for 2013, and taking into account the annual report of the court of auditors which ensures the reliability, legality and regularity of the accounts, as well as other legal provisions contained in the recitals of the proposal for a decision, i voted in favour of discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european council and the council for the financial year 2013.
‒ the european council and the council had an overall budget of eur 535 511 300, which was 86.7% lower than the previous year. in this report there are indicators that should be taken into account such as the decrease in the utilisation rate in 2013 compared to 91,8% in 2012 or the under-execution rate remaining high and covering almost all categories. i agree that the european council and the council should have separate budgets in order to contribute to the transparency of the financial management of these institutions and to better accountability by both, and i welcome the positive trend of the council budget for 2013 not to see any increase (0.3%, or eur 1.6 million).

‒ the european external action service (eeas) has continued to implement its budget without the european court of auditors having identified any material error. the final budget of the eeas headquarters for the financial year 2013 was eur 508,8 million, representing an increase of 4,09%, broken down as follows: eur 195,81 million for the eeas headquarters and eur 312,95 million for the union delegations. at the eeas headquarters, 69% of the budget is allocated to the payment of salaries and other related entitlements of statutory and external staff (eur 134,59 million) and 10% (or eur 19,92 million) to buildings and related expenditure. in the case of the union delegations, eur 106,6 million (34%) is allocated to salaries of statutory staff, eur 62,2 million (19,9%) to external staff and eur 99,6 million (31,8%) to buildings and related expenditure. i also note that significant cost savings can be made by better cooperation between member states on their foreign and security policy and by proactively identifying joint efforts which the eeas can gradually undertake so that the union can be a stronger and more effective global actor.

‒ the court of justice had commitment appropriations of eur 354 880 000 and the implementation rate was 96.3%. the lower rate of implementation can be attributed to the fact that the initial 2013 appropriations included a proposal to adjust salaries and pensions for a total amount of around eur 6 000 000, which the council ultimately did not approve. the court of justice closed 701 cases in 2013 (595 cases were transferred to the court in 2012) and 699 new cases were brought before it (632 in 2012), including 450 appeals and preliminary ruling requests, and the duration of the cases was slightly reduced. i agree with the recommendations in the report for increasing the court's operational effectiveness.

in writing. ‒ in 2013, the eesc had a budget of eur 130 104 400, with a utilization rate of 94.1% and i regret that the utilization rate in 2013 was lower than 96.8% in 2012. however, the eesc budget is purely administrative, with a large proportion allocated to expenditure on staff and the remainder to buildings, furniture, equipment and miscellaneous running costs; the committee notes the explanation of the eesc that the decrease in the utilization rate is due to precautionary measures. value and support supports the eesc's efforts to limit budgets for the coming years, thus ensuring a flat-rate increase, and its intention to plan its work more effectively in the legislative process, without necessarily increasing the number of opinions and emphasising, instead, their quality.
in writing. the report concludes that the payments for the financial year 2013 relating to administrative expenditure were free from material errors and that no significant shortcomings had been identified in the accounts of the european economic and social committee. the report also makes some pertinent comments on the eesc's accounts. it is concerned about the delay in adopting the internal whistleblowing rules and urges the eesc to apply them without delay. is concerned that several important events planned for 2013 have been cancelled or postponed, which highlights the need for the eesc to plan better the organisation of events internally; the decrease in the use of external translation should be offset by an increase in the number of interpreters/translators, which is not guaranteed. it should be noted that the eesc only makes the homepage available in portuguese, and the website is only available in english and french, although it makes the documents available in all the official eu languages. the report highlights the positive aspect that the eesc has applied the new rules on reimbursement of members' travel expenses on the basis of actual costs, as recommended by parliament.

‒ having regard to the court of auditors' annual report on the implementation of the budget of the european institutions and agencies for the financial year 2013, which ensures the reliability, legality and regularity of the accounts, and to other legal provisions contained in the recitals of the draft decision, i voted in favour of discharge for the implementation of the budget of the committee of the regions for the financial year 2013.
‒ in 2013, the committee of the regions had a budget of eur 87 373 000, of which eur 84 800 000 was in commitment appropriations, with a utilization rate of 97%, the utilization rate having decreased in 2013 compared to 98,2% in 2012. the 2013 annual report on subsidiarity, which provides an overview of the committee of the regions' subsidiarity monitoring activities throughout the year, is a valuable tool for parliament's legislative work. i also welcome the new activity-based budgeting system introduced by the committee of the regions, as it is more suited to the specific characteristics of smaller institutions and can thus give a more complete picture of the costs and planned activities.
‒ the committee of the regions is an advisory body representing local and regional authorities in the eu. it is composed of local and regional representatives with democratic legitimacy. its role is to present regional and local views on european legislation by delivering opinions on commission proposals. the commission, the council and the parliament should consult the committee of the regions before taking decisions on matters concerning local and regional government (e.g. employment policy, environment, education or public health). the committee also adopts resolutions on topical political issues. the report stresses the need to increase the committee's visibility by strengthening the indispensable information and communication policy, an objective which seems to us to be in contradiction with the policy of transferring a large number of committee staff to the new european parliamentary research service (eprs), with the intention of the committee to rationalise translation requests and with the transfer of part of the committee's internal translation staff to the new european parliamentary research service (eprs). we support the criticism of the delay in adopting the internal rules on the reporting of irregularities, and it is urgent that the committee of the regions implements these rules.

‒ the report under review concerns the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2013 - ombudsman. we welcome the fact that 98,20% of all appropriations have been committed and 91,82% paid, with a utilization rate of 98,20% (compared to 95,88% in 2012), and that there are improvements in financial programming and control. we also welcome the fact that 70% of cases brought to the ombudsman were closed in less than a year; we note that there are still cases which are close to 18 months of resolution despite an improvement over the previous year. as regards interpretation costs, we are concerned about the disparities in translation costs, but we consider this a key area in ensuring equal treatment for the various countries.
‒ the european data protection supervisor is essential for the protection of the data and privacy of european citizens. this role has been strengthened after lisbon, and will be further strengthened by the creation of an independent secretariat for a new european data protection board. with a 2013 budget of around 7,600,000, the execution rate was 84,7%, still below the desirable level despite the evolution from the previous year. the efforts made to ensure that the key performance indicators were established with due care are also to be noted, as they enable the efficiency of the use of resources to be assessed. i also found it unpleasant, for the sake of symbolism, that parliament's recommendation on the security of complaint data has not yet been implemented.

‒ having regard to the budgetary issue concerning the implementation of the budget for the european institutions and agencies for 2013, and in agreement with the considerations and suggestions concerning the financial management and control performance of the eu agencies, i voted in favour of the horizontal observations accompanying the discharge for the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2013 of the said eu institutions and agencies.
‒ the number of agencies has increased significantly over the last decade, from 3 in 2000 to 32 in 2013, and they are important in their direct impact on the daily lives of union citizens. the main purpose of the decentralised agencies was to carry out independent technical and scientific evaluations, with the executive agencies being given the role of helping the commission to manage eu programmes on behalf of the union itself. i would also stress the large number of agencies set up in the area of freedom, security and justice, but each new agency was created out of real need. based on the summary of the results of the eca's audits of the european agencies and other bodies in 2013, the budget of the agencies for 2013 amounted to around eur 2 billion, representing an increase of 25% compared to 2012 and around 1,4% of the general budget of the union. the agencies employ some 6 500 permanent and temporary staff, representing 14% of the total number of union officials authorised under the general budget of the union.

‒ as this is a budgetary matter concerning the implementation of the budget for the european institutions and agencies for 2013, and taking into account the annual report of the court of auditors which ensures the reliability, legality and regularity of the accounts, as well as other legal provisions in the recitals of the draft decision, i voted in favour of discharge for the implementation of the budget of the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec) for the financial year 2013.
in writing. the final budget of the office of the body of european regulators for electronic communications for the financial year 2013 was eur 3 557 219, representing an increase of 11,51% compared to 2012, due to the fact that the body was recently established. i would point out that budgetary surveillance efforts during the financial year 2013 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 89,55% and that the payment appropriations execution rate reached 76,58%. the office employed 25 staff and had six vacancies in 28 authorised places. i cannot but regret that 91% of reimbursements to experts made in 2013 were late and late payments were late by an average of 78 days and that the office needs to urgently correct this situation and inform the discharge authority of the measures taken to this end and the results thereof.

‒ the final budget of the european fisheries control agency for the financial year 2013 was eur 9 216 900 and is entirely financed from the union budget. the budget implementation rate was 98.64% and the rate of implementation of payment appropriations was 83.85%. a concern is the high level of committed appropriations carried over to 2014 at 38% for administrative expenditure and 43% for operational expenditure. i recognise the important role of the agency in implementing the common fisheries policy and in achieving its objectives, in particular with regard to the landing obligation and the requirements for monitoring, control and surveillance of fishing activity.
in writing. we note the call for the discharge to be granted to the accounts of the european fisheries control agency for the financial year 2013, notwithstanding the alert for all the anomalous situations or concerns identified in the motion for a resolution. we would like to stress once again that the control of fishing activities in the national exclusive economic zones should be a responsibility of the member states, which should have the necessary resources and mechanisms, with the eu's contribution. without prejudice to forms of coordination, coordination and coordination between countries, we criticise, as we have done before, the centralisation which this agency imposes, in particular by overlapping competences with those which should be the responsibility of the national authorities. we note that the appropriation made available to the agency (eur 9 216 900) for the year in question is a counterpoint to the impossibility of updating and increasing the share of the member states to fulfil their mission.

‒ having regard to the court of auditors' annual report on the implementation of the budget of the european institutions and agencies for the financial year 2013, which ensures the reliability, legality and regularity of the accounts, and to the other legal provisions contained in the recitals of the proposal for a decision, i voted in favour of discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2013.

‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context and after assessing the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of this decision giving the executive director of the european railway agency discharge in respect of the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2013.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and regular functioning of the european institutions. the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency has not presented any major problems.

in writing. the report shall cover the discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency for the financial year 2013. it notes some concerns, such as problems with commitments and carryovers, procurement and recruitment procedures, the policy on conflict of interest and transparency, and with the internal audit service which has been abolished and replaced by the commission's internal audit service. however, paragraphs 19 and 20 of the european parliament's motion for a resolution raise concerns, where it is stated that 'the european parliament regrets that the agency has two locations (lille and valenciennes) for the exercise of its activities'. several jobs may be at stake, as this could reduce the provision of services and call into question the criterion of decentralisation of the institutions. for the reasons stated, we abstained.

in writing. ‒ the final budget of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2013 was eur 28 188 749, representing an increase of 39,01% compared to 2012, due to the additional tasks assigned to the authority resulting in a budget implementation rate of 93,18% and a payment appropriations execution rate of 72,54%. in order to ensure that corrective actions relating to budget implementation were taken in due time, the authority used a number of methods, such as the submission of monthly reports to the executive director and the submission of quarterly reports to the management board. it is regrettable that late payments account for 27% of total payments for goods and services provided, which has resulted in the payment of interest in the amount of eur 3 834, with payments being late by an average of 32 days. the current funding arrangements of the authority are inflexible, create an unnecessary administrative burden and may jeopardise its independence, which should lead to a review of its current funding structure.
‒ during the eruption of the most recent and acute phase of the crisis of capitalism, in 2007-2008, in the face of the evidence of the disaster caused by the dogmas of the deregulation of the financial system, the free movement of capital, finally, in the face of the consequences of financialized capitalism (its current and natural stage of evolution), many were the promises and the takeaways criticizing the speculators, the lack of ethics of the markets and the need to put an end to all this. the eu, its institutions and its protagonists have all lined up, as they should, in this hypocritical chorus. among the promises made in those years, the end of tax havens, the end of financial derivatives, the tax on financial transactions, among others, were on the table. everything would seem to be moving forward now, immediately, from there for days. time passed and the promises that were never fulfilled were silenced and forgotten. the rhetoric of the need to regulate the financial system continued, but instead of measures that could actually have an effect, such as those mentioned above, it was just a matter of ensuring that in practice everything remained the same. this authority is the result of this process. we have denounced its significance since its inception, a position which we reiterate here today by refusing this exemption.

‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context, and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of this decision granting the director of the european police office discharge in respect of the implementation of the office's budget for the financial year 2013.
‒ the discharge procedure is the instrument that ensures accountability and transparency in the management of community funds and the supervision of the growing number of european agencies. it is for parliament to close a 'budgetary cycle'. this cannot be done without strict budgetary control, checking that money has been properly managed and accurately determining the expenditure and revenue of a year. although it may seem excessively bureaucratic and exhaustive, this is a crucial moment for the proper and regular functioning of the european institutions. the implementation of the budget of the european police office did not present any major problems.
in the light of the above, i would like to ask the commissioner to give us a brief explanation of his position on the proposal for a regulation on the european parliament's powers to discharge the budget. europol - european police office, based in the hague (as eurojust), is part of the group of 32 agencies/decentralised bodies (ao) whose accounts are the subject of this annual political assessment by the european parliament on budgetary control for year n-2 (in the present case, 2013) and of the group of 31 agencies whose accounts were closed by the positive approval in plenary of their discharge report by the committee on budgetary control following the court of auditors' statement (which carried out a careful and timely examination of europol's accounts) and the council's recommendation. as in previous declarations of vote on this same subject, i would like to conclude by saying that i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision and i would once again like to congratulate the rapporteur on the effort he has made to produce this report in terms of synthesis and clarity of explanation.

‒ in giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. in this context and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i voted in favour of this decision giving the director of the joint undertaking for iter and the development of fusion energy discharge in respect of the implementation of the joint undertaking's budget for the financial year 2013.

‒ money market funds (mmfs) provide short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or governments. by financing these entities, money market funds contribute to the financing of the european economy. on the demand side, mmfs are short-term cash management instruments that provide a high degree of liquidity, diversification and stability of the value of the invested capital, combined with a market-based return. it is with this dual perspective that the proposal in question corrects the regulation in several respects, improving its perception and clarifying some of its initial assumptions. that is why i voted in favour.
‒ money market funds (mmfs) are short-term cash management instruments that aim to provide a high degree of liquidity, diversification and stability of the value of the capital invested, combined with a market-based return. mmfs are used by a wide range of entities, from local authorities to large professional investors such as companies and pension funds, who seek to invest their excess cash for a short period. they are originally a way of evading the regulation of banks with which they compete in the intermediation of products with shorter maturities. in this sense, they are an element of the problem and not of the solution. what is desired is a sound banking system, under public control, which is actually at the service of business, households and the general development of society. the philosophy behind this report is that of insisting on the recipes which have been at the root of the present financial crisis.
‒ this regulation does not add anything new in terms of market regulation. asset-backed investment funds (amifs) have been a major factor in the instability and volatility of financial markets. the solution proposed by this regulation does not tackle the underlying problem, and i therefore voted against it.
‒ money market funds (mmfs) provide short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or governments. by financing these entities, money market funds contribute to the financing of the european economy. this regulation lays down rules on financial instruments eligible for investment by an mmf, their portfolios and valuation and the reporting requirements for an mmf established, managed or traded in the union. this resolution amends the commission proposal with regard to money market funds with net variable asset value (mmf vlac) considered to be too risky, by introducing instead money market funds with net low volatility assets (mmf vlabv) considered to be less risky because they are more structured, and which in turn should expire 5 years after they have been authorised. i voted in favour.
‒ fundamental rights and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union must be respected. this appears to be the case with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on money market funds, as regards consumer protection, freedom of establishment and the protection of personal data. i have therefore supported this report in the light of the proposal from the european commission and the opinion of the european economic and social committee.
‒ the objective of this proposal for a regulation is to create a regulatory framework for money market funds throughout the european union, with a view to ensuring greater protection for investors in money market funds and to enhancing financial stability by preventing the risk of contagion. it also aims to ensure that the liquidity of the fund is sufficient to meet investor redemption requests and to make the structure of the funds secure enough to withstand adverse market conditions. that measure introduces uniform requirements on the scope of the eligible instruments, diversification and credit exposure rules, interest rate and liquidity, with the aim of making funds more secure and efficient by mitigating the effects of systemic risk. i therefore agree with the need to establish rules on the operation of money market funds so that, in the interests of the integrity and stability of the internal market, we can guarantee the proper functioning of the short-term financing market for financial institutions, governments and companies issuing short-term debt.

in writing. ‒ at its meeting of 10 july 2014, the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission examined the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council codifying and recasting council regulation (ec) no 517/94 of 7 march 1994 on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other arrangements, or by other specific community import rules. it concluded by common accord that the proposal in question was merely a simple codification of the existing act without any substantive changes. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the content of these proposals for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other arrangements or by other specific union import rules consists mainly of technical corrections. i therefore vote in favour of the report, taking into account the opinion of the committee on legal affairs.
in writing. ‒ this proposal, which is of an eminently technical nature, deserves my vote in favour, since it seeks to codify and reformat regulation (ec) no 517/94 of 7 march 1994 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or conventions or by other specific import rules of the union. the aim is to bring the decision-making procedures on commercial policy into line with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts which follows the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. this recast sets annual quantitative limits for imports of textile products from third countries with which the eu has no bilateral agreement, protocol or arrangement (currently only belarus and north korea). surveillance and protection measures are also introduced by the european union and it is allowed to impose surveillance measures on other third countries whose imported textile products cause serious damage to eu production.
in writing. regulation (eec) no 3030/93 concerns the common rules applicable to imports of certain textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded agreements, protocols or other bilateral arrangements. in recent years, the eu has only maintained bilateral agreements on trade in textile products with russia and serbia. with the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, regulation no 3030/93 lost its main purpose. in addition, this regulation was also used to impose quantitative limits on certain textile products originating in china and, where appropriate, to use the transitional safeguard mechanism specific to china. this safeguard mechanism expired on 11 december 2013. the purpose of this report is to repeal regulation (eec) no 3030/93, which, in view of the above, no longer makes sense.

in writing. ‒ on average, the commission identifies around €500 million a year in potential fraud, although there are good reasons to estimate that this figure could be as high as €3 billion, coupled with a low prosecution rate. the need and urgency for a european public prosecutor's office is unequivocal. but i am not unaware, as the rapporteur is, that a number of procedural, substantive and organisational questions still remain. it will certainly be a long and difficult process. but the interim report points out and builds on the resistance and inconsistencies with which the member states have been conducting this process. i can therefore only fully endorse a general approach which sets out the conditions for parliament's approval.
‒ the european public prosecutor's office would have the powers to investigate, prosecute and bring to trial in the courts of the member states crimes affecting the eu budget. these frauds harm the taxpayers of all member states, as they contribute to the union budget. the future european public prosecutor's office should have competence in criminal matters relating to fraud affecting the financial interests of the union. every year, around €500 million in eu expenditure and revenue is lost due to possible fraud. the percentage of charges is low - approximately 31% in eight years, from 2006 to 2013 - when compared with the number of judicial recommendations from the european anti-fraud office (olaf) to member states. the eppo's role is to provide legal advice and assistance to the european public prosecutor's office.
‒ the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office is a step forward in creating a european area of criminal justice with competence in the fight against fraud. that is, this is another step in the usurpation of sovereignty from the states, in an area where the fulcrum of that same sovereignty lies - the area of justice. we're against it. we are against a justice system which serves the interests of dominants and leads the process of integration. the recent examples of fraud and tax evasion, with criminals on the loose and those who have disclosed the scandals brought to justice and facing prison sentences and hefty fines, show just what kind of justice we are talking about.
‒ the data collected and analysed by the commission have led to the identification of suspected fraud against the financial interests of the union amounting to an average of around eur 500 million per year, although there are good reasons to believe that an annual value of approximately eur 3 billion may be involved. an innovative approach to the investigation, prosecution and judicial prosecution of perpetrators of fraud affecting the financial interests of the union is therefore essential. this resolution endorses the proposal for a council regulation establishing the european public prosecutor's office, whose mission should be to carry out investigations and prosecutions by a single, independent body at european level in respect of cases of fraud involving eu funds, and to increase the number of prosecutions, the recovery of eu funds and the confidence of european taxpayers. the european ombudsman has also been consulted on the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, which will be responsible for the implementation of the european public prosecutor's office's legal advice. i therefore voted in favour.

‒ alcohol abuse is the second largest cause of lifestyle-related disease in some member states, representing a risk factor in more than 60 chronic diseases. in addition, a quarter of all road accidents may be related to drunk driving. it is therefore essential that the european union has a common strategy in this area to reduce the harm caused by alcohol and alcohol dependence and to support moderate and responsible consumption. although the competent authorities in each member state are better placed to develop individual policies adapted to their realities, as consumption patterns vary across social, cultural, geographical and economic boundaries, i believe that close cooperation between the member states and the european commission is essential in tackling this transnational problem. there is a need to organise education campaigns for the general public and for the most vulnerable groups such as pregnant women and minors, to regulate the marketing of alcoholic beverages, to provide for strict labelling that is easily perceived by consumers, and to set quantifiable policy targets to monitor progress. for these reasons, i support this resolution.
‒ the eu is the world's largest region for alcohol consumption double the world average, with 10.2 litres of pure alcohol per capita in 2010, according to a report by the world health organisation. the social costs of alcohol in the eu have been estimated at over €155 billion. harmful alcohol consumption remains the third leading cause of death and preventable disease in europe and a risk factor for more than 60 chronic diseases, including cancer, heart disease and liver disease. alcohol abuse is also associated with obesity, a major public health problem and the fourth largest cause of preventable disease in europe. it is therefore important to understand what proposals the commission has to make on this matter.
‒ alcohol consumption remains one of the leading causes of death in europe and is associated with a range of preventable diseases. in 2006, the european strategy to support member states in minimising the harmful effects of alcohol was presented. this strategy has identified priorities which are largely unfulfilled. during the life of this strategy, the crisis and the policies of social devastation implemented in its name not only gave rise to new situations of dependency and overconsumption, but also disrupted the necessary response capacity of public health services at various levels in several member states. the resolution calls for concrete measures for the new strategy, including the preparation of a report to assess the need for the inclusion of alcoholic beverages in the labelling regulation providing for information on ingredients and their nutritional content, adding the need for preventive labelling for pregnant women. it also calls on the member states to strengthen their legislation in this area. the member states are also called upon to take responsibility for this matter, and attention is drawn to the need to implement policies and treatments in national health systems that help and reduce alcoholism problems. we are not going to vote for the report.
in writing. ‒ an alcohol strategy should focus on alcohol abuse and misuse. we must not forget that in some member states alcohol abuse is the second most important cause of lifestyle-related illness and that alcohol dependence is a risk factor for chronic diseases. i voted in favour of the need for more campaigns targeting the most vulnerable, namely young people and pregnant women. i believe that a thorough analysis by the european commission is needed as regards the possible integration of the nutritional content of beverages. we must, of course, provide the consumer with clear and true information, but with regard to its applicability. finally, i would point out that public support and promotion of wine regions must continue because of their importance for so-called wine tourism. we must support awareness-raising and information campaigns to the public, addressing the harmful effects of excessive consumption.
in writing. ‒ alcohol abuse is the second largest cause of lifestyle-related disease in some member states and alcohol dependence is a risk factor for more than 60 chronic diseases, such as alcoholism. this resolution considers that the eu alcohol strategy has been successful in supporting member states' measures to reduce the harm caused by alcohol abuse, in particular through the exchange of best practice in areas such as the protection of young people. the commission also urges the immediate start of work on the new eu alcohol strategy, which is based on the objectives of reducing health and safety and socioeconomic problems caused by alcohol. the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of the environment and for the development of a european information system for the protection of the environment. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ i support a policy aimed at reducing alcohol consumption and all the social and health harm it causes. however, i have some reservations when it is said that 'public funds should under no circumstances be used to promote alcohol consumption', since, particularly in the economies of southern europe, this may be a principle used to prevent support for promotional campaigns and internationalisation of products such as port wine or madeira wine, to name just a few.
‒ for the four orders of reasons briefly described in the oral question to the commission: 1) harmful alcohol consumption remains the third leading cause of death and preventable disease in europe; 2) alcohol abuse is also associated with obesity (the fourth leading cause of preventable diseases in europe); 3) alcohol abuse and dependence are also associated with other social problems, such as high levels of absenteeism from work, family breakdown and violence; 4) europe has the highest rate of alcohol consumption in the world. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which was signed by the seven groups in this house, and which calls on the commission and the member states to draw up a (new) strategy for responsible consumption of alcoholic beverages, proposing very specific measures on labelling, the promotion of education and/or prevention, legislation on marketing and on consumption by pregnant women. with this resolution, we also stated that the new eu strategy should not set new objectives, but should support those already agreed under the who european action plan to reduce harmful alcohol consumption in the period 2012-2020.
‒ alcohol consumption remains the third leading cause of death in europe from a range of preventable diseases. it's also a risk factor for over 60 other chronic diseases. furthermore, problems associated with excessive drinking are linked to a number of social problems. europe has the highest rate of alcohol consumption in the world. the aim of both the oral question and this resolution is to obtain more information on this subject. furthermore, it requests clarification as to why a new separate report on the implementation of the requirements for the provision of information on the ingredients of alcoholic beverages and nutritional information on those beverages, which should have been submitted in december 2014, has not yet been published.
‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the alcohol strategy because, while recognising the importance of differences in consumption patterns between member states and the cultural aspects of responsible drinking, its focus is on the concern about limiting the intake of alcoholic beverages by minors and individuals suffering from serious disorders, chronic diseases or correlated dependencies. in order to reduce the harm caused by alcohol, to ensure the lasting impact of the results achieved to date and to continue to support national governments in tackling the long-term harm caused by alcohol, the european commission is called upon to start work immediately on a new alcohol strategy for 2016-2022, which i clearly agree with. finally, it called on the commission and the member states to carry out awareness-raising campaigns and to invest in education as a means of preventing the harmful effects on health and society of alcohol consumption, while promoting responsible and moderate consumption of alcoholic beverages.
the resolution calls for concrete measures for the new strategy, including the preparation of a report to assess the need for the inclusion of alcoholic beverages in the labelling regulation providing for information on ingredients and their nutritional content, adding the need for preventive labelling for pregnant women. the member states are also called upon to strengthen their legislation in this area. the member states are also called upon to take responsibility for this matter, and attention is drawn to the need to implement policies and treatments in the national health systems that help and reduce alcoholism problems. we are not going to vote for the report.
‒ the collapse of rana plaza, an eight-storey building in savar, on the outskirts of dhaka, which housed several garment factories, killed more than 1100 people and injured more than 2500, making it the worst industrial disaster in bangladesh. factory fires, building collapses and other incidents related to health and safety issues at the workplace are not limited to the garment sector in bangladesh, but are very concerning issues in other developing and least developed countries. in addition to the need to comply with international standards regarding safety and conditions for workers, it is important that the us$ 3 million available for compensation be distributed without further delay.
‒ the tragedy in bangladesh has brought to light a long-known problem: that of inhuman working conditions and extreme exploitation in the production chain of the multinationals supplying the european market. a few thousand more lives have been taken on the altar of global capitalism. the country is the world's second largest textile producer. almost 90% of production is destined for europe, the usa and canada. the dhaka region has been reshaped by the proliferation of factory units operating in unsanitary spaces, outsourced, with miserable wages of 30 euros/month and denied the most basic labour rights. there are about 100,000 factories in the capital region alone. two years after the rana plaza tragedy, action is still lagging behind against the companies that profit from the persistence of this situation. mechanisms to deal with imports of products of this origin are still lagging behind. the eu is not interested in making any real change to the situation and this resolution is, in fact, a demonstration of that.
in writing. ‒ on 24 april 2013, the rana plaza, an eight-storey building in savar, on the outskirts of dhaka, where several garment factories were located, collapsed, killing more than 1100 people and injuring more than 2500. as a result of these tragic events and with public protests and calls for action by the european parliament, the eu, in collaboration with the government of bangladesh and the world labour organisation, launched on 8 july 2013 the 'pact for the continuous improvement of labour rights and factory safety in the knitting and knitwear industry in bangladesh' (the sustainability pact), under which bangladesh committed to take action to improve labour standards and working conditions in the country's garment industry. this resolution commemorates the victims on the second anniversary of the tragedy and takes note of the conclusions of the first evaluation of the pact in october 2014. it therefore notes good progress by the bangladeshi authorities and recognises the contribution of the pact to improving health and safety in factories and working conditions in the garment industry. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ although two years have passed, the rana plaza tragedy is still very much alive in our memories, if not one of the most devastating industrial disasters ever. the implementation of an effective workplace safety system is imperative and situations like this could have been avoided. it is important that the government of bangladesh takes an active stance in implementing safety measures at work. it is important to focus on safety training at work and it is even more important to ensure that the guidelines are implemented in the workplace.
in writing. - as the epp's spokesperson for this debate, i welcome the fact that the 7 political groups in this parliament have managed to draft a single resolution on these tragic events, which was approved by 97% of the votes cast. this demonstrates our commitment and our unity in defending and promoting decent, fair and properly legislated working conditions on a global scale. two years after this terrible tragedy, we remember that there are still compensation payments to be made to the victims and their families and that, despite much that has been done to improve the working conditions and safety of factory buildings in this country, there is still much to be done. i therefore stress the absolute need for future monitoring of the implementation of the ongoing measures (the sustainability compact, the agreement, the alliance and the better work programme) by the international community (notably the ilo, the eu, the us, the business and trade union community) and for support to the government of bangladesh so that these measures (and other announced ones, such as the amendment of the labour law) are effectively implemented on the ground, intensified (e.g. increased number of inspections, improvement of labour rights in the export free zones ‒ efz) and deepened (e.g. by hiring more labour inspectors).
in writing. ‒ on april 24, 2013, 1,134 people died and hundreds were injured in the rana plaza building collapse in savar, bangladesh. later, 112 people lost their lives in the tazreen factory fire in ashulia district of dhaka, bangladesh and on 24 november 2012, another 289 people lost their lives in a fire in karachi, pakistan in september 2012. they are striking examples of a wider list. this is a poignant demonstration of what the most savage capitalism is capable of. bangladesh's garment industry developed in just a few decades to become the second largest in the world, thanks to large multinational chains that saw it as a way to increase the exploitation of the workforce and increase their profits. indeed, it is no coincidence that bangladesh benefits from duty-free and eu quota-free access to the eu market for all its products included in the 'everything but arms' initiative, which covers 55% of bangladesh's exports, largely textiles/clothing.
