in writing. ‒ the mediterranean, the sea of antiquity, has become a vast liquid cemetery. the sea of civilization is now the sea of death. almost every day, human beings die trying to reach europe. a little over a week ago, the tragedy of the death of 700 people again shook our daily lives. after a joint meeting of the home and foreign ministers, the commissioner responsible for migration, home affairs and citizenship presented a ten-point plan to deal with this tremendous humanitarian crisis. the plan aims to strengthen joint action by member states, to improve reception and treatment conditions for displaced persons and to cooperate with third countries considered to be essential for controlling these migratory flows. it is imperative that we increase our capacity to patrol the waters to try to prevent disasters and to destroy human trafficking networks. it is important that we provide dignified conditions for those who reach our shores. but it is crucial that we commit ourselves to contributing to the solution of the problems facing the middle east and africa. those who are so desperate to reach europe just want to leave behind the fear. it is up to europe to fight it.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, we are once again faced with a resolution following a tragedy in the mediterranean. the resolution also highlights once again the failure of the member states to respond to the humanitarian emergency facing europe. saving lives is a priority, and to do that, we need more solidarity. we need frontex to have sufficient means to carry out effective search and rescue operations, thus implementing regulation no 656/2014. on the other hand, the resolution also looks at the underlying problem. and here the european council has failed again. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat illegal immigration and to help bring about peace in war-torn areas, particularly syria, to end the power vacuum in libya, to defeat the self-styled islamic state, to combat human trafficking effectively and to invest more in cooperation and development. now is the time for action!

‒ this resolution aims to respond to the recent events in the mediterranean, with the disappearance of 700 migrants after the sinking of the fishing vessel on which they were travelling, and to the subsequent european council conclusions of 23 april 2015. globally, the eu faces the challenge of the increasing proportion of people trying to cross the mediterranean, exploited by smugglers and traffickers, to escape conflict or persecution in syria, iraq, eritrea, somalia and libya. the resolution therefore reiterates the need for the eu and its member states to make every effort to prevent more lives being lost at sea by making available the necessary resources to ensure that search and rescue obligations are effectively met. it also urged the eu to base its response on solidarity and equitable sharing of responsibility, adopting a comprehensive european approach. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal, because i agree with the call for closer coordination of eu and member state policies in tackling the root causes of migration.

‒ the fundamental objective of the proposed amendments is to confirm the eu's real and deep commitment to the future of european integration in the countries and territories covered by this regulation, through the granting of unilateral trade preferences. in this context, such concessions, or their possible suspension, should be accepted as an impetus to accelerate the transition of the political and socioeconomic reforms highlighted in the 'growth pact', which are indispensable for the western balkan countries to comply with the copenhagen criteria and the acquis.
‒ stabilisation and association agreements with the western balkan countries are, as a rule, preceded by asymmetrical trade liberalisation. asymmetric trade liberalisation is provided for by council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 adopting exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the stabilisation and association process. this regulation shall apply until 31 december 2015. the amendments to this regulation are related to the following objectives:- extension of the period of application of the regulation until 31 december 2020,- introduction of the human rights clause, - possible suspension of the autonomous trade measures to bosnia and herzegovina, as of 1 january 2016, because it has not accepted to adapt the trade concessions granted under the interim agreement in order to take into account the preferential traditional trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina, under the central european free trade agreement (cefta). in addition, taking into account that the stabilisation and association agreement with kosovo was initialled in july 2014, this regulation will also cover kosovo.
‒ trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is liberalised through a series of stabilisation and association agreements (saas) and an interim agreement (ia) in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. kosovo and the whole region also benefit from autonomous trade measures (atm). these unilateral preferences allow unlimited access to the union with exemption from customs duties for most products. this resolution suggests three main amendments to regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 concerning these preferences. on the one hand, it introduces the extension of the current preferences until the end of 2020, and the scheme has contributed to the increase of trade. it also includes the human rights clause in the csf regulation, allowing for the suspension of preferences in the event of serious and systematic violations of these principles by any of the beneficiary countries. finally, the proposal provides for the possible suspension of the csms for bosnia and herzegovina (bh) as from 1 january 2016, as it has not yet agreed to adapt the interim agreement to take account of preferential traditional trade between croatia and bh following the accession of croatia to the eu on 1 july 2013. i voted in favour.
‒ european policy towards the western balkan countries is defined in the framework of the stabilisation and association process, launched in may 1999. this proposal aims to amend regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 adopting exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the stabilisation and association process. the amendments considered include the extension of the preferences for a further 5 years, the suspension of the trade preferences with regard to bosnia and herzegovina as from 01/01/2016 and the introduction of the so-called 'human rights clause'. all the western balkan cefta member countries have completed negotiations to amend their agreements with the european union. bosnia-herzegovina was missing, having recently agreed to sign and provisionally apply an agreement on the adjustment of trade concessions, and trade preferences have therefore been re-established for that country. i support this proposal, which calls on bosnia-herzegovina to adapt the interim preferential trade agreement with croatia and further calls on the parties to take account of their mutual interests in order to reach an agreement satisfactory to both eu member states and cefta members.

in writing. ‒ in recent times we have been confronted with an exponential increase in the number of attacks on religious minorities, in particular christians, around the world. every day there are christians who are executed, beaten or arrested, especially in some parts of the arab world, by jihadist terrorists. in line with european values, all religious and ethnic minorities have the inalienable right to live in their traditional and historical homelands in dignity, equality and security. i therefore condemn the recent attacks on christian communities in several countries and support the international efforts to combat the actions of the islamic state. on the other hand, there is a need to increase humanitarian aid and international assistance to protect the lives of christians and other religious minorities in conflict zones and refugee camps. i support the need for the kenyan government to investigate and bring to justice all those responsible for the executions that have taken place on its territory.

‒ recently, numerous sites of archaeological, religious and cultural interest have been destroyed in iraq and syria by extremist groups linked mainly to the islamic state in iraq and syria, with the director-general of unesco defining such destruction as acts of 'cultural cleansing'. on the other hand, the illicit trade in cultural goods is currently the third most important illegal trade, after drug and arms trafficking, and is dominated by organised crime networks. i strongly condemn the intentional destruction of places of worship and of cultural and archaeological interest by the islamic state in syria and iraq. i agree with the need for the eu and the member states to implement security measures at the eu's external borders to prevent the smuggling of cultural goods. i support the need to include acts that deliberately damage or destroy on a large scale the cultural heritage of humanity in the category of crimes against humanity.
in writing. ‒ numerous sites of archaeological, religious and cultural interest in syria and iraq have recently been destroyed by extremist groups linked mainly to the islamic state, in systematic attacks on cultural heritage. the director-general of unesco calls it the "cultural cleansing". i strongly condemn the intentional destruction of places of worship and of cultural and archaeological interest, including through the deliberate persecution of individuals identified on the basis of their ethnic, religious or cultural origin, combined with deliberate attacks on their places of worship, memory and education.
in writing. the rome statute of the international criminal court, adopted on 17 july 1998, recognises as war crimes intentional attacks on, among others, buildings dedicated to religious worship, education and the arts, as well as historical monuments. in syria and iraq, numerous sites of archaeological, religious and cultural interest have recently been destroyed by extremist groups linked mainly to the islamic state (isil/daesh). these systematic attacks on cultural heritage have been defined by the director-general of unesco as cultural cleansing, signalling the cadence and correlation of these, a deliberate strategy that seeks to destroy cultural diversity through the deliberate persecution of individuals identified on the basis of their ethnic, religious or cultural origin. some of these acts of destruction of cultural heritage have therefore been considered, in certain circumstances, crimes against humanity. this resolution strongly condemns the intentional destruction of places of worship and of cultural and archaeological interest by isil in syria and iraq and calls on the eu and its member states to make every effort to combat the illicit trade in lost cultural objects from iraq and syria. it's the only way to avoid the risk of mis-funding isis. i voted in favour.
‒ the intentional destruction of places of worship and of cultural and archaeological interest by isil in syria and iraq should be the subject of the utmost condemnation and of deep consternation and concern. we are facing real terrorist acts, which aim not only to destroy the heritage and cultural identity of peoples, but also to use cultural objects to finance criminal activities, since the illicit trade in cultural goods is the third most important illegal trade, after drug and arms trafficking. i therefore voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution which seeks to draw attention to the urgent need to stop the smuggling and illegal trade of cultural goods from these territories (e.g. through increased controls at the external borders) and to develop an integrated policy of cooperation which urges member states to engage in awareness-raising campaigns together with the relevant international bodies for the protection of our cultural and heritage heritage, particularly in these conflict zones.
‒ the eu is deeply concerned that in syria, iraq and tunisia, numerous sites of archaeological, religious and cultural interest are being destroyed by extremist groups linked mainly to the islamic state in iraq and syria. according to unesco, the term 'cultural cleansing' indicates an intentional strategy that seeks to destroy cultural diversity through the deliberate persecution of individuals identified on the basis of their ethnic, religious or cultural origin, combined with deliberate attacks on their places of worship, memory and education. it is a pity that this is the same eu which is making a decisive contribution to arming and training the fanatical gangs which are now carrying out these barbaric attacks. as for destabilizing countries like libya, syria or iraq, these same gangs were liberation heroes who were going to impose democracy against regimes that no longer served the interests of the west. it's a shame! the eu, the united states and nato, which have lied to the people of europe and dragged their countries into this senseless war which has already killed millions of innocent people, should be in the dock.
the resolution also calls on the eu to take action to ensure that the rights of women and girls are protected in all eu countries, including in the countries of the former soviet union, and calls on the eu to take action to ensure that women and girls are protected in all eu countries.
‒ the increasing trend towards an authoritarian regime in the maldives, the repression of political opponents and the intimidation of the media and civil society, which may jeopardise the progress made in recent years in the field of human rights, democracy and the rule of law in the country, are worrying developments. the most basic basic rights of justice are also not being fully respected, as the trial of the former president of the maldives proves. the international community has expressed serious doubts about the verdict, insisting on their release and full respect for their rights, particularly in court, and respect for the national constitution and international obligations. the reintroduction of the death penalty is to be condemned and an immediate end to all forms of violence, including violence against peaceful protesters, must be ensured. the national authorities should focus their efforts on eliminating trafficking in human beings and on achieving stability, strengthening democracy and the rule of law, and ensuring full respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. ‒ on 13 march 2015, mohamed nasheed, former president of the maldives, was sentenced to 13 years in prison on terrorism charges for the arrest in january 2012 of the then-president of the criminal court. the controversial trial failed to meet national and international standards in the field of justice, despite the call by the un and the eu for the judicial process against former president nasheed to be fair and transparent. this event is symptomatic of a set of violations of the rule of law, democracy and individual freedoms that have recently occurred in the maldives. the report we have just seen expresses its deep concern at the trends threatening the democratic regime in the maldives and deplores the irregularities in the trial of former president mohamed nasheed, insisting that he should be released immediately. therefore, should his conviction be subject to appeal, his rights should be fully respected in accordance with maldives' international obligations, its own constitution and all internationally recognised fair trial guarantees. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ reports of continued political pressure, intimidation of the media and civil society, and lack of independence and credibility of the judiciary in the maldives are raising serious concerns about the actual progress made over the past years in terms of advances in the defence of human rights, the principles of democracy and the rule of law. the circumstances surrounding the recent conviction of former president mohamed nasheed on terrorism charges and the end of the moratorium on the use of the death penalty raise serious doubts as to the true state of the rule of law in the maldives. it is therefore extremely important that the european union should follow the future developments in this country and, in the exercise of its external powers, help to re-establish the basis for a credible and fair political process, rooted in democracy, capable of ensuring the principles of the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary and the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens, which is why i voted in favour of this joint resolution.

‒ albania, unlike other candidate countries, has made great progress which should be an inspiration for the intensification of reform efforts in other candidate countries. the efforts to combat human trafficking, the promotion of human rights and the climate of religious tolerance and good inter-ethnic relations in the country are also to be commended. however, some problems and challenges remain which need to be addressed quickly and efficiently, such as the independence of the judiciary and the fight against corruption and organised crime, freedom of expression and media independence, and the fragmentation of the local administration system.
‒ albania has made remarkable progress in recent years on its path towards eu membership and has therefore been granted candidate country status. the opening of accession negotiations has become a driver for eu-related reforms in albania. i therefore welcome the reform efforts albania is making and express my support for the process of integration in albania. i also recognise that concrete measures and sustained political commitment are needed to put these measures into practice, to successfully address the challenges of consolidating the process of democratic transformation and to pursue eu-related reforms.
in writing. this motion for a resolution contains a broad set of considerations on the process of albania's integration into the eu. the assessment of the process here presented and the list of conditions put forward indicate the extent of the interference and loss of sovereignty imposed on countries and peoples in the process of eu accession, in particular in matters such as the economic organization of the state, the judiciary, the public administration, the requirement to align the positions of that country with those of the eu, particularly as regards foreign and border policy. we consider unacceptable the paternalistic attitude with which the considerations and conditions required to satisfy the requirements for the integration of the country are set out, depriving the peoples of their legitimate right to decide their future, which includes the free and sovereign choice of eu membership, but also the strategies of economic and social development. for these reasons, we voted against.
albania has made significant progress in recent years towards eu accession and was therefore granted candidate country status in june 2014. the opening of eu accession negotiations depends on the consistent adoption and effective implementation of sustainable reforms in the five key priorities, namely public administration reform, strengthening the judiciary, fighting corruption and organised crime, and strengthening the protection of human rights. this resolution, while deploring the persistent shortcomings in the functioning of the judiciary and the high levels of corruption, congratulates albania on its accession to the eu and considers that this should be seen as an incentive to persevere in its reform efforts. it also expressed its continued support for the eu integration process in albania and recommended that the future meeting schedule of the eu-albania stabilisation and association parliamentary committee and the high level dialogue on key priorities be harmonised in order to strengthen parliamentary oversight of the eu accession process. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the 2014 progress report on albania, which reflects well the efforts that this country has made towards its european integration, as well demonstrated by its current status as a candidate country to the european union. however, as the report points out, there are still many areas where there is a need for greater and deeper intervention, such as judicial reform, the fight against drug trafficking and greater freedom of the press. however, i would also like to point out the progress made in promoting religious tolerance and good relations between the different ethnic groups in this country, as well as the excellent work done by the ombudsman, which are in themselves a sign of the constructive and proactive stance that albania intends to adopt on its path towards european integration.

in writing. ‒ despite the new opportunity for bosnia and herzegovina to resume the reform process, improve its social and economic situation and move closer to the european union, some structural problems remain to be resolved. this resolution, in a coherent manner, calls on the bosnian authorities and leaders to refrain from using nationalist and divisive rhetoric, and to implement the economic and social structural reforms necessary to improve the lives of its citizens, based on respect for human rights, the principle of the rule of law and the principle of direct and fair universal suffrage. the fight against corruption and inefficiency in the judicial system should also be a priority, with concern being expressed at the persistently high number of disappeared persons and the lack of progress in this area. equally worrying is the fact that it remains a country of origin, transit and destination for trafficking in human beings. i agree that it is essential to promote an inclusive and tolerant society that protects the rights of minorities and vulnerable groups.

‒ the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and bosnia and herzegovina, of the other part, was signed on 16 june 2008. the eu has given bosnia and herzegovina a new opportunity based on a coordinated approach designed to help the country to resume the reform process, improve its social and economic situation and move closer to the union. this resolution strongly supports the european integration of bosnia and herzegovina and believes that the eu's enhanced engagement should focus, inter alia, on socioeconomic issues, the business environment, the institutional framework, the rule of law and governance, law enforcement policy, the independence of the judiciary, the fight against corruption, public administration reform, civil society and youth. it also called on the authorities to make the fight against corruption a top priority and noted the progress made in the fight against organised crime and terrorism. it also welcomes the written commitment to eu integration adopted by the presidency of bosnia and herzegovina, signed by the leaders of all political parties and supported by the parliament of bosnia and herzegovina on 23 february 2015. i voted in favour.

‒ the eib's annual report for the financial year 2013 shows the 37% increase in the group's financing activities to eur 75,1 billion and the implementation of the eib's capital increase in 2013, showing its concern about the current economic stagnation in the eu and in particular the significant decline in public and private investment. smes are the backbone of the european economy and as such should be one of the main targets for investment. i welcome the increase in support for smes in the european union, which has now reached eur 21.9 billion, thus enabling more than 230 000 smes to access finance.
‒ we follow this report in a number of respects. the eib should pay more attention to smes, take account of the geographical distribution of the funds it lends (meeting the needs of the countries most affected by the crisis), and pay attention to investment in research and development. we also support the rapporteur's position that the eib should be more transparent in its management. however, this report should go deeper in its criticism of this institution, which is better known for the scandals surrounding its business than for its role in development aid. the eib is accused of acting with opacity, without satisfactory social and environmental standards and of being involved in controversial projects such as the tenke fungurume mining project in the democratic republic of congo (drc), just one example among many. the eib is not playing its role as a development bank. in latin america, more than 90% of eib financing is provided to subsidiaries of european companies or large multinationals. within the eu, the eib is now associated with the giant public-private partnership programme, the juncker plan, and thus removed from support for public investment. in the past we have denounced the restrictions on access to eib financing by cooperatives. all issues ignored by this report.
‒ this report contains some very positive elements. it draws attention to the disastrous consequences of the economic crisis and the implementation of austerity measures. it stresses the need to strike a new balance between better valuation and the best possible investment, and to steer the economy towards sustainable growth and a job-creating recovery. regrets that the ppps with shortcomings have become a costly public financing system for the private sector, generating public debt. regrets that the eib has financed the passante di mestre motorway section and the castor project; for these reasons, i voted in favour.
‒ this resolution concerns the 2013 annual report of the european parliament on the european investment bank (eib). the eib is not a commercial bank and should continue to play its essential role as a catalyst for sound investment of public and private financing for long-term investments, and should ensure the effective application of best banking practices in prudential matters in order to maintain its sound capital position with the subsequent positive impacts on lending conditions. the report therefore calls for efforts to be made to extend joint interventions to finance smes or sustainable infrastructure, whether tangible or intangible, recognising that one of the reasons for the investment and credit crunch is the loss of competitiveness of member states' economies. the creation of a working group, led by the commission and the eib, is therefore welcome, as are the legislative proposals for the creation of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), which aims to facilitate access to finance for member states and regions with high levels of unemployment and a gdp per capita below the eu average. i voted in favour.

‒ with the expo theme 'feeding the planet: energy for life', it is important to significantly boost the debate on improving food production and distribution, combating food waste, promoting and developing existing positive strategies to address the challenge of food insecurity, undernutrition and food imbalances, and creating a balance between the availability and consumption of resources. the milan fair offers an opportunity to debate the different approaches, finding solutions to the paradoxes of a globalised world where, on the one hand, there are some 870 million undernourished and hungry people and, on the other, some 2.8 million people die from health problems linked to poor diet, obesity and overweight.
‒ this resolution is the result of the decision of the committee on agriculture and rural development on the eu's participation in expo milano 2015. the eu will be represented at expo milano with a pavilion under the theme 'feeding the planet: energy for life'. after several hearings in the committee on agriculture on this topic, it was agreed that topics such as food security, the fight against food waste and the promotion of healthy eating and nutritional requirements, through the promotion of research and education, would be raised and focused in order to help prevent and eradicate malnutrition and prevent obesity. the resolution omits some important aspects, such as the defence of small farms and sustainable agriculture against intensive production methods, soil erosion, deforestation, water scarcity and the loss of biodiversity, which lead precisely to the lack of food on the planet. there is no mention of the struggle of farmers for the right to produce. the reference to the right to water is missing.
the milan world expo will run from 1 may to 30 october 2015, and will be devoted to the theme 'feeding the planet: energy for life'. the expo's themes focus mainly on the agricultural sector, which remains a key sector of the union's economy, with agricultural exports accounting for two thirds of its total external trade. the union remains the world's largest agricultural exporter and the eu food industry generates an annual turnover of approximately eur 1 trillion, employing more than 4 million people. the united nations food and agriculture organization (fao) on the other hand predicts that the world population will grow from 7 to 9.1 billion, requiring a 70% increase in food supply by the year 2050. to meet the challenge of food security, this resolution considers the following components to be essential: a strong and sustainable agricultural sector in the eu, a prosperous and diversified rural economy, a clean environment and family farms ensured by a sound, fair, internationally sustainable and adequately funded common agricultural policy. i voted in favour.
‒ i support this motion for a resolution on the eu's participation in the 2015 world expo in milan, entitled 'feeding the planet: energy for life', which will take place between 1 may and 30 october 2015, as it is a unique opportunity for the eu to massively disseminate its main achievements in the fields of food and sustainability. the initiative coincides with the closing year of the millennium development goals and the start of a post-2015 framework that will also address the sustainable development goals. at the same time, the europe 2020 strategy will also be halfway through its implementation period, so expo milano will serve not only as a channel for presenting the strategy's interim results, but also for disseminating its objectives for the future, especially in the areas of food security and sustainability. as such, the eu's participation in this exhibition represents a unique opportunity to strengthen its role as a global player in the development of future initiatives on food, health and food safety and to communicate with citizens and raise awareness of current challenges and future sustainability goals.

‒ the scourge of terrorism has left very deep marks in nigeria. despite being the largest economy in africa and also the largest country in terms of population, ethnic and religious differences as well as economic and social disparities fuel the violence that seriously threatens this state. the actions of the terrorist group boko haram have been condemned internationally, but unfortunately the initial response of the nigerian authorities was not adequate, contributing to the population's estrangement from government institutions. this terrorist group has used the most heinous and despicable means to achieve its goals and to spread terror not only in nigeria but also in neighboring countries. the announced intention of the united states to join forces with the so-called islamic state only reinforces the need for wider cooperation against those who seek to spread terror. it is important that efforts to combat terrorism are effective and sustained. only with a return to normalcy can we hope that nigeria can resume the path of democracy and consolidate the steps it has been trying to implement towards establishing a rule of law for all its inhabitants.
‒ the situation of christians in north-eastern nigeria, the elections held at the end of march, the use of children as human bombs, the abduction of women and girls and the measures to be taken by the international community are problems that should make us all reflect. the local government has been unable to stop the atrocities being committed by boko haram, a recognized extremist group. its eradication is crucial because the group is seen as a threat to peace and security in africa and to global peace and security, even though this requires activating the common security and defence policy, defending the people of nigeria and helping to eradicate boko haram.
‒ the situation in nigeria is inextricably linked to the exploitation of its natural resources, in particular oil. discovered in 1956, oil now accounts for 95 percent of nigeria's export earnings and 80 percent of its income. run by six large multinational companies in partnership with the state, oil extraction does not benefit everyone equally. the country, the continent's third-largest economy, is ranked 158th in the un human development index. seventy percent of nigerians live below the poverty line. local employment is increasingly a mirage because once important resources such as fishing or hunting are increasingly in jeopardy because of the impact of oil exploration and deforestation. pollution has turned the niger delta into one of the most polluted places on the planet. this dramatic situation has created tensions in the region. in the early 1990s, conflicts broke out between the multinationals and the various communities demanding fair compensation. the repressive and brutal response directed at these communities has triggered other responses, increasingly radical, putting the country in a state of permanent war. once again, we have the economic interests of capital at the root of the conflicts in one of the richest countries on the african continent.
‒ nigeria is the most populous and ethnically diverse country in africa, yet it is characterised by regional disparities and religious cleavages, as well as a north-south divide marked by severe economic and social disparities. nevertheless, and despite the looming economic crisis, nigeria is a leading player in the african economy and therefore an important trading partner of the eu. but it does not have a consolidated democracy and a track record of democracy. in this context, the attacks by boko haram between 3 and 8 january 2015 on baga and 16 neighbouring towns and villages resulted in the destruction of 3 700 structures and the death of thousands of people, and ushered in a climate of continued violence and permanent insecurity. the resolution strongly condemns the crimes, suffering and destruction inflicted by the boko haram sect and calls on the new nigerian authorities to adopt a road map for social and economic development. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution calling on the eu and its member states to honour their external commitments in political and humanitarian aid which is indispensable to nigeria's development.

the report on financing for development beyond 2015 which i am presenting here today and which will be voted on tomorrow is the result of an intense and productive political debate in this parliament, which has benefited from a very significant participation of non-governmental organisations and civil society. the broad consensus reached in the committee on development, which i hope will be reinforced in the vote in plenary tomorrow, was only possible thanks to the commitment of all the political groups, and so my first words are to thank all the colleagues, especially the shadow rapporteurs, for their contribution and also for the strong support we have always had from the chair of the deve committee, linda mcavan. we know that the price of extended commitments is often political irrelevance. experience shows that the search for a minimum common denominator often leads to empty proclamations, to the mere assertion of general principles without practical implications. and in the end, we all agree more or less, we go home satisfied because each one reads in the text what suits him best. fortunately, that is not the case in this report. my report proposes, without ambiguity, that the european parliament make a choice, take a clear position and send a strong political message to the commission, the council and the member states on the leading role and responsibility that the european union should have in the negotiations that will take place at the third international conference on financing for development in addis ababa as early as next july. it is true that the new challenges we face are difficult and place the shared responsibility that was already placed in the monterrey consensus in 2002 in a different position. but what is at stake now is very concrete things: firstly, that the european union urgently reconfirm its commitment to allocate 0.7% of gni to official development aid. there can be no more delays or excuses because there will be no leadership by example in addis ababa without this commitment; secondly, that the european union gives credibility to its commitment and takes on a timetable for meeting this financial target by 2020; thirdly, that 50% of this aid, at least 0.2% of gni, is reserved for the least developed countries and, because it would be a grave mistake to minimize the importance of official development aid, we must do what needs to be done. there are other issues on the table which will be discussed in addis ababa and they are equally very important: the mobilisation of domestic resources of developing countries, which requires fairer and more efficient tax systems, more combating tax evasion and avoidance, more international tax cooperation, including through an intergovernmental body for tax cooperation within the framework of the united nations. and it is also very important that the private sector is more aligned with the objectives of sustainable development, with a regulatory framework that favours it and also with financial instruments and incentive structures that ensure that alignment. mr president, after the tragedy we are living through and witnessing in the mediterranean, development cooperation with the countries of origin of the migratory flows, of the refugees who are truly desperate, also reminds us of the urgency of taking this commitment to the development objectives seriously, but there will be no serious commitment without financing instruments that are commensurate with our values and our responsibilities.

‒ having examined the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council codifying the regulation on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation, it appears that the proposal is in fact a mere codification without any change in the substance of the acts to which it relates.
in writing. the purpose of this report is to consolidate previous legislation on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. in 1987, the european commission decided to ask its services to codify all acts at the latest after 10 amendments, in order to make eu legislation more accessible and easier to understand for the ordinary citizen, which would allow him new opportunities and the possibility of benefiting from the specific rights attributed to him. this objective cannot be achieved as long as there is a dispersion of numerous provisions, amended on several occasions, often substantially, which requires a reading both of the original act and of the acts amending it. for this reason, and in order to ensure the clarity and transparency of the law, it is necessary to codify the rules which have been subject to frequent amendments. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, preserving the content of the codified acts in full and introducing only the formal changes required by the codification process itself. it is therefore a purely technical amendment.
the purpose of this proposal is to codify council regulation (eec) no 2841/72 of 19 december 1972 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it. the present proposal preserves the content of the consolidated acts in full, limiting itself to bringing them together and only to the formal changes required by the consolidation process itself.
in writing. the successive amendments to council regulation (eec) no 2841/72 justify its codification for reasons of legal certainty and clarity. the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation, hereinafter referred to as the 'agreement', signed on 22 july 1972, lacks rules for the implementation of the safeguard clauses and precautionary measures provided for in articles 22 to 27 of the agreement. the application of the bilateral safeguard clauses of the agreement requires uniform conditions for the adoption of safeguard measures, which should comply with regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council. i voted in favour of this amendment, on the understanding that the commission should adopt immediately applicable implementing acts if, in duly justified cases relating to situations referred to in articles 24, 24a and 26 of the agreement or in the case of export aid having a direct and immediate effect on trade, imperative grounds of urgency so require.
in writing. ‒ at its meeting on 10 july 2014, the consultative working party, composed of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, examined the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council codifying council regulation (eec) no 2841/72 of 19 december 1972 on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. it concluded by common accord that the proposal in question was merely a codification of the existing texts without any substantive changes. i therefore voted in favour.
in the light of the foregoing, the commission considers that the proposal in question does not contain any substantive amendments other than those identified as such in the proposal and that it is confined to the mere codification of the existing texts without any substantive amendments, there would be no reason to vote against it.
the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (eec) no 2841/72 of 19 december 1972 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, preserving the content of the codified acts in full and introducing only the formal changes required by the codification process itself. we have nothing to object to.
the purpose of this report is to codify for the council council regulation (eec) no 2841/72 of 19 december 1972 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. in 1987, the commission decided to ask its services to codify all acts at the latest after 10 amendments, expressing the aim of making eu legislation more accessible and easier to understand for the ordinary citizen. this objective cannot be achieved, of course, as long as there is a dispersion of numerous provisions, amended on several occasions, often substantially, which requires a reading both of the original act and of the acts amending it. the european parliament, the council and the commission have agreed, by means of an interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994, on an accelerated procedure which can be used for the rapid adoption of consolidated acts. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, preserving the content of the codified acts in full and introducing only the formal amendments required by the codification process itself. so we abstained.
‒ this report concerns the european parliament's approval of the convention on the legal protection of services based on or consisting of conditional access. in adopting directive 98/84/ec, the eu exercised its competence in the areas covered by the convention, except for articles 6 (loss measures) and 8 (international cooperation), which cover topics such as international cooperation, civil procedure and confiscation measures. the convention should therefore be approved by both the eu and its member states. the convention covers information society services and broadcasting services provided for remuneration and based on or consisting of conditional access. the purpose of this convention is to make illegal in the territories of the parties a number of activities (identified in article 4) which allow unauthorised access to protected services, and to approximate the laws of the parties in this field. understanding the general scope and purposes of the convention and generally accepting them, we consider that the subject matter of this report is not without other consequences, going beyond those set out in the text of the convention.
‒ this directive has created a common legal framework throughout the european union for the fight against illegal devices allowing unauthorised access to pay-tv services and for the effective protection of such services. the protection covers both traditional television and radio broadcasting and internet transmission. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the council decision is related to directive 98/84/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 20 november 1998 on the legal protection of services based on or consisting of conditional access, which created the common legal framework for member states on measures to combat illicit devices that provide unauthorised access to protected services. broadcasting services, including internet, television and radio services, are covered by this protection. the contentious dispute which has so far prevented the conclusion of the convention having been overcome, i approve the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the signing, on behalf of the european union, of the european convention on the legal protection of services based on or consisting of conditional access.
in writing. ‒ on 20 november 1998, the council and the european parliament adopted directive 98/84/ec on the legal protection of services based on or consisting of conditional access. the aim was to establish a common union-wide legal framework to combat illicit devices allowing unauthorised access to television services provided for a fee. this protection covers both traditional television and radio broadcasting and internet transmission. on 24 january 2001, a council of europe convention on this subject was adopted in terms fully compatible with the said directive. the court of justice has held that the convention is not a legal instrument and that the convention is not a legal instrument. following this decision, the council then corrected the legal basis by adopting a new decision with a view to approving the convention on behalf of the union. the aim of this resolution is precisely to bring the convention to a conclusion and to obtain the consent of the european parliament. i voted in favour.
‒ this is a convention of our time, relating to access to information and entertainment services (tv, radio and internet) for a fee. the main purpose of the convention is to establish common legislation for a range of activities which allow unauthorised access to certain protected services. more specifically, this protection will consist in declaring illegal all commercial activity related to equipment which allows or facilitates access to these services without authorization or payment to the provider thereof, and establishing appropriate sanctions. the aim is to provide legal protection for service providers while ensuring the quality of services.

‒ i agree with the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of viktor uspaskich, since the crimes he is accused of humiliation of a court or judge due to the exercise of judicial functions by actions, oral or written statements, punishable by fine, detention or imprisonment for a maximum period of two years were committed before his election to the european parliament. immunity is usually waived when the offence is in no way connected with the performance of the duties of a member, provided that there is no fumus persecutionis, i.e. a sufficiently serious and precise suspicion that the motive behind the prosecution is to cause political damage to the member concerned. consequently, the criminal proceedings brought against viktor uspaskich are not linked to his current mandate as a member of the european parliament.
‒ viktor uspaskich, lithuanian member of the european parliament, was a member of the lithuanian parliament at the time of the alleged crime of which he is accused. in july 2013, viktor uspaskich was answering questions from journalists at vilnius airport when he allegedly described the judges who found him guilty in a criminal case against him as cowards, criminals and puppets. in accordance with article 232 of the lithuanian criminal code, public humiliation of a court or a judge due to the exercise of judicial functions is punishable by a fine, detention or imprisonment for a maximum period of two years. it happens that this member of parliament says he is discriminated against and persecuted in lithuania because he belongs to the russian-speaking minority in a country where anti-russian sentiment is rife in the institutions of the state. uspaskich says his party's headquarters were searched when he went to russia for his mother's funeral. the alde group, to which mr uspaskich belongs, has asked that the report be referred back to the commission for further consideration. specifically, it was requested that all of uspaskich's statements be analysed and not just the part that had been analysed and allegedly decontextualised. we supported this request.
‒ the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and that independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. the prosecutor-general of lithuania has requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr viktor uspaskich, member of the european parliament, in the context of a preliminary investigation into the alleged commission of a crime. viktor uspaskich is accused of committing the crime of contempt of court under article 232 of the criminal code of the republic of lithuania. there is no evidence of fumus persecutionis, i.e. reasonable suspicion that the legal action was brought with the aim of politically harming the member. i therefore voted in favour of the waiver of parliamentary immunity.
in writing. ‒ on 1 october 2014, the prosecutor general of lithuania requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of viktor uspaskich, member of the european parliament, in the framework of a preliminary investigation into the alleged criminal contempt of court practice on 28 july 2013 pursuant to article 232 of the criminal code of the republic of lithuania. in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. according to the report of the committee on legal affairs, article 8 of the protocol does not apply in this case, since viktor uspaskich was not a member of the european parliament at the time of the events. in these terms and on the basis of the report, i voted in favour of this decision to waive the immunity of viktor uspaskich.

in writing. ‒ we have no illusions whatsoever about the meaning of the 'strengthening of the functioning of the eu' in question. this is all the more so when such strengthening is advocated 'on the basis of the potential of the lisbon treaty'. it is nothing more than an attempt to deepen the pillars of this capitalist integration: federalism, neoliberalism and militarism. this is a path that, in the face of the deep crisis facing the eu, the main political families - the right and the social democrats - have been trying for some time. the intention is to take this deepening as far as possible, within the limits (which are obviously already broad, although not as broad as some new leaps, desired by some, might require) of the lisbon treaty, escaping the public, democratic scrutiny of the peoples, in particular by means of referendums. for our part, we reaffirm our opposition to the lisbon treaty and the need for its repeal. we reaffirm the proposal to enshrine the possibility of revoking the treaties, adapting the status of each country to the will of its people. we are not opposed to consulting the european economic and social committee. but we are obviously aware - and here we denounce it - of the underlying meaning of this whole process.

‒ the european economic and social committee (eesc) was set up in 1957 as a forum for debate on matters relating to the single market. the eesc provides european interest groups, such as trade unions, employers' associations and farmers' associations, with the opportunity to formally comment on eu legislative proposals. the opinions issued are addressed to the main european institutions, namely the council, the commission and the european parliament. this request for consultation, as provided for in rule 137 of the rules of procedure, is intended to seek the views of representatives of employers, workers and other european interest groups on the strengthening of the functioning of the european union within the framework of the treaty of lisbon. i voted in favour.

‒ i voted in favour of the request for consultation of the committee of the regions on 'evolution and possible adaptations of the current institutional structure of the european union', given that it is consistent with the constant analysis and evaluation of our joint project. this study will not only trace the path we have taken so far, but will also provide a perspective and a roadmap for the future.
‒ the committee of the regions is an advisory body representing local and regional authorities in the european union. the committee's role is to present regional and local views on european legislation by delivering opinions on commission proposals and adopting resolutions on current political issues. the commission, the council and the parliament should also consult the committee of the regions before taking decisions on matters concerning local and regional government (e.g. employment policy, the environment, education or public health). this request for consultation, as provided for in rule 137 of the rules of procedure, is intended to gather the views of local and regional authorities on the evolution and possible adaptations of the current institutional structure of the european union. i voted in favour.
‒ we have serious reservations about the meaning of the 'strengthening of the functioning of the eu' in question here. this is all the more so when such strengthening is advocated 'on the basis of the potential of the lisbon treaty'. it is nothing more than an attempt to deepen the pillars of this capitalist integration: federalism, neoliberalism and militarism. this is a path that, in the face of the deep crisis facing the eu, the main political families - the right and the social democrats - have been rehearsing for some time. the intention is to take this deepening as far as possible, within the limits (which are obviously already broad, although not as broad as some new leaps, desired by some, might require) of the lisbon treaty, escaping the public, democratic scrutiny of the peoples, in particular by means of referendums. we reaffirm our opposition to the lisbon treaty and the need for its repeal. we reaffirm the proposal to enshrine the possibility of revoking the treaties, adapting the status of each country to the will of its people.
in writing. ‒ the proposed amendments underlie three essential objectives: first, to strengthen governance systems and standards, in particular for widely used and systemically important benchmarks, and to reduce their vulnerability to manipulation and abuse; second, to increase transparency by making all benchmarks more widely available to users in order to enable informed decisions; and third, to maintain the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks through the application of proportionate governance requirements. additional legislation should also take into account that many companies, households, investors and financial institutions depend on daily basis on benchmarks accessible across the eu and abroad in order to carry out their business, trade and investment activities, as well as to prevent risks or grant or obtain credit effectively. therefore, the stability and efficiency of markets and the overall economy also require that legislative action avoid restricting, as far as possible, the number and variety of benchmarks offered and used in the union.
‒ following the libor and euribor manipulation scandals, the european commission has indicated its intention to move forward with a legislative proposal seeking to regulate all activity related to the production and dissemination of benchmarks, with the aim of restoring market confidence. the commission proposal has chosen to treat all economic activities in the same way, which has raised criticism and concerns from various actors and sectors (in particular the raw materials markets), who have recommended the application of the principle of proportionality, based on an assessment of the transparency of the data, the sources and the complexity of the indices. as is well known, many of the benchmarks used in the markets for physical goods are calculated on the basis of transaction prices, through direct observation of the markets. but the essential question is whether these indices are credible, or, more precisely, whether they are not. who builds them and how they do it. it is the most powerful interests, whose actions are supposed to be regulated by these indices, that ultimately determine them, directly or indirectly.
‒ the manipulation of libor and foreign exchange benchmarks, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, has highlighted the importance of benchmarks and their vulnerabilities. in response to these revelations, the eu has amended eu market abuse legislation to clarify that such manipulation of benchmarks is illegal and to incorporate this matter into the framework of criminal law. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ there are serious cases of manipulation of interest rate benchmarks such as libor, euribor and foreign currency benchmarks, inflicting considerable losses on consumers and investors. such manipulation contributes decisively to the poor reputation of financial institutions and to the loss of trust by citizens, demonstrating that benchmarks can be subject to conflicts of interest and have discretionary governance and regulation regimes. i am voting in favour of this report which safeguards the independence of the european central bank and the national central banks from the european system of central banks in the exercise of their powers, duties and responsibilities, and the administrators must be obliged to adopt appropriate governance mechanisms to deal with a possible conflict of interest.
‒ indices are essential for pricing crossborder transactions and facilitate the effective functioning of the internal market for a wide range of financial instruments and services. the vast majority of european citizens are therefore directly or indirectly affected by indices. currently, different benchmarks are produced by different providers using different methodologies. reference indices have in fact become public goods and must therefore be subject to strict scrutiny. it is important to maximise their benefits and to take measures to prevent any damage resulting from their manipulation. this regulation precisely introduces a common framework to ensure the high accuracy and integrity of indices used as benchmarks in the framework of financial instruments and contracts in the union, thereby contributing to the smooth functioning of the internal market and to a high level of consumer and investor protection. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts advocates three key aspects: strengthening governance systems and rules, greater transparency for users of all benchmarks and access to a wide variety of benchmarks. i believe that benchmarks are fundamental to the pricing of crossborder transactions and the functioning of the internal market, especially in terms of consumer and investor protection, and it is therefore essential to ensure that they are not manipulated, making them illegal and incorporating this matter into the framework of criminal law.
‒ following the libor and euribor manipulation scandals, the european commission has indicated its intention to move forward with a legislative proposal seeking to regulate all activity related to the production and dissemination of benchmarks, with the aim of restoring market confidence. it is true that the commission proposal, by treating all economic activities in the same way, is creating great concern for those who deal with the markets for raw materials. iosco recommends that different situations be treated differently. it proposes that the principle of proportionality be applied on the basis of an assessment of the transparency of the data, the sources and the complexity of the indices. as is well known, most of the benchmarks used in the markets for physical goods are calculated on the basis of transaction prices through direct observation of the markets. in this sense, and within the risk hierarchy provided by iosco, these indicators are at the base, i.e. of minimum risk.
‒ this year will be of the utmost importance in the development agenda with the adoption of the sustainable development goals which should guide national policies and international cooperation activities over the next 15 years, succeeding the millennium development goals, with the adoption of the agreement on global action against climate change and the international conference on financing for development, which will allow for the establishment of targets and plans for financing and implementation of the post-2015 agenda. as in the past, the european union must play a leading role in these negotiations and be at the forefront of the new process of financing development. i support this report because i consider it vital to reconfirm the commitment to allocate 0.7% of gross national income to official development assistance and to insist on a partnership with other public and private partners in this worldwide endeavour. i would remind you that, in parallel with the mobilisation of resources, efforts must also be made to manage financial resources, to combat corruption and tax evasion in the countries concerned, and that development aid must always be characterised by principles of good governance and the protection of human rights, with particular attention to the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. ‒ 2015 is a pivotal year for global development efforts, with the adoption of the sustainable development goals (sdgs) and an agreement on global action on climate change, valid until 2030. 1.5 billion people still live in poverty, with poor health, education and living conditions, particularly in fragile states ravaged by conflict. i believe that the eradication of poverty and inequalities will only be achieved by mobilising sufficient and adequate resources for all and by specific measures for marginalised groups, such as children, women, the elderly or people with disabilities. three-quarters of the world's poorest people about 960 million people currently live in middle-income countries, with unctad estimating that developing countries' financing needs for the new sdgs are about usd 3.9 billion per year, with usd 2.5 billion currently missing per year. the eu and its member states must maintain their position as major donors of development aid, while upholding shared responsibility.
‒ the approach to development finance in this report ignores the framework of asymmetric interdependence relations typical of globalised capitalism, which generate uneven development on a global scale. hence its great and inescapable limitation. with economic inequality comes political dependence and subordination. they are the various instruments that promote the vicious circle of impoverishment, dependence and subordination. this is the case with the external debt. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council and the european parliament, and the council will be consulted on the matter. this is a question that is simply ignored by the report. the same applies to the devastating effects of the imf and world bank interventions, which drain endogenous resources from the donors, which even exceed the amount of official development assistance. official development assistance (oda) is crucial and should increase, even in line with commitments made but not fulfilled. we appreciate what the report says on this point. but just as oda alone (even at desirable levels) is not enough, so this positive aspect of the report is not enough to make it a good report. far from it.
‒ development finance is one of the key instruments the eu has at its disposal to help growth and to help eradicate poverty and inequalities. only by mobilising sufficient and appropriate financial resources for all and specific measures for marginalised groups such as children, women, the elderly or people with disabilities will we be able to successfully tackle the inequalities that still exist around the world. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the european union is the world's largest donor of development aid, accounting for almost 60% of global official development assistance, and this year is pivotal for global development efforts, with the adoption of the sustainable development goals (sdgs) and an agreement on global action on climate change, valid until 2030. the importance of the challenge of financing the sustainable development goals (sdgs) requires a strong and comprehensive partnership and the use of all forms of financing (national, international, public, private and innovative resources) and non-financial means; private financing can complement, but not replace, public financing. i am in favour of the view that the european union and its member states, as major donors of development aid, should lead the development finance process and contribute to a credible response to development finance challenges by ensuring policy coherence for development in the context of the post-2015 agenda; and that other developing and emerging countries should follow the eu's lead.
‒ 2015 is a pivotal year for global development efforts, with the adoption of the sustainable development goals (sdgs) and an agreement on global action on climate change, valid until 2030. the third international conference on financing for development, to be held in addis ababa, ethiopia, from 13 to 16 july 2015, should therefore create the conditions for the financing and implementation of the post-2015 agenda. in fact, 1.5 billion people still live in poverty, with poor health, education and living conditions, particularly in fragile states ravaged by conflict. this resolution considers that the eu and its member states, as major donors of development aid, should lead the development finance process and contribute to a credible response to development finance challenges by ensuring policy coherence for development in the context of the post-2015 agenda. the resolution also calls for the adoption of an international initiative to improve the quality of statistics, data and information in order to monitor expenditure, investment and progress towards specific commitments and objectives. i voted in favour.
‒ i welcome and support this report for its focus on poverty eradication, human rights and gender equality. this approach can help to renew hope for the 1.5 billion people living in extreme poverty, with limited access to health and education. the report on financing for development does not solve everything, but it is a start for a new model of development based on universality. we can't compartmentalize interests. the world's problems concern us all.
‒ we subscribe to the pious intentions of this report. however, a critical reading of the current situation is necessary. the millennium development goals are far from being achieved. the contributions of the rich states are far below all the commitments. it's been that way for decades, and it's important to understand why. the reason lies in the oppressive, exploitative nature of capitalism. while pretending to be humanistic, it exploits developing countries, corrupts governments and does not hesitate to use force to defend the interests of large multinationals. we are therefore witnessing the destruction of schools built with funds from international aid, and we do not see the slightest openness to contributing to solutions that guarantee the poorest countries the right to sovereign and autonomous development. it's all conditioning, greed and self-interest. tax evasion and avoidance by multinational corporations operating in developing countries exceeds international aid. words for what?

‒ the main dimension of overall quality of healthcare is patient safety, with a culture of care safety and the management of incidents that compromise patient safety at the core. it is estimated that 8% to 12% of patients admitted to hospitals in the eu suffer adverse events while receiving healthcare and that about half of these events could be prevented, as they are infections associated with such care, medication-related episodes and complications during or after surgical interventions. thirty to 50 percent of patients are not taking their prescription medications or are taking them without a prescription, and it's estimated that by 2050, 10 million people will die every year from antimicrobial resistance. it is important that member states ensure, in this period of economic crisis, that health systems are not affected by austerity measures and continue to be adequately funded and, in particular, avoid the most harmful measures, such as short-term savings that will lead to high costs in the medium and long term, and focus on the continuous development of high quality and efficient health systems.
in writing. ‒ between 8 and 12% of patients admitted to hospitals in the eu suffer adverse effects while receiving medical care, with the most common being healthcare-associated infections (hcais), medication-related events and complications arising from surgical interventions. almost half of these events could be prevented. iacs in particular is a public health problem that can be prevented through intensive hygiene and control programmes. antimicrobial resistance has been increasing in the eu for pathogenic bacteria, leading to an increase in acsi caused by multi-resistant bacteria, a burning public health problem. the report covers this subject in a comprehensive and well-documented way. it refers to the effects of the disinvestment in public health services and their professionals as a result of the so-called austerity policies and advocates the reversal of this path. while we agree with the general thrust of the report, we believe that in some areas more could have been done. this is the case for the price of medicines and their implications for access restrictions, patient safety and antimicrobial resistance (as a result of incomplete doses, for example). the same is true of the need to strengthen public capacity in the field of research and development of new medicines, with multinational pharmaceutical companies vying for primacy.
‒ at a time when one of the main consequences of austerity measures has been the reduction in health care and the conditions under which it is provided, it is important to affirm that patients have the right not to be put at risk by medical treatment and that this has to be central to the quality of health care. that's why i voted yes.
‒ the topic of patient safety and the fight against drug resistance, especially antimicrobial resistance, is certainly not unknown to anyone involved in the management of health systems or who has attended the sessions of the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety in recent years. this is a subject widely discussed both by the world health organisation (who) and by european institutions such as the commission, the council and the specialised agencies (ecdc, ema, easa). this draft report is based on the need for patient safety, i.e. the freedom of the patient from actual or potential harm as a consequence of the provision of health care, to be an essential element for the quality of health systems. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ patient safety and the fight against drug resistance, especially resistance to antimicrobial agents, are widely discussed issues both by the world health organisation (who) and by european institutions such as the commission, the council and the specialised agencies (ecdc, ema, efsa) and the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety. this draft report is based on the need for patient safety to be an essential element for the quality of health systems. i am voting in favour of the report because i believe that the patient should be the centre of treatment and not allow health systems to suffer unjustified cuts in the name of austerity.
‒ patient safety and the fight against drug resistance are central to the management of health systems. in fact, according to the available data, 8% to 12% of hospitalized patients suffer harm or adverse events, and it is estimated that about half of these adverse events could be avoided. on the other hand, antimicrobial resistance by pathogenic bacteria has increased worldwide, leading to an increasing prevalence of iacs and failures in the treatment of infectious diseases. this report attempts to identify the various factors that compromise patient safety and to identify the measures to be taken to ensure the highest possible standard of patient safety. i voted in favour.
‒ the european union and the european parliament itself should play an active role in the healthcare provided by its member states. improving patient safety and tackling antimicrobial resistance are key issues today. the resolution in question, in its general outline, points to gaps that may exist in the field in question and also warns of some of the problems that need to be addressed in the national health systems. all member states should invest in a national health system suited to the needs of their population. we must continue to invest in the research of new and effective medicines and, in this context, give priority to partnerships with universities.
in writing. ‒ the costs of drug-resistant infections are estimated at around €1.5 billion annually due to increased healthcare expenditure and lost productivity, whereas patients infected with resistant bacteria have to be isolated when treated in hospital and this additional provision costs more than €900 million and an additional 2.5 million days of hospital stay per year. these resistances stem from a fundamental contradiction which lies in the incompatibility between the moderate use of antibiotics and the needs of the pharmaceutical industry to maximise its profits and return on its investments. unfortunately, we haven't heard a word about this. in this way, there is no change in the drama.
