‒ the sectors covered by green growth provide major economic and environmental benefits to smes, which are the backbone of the european economy and are important drivers of economic growth and job creation. there is a broad consensus that green growth offers numerous advantages. but there are also many problems associated with this growth identified by the companies themselves, notably the information gap between smes and lenders in negotiating a loan. in developing programmes, instruments and initiatives, the commission must take into account the wide range of financing needs, which vary according to product, company size, technology, innovation, etc. another key point in developing green growth opportunities is the need for knowledge sharing and transfer. for these reasons, this report devotes a separate section to how smes can make the most of the available knowledge. the great potential of the green economy can only be fully exploited if the appropriate framework for research, development and innovation is established.
‒ the report begins by declaring its support for the concept of green growth, the economically viable exploitation of wind, solar, hydro and geothermal energy, energy efficiency and resource use, waste management, the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the circular flow of recycling and reuse of raw materials. it refers to the importance of the role of smes in this comprehensive framework for promoting job creation and economic growth. we're not going to disagree. these are fair objectives, which are undoubtedly opportunities for the development of a wide range of small and mediumsized enterprises. but it is clear that the concept of growth here is capitalist growth, which is by its nature unsustainable, no matter how much you try to paint it green. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus, and for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus. it called on the commission to 'relieve the fear of bankruptcy' by promoting awareness-raising and education campaigns. moreover, it challenges the rhetoric of the apologist for entrepreneurship and completely ignores the important role of the state in these areas, which if fully taken on would create different and better conditions for smes themselves.
in writing. ‒ this report does a good job of listing the challenges facing smes, but it is short on solutions. it is well known that one of the main problems facing smes is access to finance. programmes such as cosme or h2020 are essential, but more needs to be done, such as facilitating access to other types of finance such as microcredit. that is why i abstained.
‒ smes represent more than 98% of european enterprises and account for more than 67% of total employment in the union and 58% of gross value added. smes are the backbone of the european union's economy and are the key drivers of europe's long-term economic growth and the creation of sustainable employment opportunities in the 28 member states. we must support the concept of green growth and the circular economy. the opportunities arising from this cover multiple areas of significant importance, such as renewable energy sources and in particular the economically viable exploitation of wind, solar, hydro and geothermal energy , energy efficiency, resource efficiency, waste management, emission reduction, electrification and the circular flow of recycling and reuse of materials. green growth must be part of a broader strategy to promote job creation and economic growth for smes. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the backbone of the european union's economy and are the engines of economic growth and job creation in the 28 member states. it should be noted that smes represent more than 98% of european enterprises, account for more than 67% of total employment in the union and 58% of gross value added. i support this report and i vote in favour of this legislative initiative because i believe that green growth is of paramount economic importance in our european economy. this is due not only to the economic activities associated with the green economy (e.g. renewable energy, forestry, waste management) but also to the amount of jobs that could be generated in the future. i would like to stress the importance of financing green initiatives, knowledge management of previously developed projects and the interest of the horizon 2020 research and innovation programme in increasingly supporting this type of economic activity.
‒ smes represent more than 98% of european enterprises and account for more than 67% of total employment in the union and 58% of gross value added, thus constituting the backbone of the eu economy and a key driver of its long-term economic growth and the creation of sustainable employment opportunities in the 28 member states. the global market for environmental goods and services is estimated to be worth €1 trillion per year and is expected to double or even triple by 2020, creating huge opportunities for european smes and for eu economic growth in general. it is therefore important to support green growth and to tackle the main problems smes are currently facing in this area. this includes creating a stronger culture of entrepreneurship, developing open and innovation-friendly standards, establishing more diversified access to finance and increasing the possibilities for knowledge sharing. i voted in favour.
‒ this report calls on policy makers to fully understand the potential of the green economy at the level of smes, as they now represent over 98% of european enterprises and account for over 67% of total employment in the union, and are one of the pillars of the european economy, long-term economic growth and the creation of sustainable employment opportunities in the 28 member states. given the importance of smes, it is essential that we are all aware of the various problems they are currently facing, whether they relate to funding, research and innovation, the acquisition of the appropriate knowledge or the existing regulatory framework. unlike multinational companies, smes often do not have the same easy access to knowledge networks to keep abreast of new technologies or to convey their message to potential customers and investors. the development of a set of guidelines to overcome some of these difficulties and to streamline and unify the various divergent national systems will undoubtedly be a very positive development.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the employment crisis and the lack of sustainability in employment, smes have a social role and added value that deserve our full attention. these companies should, as far as possible, have green or blue approaches in the case of marine companies. by combining sustainability with concepts such as the circular economy, regionalisation, knowledge, innovation, the latest digital technologies, bureaucratization, entrepreneurship and micro-credit, we will be fostering a more equitable, transparent, fair and inclusive society. i have seen several good examples of this approach in the maritime world in europe. we are facing a new generation of companies which do not seek profit at any cost, but rather the happiness and quality of life of those who lead them, of those who work in them and of those who use their services. that is the future i want for europe and that is why i voted in favour of this proposal.

the council's decision yesterday to launch a naval mission in the mediterranean under the common security and defence policy is a decisive step in the right direction, but it must be justified by the imperative of saving lives and thus preventing the principles and values on which the european project is based from being undermined. only then to dismantle the slave networks that exploit the tragedies that drive refugees and migrants to europe. it is regrettable, in this context, that some governments refuse to accept quotas for the reception of persons in need of protection. this is a long-term task, the mediterranean tragedy did not start yesterday and is a problem for all of europe and not just for a few states on the front line. it is in the strategic sense and consistency of all internal security and external action policies, including development, trade and energy supply policies, that the european union must act on all fronts to help people resolve conflicts, get rid of oppressive regimes and to tackle other causes of migration flows, such as poverty. opening legal pathways for migrants is essential to take the profit out of smugglers and give opportunities to those who are desperate for them, and a europe in demographic decline must assume that it needs immigrants. we must not delay any longer and put eunavfor mediterranean at sea. we must also do security, development and governance support work in our neighbourhood, in the south, namely libya, syria and iraq. it is shocking that there is no coordination between europeans in providing military supplies to forces in iraq and syria to train fighters against the islamic state. on the other hand, it is urgent to prepare a commitment which must be long-term. i am talking about libya where we have special responsibilities for action and omission and where we have strategic interests and even today we have a vital interest in not allowing it to become a terrorist sanctuary on our doorstep. the european effort to support capacity building, including the organisation of the security sector, should be programmed on the assumption that the un special representative, bernardino léon, can forge an agreement for a government of national unity. but if it fails and the state failure in libya continues and worsens, let us agree that we will need to intervene for our own security and defence and must now work to seek backing from the united nations security council. for this mission in the mediterranean, we are moving forward without a mandate from the security council and, despite the efforts of the high representative in new york recently, the responsibility to protect, save lives and combat the slave traders is in fact at stake, as i said. but this failure highlights the urgent need for reform of the un security council. this must be put on the european agenda: it is time to demand reform of the security council and to reclaim a mandate, a permanent seat for europe. in order to make eunavfor mediterranean operational as soon as possible, as the council wants, the member states must make available the human resources and equipment, because the union does not have its own civilian or military resources. the report i have authored and which we are going to examine today calls for a radical change in the culture of our governments. it is essential that the member states, under the guidance of the high representative, cooperate more in the field of the acquisition of military material and equipment. it is essential that they articulate their policies and weaponry options. it is essential that they invest in pooling and sharing, and that a plan of needs and objectives for joint military equipment is drawn up which actually meets the needs and which enables us as a union to meet our obligations. we must recognize that good intentions are of no use when we know in advance that it will take months before eunavfor mediterranean is operational. the price is too high. we cannot allow the illusion of sovereignty and the protectionist opacity of some governments to hold back the european union's action on a matter so fundamental to the union's collective security and credibility. we therefore ask the commission to monitor the implementation of the two internal market directives in the field of the acquisition and transfer of defence material and equipment and to require member states to comply with the new rules. for us to have a functioning internal market in this area, it is crucial that corrupt and opaque practices which undermine the sector, which prevent opportunities for cooperation, competition and technological development and which, moreover, constitute a bad return on taxpayers' money invested in national defence budgets, are purged. the proper implementation of these directives is essential for the defence industrial and technological base which, as the council also identified yesterday, is the key to the union's strategy for collective security and defence.

it could also do this for the mediterranean mission. yet they do not have a mandate for that. is this not stupid? should we not actually acknowledge and actually make full potential of that contribution? the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. ‒ massive flows of illicit money can undermine the stability and reputation of the financial sector, threaten the single market and international development. tax evasion and non-disclosure and concealment mechanisms can be used as money laundering strategies and it is important that measures are taken at european level to combat illicit activities. i am voting in favour of the measures presented which aim to achieve full traceability of transfers of funds, to investigate money laundering and to detect the financing of terrorism. it is also necessary to ensure the transmission of information throughout the payment chain and to provide for the establishment of a system requiring payment service providers to ensure that transfers of funds are accompanied by information on the payer and the payee.
‒ this legislative resolution approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on information accompanying transfers of funds and repealing regulation (ec) no 1781/2006. the regulation aims to improve the traceability of payments and the prevention and detection of money laundering and terrorist financing when funds are transferred. to this end, it aims to eliminate areas where transparency gaps still persist, by ensuring, inter alia, access to information on the payer; the extension of the scope of action to credit and debit cards and mobile phones and digital devices; the verification of the identity of the payee; and the strengthening of the sanctioning powers of the competent authorities and the publication of sanctions. i voted in favour of the motion.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. due to the constant technological evolution at the disposal of criminals, which allows or facilitates new forms of money laundering, a permanent review of the ways of acting at international level is necessary.
‒ the directive proposes to raise the level of customer due diligence to be exercised in relation to 'politically exposed persons', in particular by requiring that such persons, as well as their family members and closest collaborators, be subject to enhanced customer due diligence procedures. the pps will now include not only 'foreign' individuals but also 'domestic' individuals who have been entrusted with prominent public functions. the proposed directive provides for more stringent rules and more specific rules and procedures for the identification of the beneficial owners of companies or other legal persons or trusts, although the definition of beneficial owner remains unchanged. in addition, companies or other legal persons or trusts will be required to keep records relating to the identification of their beneficial owners. these are positive measures but they are not convincing and they create the illusion that it is possible to reform an unreformable system which will certainly find ways to turn these regulations into the next scandal.
‒ this regulation contains some improvements over the existing legislation which should be highlighted. in the case of the latter, however, workers are looked down upon and reduced to the status of mere creditors who are not granted credit privileges and whose credits are not given any specific guarantees. similarly, the regulation does not provide unequivocally for the identification, methods of selection and duties of workers' representatives in the proceedings to which it applies and thus jeopardises the exercise of their rights to be informed, to be consulted and, more generally, to participate actively in such proceedings. moreover, the way in which the regulation defines the centre of the debtor company's main interests, the location of which is decisive for the choice of the member state in which the main insolvency proceedings may be opened, does not preclude such a location from being deliberately chosen because it has a legislative environment favourable to the interests of shareholders and thus unfavourable to those of employees, which provides incentives for member states to use their company law as a tool of legislative competition to the detriment of the rights of employees.
‒ this proposal amends council regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings (hereinafter referred to as the 'insolvency regulation' or 'the regulation'). the general objective of the review of the insolvency regulation is to enhance the efficiency of the european regulatory framework in the resolution of cross-border insolvency cases in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and its resilience during economic crises. this objective is linked to the eu's current policies to promote economic recovery and sustainable growth, a higher investment rate and the preservation of jobs, as envisaged in the europe 2020 strategy. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ this matter relates to the provisions of council regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings. the proper functioning of the internal market requires that insolvency proceedings with cross-border effects be conducted efficiently and effectively. such cases occur when the insolvent's assets, liabilities, etc. are situated in more than one member state, or even when the insolvent is subject to the legal systems of several member states. insolvency laws differ significantly between member states. the current regulation does not standardize or harmonize insolvency situations, but rather regulates situations of conflict between the legal systems of different member states. i am voting in favour of this recommendation, as i support the establishment of a crossborder insolvency procedure.
in writing. ‒ this legislative resolution approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on insolvency proceedings. cross-border insolvency occurs where the assets or liabilities of a debtor are located in more than one state or where the debtor is subject to the jurisdiction of more than one member state. the proposal for a regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings aims to make insolvency proceedings more efficient and effective with a view to ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market and its resilience in economic crisis situations. to this end, it proposes, inter alia, to extend the scope of application to debt adjustments and reorganisations; to clarify the rules of jurisdiction and improve the procedural framework for determining jurisdiction; and to lay down detailed rules on cooperation between courts and liquidators. i voted in favour.
‒ this recommendation aims to establish a set of procedures to improve the efficiency of crossborder insolvency resolution, while ensuring the fluidity of the internal market and resilience to economic crises. with the increasing globalisation and internationalisation of business, clarification of procedures is a priority.
‒ this report reformulates the regulation on insolvency proceedings. the main objective is to review regulation 1346/2000 on transnational insolvencies. the regulation applies to public collective insolvency proceedings, including interim proceedings, based on the insolvency act and in which, for the purposes of recovery, debt adjustment, reorganisation or liquidation, the insolvency proceedings are conducted in accordance with the insolvency law.
‒ the purpose of this report is to reformulate the insolvency procedure regulation. the main objective is to review regulation 1346/2000 on transnational insolvencies. this text is the result of negotiations with the council. there being no amendment to reject it, the president declared it approved. the regulation applies to public collective insolvency proceedings, including interim proceedings, based on the insolvency act, in which, for the purposes of recovery, debt adjustment, reorganisation or liquidation: the debtor is deprived of all or part of his assets; an insolvency practitioner is appointed; the business is placed under the control and supervision of a court or a temporary stay of enforcement is ordered. in cases where there is only a probability of insolvency, it was decided in the negotiations that the aim should be to avoid the debtor's bankruptcy or the cessation of his activity, which we consider to be positive. as far as workers' credits are concerned, nothing has changed, since they are not granted credit privileges, which we consider to be negative.
‒ this draft resolution establishes a system of self-certification, within the framework of the duty of care in the supply chains of importers of tin, tungsten, tantalum and gold from conflict and high-risk areas, thus reducing the illegal financing of armies and other armed groups in conflict areas. the draft regulation gives european importers the possibility to step up their efforts to ensure transparent supply chains when trading legitimately with companies and other actors in conflict-affected countries. to increase accountability, improve the transparency of its supply chains and facilitate responsible sourcing, the eu intends to publish annual lists of responsible companies. with over 400 importers, the eu is among the largest markets for tin, tungsten, tantalum and gold.
in writing. ‒ persistent global shortages of raw materials are at the root of many internal and regional conflicts, crimes against humanity, interference, and ongoing violations of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states, often with the complicity of international organisations and foreign powers interested in maintaining control of resources. despite the obvious limitations of such mechanisms, we acknowledge that it may be relevant to discuss mechanisms for the certification of importers of minerals from conflict and high-risk areas, by creating traceability mechanisms that allow the identification of raw materials originating from these areas. the original proposal covered only a part of the marketed minerals and did not go beyond the first link in the value chain, deliberately forgetting the myriad of end products and intermediates where these raw materials are incorporated. a proposed amendment adopted during the vote (against the right-wing position of parliament and the european commission) has bypassed these limitations, broadening the range of raw materials covered and covering other links in the value chain, which are also subject to traceability rules, thus eliminating an ineffective and perverse aspect of the original proposal. we have voted in favour of these amendments, although other restrictions remain.
‒ unlike the commission and council proposal, the final report sets out a system of mandatory traceability of the origin of minerals from conflict or high-risk areas, which is why i voted in favour.
‒ this proposal aims to make it more difficult to finance the activities of armed groups in conflict and high-risk areas through the exploitation and trade of minerals. the main objectives of the proposed regulation are to prevent profits from the trade in minerals from being used to finance armed conflict, to promote responsible sourcing of these minerals by companies and to favour legitimate channels of trade. the minerals concerned - tin, tantalum, tungsten, their ores and gold - are used, for example, in the automotive, construction, electrical and electronic industries and are present in consumer products used by many europeans, such as computers, printers, washing machines and refrigerators. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the aim of this draft regulation is to break the vicious circle between mining, trade in minerals and the financing of armed conflict by establishing a european self-certification system for importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold. self-certification requires eu importers of these metals and their ores to meet the duty of care - i.e. not to cause adverse effects on the ground - by controlling and managing their purchases and sales in accordance with the five steps prescribed in the oecd due diligence guidance. the regulation also allows eu importers to further their current efforts to ensure fair supply chains by establishing legitimate trade relations with operators in conflict-affected countries. i voted in favour.
‒ as s&d president gianni pittella said, 'all those who fight for respect for human rights have won, and they must always prevail over any multinational interests'. the proposal increases the guarantee that the eu's import of certain minerals from conflict zones will not fund armed militias that commit human rights abuses. importers will be certified and obliged to comply with certain rules under penalty of a fine.
‒ i fully support the creation of a european market free from complicity in bloody conflicts. i believe that if producers and consumers unite for a responsible mineral market in the european space, we will be closer to breaking the link between mining and trading of minerals and the financing of conflicts on a global scale. i believe, however, that the winkler report's proposals still fall short of contributing to the truly ambitious legislation needed to eliminate the presence of 'conflict minerals' in the european union. legislation which imposes a duty of care only on refiners and smelters has too limited an impact. effective mechanisms are needed along the entire production chain, from the importer of the raw material to the final consumer. a chain-wide certification system should be implemented, making all actors responsible for the reliability of the information provided to the final consumer. i therefore voted in favour of extending the duty of care to all companies operating in the minerals market, including companies down the supply chain.
‒ the current and increasing persistent shortage of raw materials at global level is obvious. important mineral resources with restricted distribution on a planetary scale are in short supply. and it is no coincidence that some of the largest reserves are located in countries ravaged by internal, regional conflicts, crimes against humanity, interference, permanent violations of their sovereignty and territorial integrity, almost always with the complicity of international organizations and foreign powers interested in maintaining control of resources. this is the case in the great lakes region. it is appropriate to discuss mechanisms for the certification of importers of minerals from conflict-affected and high-risk areas, by establishing traceability mechanisms to identify raw materials originating from these areas. however, this proposal, which covers only a part of the marketed minerals and does not go beyond the first link in the value chain, deliberately ignores the myriad of final and intermediate products in which these raw materials are incorporated. he doesn't deserve our credit.

‒ the directive on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment limits, inter alia, the use of cadmium in electrical and electronic equipment. the extension of exemption 39 concerns two different applications of cadmium quantum dots: one concerns the use in solid state lighting and the other concerns display systems. the commission explicitly states that quantum dot leds (with and without cadmium) for lighting are not yet available and acknowledges that their positive environmental impact could therefore not be demonstrated. this delegated directive does not fulfil the conditions set out and the justification given for exemption 39 (b) is based on an outdated situation regarding the feasibility of substituting cadmium in quantum dots.
‒ this resolution objects to the directive amending, for the purpose of adapting to technical progress, annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu as regards an exemption for cadmium in lighting and display lighting applications. in january 2015, the european commission proposed a delegated act extending the lifetime of cadmium in televisions until june 2018. the commission is thus reintroducing cadmium on the eu market, as manufacturers had already removed it from the lighting and backlighting applications of cadmium-based monitors in light of the expiry of this exemption in july 2014. the commission justified this by stating that 'cadmium-free quantum dots are not technically available yet'. however, according to the commission's explanatory memorandum, for one of the applications, there are no products on the market using quantum dots (cd and cdlivres), so it is difficult to understand why such an exemption would still be necessary. and indeed, the commission's advisers who assessed this request for exemption do not consider it to be justified at this stage. furthermore, according to industry information, there are at least two companies offering quantum dots cd-free, and there are products with this technology already on the market. as such, the justification by the commission appears to be incorrect.
‒ i have cast my vote in favour of the objection raised by the european parliament to the delegated act on the subject. the commission delegated directive extends an exemption for a longer period, which may be relevant in the future but which can only be granted on the basis of a careful and appropriate assessment.
in writing. ‒ the article 4 (1) of directive 2011/65/eu on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment limits, inter alia, the use of cadmium in electrical and electronic equipment. annex iii to that directive provides for exemptions from the restrictions provided for in article 4 (1). point 39 of annex iii contains a derogation for cadmium in colour conversion led ii-vi (less than 10 μg cd per mm2 of light emitting surface) for use in solid state or display lighting systems, which expires on 1 july 2014. the commission indicated that it received an application for the renewal of exemption 39 in december 2012 and a related application for a more restricted and specific exemption for the use of cadmium in quantum dots in monitors in may 2013. applications for renewal of an exemption must be submitted no later than 18 months before the expiry of the exemption; the application for the specific exemption was submitted after that deadline. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

‒ the regulatory role of the european union in promoting sustainable development and often opening legislative pathways to international standards is recognised. at the same time, through funding programmes such as horizon 2020, the union has catalysed scientific and technological research, which is the basis for much of the innovation that reduces the effects of pollution and offers citizens in general a better quality of life. cadmium is a naturally occurring element that is scarce and has no relevant role in living systems. even in low concentrations, cadmium is harmful to human and animal health in general. in technological terms, cadmium has numerous uses that are not yet replaceable. however, the proposed delegated directive allowed the continued use of cadmium in monitors, a prospect which is no longer justified. i think we need to continue to promote sustainable solutions and to discourage the use of techniques and methods that are outdated or have environmentally more suitable alternatives. for that reason, i voted to make this delegated directive unworkable and to impose the best available environmental and technological practices.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i think it is shameful that a directive which aims to regulate something as fundamental as maternity and paternity leave has been dragged out for years because of a lack of will on the part of the member states. it cannot be repeated over and over again that europe has a demographic problem, that the birth rate must be increased, without creating the basic conditions for those who want to be mothers and those who want to be fathers to be able to be so.

‒ xylella fastidiosa poses a very serious direct threat to the production of certain crops in southern europe, in particular olive trees, almond trees, peaches and ornamental plants. the strain that is infecting olive trees in the apulia region of southern italy is different from the strain that is causing the disease in the vine or citrus trees in other parts of the world. the commission notes that the italian authorities have not provided any evidence that the aid granted to the beneficiaries was compatible with the internal market. i agree with the need for the european commission to take effective measures to prevent the spread of xylella fastidiosa in the european union and to compensate producers for the eradication measures and the loss of income, which imply losses not only in terms of agricultural production but also in terms of historical, cultural heritage and tourism-related activities.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the occurrence of infection by xyllela fastidiosa was first reported by the italian authorities. it is a bacterial infection that mainly affects olive trees. the lack of effective treatments to cure plants infected by this microorganism, the wide range of infection of susceptible plant species, as well as the high probability of contamination, make this bacterium a serious threat. the resolution calls on the commission to take action not only to stop this outbreak but also to protect the sector from future outbreaks through preventive measures. it called for support for targeted farmers who see their crops destroyed and for incentives for farmers who take effective measures to prevent infection and for those who have appropriate agricultural practices to deal with this problem. it also called for funding for research institutes to increase scientific knowledge about xyllela fastidiosa and to identify the nature of the link between the pathogen, the symptoms and the development of the disease. although we believe that the resolution tabled by our group contains a more correct and complete approach to this problem, we believe that the resolution adopted contains a minimum set of measures necessary at this stage of emergency.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the measures proposed by the member states should be considered as a means of ensuring that the eradication programme is not disrupted by the introduction of new species of invasive alien species.
‒ xylella fastidiosa is a bacterium that infects more than 300 plant species (including olive trees, almond trees, vines and citrus trees) and whose treatment is not always effective, as it lives inside the tree, making it difficult to fight it, and is mainly transmitted through contaminated plants. a plague has broken out in the apulia region of italy, and more than half a million olive trees have already been infected. this is not a problem of italy, portugal or spain. unfortunately, as the january report of the european food safety authority shows, this is a european problem that has all the conditions to worsen. the spread of the disease to other countries of the european union is very likely. portugal is, as is well known, the fourth largest producer of olive oil in the world. i am therefore very concerned about this as a member of the committee on agriculture and rural development. hence my vote.
‒ the european food safety authority, in a recent scientific opinion on the risk assessment of xylella fastidiosa, has shown that 'intensive use of insecticide treatments to limit disease transmission and control the vector insect can have direct and indirect impacts on the environment by altering entire food webs with chain-linked consequences, thus affecting different food levels'. however, in the present case, the agri-food sector in apulia is one of the most important industries in the region and the trade unions estimate that 8,000 workers in the olive sector are at risk of losing their jobs. i am voting in favour of this resolution for asking the commission to carry out a cost-benefit analysis of the eradication strategy, for calling for consideration of alternative measures depending on the extent of the spread of the bacterium, the plants affected and the strain of the bacterium, and for urging the commission to limit the large-scale use of pesticides and to implement directive 2009/128/ec establishing a framework for community action on the sustainable use of pesticides.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the directives set out in the proposal must be taken into account in order to prevent their spread, while at the same time ensuring the economic recovery of the affected areas.
‒ we live in a globalised market context, where our borders are more open, but where permeability is obviously controlled. this control includes a type of supervision which must be based on reciprocity with regard to the practices of our trading partners and the risk associated with the origin of the products. animal and plant diseases can have devastating economic and environmental effects and the risk of spread is high in this context. border control must be carried out effectively, but this is hardly absolute. it is a competence which, by its nature, falls within the sphere of the european union to implement, naturally relying on the capabilities of the member states. in the event of an outbreak of animal and plant diseases, all means must be mobilised to contain the spread and european solidarity is required to do this.
‒ this resolution calls on the commission to take action not only to stop this outbreak, but also to protect the sector from future outbreaks through preventive measures. it called for support for targeted farmers who see their crops destroyed and for incentives for farmers who take effective measures to prevent infection and for those who have appropriate agricultural practices to deal with this problem. it also called for funding for research institutes to increase scientific knowledge of xyllela fastidiosa and to identify the nature of the link between the pathogen, the symptoms and the development of the disease. we welcome it.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the occurrence of infection by xyllela fastidiosa was first reported by the italian authorities, infecting the entire province of apulia in southern italy. in the audit of the region, the audit committee found that at the time of the audit, no measures had been taken by the italian authorities to stop the infection and contamination in the region, as there were already several affected areas. it is a bacterial infection which affects mainly olive trees in europe and can infect several other fruit trees. in february 2014 emergency measures were adopted and detailed in july of the same year. the commission is proposing concrete measures to curb this outbreak, such as a ban on the import of plants without a phytosanitary certificate that excludes xyllela fastidiosa infection, a ban on the movement of plants for planting, with the exception of seeds and plants listed in the annexes to the directive. other recommendations include the suspension of the issuing of host plant passports, the immediate destruction of all infected plants, the compulsory removal and cleaning of surrounding grasses and the compulsory treatment of nurseries with insecticides to control vectors of infection. we voted yes.

‒ the common security and defence policy is one of the pillars of the european union's foreign policy. this includes civilian missions and military operations whose main objective is conflict prevention and management. since 2003, the union has launched more than 30 missions. despite the measures introduced by the european commission, problems remain which directly affect the effectiveness of these operations. the steady reduction in member states' military budgets leads to delays in the supply of essential equipment and services. the council's slow decision-making process also jeopardises security and the objectives of the common security policy. i support this report because i believe that there must be more transparency and accountability, but also more coherence and complementarity between the union and the member states. i believe that the principle of solidarity should be applied and that all member states should support these missions even when they are not directly involved. the long-term financing of military and civilian missions should be established.
‒ the discussion of the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy is an opportunity to recover some provisions of the lisbon treaty that have not yet been exploited. i am aware that the defence capabilities of the european union need to be strengthened, but it is also necessary to take account of the budgetary constraints faced by some member states. we know that the european union and its member states must act as peacekeepers. but i think that the european union cannot fail to be at the forefront of solving world problems, keeping abreast of the cultural, social and political changes taking place in the world and affecting us all.
in the report, the commission has been able to demonstrate that it is not only the european union, but also the european union itself, which is responsible for the development of the european union. its objectives continue to be the european standardisation of security measures on the various fronts, intervention within the framework of nato's policies and objectives, a tool in the service of us imperialist policy, the european federalisation of its foreign policy, in particular through the role of the vp/hr which we do not recognise and reject, the enhancement of the athena mechanism, a way to decide on militarization outside the control of the member states and parliament.
the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of civil protection authorities, including the european union's national police and police committees (npscs). it called for concrete proposals to be drawn up on the reform of the csdp mission and operations financing schemes, and considered that concrete measures should be taken to strengthen the eu's defence capabilities in complementarity with nato. it called for the strengthening of defence cooperation, the pooling and sharing of resources, capabilities and means, i.e. it supported and called for an extension of the costs eligible under the athena mechanism, extending its scope to the financing of eu military missions. the commission is also proposing to set up a fund for military operations. the reality is that the eu is becoming increasingly militaristic, involved in almost every scenario of interference, destabilisation and military intervention, activities which require funding, which is proposed to be increased here, a perspective which we reject and which we have once again rejected.
‒ the report analyses the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. the reduction in european demand due to budget cuts, growing external dependencies, the potential of internal market rules and the review of the defence procurement package are some of the issues addressed in the paper. parliament called on the commission to monitor the implementation of the two internal market directives on the acquisition and transfer of defence material and equipment and to require member states to comply with these rules.
in the first place, the european union must be able to take action to prevent the spread of the virus, and to prevent the spread of the disease, and to prevent the spread of the disease. the report also calls for the development and realisation of the european defence market - the war industry - as an indispensable tool for strengthening the eu's war capacity. the objectives of the european union are the continuing european standardisation of security measures on all fronts, intervention in the framework of nato's policies and objectives, a tool in the service of us imperialist policy, and the european federalisation of its foreign policy, notably through the role of the vp/hr, which we do not recognise and reject. it reinforces support for and the promotion of research for the security industry, and strengthens financial incentives and tax benefits for the european defence industry, with the aim of consolidating a common european defence industry market, with advances in cybersecurity and increased surveillance. we obviously voted against it.

mr president, it is important to defend and understand intellectual property rights as a matter which, in our view, is primarily concerned with the interests of authors and creators and not primarily with the interests of intermediary companies, which profit from what they consider to be merely a commodity within the framework of the internal market, which naturally favours the largest companies and the economically strongest countries. but there is one point that we think is important to stress. the european union is also committed to the development of the cultural sector, which is a key element in the development of the european union. and it is up to the states to ensure that dignity. unfortunately, the opposite has been true. on the other hand, everyone has the right to enjoy culture and knowledge, and the essential part of the remuneration of authors and creators should not fall on them. it would be more fair, indeed, if it were left to the intermediaries who profit from this work.

mr president, it is indisputable that the russian regime has unfortunately evolved in an increasingly autocratic direction, with disregard for individual freedoms and disregard for the actions of the opposition and minorities. this also contributes to a large extent to the fact that, at the external level, we are witnessing a systematic violation of some elementary principles of international law, and in this respect the positions which the european union has been adopting over the last few months, with the support, moreover, of the united nations, have proved to be the most correct and appropriate. this should not, however, make us lose sight of the geopolitical importance of the relationship between the european union and russia. i think that we should be careful in the way we approach the possibility of increasing sanctions against russia. on the one hand, we must support those in russia who are fighting for human rights. i think that is absolutely fundamental. on the other hand, we must have some thought in the way we approach the russian question in international terms.
in writing. it is extraordinary that this report expresses concern about the increasingly intense contacts and cooperation, tolerated by the russian leadership, between populist, fascist and far-right european parties and nationalist forces in russia. the majority of this parliament, on the contrary, seems not at all concerned about the enactment last may of laws in ukraine which criminalize communist ideology and symbols and impede the activity of the communist party of ukraine and other democratic and anti-fascist forces in ukraine. the majority of meps seem to be satisfied with the presence of fascist forces in the ukrainian government and the repression of democratic freedoms.
‒ the amount of the reserve for crises in the agricultural sector to be included in the commission's draft budget for 2016 is eur 441,6 million in current prices. in order to reach this amount, the financial discipline mechanism should be applied to direct payments. however, neither the preliminary forecasts of direct payments nor the market-related expenditure require additional financial discipline measures. as a general rule, farmers who submit an aid application for direct payments for a calendar year n shall be paid during the fixed period of the financial year n + 1. therefore, in order to ensure equal treatment of farmers, the adjustment rate should only be applied to payments corresponding to aid applications submitted in the calendar year to which the financial discipline applies, irrespective of the date on which the payment to the farmer is made. i agree to apply a reduction rate of 1,393041% to the part of direct payments to farmers exceeding eur 2000 corresponding to the aid applications submitted for the calendar year 2015.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a regulation on the establishment of a european union agency for fundamental rights (fra) to assist the member states in the implementation of the european union agency for fundamental rights (fra). the regulation provides that the total amount of the reserve shall be eur 2 800 million, with equal annual instalments of eur 400 million (2011 prices) for the period 2014-2020. it also provides that this adjustment rate should only be applied to direct payments exceeding eur 2 000. the application of this adjustment rate will result in the reduction of the amounts of direct payments for budget lines relating to expenditure relating to aid applications submitted by farmers, as regards the calendar year 2015 (financial year 2016). the total reduction resulting from the application of this mechanism is eur 441,6 million and the adjustment rate will be 1,393041%. we agree with the constitution of this reserve. two aspects, however, deserve greater consideration:- the need to supplement the reserve with additional funds from the eu budget (not taken from direct payments) in the face of severe crises;- the possibility of introducing the principle of progressiveness, with differentiated, higher rates for the highest payments.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because i consider it essential to safeguard financing for the agricultural sector in the event of natural or other disasters affecting agricultural production and distribution.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report setting the adjustment rate for direct payments provided for in regulation (eu) no 1306/2013 for the calendar year 2015. this ensures that the special reserve to support farmers in the event of a serious crisis is financed, making it unnecessary to use additional financial discipline measures.
‒ i agree with the reduction of direct payments, as provided for in article 26 (1) of regulation (eu) no 1306/2013, with the aim of creating a reserve to provide additional support to the agricultural sector in the event of serious crises affecting agricultural production or distribution, as provided for in article 25 of the same regulation. moreover, it is recommended to adjust the adjustment rate for direct payments where the forecasts for the financing of measures financed under this sub-ceiling for a given financial year indicate that the applicable annual ceilings will be exceeded. the proposed rate of reduction of 1,393041% to the part of direct payments over eur 2000 under the support schemes listed in annex i to regulation (eu) no 1307/2013 to farmers corresponding to the aid applications submitted for the calendar year 2015 deserves my vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour because i consider it crucial to ensure respect for the principle of equal treatment of farmers. in this regard, since financial discipline measures are necessary in order not to exceed the amounts of the reserve for crises in the agricultural sector in respect of a given calendar year, the adjustment rate should not be applied to payments for which aid applications have been submitted in calendar years other than the calendar year to which financial discipline applies.
‒ in order to support the agricultural sector in situations of serious crises that may affect production and/or distribution, the european commission has proposed the creation of a financial reserve of eur 2 800 million, established by applying, at the beginning of each year, a reduction in direct payments through a financial discipline mechanism. the large added value of this regulation is the result of applying the adjustment rate only to direct payments above eur 2000 which safeguards and exempts small producers. the application of this adjustment rate, which shall be 1,393041%, will lead to a reduction in the amounts of direct payments for budget lines relating to expenditure relating to aid applications submitted by farmers for the calendar year 2015. i therefore support this proposal and i give my vote in favour.
‒ the crisis reserve of the common agricultural policy, which is set up through this procedure, is a last resort in cases of extreme crisis which, by its nature, requires the contribution and solidarity of all farmers and direct payment beneficiaries. the proposal exempts from this contribution all beneficiaries whose annual amount received is equal to or less than eur 2000 and i am of the opinion that this exemption should be set at a higher amount. the russian embargo has tested the crisis management instruments we have in the european union to deal with serious imbalances in agricultural markets, where sectors such as milk and fruit and vegetables have been particularly affected. so far, it has been possible to use instruments other than the crisis reserve. i hope that the new european commission will have the political will to develop appropriate instruments for prevention and for situations of widespread crisis. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the farmers are not left behind.
in writing. ‒ the need for a reserve for crisis situations is not in question. it is the fact that this cap is itself a permanent factor in the crisis. the last reform has maintained scandalous inequalities in the distribution of cap funds between countries, production and producers. liberalisation and market orientation are the watchwords. millions of small and mediumsized farmers know the meaning of these words: prices that do not compensate for production, the ruin of millions of farms, the concentration of production, the increase in food dependence and the imbalance in the agri-food balances of several countries. competitiveness is another buzzword. but some receive double or triple the per-acre payments that others receive. it's easy to be competitive like that. in portugal, many thousands of small and medium-sized farmers struggle to survive and stay in business, with production prices that often do not cover production costs. for these, it is not the 500 euro parks, which will receive a one-off payment, that will end the crisis.
in writing. ‒ several indicators show that member states have moved towards greater gender equality. this form of inequality, however, remains a frequent reality, affecting women above all. parliament should play an active role in promoting equality, in particular by contributing to the definition of a european strategy. however, it should not interfere with the competences of the member states, nor take advantage of reports which should aim at the widest possible consensus, to make considerations which are imminently within the domain of national law or of the convictions of each one, such as the case of abortion. i agree with the general thrust of this report, but i have decided to abstain.
‒ progress in the eu has been slow and there is still much to be done in the coming years. the eu is preparing a new strategy for equality between men and women after 2015. gender equality is one of the founding principles of the european union. the 2014-2015 gender equality strategy contains a set of commitments that are evaluated each year in a report by the european commission. the european union needs a new strategy with effective measures to deal with the issue and suggest ways to continue the evaluation. at the same time, new and lasting forms are needed, with binding and non-binding measures, which take into account the various forms of discrimination faced by women. it is recalled that the european parliament has already voted in favour of a gender balance in the boards of directors and the fight against violence against women.
‒ this report takes a critical, though light-hearted, look at some of the policies pursued over the past five years on gender equality in the eu. it considers that at eu level, some goals remain to be achieved on the way to genuine gender equality, covering all aspects of life, the right to integrity and a life in dignity. it refers to outdated economic models based on an outdated sexual division of labour; violence against women; gender pay gaps; domestic work, childcare and elderly care, which are mainly the responsibility of women; and the failure of policies aimed at a work-life balance. it reaffirms that poverty is mainly a female problem, which has been aggravated by the economic crisis, precarious part-time jobs, low wages and pensions, difficulty in accessing basic social and health services and the disappearance of jobs, particularly in the public sector, among other important aspects. we voted in favour, although there are some aspects of the report from which we disassociate ourselves. this is the case with quotas, the paragraph legitimising the european semester and the concept of 'forced prostitution'.
‒ i voted in favour, despite the rejection of several amendments by the gue/ngl linked to such important issues as austerity measures and their negative impact on gender equality and equal rights for migrants in the eu, as well as others linked to lgbti rights. i think very important issues have been included, such as an inclusive definition of family, which recognises single parenting and lgbti parenting, as well as the right to legal and safe abortion, not to mention the call to the european commission to include sexual and reproductive health and rights in the eu health strategy.
‒ while i support all initiatives to eradicate violence against women and against gender discrimination at legislative, cultural and political levels, i believe that matters which are sociologically sensitive and deeply divisive have been introduced into the text and should be dealt with separately. that is why i am voting against.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the union needs a new strategy to give greater impetus to the promotion of gender equality. the statistics show that we have made considerable progress. however, huge inequalities remain. in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity, i consider it essential to support initiatives and strategies for reconciling work and family life, in particular through a network of school support, tax support and job flexibility. i also agree that we should focus on the importance of family planning and training through education. i cannot, however, agree with the criterion of equal treatment and gender equality as a prerequisite for the award of public contracts, nor with the conditioning of our support to developing countries. i would like to stress once again that our relations with third countries must take account of the achievement of gender equality. i believe that this document deals with controversial issues which concern each member state in particular, and i therefore abstained in the final vote.
in writing. as a supporter of the development of a strategy for equality between men and women and having therefore supported the alternative resolution tabled by my political group, i voted against the strategy put forward by the socialist rapporteur because i do not see myself in these proposals put forward by the left.
‒ the economic crisis and the resulting austerity measures have not treated men and women equally. women were at a disadvantage and this was accentuated. many european governments have implemented measures that exacerbate the negative effect of the economic crisis on women. we are witnessing a regression in the progress made towards gender equality and we must be able to give a sensitive and firm response in an attempt to reverse this trend. we have to do something. we can't just sit around and wait for things to work themselves out. the economic crisis cannot be used as a pretext to aggravate (even more) social and gender inequalities by taking away the rights that have been won. on the contrary, it is times of crisis that serve as a test of our humanity. the dominant growth model and the policy guidelines that have underpinned it do not serve these purposes. there is always an alternative that does not involve violating human rights. we make the choices. it is possible to reconcile economic growth with high human development and gender equality rates. you just have to want it. the adoption of the noichl report was a very important step in this direction.
‒ this report takes a critical approach to gender equality policies within the eu, demonstrating, through the analysis of some indicators, that member states have moved towards greater gender equality. in this respect, i believe that the european parliament, as well as the european institutions and the governments of the member states, should play a proactive role in promoting gender equality, while the european institutions should scrupulously respect the principle of subsidiarity as enshrined in the treaties. to that extent, and because i consider that this own-initiative report introduces matters which should be within the sphere of competence of each member state, i have decided not to support the adoption of this report.
in writing. - i strongly support the report by mrs maria noichl. it is a report which is incisive in its diagnosis: it is true that we cannot continue to be trapped in outdated economic models, which are unsustainable from an environmental point of view and are based on an obsolete gender division of labour, which has been superseded by the integration of women into the labour market. it is also clear and determined in what can already be done differently. it called for the immediate correction of a recent injustice by urging the commission and the council to ensure that gender equality is mainstreamed in all strategy 2020 programmes. finally, the report is ambitious, as it could not be otherwise, as regards the role that the european union should play in the world, in collaboration with the member states, including their competent authorities, in promoting gender equality, within or beyond the union's borders, and as regards the need to pursue these objectives, both through the concept of gender mainstreaming in all areas and through specific concrete measures.
in writing. ‒ it is important that this strategy for gender equality moves from paper to practice, which has not happened. this report contains many truths with which we agree. the reality is that equality issues - and in particular the realisation of women's rights - cannot be put on the back burner, as they are deeply linked to the major political and economic choices. and it would be good if the two major political groups would remember this strategy when they reach consensus on so many of the obligations imposed on the member states. because if the eu cuts public services, such as childcare, it is women who suffer the most. one of the major problems with the report is that it does not hold the eu and the troika accountable for the policies that have led to the situation we are in today, namely the backsliding on women's rights. the report also argues that child and elderly care services and health services should be 'affordable services' and not public services, as we advocate. we cannot but stress our disagreement with the term 'forced prostitution'. nevertheless, and in view of the general thrust of the report, we voted in favour.
‒ technological developments, increasingly globalised trade, e-commerce and outsourcing have created the need for new measures to combat rights violations in third countries. among other measures, the strategy seeks to help identify countries where the protection and/or enforcement of intellectual property rights is weak. i share the view that it is important for the eu and the european parliament to show that they are serious about this and that they want to help improve the intellectual property rights system.

‒ i voted in favour of the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights (ipr) in third countries. i share the approach taken in the european parliament resolution to step up the protection of european ipr in relations with its trading partners, with the aim of developing the competitiveness of the knowledge and innovation-based economies and combating the parallel economies that feed organised crime through counterfeit products, which can also involve serious risks to the health and safety of consumers.
‒ the intellectual property industry accounts for about 39% of the eu's gross domestic product and directly and indirectly employs about 35% of all employment in the eu. despite its vitality and size, the european union loses €8 billion of its gross domestic product annually to counterfeiting and piracy. this report deserves my vote in favour because it recognises that intellectual property is one of the keys to growth and innovation and because it stresses the importance of combating counterfeiting and piracy.

‒ intellectual property rights make a decisive contribution to the development of creativity and innovation. their protection is a key challenge in the course of our day which deserves our attention and concern. i agree with the rapporteur that the european union must have an ambitious and coherent strategy to protect intellectual property rights, just as i believe that this strategy should not only be extended to eu member states but also to third countries.
‒ the purpose of this own-initiative report is to contribute to the definition of a strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights (ipr) in third countries. recent studies show that ipr-intensive sectors account for some 39% of eu gdp and account for 35% of total employment. however, it is estimated that the eu is losing around €8 billion of its annual gdp to counterfeiting and piracy. it is therefore urgent to define a 'strategy for the enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries', given that this is a key sector for the eu's growth, innovation and industrial competitiveness at global level. i agree with this resolution overall and stress the need to improve data collection on goods held at eu borders, to improve the international ipr framework, especially at the level of the conclusion of bilateral trade agreements (where adequate and effective protection of protected rights holders must be ensured), as well as the recognition and effective protection of geographical indications and access to the wto dispute settlement body for ipr infringement cases.

in writing. ‒ the eu action plan focuses mainly on responding to infringements on a commercial scale and raising awareness among citizens of the problem of intellectual property. an effective campaign is needed, especially among the younger generation, involving the criminalisation of the individual user. another aspect which i agree with is the need to support small and mediumsized enterprises in the enforcement of their rights.
‒ this is an own-initiative report on the enforcement of intellectual property rights (ipr), covering economic, social and health issues. the report is extensive in its content. while some general principles may merit our support, particularly as regards the remuneration of artists (copyright is an integral part of intellectual property), there are other aspects which cannot merit our support: for example, the proposal for operators to exchange information among themselves in order to prevent infringement of intellectual property rights as early as possible. we have put forward a proposal in the national parliament on sharing, a proposal which is innovative, not only at national level but also at european level. this report, while talking about internet operators and the 'follow the money' strategy, does not go as far as it could and should, and merely urges operators to reduce the profits made on the basis of sharing. we are proposing the taxation of operators, which is clearly something different. the report also calls on operators to find ways of banning access to websites and preventing the provision of content in more permanent ways than the current ones (which is the opposite of what we are proposing), reasons why we cannot support this report.
in writing. ‒ this report is based, among other things, on the idea that strengthening intellectual property rights is crucial for economic development, an idea with which i could not disagree more. on the other hand, it is very vague on the question of data protection, which i consider essential. finally, this proposal for an 'eu action plan' does not provide for a flexible approach that fairly includes the different creators. for all these reasons, i voted against.
‒ i voted in favour of the report entitled 'towards a renewed consensus on the effective protection of intellectual property rights (ipr): an eu action plan'. i share the view expressed in the european parliament's resolution that in order to promote ipr, it is necessary to raise awareness among europeans themselves of its social and economic importance, through an internal action plan, which will be reflected in the future in the effective protection of these rights.
in writing. ‒ infringements of intellectual property rights represent a moral and economic damage for european companies and entail heavy economic and fiscal losses for member states. those offences, including counterfeiting, discourage growth, job creation, innovation and creativity. it is therefore essential to step up efforts to combat the illegal trade in counterfeit goods and to make it clear that no one should profit from infringements of intellectual property rights. this report, which presents a european union action plan on property rights, emphasises the importance of this subject for our market, innovation, competitiveness, growth and cultural diversity. i am voting in favour of this report because of the importance of intellectual property and because of the range of measures it contains.
‒ i voted in favour of the view that the implementation of an action plan for the protection of intellectual property rights is crucial to stimulating growth and innovation.
‒ the treaty of lisbon and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union guarantee the protection of intellectual property. in addition to being an important means of wealth generation and job creation, intellectual property rights (ipr) are also a driver of innovation, creativity and competitiveness. now more than ever, consumers need to be informed about what ipr is and what can and cannot be done with protected goods and content, and i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to develop awareness and information campaigns for consumers.
in writing. ‒ this is an own-initiative report which aims to contribute to the creation of a european action plan, based on ten points, aimed at defending intellectual property rights. in the light of the subject-matter itself, which encompasses a very wide range of rights, i believe that the main aspects and sectors targeted by this system, especially in economic and social matters, have been listed and defended. the proposals on copyright, consumer protection and aid to smes are particularly noteworthy. i would also like to point out as very positive points the cooperation between national authorities to share best practice, the encouragement of training programmes on intellectual property for each member state in the context of the single market and the commission's proposal to develop, promote and publish a guide to best practice for public authorities to prevent counterfeit transactions. i agree with this report on the whole, which is why i voted in favour of it.
