madam president, commissioner, madam representative of the council, i too would like to congratulate the rapporteurs of this important document: elisabetta gardini and giovanni la via. ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the ratification by the european union of the second period of the kyoto protocol. this is an important and unequivocal signal to our external partners of the union's commitment to halting global warming, already embedded in its 2020 energy and climate strategy. we must continue to make efforts and there is much work to be done to secure ambitious and binding commitments at the paris conference of the united nations framework convention on climate change, which will take place later this year and involve 195 countries. in europe, we are making good progress in reducing co2 emissions in certain areas, such as the industrial, energy and housing sectors. we must continue this work. on the other hand, we continue to see co2 emissions in the transport sector rise because of forms of mobility that we have not yet changed, or because we are tied to sectoral interests, or because of technological barriers, or because of the need for huge investments to effect the transition to a new mobility paradigm. but let us not forget that there are also green growth opportunities that will be unleashed by this investment. if we don't take advantage of them, someone else will. at the international level, decisions are imperative and can only be taken at the highest level. the negotiating process cannot be dragged on indefinitely and there are countries for whom climate change is a threat to their very existence. i therefore call for talks to be resumed at ministerial level and at the level of heads of state or government so that we can reach an agreement and overcome a stalemate which has lasted for too long.
in writing. the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change was signed in 1997, setting a binding target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions at international level. but we know that kyoto has not been ratified by all the major polluters in the world. in particular, it has not been ratified by the us - the world's largest polluter (in absolute terms and per capita) - for decades. in 2012, as the kyoto protocol expired and in the absence of a comprehensive and effective agreement capable of replacing it , it was decided to extend the kyoto protocol, thus prolonging all its weaknesses, including the perverse flexibility mechanisms. the eu has proposed a 20% reduction in its emissions (compared to 1990) for the second commitment period of kyoto. despite the frequent publicity about the eu's 'leadership' role in combating climate change, this figure fell short of the united nations panel on climate change's recommendation of a reduction of at least 25% by 2020. but above all, the biggest problem is that the eu still has a market-based approach to climate change, which is ineffective and perverse, and the carbon market is a prime example of this.
madam president, several important issues arise when we approach a strategy for energy security in europe: the critical importance of progress in energy efficiency in transport, industry and buildings; the need to diversify the sources of energy supply both internally and externally; the increased use of renewable energy and the recognition of the inevitable exhaustion of fossil fuels; the need for major investments in energy production and distribution chains and in research and development of less mature technologies; the need to lift certain member states out of energy isolation. finally, these and other issues will only be properly addressed and implemented within the framework of public, democratic control of the energy sector, including planning, production and distribution of energy. it is not the miraculous virtues of the internal energy market that will ensure the objectives of progress, social justice, sustainability, development. energy is a precious public good which must be rescued from the hands of private monopolies.
mr president, commissioner, the development of the single energy market is one of the areas where the european union has fallen behind in relation to the dynamics of globalisation, technology and the needs of sustainability and competitiveness. external pressure, particularly the conflict with russia, forced a change of attitude. we must therefore seize this opportunity, not only to respond to the immediate challenge, but to give a decisive boost to europe's leadership in the energy transition. we have learned the lesson not to repeat the same mistakes in other dossiers. for example, the digital union dossier which links so strongly with the energy union and which pointed to security threats due to our delays in creating a regulated and transparent single market. but let us return to energy security. the strategic pillars highlighted in this report are appropriate: more efficiency, more own production with priority for renewable and environmentally friendly energy, technological leadership, an integrated market with strong interconnections, diversification of sources and geographical origins of the necessary imports. the implementation of this strategy implies a single market and an energy union. the levels of planning and regulation must be supranational and strengthened. but it also means giving a new impetus to the sustainable growth of the european economy, with a new model of spatial organisation, mobility and social organisation. let's not let ambition die. security and change go hand in hand. energy security and economic change, too. let's take a chance.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, energy policy is now of central importance for european competitiveness and for the union's climate objectives. we need energy at competitive prices, energy that is safe, energy that is clean. electricity interconnections are essential to balance higher levels of renewable energy penetration into the grid, thus helping to reduce its cost to the final consumer and the taxpayer. i would therefore like to stress the need for binding, not indicative, interconnection capacity targets. furthermore, the gas interconnections and the existing capacity to receive liquefied natural gas in the iberian peninsula can also contribute to the diversification of supply sources, energy security and price convergence in europe. i therefore stress the urgent need to implement the third energy package, to support investments in interconnection infrastructure and to ensure close and real-time monitoring by the european commission of the implementation of these priority projects.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the attacks in paris have re-ignited the debate on police access to databases. with the tragedies in the mediterranean, border management has made headlines. and suddenly, an entry-exit system and a registered traveler program appeared as a solution to both problems. it seems that we have forgotten its original purpose: to facilitate border controls and to know how many overstayers we have in the european union. we continue to ignore the impact of the judgment of the court of justice of the union that annulled the data retention directive, despite the fact that several officials have repeatedly assured us that this impact would not be ignored. and we are persistently moving forward with more and more comprehensive data collection and processing tools. i have no doubt that the safety of citizens should be a priority and that we need to act. but we cannot ignore the work that has been done, we must not underestimate the instruments we have in place whose potential we have not yet fully exploited, nor must we give up identifying and correcting shortcomings in the systems we have before proposing new and costly systems. there is therefore a need for urgent clarifications, such as those requested by colleagues días de mera and tanja fajon. the commission must react to these changes and fulfil the commitment of vice-president timmermans to ensure systematic checks on fundamental rights throughout the legislative process, to clearly define the purpose of the systems and to present an impact assessment that fully demonstrates their need.
‒ the kyoto protocol, signed in 1997, established a binding international emission reduction target. the protocol was ratified by the eu in 2002. in march 2012, the council decided to propose a joint quantified commitment of a 20% reduction of the union's emissions below 1990 levels for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. this council position was followed by the member states at the doha conference where the amendment to the protocol was adopted. the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the protocol, which includes legally binding emission reduction commitments, under which the eu and its member states are jointly committed to limit their average annual greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the years 2013 to 2020 to 80% of their reference annual emissions. i supported this recommendation, as with this decision to ratify the doha amendment, the eu sends a clear signal regarding the efforts and leadership of the eu and its member states in addressing climate change at international level.
in writing. ‒ i recognise the urgency for member states to ratify the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol by the end of 2015, with the second commitment period having the support of eu countries in particular. member states are already implementing a 20% reduction in emissions by 2020. a new agreement is in the works with experts and meps joining forces to negotiate the text that will succeed the kyoto protocol, which is expected to be adopted in december 2015 and implemented from 2020.
‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol (20132020). in 2012, in the absence of a comprehensive and effective agreement capable of replacing it, it was decided to extend the kyoto protocol, extending with it all its fragility, including the perverse flexibility mechanisms. it is, however, the only legally binding emission reduction commitment. the eu, its member states and iceland commit to limiting their average annual greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the period 2013 to 2020 to 80% of their emissions in the base year (generally 1990). this commitment was determined on the basis of the total level of ghg emissions allowed during the period 2013-2020 under the eu climate and energy package and falls short of the one recommended by the united nations panel on climate change, despite all the hype about the eu's 'leadership' role in combating climate change. we supported this resolution, even though we know that we are very different from the majority in parliament on the approach to climate change. the effects of the liberalisation and deregulation of international trade and the absence of criticism of the carbon market are emphasised.
‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change and on the joint fulfilment of its commitments. a significant reduction in collective greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions is a clear sign of the eu's efforts and leadership in meeting the kyoto objectives to combat climate change at international level.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change, as the formal entry into force of the doha amendment is among the european union's priority objectives, considering that the kyoto protocol constitutes a fundamental contribution to global efforts to combat climate change. the ratification decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and the joint fulfilment of the commitments undertaken by the european union will send a clear signal with regard to the efforts and leadership of the european union and its member states in addressing climate change at international level.
‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol, starting on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020, with legally binding emission reduction commitments under which the european union, its member states and iceland commit to limit their average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the period 2013 to 2020 to 80% of their emissions in the base year (generally 1990). that commitment was determined on the basis of the total level of greenhouse gas emissions permitted for the period 2013 to 2020 under the eu climate and energy package. given the importance of making ambitious commitments to combat climate change, in particular in order to achieve the objective of keeping the global temperature rise below 2°c, i voted in favour of this decision to approve the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol.
‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol, starting on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020, with commitments to reduce annual average greenhouse gas emissions over the period 2013-2020. like the rapporteur, i believe that this decision on the joint fulfilment of the european union's commitments will send a clear signal regarding the efforts and leadership of the eu and its member states in tackling climate change at international level. it is a pity that the countries with the highest pollution rates systematically abstain from participating.
in writing. the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change entered into force on 16 february 2005, establishing a set of legally binding emission reduction commitments for the period 2008 to 2012. in 2012, at the doha climate change conference, it was decided to approve an amendment to the kyoto protocol, which would establish a second commitment period, 2013-2020, with equally binding commitments to reduce emissions. the european union, its member states and iceland commit to limit their average annual greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the period 2013-2020 to 80% of their emissions in the base year (generally 1990). this commitment was determined on the basis of the total level of greenhouse gas emissions permitted for the period 2013-2020 under the eu climate and energy package. in view of the commitments mentioned above, i am signing this legislative resolution to proceed with the early entry into force of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol.
‒ all efforts will be limited to achieving the ambitious targets that can mitigate the effects of climate change and one day reverse its effects. this amendment, proposed in doha, is a good step, but it is not enough. we have to be even more ambitious. we owe it to future generations, that is, to our children and grandchildren. in addition to what is stated on paper, it is necessary to ensure rapid adoption and implementation by the member states. it is also essential to encourage the other polluting countries to meet ambitious targets. the united states, china and japan are, along with the european union, the main culprits for the planet's unfortunate environmental condition. as was the case with the call for global ocean governance put forward by commissioner vella during blue week in lisbon last week, the mechanisms for global environmental governance must be strengthened. the timing is exceptional. for exceptional moments, exceptional people and exceptional capacities for mobilization and action are needed. we roll up our sleeves!
‒ iceland is a party to the kyoto protocol which has respected its individual targets during the first commitment period. in 2009, iceland expressed its intention to jointly fulfil its commitments to the european union and its member states in the second commitment period, regardless of whether or not it joins the eu. the council welcomed this request and concluded that the joint length in the second period should include iceland. the agreement between the european union and the member states on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments in the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol is a clear signal for coordinated european efforts to combat climate change at international level.
‒ the proposal for a council decision provides the basis for the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol to the unfccc. during this period, the country had to limit its emissions increase to below 10% on average. in the end, emissions decreased on average by 2% during this period. the agreement on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments in the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change will be a clear signal for coordinated european efforts to combat climate change at international level.
‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol (20132020). in 2012, in the absence of a comprehensive and effective agreement capable of replacing it, it was decided to extend the kyoto protocol, extending with it all its fragility, including the perverse flexibility mechanisms. it is, however, the only legally binding emission reduction commitment. the eu, its member states and iceland commit to reducing their average annual greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by 20% in the period 2013 to 2020. that commitment was determined on the basis of the total level of ghg emissions permitted for the period 2013 to 2020 under the eu climate and energy package, which falls short of the level recommended by the united nations panel on climate change. although iceland is not an eu member state, it intends to fulfil its commitment in this second period of the kyoto protocol, together with the eu and its member states. i'm not against it. that is why we supported this report. as for its participation in the emissions trading scheme, although this is a sovereign decision of iceland, we reiterate our criticism and deep disagreement with it.
‒ i have cast my vote in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments under the second period of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc). the eu is a strategic player in the international climate change negotiations and this agreement is further proof of its serious commitment to delivering on its commitments together.
‒ iceland is a party to the kyoto protocol, respecting the commitments made during the first commitment period. the commission, on behalf of the european union and its member states, and iceland concluded in 2014 the negotiations necessary for joint compliance with the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. iceland participates in the eu emission trading scheme (ets) and the greenhouse gas emissions monitoring and reporting mechanism. the rights and obligations that apply to member states in the framework of joint compliance should be applicable to iceland through eu legislation. iceland has shown an interest in participating in joint compliance with the eu and its member states, regardless of whether it is an eu member or not. i am voting in favour of this report because i share the rapporteur's view that the agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments under the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change will be a clear signal for coordinated european efforts to combat climate change at international level.
‒ the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period under the kyoto protocol, starting on 1 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020, with legally binding emission reduction commitments under which the european union, its member states and iceland commit to limit their average annual greenhouse gas emissions in the period 2013 to 2020 to 80% of their emissions in the base year (generally 1990). this proposal for a council decision provides the basis for the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and its member states, of the one part, and iceland, of the other part, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of commitments for this second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. i voted in favour of the conclusion of the agreement, considering it to be another sign of the european union's determination to combat climate change and to define an ambitious policy in this field.
in writing. ‒ although iceland is not an eu member state, it intends to fulfil this second commitment of the kyoto protocol together with the eu and its member states. the rights and obligations that apply to member states in joint compliance have to be applicable to iceland through eu legislation. it is yet another clear signal from the eu to european efforts to combat climate change at international level.

in the light of the recent developments in the field of nuclear safety, the commission has decided to extend the scope of the proposal to include the use of radioactive waste in the transport of nuclear materials. this is a particularly important moment, but it is still insufficient. more countries need to be engaged in fully meeting the targets set out in kyoto and other relevant conventions to combat and mitigate climate change. as with the so-called ozone hole, we need to take swift and decisive action that will make a real difference. does it cost anything? yes, it does have costs, and those are very, very high. yet, what is the price of looking at our children and grandchildren a few years hence and saying that we did not do all that was in our power? i'm not willing to pay that price. it has to be done and done now. i congratulate the european union for aligning itself with iceland, a country that has managed to reduce emissions with a practically wasteful use of fossil fuels.

the european union is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy, which is based on the principles of the united nations charter and the international covenant on civil and political rights. in addition to these military actions, a number of domestic legislative measures restricting freedom of expression and the persecution of minorities are calling into question the spirit of good neighbourly relations between the eu and russia, which are incompatible with the values of the rule of law, democracy and respect for individual freedoms. i support the sanctions against russia and believe that the eu must keep the pressure on the values of peace and the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms.

‒ this report confirms the confrontational position that the eu, subservient to the geostrategic interests of nato and the usa, has been deepening towards russia. it is a book about the breakdown of relations between the eu and russia and an approach to the situation in crimea that is completely removed from the context of the conflict in ukraine, where the far right seized power in a coup d'état legitimized by the eu. all this is part of the policy of siege and the bellicose offensive that nato and the united states have been carrying out. this report makes it clear that, among other things, the basis of the conflict with russia is an economic war over spheres of influence, which overrides the sovereign right of each people to decide its own destiny, free from interference. the question of the eu's energy dependence is worth mentioning, as the justification for pursuing the european energy security policy, which among other things provides for the transfer of energy dependence to the us, is being sought. so are the unacceptable instruments of interference, of which the explicit support for the alleged 'ngos' that the eu funds and which, acting inside russia, are elements of mere political destabilisation is a simple example. we voted against it.

', which may describe russia's action, but also describes exactly what the european union has been doing through sanctions, political, economic or military pressure in various parts of the world, especially in the region in the eu's and russia's neighbourhood. there are many rivalries between the eu's international policy and russia's international policy, not because they are so different, but precisely because they are so similar and they are competing for dominance in the same geographical space, where they use their influence in rival groups that fight politically and militarily on the ground, waving the russian and eu flags, without any respect for the interests of the peoples, development and peace in the region. my strong disapproval of the eu's foreign policy does not imply any sympathy or support for its rivals who do not respect fundamental human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the state of relations between the european union and russia. russia, with its actions in crimea and eastern ukraine, can hardly be considered a 'strategic partner'. strategic partnerships should be based on mutual trust and respect for international law, which recognises democracy, the sovereignty of states, territorial integrity, respect for the rule of law and human rights.
‒ over the past decades, the european union has been working to build a strategic partnership with russia based on shared values and principles, such as democracy and the rule of law. however, the recent positions adopted by russia require a position from the european union. i am voting in favour of this report, which strongly condemns the illegal annexation of crimea, russia's support for ukrainian separatists and the recent ban on entry to russia for several european politicians. i therefore express my support for the maintenance or even the strengthening of european sanctions against russia at the next european council in june. i believe that a normal relationship between the european union and russia can only be established when the russian authorities leave the territory of ukraine and respect the primacy of human rights and territorial freedom.
‒ russia's involvement in the armed conflict in ukraine and the illegal annexation of crimea, as well as the violation of georgia's territorial integrity and the economic coercion and political destabilisation of its european neighbours, constitute a deliberate violation of democratic principles, fundamental values and international law. equally worrying is the deterioration of the rule of law, human rights, political rights and civil liberties that has been witnessed in russia in recent years, as well as the arbitrary measure taken by the authorities to ban eu politicians and officials from entering russian territory. in this context, the eu cannot of course fail to critically reassess its relations with russia. in the long term, it would of course be important for the eu and russia to be able to establish a constructive relationship, but the relaunch of this cooperation can only be achieved in a context of dialogue and full respect for international law, implying russia's respect for ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the full implementation of the minsk agreements and the cessation of all destabilising activities at the borders of the member states.
in writing. ‒ it is important that the european union and its member states rethink the bilateral agreements concluded with russia. the violation (in 2008) of georgia's territorial integrity and the illegal annexation of crimea were situations constantly denounced. in addition, there are situations on russian territory that are less denounced but that we cannot ignore, such as the constant disregard for human rights and gender equality, and also towards religious minorities. it is imperative that the european union takes an active stance in future strategic partnerships that may be concluded with russia, never forgetting the breach of principles given the recent events in ukraine.
‒ this report draws attention to the deliberate and systematic violation of democratic principles and fundamental values of international law by russia through its direct and indirect participation in the armed conflict in ukraine, the illegal annexation of crimea, the violation of the territorial integrity of georgia, and the economic coercion and political destabilisation of its european neighbours. the eu must therefore review its approach to relations with russia, which will require the development of a non-binding contingency plan and a detailed plan for future relations with russia and its eastern european partners. despite the growing concern and social alarm over the violations of human and minority rights, there is a belief that a constructive and predictable relationship between the eu and russia will be possible in the long term, within a framework of mutual dialogue and cooperation based on respect for international law. to do so, russia will have to respect the territorial integrity and sovereignty of ukraine, including crimea, comply with the minsk agreements and cease military destabilising activities on the eu's borders.
in writing. ‒ global energy demand is increasing, forecast to increase by 27% by 2030. currently, more than 50% of the eu's energy needs are met by external suppliers, making the eu vulnerable in terms of its energy policy. i believe that a common, coordinated and strong eu strategy is vital to moderate demand through energy efficiency on the one hand and to increase own energy production and define measures for an integrated, coordinated and effective internal energy market on the other. the current geopolitics have demonstrated what the european parliament has been saying on many occasions. the eastern partners are not reliable when they use energy supply as a political weapon. so sources and supply routes must be diversified, and efforts must also be stepped up to implement projects for strategic energy infrastructure in europe. i regret that not all member states are equally committed to the objective of interconnectedness of networks and systems, in particular in connecting the iberian peninsula to the rest of the eu. the energy island phenomenon must be brought to an end.
‒ the eu's over-reliance on imports from russia, demand moderation, prices, renewable energy, the achievement of a fully integrated internal energy market, levels of electricity and gas interconnection and investment are some of the issues addressed in this report. it should be noted that the eu imports 53% of its total energy consumption. the main challenges in this area are the creation of an energy union, demand moderation, increasing own energy production, developing energy technologies, achieving a fully integrated internal energy market, diversifying external supply and the need for coordination and solidarity between all member states.
‒ the report contains some guidelines which deserve our agreement. the exclusive competence of the member states to define their energy targets, the need to find solutions and compromises in terms of technologies (technologically neutral approach) and prices, which will make it possible to support reindustrialisation processes, and the key role of renewable energies are highlighted. other guidelines raise serious doubts and others deserve our full disagreement and opposition. the main points of view are: the market is seen as playing a decisive role in the management of energy issues, even if mitigated by possible mechanisms of solidarity; consumers are seen as becoming investors in energy assets; there is no clear and specific reference to the issue of the lack of energy resources (in the case of fossil fuels); and there is no consideration of strong state intervention, particularly in energy production and distribution and planning. but overall, the negative and even very negative aspects are the ones that prevail, and they end up weighing clearly more heavily than anything positive that the resolution might have.
in writing. ‒ we cannot continue to treat energy as a source of profit and income for multinationals and monopolies. energy is a common good and any european energy strategy must take this into account. the strategy outlined in this report is also to defend nuclear energy or the exploitation of shale gas. it is true that the report mentions a change in the energy model, but it is all a deliberate and misleading misunderstanding, because the 'new' model to which the report is aiming is a model of dependence, which is unsustainable, asymmetrical and socially unfair, in other words, the complete opposite of what it should be. i could not help but vote against it.
‒ despite the increasing focus on renewable energy and the diversification of energy sources, the european union still imports 53% of its total energy consumption, namely 85% of oil, 67% of gas, 41% of solid fuels and around 95% of uranium. it should also be noted that the eu is highly dependent on russian energy sources. i am in favour of fusion and i believe that more strategic studies are needed on the banning of nuclear energy and the future use of shale gas. however, because i believe that it is necessary to go further into energy issues in such fundamental areas as energy security and energy independence, i have decided to abstain in the final vote. i would also like to take this opportunity to stress the special importance which must be attached to the outermost regions, which have natural economic, social and territorial constraints and where energy supply is becoming more difficult and more costly.
in writing. ‒ the eu's external energy bill is over €1 billion per day €400 billion in 2013 and more than a fifth of the eu's total imports, largely dependent on a single country, the russian federation, which is the largest source of imports of oil (35%), gas (26%), coal (30%) and uranium (25%), often using its energy resources as a political weapon. the prosperity and security of the eu require the rational use of energy and a stable, affordable and sustainable energy supply. energy security is also political independence. it is therefore essential to develop an energy security strategy based on technology and the decarbonisation of energy resources. energy efficiency, renewable energy and smart infrastructure are three pillars that do not compromise our future.
‒ following the serious ukrainian crisis, the european commission proposed a european strategy for energy security in may 2014 and the committee on industry, research and energy of the european parliament decided to draw up an own-initiative report on this issue. this report was structured to try to respond to the future challenges of the union in terms of its energy policy, stressing from the outset the importance of achieving the objective of the 'european energy union', the promotion of energy saving and efficiency, the increase of domestic energy production, the focus on technological innovation/research and development, the identification of constraints and the creation of european legislation that allows the development of a fully integrated european energy market, as well as in external terms, the diversification of energy sources and the absolute need for a single discourse across the union. unfortunately, differences between the various political groups on the setting of binding energy efficiency targets, the use of nuclear energy or the legislative framework for shale gas exploitation led to the failure of this report and i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ there have long been doubts about the investigative activities of this body, in particular the dragging of investigations, sometimes for years, and the disregard of the rules on the protection of the persons concerned. now questions are being raised about the disregard for the supervisory rules and the independence of this body. this resolution is based on the 2014 annual report of the supervisory committee (cf) of olaf (european anti-fraud office) and its recommendations. in this report, doubts are raised as to the opening of 423 cases in one day by a single decision of the director-general of olaf, without adequate assessments of the information received on any of the cases examined by the jf having been made. most of the cases show no evidence of evaluation activity. the report also states that the olaf dg does not take into account the recommendations of the cf, notes the insufficient information provided to the cf to enable it to perform its task and the absence of dialogue between the two bodies, leaving the cf unable to supervise the independence of olaf, and that there is a clear divergence as to the role and function of the cf by the two bodies. these are among the issues addressed in this resolution, which we consider timely and relevant, and we therefore voted in favour of it.
‒ i voted in favour of the 2014 annual report of the olaf supervisory committee. it is a legal imperative that the requirements laid down for the opening of an investigation be complied with, which olaf must follow. i would stress the need for olaf and the supervisory committee to cooperate in order to improve the information transmitted and to fulfil olaf's commitment to inform the supervisory committee of the number of complaints received and the speed with which they are dealt with.
‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that measures must be taken to ensure olaf's independence and at the same time that the olaf supervisory committee has the conditions and resources it needs to fulfil its mandate.
in writing. the annual activity report of the olaf supervisory committee records that, when olaf was reorganised on 1 february 2012, 423 cases were opened on the same day by a single decision of the director-general (dg) of the office. the opening of these cases was in contradiction with the legal requirement to open an investigation, which requires that there is a sufficiently serious suspicion of fraud, corruption or other illegal activity likely to affect the financial interests of the union. in this regard, parliament stresses olaf's responsibility for complying with the legal requirements concerning the opening of an investigation, noting further that, of the 423 cases opened in february 2012, only 8.4% resulted in recommendations this signals the insubstantiality of olaf's decisions and the lack of transparency in its accountability. finally, the european parliament resolution calls on olaf to consider a redistribution of resources, having pointed out an imbalance in the distribution of human resources; the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules. i voted in favour.
‒ this joint resolution is based on the analysis of the 2014 annual report of the olaf (european anti-fraud office) supervisory committee (cf) and its recommendations. the report also notes that the director-general of olaf has not taken into account the recommendations of the supervisory board (cf), that the cf does not have sufficient information to carry out its duties and that there is a lack of understanding between the two bodies, which means that the cf has a limited scope for supervising olaf's action and independence. the report also requires olaf to comply with legal requirements in order for the cf to fulfil one of its essential functions, namely the monitoring of the duration of olaf investigations. this report by the cor was considered appropriate and relevant, and in view of the above and the more consistent content of the report, i believe that this resolution deserves my welcome and my vote in favour.

‒ the integrity of sports organisations is important, as both professional and amateur sport play a key role in promoting peace, respect for human rights and solidarity worldwide, bringing health and economic benefits to society and being essential in drawing attention to core cultural and educational values as well as promoting social inclusion. unfortunately, for several years fifa has operated as an unreputable, opaque and blatantly corrupt organisation and the recent arrests confirm that fraud and corruption in fifa is systematic. i support this resolution because i believe that the commission and the member states must take action to combat any evidence of corruption by fifa officials or national football federations on eu territory. police cooperation in europe should also be strengthened through the setting up of joint investigation teams and greater cooperation between judicial authorities. i also consider it essential that all countries applying to host major sporting events respect international fundamental rights standards in all activities relating to the organisation and conduct of the event.

in writing. ‒ corruption must be fought wherever it is found. in the last few days, we have been shown how corrupt fifa and the sports bodies have been over the years. increased transparency and accountability are essential, in particular as regards the decision-making process and the remuneration of the management and senior management of these bodies. a serious investigation is needed into the awarding procedures for the world cups, both in the past, such as those held in france or south africa, and in the near future, such as those in russia or qatar, where all the allegations of human rights violations, in particular the use of slave labour for the construction of infrastructure, cannot be ignored.
‒ fifa has been suspected of a number of economic and financial irregularities in relation to the designation of the countries organising the football world championships. this mistrust has existed for a number of years and has recently increased due to the awarding of the world cup to russia (2018) and qatar (2022). i am voting in favour of this resolution which calls for greater transparency in the leadership of world football, the elimination of all suspicion of corruption and the adoption of clearer decision-making processes. i also welcome the fact that there is a new leadership in world football, with new players who are giving the sport credibility on an international scale.
‒ the integrity of sports organisations is of vital importance to the eu and its citizens, given the key role that professional and amateur sport play in promoting peace, respect for human rights and social values. in parallel, sport provides economic and public health benefits, with the added advantage of social inclusion and the enhancement of educational and cultural values facilitated by its peculiarly aggregative character. to our dismay, the latest revelations of corruption at the highest level of fifa undermine the confidence of citizens and fans in sports institutions and threaten the integrity of sport as a whole. considering that fifa has operated for many years as a notoriously opaque, corrupt and uncensored organisation, and considering further that the recent arrests attest to the systematic, widespread and persistent nature of cases of fraud and corruption within fifa, the european parliament takes note in the present position of the rapporteur, which i subscribe to, of the outrage at fifa's practices and the support given to the campaign for the establishment of a fifa reform commission, which is non-governmental, independent and supervised by an international authority.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, the european parliament calls for a strong commitment from the international federation of association football (fifa), as well as from other sports organisations, to combat corruption and to implement a code of conduct and a zero-tolerance policy against corruption in sport. without transparency and good governance by sports organisations we are violating the fundamental values and principles of sport.
in writing. the european parliament's resolution follows the recent revelations of high-level corruption at fifa, following the arrest of 14 fifa officials, including its vice-president, by the swiss authorities in zurich on 27 may. the corruption that is rampant within fifa, which not only undermines the credibility of competitive sport but above all the integrity of world football, and has a devastating impact from the professional football ranks at the top of the pyramid to the amateur clubs at the bottom, deserves total condemnation. in this respect, it is essential to implement structural reforms capable of guaranteeing the transparency, rigour and sense of responsibility that a federation of this kind must possess, which must be guided by strict ethical standards and zero tolerance in matters of corruption, favours or convenient omissions. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, as i consider it absolutely essential that the european institutions and the member states take all the measures in their power to combat any and all evidence of corruption in this case, but also in sport in general.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, europe is the only major bloc that, seven years after the 2008 crisis, has not yet managed to emerge from it. when it leaves, it will have deep scars: unemployment has doubled, skilled young people from less competitive regions have emigrated and investment has fallen to historic lows. the conditions for us to grow up together have never been more difficult. we must be aware that the greater the divergences, the less viable the single currency will be. that is why the juncker commission's choice to finally apply the flexibility contained in the stability and growth pact makes perfect sense. the rules governing strategic investment and structural reforms, and the way in which they are reconciled with the business cycle, are purely a matter of common sense. the berès report touches on some of these aspects, but it is important to remember here that the single currency will not survive unless we review the concept of structural reforms and select those which promote genuine convergence of competitiveness. it will not survive unless we create minimum social rights at european level; unless we stabilise the markets by fulfilling the promise to create a common deposit guarantee up to eur 100 000 in the banking union; unless we bring the troika, the european stability mechanism and the budgetary treaty under the community method; unless we find a common solution to the problem of sovereign debts; unless we create a european instrument capable of reviving crisis economies without triggering a recession; unless we put an end to the practice whereby countries steal taxpayers' money from each other while at the same time punishing each other when their budgets are not balanced. there is an agenda under way, the berès report is only one step, an important step but one step, but the fundamental reforms which are partly covered in the five presidents' report must, in combination with the berès report, be carried out with the utmost urgency if we are to really save the european project.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on the amended proposal for a regulation laying down various european union procedures in the field of the common commercial policy. the main objective is to codify council regulation (ec) no 3286/94 of 22 december 1994 in order to ensure that the union can exercise its rights under international trade rules, in particular those established under the auspices of the world trade organisation (wto). this is a procedure whereby the european parliament decides in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure and on an equal footing with the council. the common commercial policy must be governed by criteria of standardisation and the codification of this regulation has therefore established procedures ensuring the effective exercise of the union's rights under the rules of international trade, in particular by introducing a transparent legal mechanism to which member states may have recourse when trade is impeded or affected by third countries. the consolidation of this regulation has brought clarification of the commission's powers and the examination and consultation procedures.
‒ this report codifies council regulation (eec) no 3286/94 of 22 december 1994 laying down union procedures in the field of the common commercial policy to ensure the exercise by the union of its rights under international trade rules, in particular those established under the auspices of the world trade organisation. we accept the principle of simplification, but we condemn the liberalization of world trade, that is, the opening up of markets to competition between countries with enormous disparities in the level of economic development, and its consequences: the increase in poverty and inequalities worldwide, the attack on the achievements of workers and the sovereignty of peoples, the appropriation by the large multinationals of natural resources and biodiversity, environmental destruction, the increase in unemployment and the ruin of millions of small farmers.
‒ the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (eec) no 3286/94 of 22 december 1994 establishing european union procedures in the field of the common commercial policy to ensure the exercise by the eu of its rights under international trade rules, in particular those established under the auspices of the world trade organisation. we reject the liberalization of world trade, that is, the opening up of markets to competition between countries with enormous disparities in the levels of economic development, with all the consequences that this entails: increasing poverty and inequalities worldwide, the attack on the achievements of workers and the sovereignty of peoples, the appropriation by the large multinationals of natural resources and biodiversity, environmental destruction, the increase in unemployment, the ruin of millions of small farmers and the undermining of food sovereignty and food security. so, although this proposal is merely a simple codification of existing texts, we voted against it.
‒ codification is a means of simplifying and clarifying union law in order to make it more accessible and easier for the ordinary citizen to understand. this objective cannot be achieved as long as there is a dispersion of numerous provisions, amended on several occasions, often substantially, which requires a reading both of the original act and of the acts amending it. the commission has therefore undertaken to carry out an analysis to identify the rules in force, based on a comparison of a multitude of different acts. for this reason, and in order to ensure the clarity and transparency of the law, it is necessary to codify the rules which have been subject to frequent amendments. the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (ec) no 385/96 of 29 january 1996 on protection against injurious pricing in the sale of ships. the new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it. the report preserves the content of the codified acts in full, merely bringing them together and only making the formal changes required by the codification process itself. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

‒ the manufacturing industry in french guiana is partly dependent on the exploitation of the living natural resources of its exclusive economic zone (eez). since there is no eu-venezuela international fisheries agreement, cooperation is not in line with the european legal order. the commission has therefore proposed an eu commitment to give up fishing rights to venezuelan vessels. the legal solution found - a statement to be made by the council with the approval of the european parliament - seems appropriate to the small scale of the activity in question. the declaration takes shape by virtue of decision no 2012/19/eu, but the council changed the legal basis, making parliament an advisory body instead of a body to which it needed to seek approval. parliament and the commission brought actions before the court of justice of the european union, which held that parliament's decision was not only advisory but binding in the sense that its approval is required. the institutional conflict being resolved, i support this recommendation that the procedure for adopting this proposal should be completed as soon as possible, thus providing the appropriate framework for fishing activity in this region.
‒ the processing industry of french guiana depends in part on the exploitation of the natural resources of its eez by the fishing fleet of the bolivarian republic of venezuela. this is a mutually beneficial situation that has been in place and allowed for decades, with some of the catches landing in local ports, which ensure an important source of income and job creation in the region. this is the case despite the absence of an international agreement between the eu and the bolivarian republic of venezuela, a situation which has been hampered by an institutional conflict promoted by the council over the legal basis for the operation of the venezuelan fleet in french guiana waters, which should have been overcome long ago. it should be noted that the bolivarian republic of venezuela has been complying with the counterparts associated with this proposal, in particular with respect to eu regulations, in particular as regards stocks of target species, types of fishing gear, vessel tracking devices, catch declarations, maximum number of authorised vessels and proportion of catches landed in french guiana ports. we regret that the council's position has caused the conclusion of this agreement to be unduly delayed.
‒ given the economic and social importance of the activity in the region, venezuelan vessels have been allowed to fish for several decades, in return for some of the catches being landed in local ports. the landing and processing of fishery products thus represent an important source of resources and jobs for french guiana. that's why i'm in favour.
the european parliament's resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo (drc) calls on the government of the drc to take all necessary measures to ensure that the drc is not subject to any form of sanctions. this statement was given shape in decision no 2012/19/eu, whereby the council took parliament as an advisory body, rather than a body from which it needed to seek approval. in order to resolve this institutional conflict, the commission and the european parliament brought actions before the court of justice of the european union (cjeu), which, after examining the cases, ruled in favour of parliament's position, confirming in it that decisions on the conclusion of fisheries agreements are fully covered by the treaty on the functioning of the eu. as a result of the ecj's interpretation, the ep's decision is not only advisory but binding, and therefore the ep's approval is indispensable. the commission has therefore again submitted the statement to parliament and, in line with the requirements of the community legal order and also taking into account that venezuela has been complying with the counterparts associated with the proposal, i voted in favour of the above legislative proposal.

‒ draft amending budget no 3/2015 aims to enter in the 2015 budget the surplus for the financial year 2014 amounting to eur 1 435 million, in accordance with article 18 of the financial regulation and the council's position on it. i support this report and stress that its adoption will reduce the share of member states' gni-based contributions to the union budget by eur 1 435 million and therefore more than offset its contribution to the financing of draft amending budget no 4/2015 relating to the mobilisation of the eusf for romania, bulgaria and italy, with a total amount of eur 66.5 million.
‒ this is a highly technical project, aimed at introducing the surplus of eur 1 435 million for the financial year 2014 into the 2015 budget. transfers between headings are not possible due to the lack of flexibility of the eu budget imposed by the eu treaties and the requirements of the multiannual financial framework. each year, although there is a budget deficit in some headings, there are others which, due to lack of sufficient applications or implementation problems, may show a surplus at the end of the year. if there is money that has not been spent on an item in a given year, one of two things can happen, either that money is deducted from the member states' contribution (indexed to gni) or there is an effort to try to reintroduce it in the next year in the eu budget. in practice, this amount will be used to partially reduce member states' contributions, where it could and should be used as a boost, not by reducing those contributions, which are already insufficient, in particular for programmes where a lack of payment appropriations has been detected: in the social and environmental areas.

‒ this proposal is intended to mobilise the eu solidarity fund following the floods in romania, bulgaria and italy in 2014. regulation (eu) no 1311/2013 lays down the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020, in which the eusf is intended to be mobilised, within an annual ceiling of eur 541,2 million, in addition to the corresponding headings of the financial framework. in the light of the requests from romania, bulgaria and italy, the calculation of the fund's assistance, based on the estimate of the total damage caused, amounts to eur 66 505 850, and the commission has proposed to mobilise the fund for the same amount. the commission also proposes to apply a rate of 2.5% to total direct losses in the four cases, as the respective threshold for major disasters was not reached in any of them. this mobilisation will entail an adjustment to the 2015 budget which should be budgeted outside the ceilings foreseen for the mff. this amount is in line with the ceiling of eur 541.2 million applicable to the eusf and since there are no grounds for rejecting this proposal, i have voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ the financial aid we have approved amounts to €4 198 175 (floods in romania, spring), €4 297 775 (floods in romania, summer), €1 983 600 (bulgaria) and €56 026 300 (italy). an increase of eur 66 505 850 is to be provided in budget article 13 06 01 (eu solidarity fund for member states), to be budgeted outside the ceilings of the multiannual financial framework. in addition, the amounts of eur 403,9 million not used in 2014 can be used during 2015, while eur 50 million has already been mobilised and entered in the 2015 budget. eur 895,1 million remains available for mobilisation of the eusf in 2015. we voted yes.
‒ the mobility of european citizens is an essential requirement for the exercise of their fundamental freedoms, with crossborder multimodal travel planning and ticketing services for long-distance journeys posing a major challenge to the transport sector, benefiting consumers, the wider economy, the environment and the tourism sector. i therefore support the dieter-lebrecht koch report because i think it deals in a coordinated and moderate way with the creation of integrated tickets, with measures to remove existing obstacles, stressing the crucial importance of social mobility, but always taking into account the possibility of choosing, on the basis of complete information, the user's journey, taking into account, on the other hand, the high costs of introducing an integrated ticket which should not lead to a significant increase in the price of tickets, discouraging the use of public transport. i would stress the importance of this interoperability of multimodal travel plans with information technology systems and the parties involved should develop joint solutions in this regard.
in writing. ‒ we are faced with a report full of apparently good intentions which cannot, however, hide its real intentions. the aim will not be so much to ensure better and more sustainable mobility for people as to further liberalize and privatise the transport sector and the inevitable monopolistic concentration that always follows. this is evidenced by the references to the fourth railway package, the single european transport area or the single european sky. the report also includes some logical and pertinent considerations on multimodality and the ease of transport and travel planning in the european area, but unfortunately these seem to be the cover that covers the real wishes of the report, which seem to fall within the scope of tisa (international agreement on trade and services). the intention to promote good business for multinationals at the expense of public investment is evident. as for the rest, not a word about the attacks on the public transport system, such as those currently taking place in portugal, promoted by the eu, aimed at privatising public transport. this is after the attack under the imf-eu aggression programme, which has brutally increased the price of transport, reduced supply and degraded the quality of service.
‒ with the creation of this integrated ticketing system for multimodal travel in europe, we are making a significant contribution to the realisation of a single european transport area and a european internal market. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the possibility of a single, integrated ticket for the different modes of transport in the 28 member states is still far from being a reality. for a tourist, travel information, the possibility to plan, book and/or buy online are elements that will make the union a more accessible and attractive destination. on the other hand, peer-to-peer mobility will bring direct benefits to union citizens. in addition, the integrated single ticket provides a solution to congestion and other traffic problems. i believe that this system for multimodal travel in europe should be implemented by developing products and services in the private sector, which, together with the public authorities, should provide the means for its implementation. however, for this to be possible, it is imperative that there is equal access on a non-discriminatory basis to travel data in different countries. local and regional authorities must also be linked together via an interoperable platform. looking at an example where ticketing is already a reality, the case of the united kingdom, the platforms and data are open to all operators, making it possible to create a single system. for the reasons i have just described, i am voting in favour of this document.
‒ in order to make it easier, more feasible and cheaper to choose, book and pay for door-to-door multimodal transport, the european commission is defining, by means of a delegated act, specifications to ensure the exchange and development of the real-time traffic information service for european passengers. the proposal is part of the european transport policy and its ultimate aim is to strengthen the exercise of the fundamental freedoms of eu citizens while stimulating tourism and, consequently, the economy. the economic gains are complemented by the contributions to the sustainability of the european transport sector and the more efficient use of available infrastructure. the draft resolution which i voted for calls on the competent authorities of the member states to introduce, by 2020, up-to-date national information systems and intelligent systems providing real-time information on the location of transport.
