in writing. ‒ in recent months, as we have been observing and warning, there has been a fall in demand from external markets. the volatility of the global price and the effects of the russian embargo have put increased pressure on the milk sector and downward pressure on prices. it is therefore clear that the eu's crisis measures for the dairy sector are grossly inadequate and do not correspond to the reality and needs of all the member states. existing safeguards, such as public intervention and aid for private storage, are neither adequate nor sufficient. the eu regulatory framework does not allow for episodes of extreme market volatility or a crisis situation after the end of the quota system. this 'milk package' argues that market conditions are favourable and that there are large export opportunities to be exploited, recommending that the european fund for strategic investments should be used to drive this expansion. finally, they try to hide the fact that only regulation of production, in particular through a system of quotas adapted to the needs and potential of each country, can safeguard production in countries like portugal and prevent the real liquidation situations which are already looming. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the european commission must urgently take additional market measures to resolve the milk crisis. following the downward pressure on prices resulting from the lack of adequate crisis prevention instruments, a slump in world demand, price volatility and the russian embargo on european dairy products, it is of the utmost importance to safeguard a sector with a significant socioeconomic contribution to agricultural and rural development.
in writing. ‒ the so-called 'milk package' entered into force on 3 october 2012 and is valid until 30 june 2020. it was decided in the 2003 mid-term review of the common agricultural policy (cap) that milk quotas were to expire on 31 march 2015. however, given the specific nature of milk production in mountain areas, less-favoured areas and the outermost regions of the european union, the measures set out in the resolution of 11 december 2013 advocate the maintenance of such production after the expiry of the milk quota system. i am voting in favour of this report because it argues that the abolition of quotas would have a largely detrimental effect on the outermost regions, especially in the autonomous region of the azores, where milk production is the main economic activity, representing some 46% of the regional economy. i am therefore voting in favour of this report because of the foregoing and because the rapporteur stresses the importance of creating a transitional mechanism in the outermost regions between the end of quotas and the liberalisation of the markets, which will protect producers and the sector in these regions.
‒ the report made a first effort to assess the effects of the 'milk package' in the dairy sector, adopted under the co-decision procedure in 2012, with the aim of strengthening the position of milk and milk products producers in the supply chain and preparing the sector for a sustainable and more market-oriented future. the end of milk production quotas, after 30 years of implementation, presents challenges in terms of market volatility or a crisis situation, and which the milk package considers necessary to prepare the sector for a sustainable future. in terms of the operation of the 'milk package', the report indicates that it has improved relationships throughout the supply chain, stressing that it is too early to see any significant effects. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. i voted in favour of the report.
‒ my colleague ricardo serrão santos, azorean mep for the s&d, was the shadow rapporteur for this report by the parliament's agriculture committee. it finds that a significant proportion of dairy farms in the eu are located in disadvantaged, outermost, island or mountain regions, where the costs of producing, collecting and marketing milk and milk products are often much higher than in other areas better located within the eu. the abolition of quotas is expected to have a very negative impact on these outermost regions, such as the autonomous region of the azores, where milk production is the main economic activity, representing about 46% of the regional economy. the european commission therefore needs to take additional market measures to address the crisis facing the sector, by pursuing ambitious policies to support these regions, increasing the bargaining power and influence of producers, working to open up new markets in third countries and removing barriers to trade, while balancing exports with a stable internal market.
‒ there are several challenges facing the dairy sector after the end of milk quotas on 31 march this year. the volatility of prices, the impact of the russian embargo and the need to pay particular attention to the outermost regions, in particular the azores, where milk production is the main economic activity, representing approximately 46% of the total value of the regional economy, are highlighted. in this respect, i agree with the rapporteur's recommendations, particularly as regards the existence of regulatory instruments, the adjustment of intervention prices by raising them, the definition of indicators on production costs, the development of instruments to protect against milk price falls, the analysis of new instruments to stabilise incomes and the need to create a limit for unfair trading practices. i therefore agree with the adoption of this report, which also proposes the allocation of additional resources to the posei programme, creating a transitional mechanism between the end of quotas and the liberalisation of markets. i would also stress the importance of bilateral trade negotiations, the opening up of new markets in third countries and the removal of barriers to trade and exports.
‒ i welcome the content of this report, which identifies the needs of the milk sector, particularly in the azores, and calls on the european commission to act swiftly to promote the stabilisation of the internal market. the combined effect of the end of quotas, the russian embargo and the prolonged and ongoing price collapse limits future options for milk producers and incentives for generational renewal and investment in farms. this issue is of particular importance in areas with natural constraints and economic disadvantages, such as the azores, where dairy activity as an economic activity is hardly substitutable. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment and occupation is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. other measures include strengthening posei, measures to address the impact of the end of quotas in the azores, supply management, transparency of the value chain, ensuring that wholesale distribution practices do not undermine the payment of a fair price to the producer, strengthening the milk observatory, mechanisms to protect against sudden income losses in the milk sector and new crisis management tools.
in writing. ‒ as is recognised, the 'milk package' has failed in its attempt to improve the position of milk producers on the market. even with contracts embedded in organisations, milk producers are unable to negotiate an acceptable price for their product with industry. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a new regulation on the common organization of the market in bananas. we believe that supply management and price setting cannot be done merely on the basis of commercial logic. we therefore propose, through the european milk observatory in conjunction with the national authorities, the introduction of sustainability criteria which take into account production costs and the economic and financial viability of farms.
in writing. ‒ the 'milk package' has failed in its attempt to improve the position of milk producers on the market. even with contracts embedded in organisations, milk producers are unable to negotiate an acceptable price for their product with industry. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the market is not distorted. alternative supply regulation mechanisms are essential to solving this problem and this report does not assume that.
‒ in the wake of the economic crisis europe is experiencing, ppps can be a stimulus for job creation, competitiveness and productivity in third countries. despite the negative value attributed to them, for example in portugal, due to their poor implementation, ppps are essentially intended to create high added value for citizens and consumers, to guarantee quality services and goods, and to provide competitive and economic advantages for public administrations. i support the zahradil report because it considers that both smes and large companies can provide knowledge, experience, good practices and networks specific to the private sector involving public authorities in third countries, contributing to the implementation of policies for sustainable development. the obstacles which european companies continue to face on third country markets must be tackled.
‒ the report deals with eu investment in so-called public-private partnerships (ppps) in third countries. ppps are one of the most visible and finished demonstrations of a certain vision of the state, captured and at the service of private interests. we are well aware of the disastrous results in portugal and the consequences of the waste of public resources and their transfer to large economic and financial groups. the report considers that some positive experiences of ppps result from 'better project execution, good quality or value for money, long-term financing of infrastructure construction costs, stimulation of innovation and research', etc. this report attributes to ppps a whole set of virtues which are not true. ppps have contributed to the dismantling of public services and their democratic character. they have been a determining factor in the worsening of regional asymmetries. this report aims to 'export' ppps and force them through trade policies with third countries. obviously, we voted against it.
‒ there are positive experiences of ppps which result from the following elements: better project execution, good quality or value for money, long-term financing of infrastructure construction costs, stimulation of innovation and research, participation of the private sector both in the construction and operation of projects and also in terms of financing, more flexible and qualified management environment, resource benefits for renowned companies and smes and enhanced competitiveness of eu companies for participation in public contracts in third countries. increased participation by european companies in large-scale international projects, including ppps, could bring substantial benefits in terms of job creation, productivity, competitiveness, technology and innovation, resulting in socio-economic benefits and economic growth throughout the eu and in host countries. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ public-private partnerships (ppps) are important as drivers of economic growth, innovation, competitiveness and job creation, both in the european single market and internationally, playing a strategic role in modernising energy, water, road and digital infrastructure. i am in favour of this report which calls on the european commission to promote innovative solutions that mobilise private finance and long-term national resources for development objectives, as large-scale investments in developing countries are needed.
‒ free trade agreements concluded by the european union (eu) have an external impact on public/private initiatives in third countries. these agreements are useful for third country governments in ensuring that their citizens have access to infrastructure, goods and services of general interest, while ensuring that european companies, large, medium-sized, small and micro, have the best possible access to public procurement markets in third countries. given the economic, social and technological benefits across the eu and in host countries inherent in public-private partnerships (ppps) between the parties, i voted in favour of the report i have just seen calling on the eu institutions to promote and encourage the participation of european companies in ppp projects.
‒ i welcome the adoption of this report on the external impact of eu trade and investment policy on public-private initiatives in third countries, as it contains a number of key points, including references to sound regulatory frameworks, smes, principles of good governance and the fight against corruption. increased participation by european companies in large-scale international projects, including ppps, could bring substantial benefits in terms of productivity, competitiveness, technology and innovation, resulting in socio-economic benefits and economic growth throughout the eu and in host countries. for these reasons, and because it is crucial to revitalise job creation, i voted in favour of this document.
‒ public-private partnerships (ppps) can be an important boost to the competitiveness of eu smes vis-à-vis third countries. i share the rapporteur's view that increased participation by european companies in international projects of this kind can bring substantial benefits in terms of job creation and increased productivity, competitiveness, technology and innovation. it is of particular interest that this participation translates into socioeconomic benefits in the eu and in the host countries. given these potentials, it is all the more important for the eu institutions to take the necessary measures to promote the participation of eu companies, in particular smes, in ppp projects in third countries.
‒ this own-initiative report, for which i was the shadow rapporteur, highlights the main challenges posed by ppps in the framework of the common commercial policy, with the aim of strengthening the competitiveness of european companies when participating in public contracts in third countries. in this context, the increased participation of european enterprises in large-scale international projects, particularly in the framework of ppps, will make a significant contribution in terms of job creation, increased productivity and competitiveness and increased technology and innovation, with a clear reflection in terms of economic growth not only in the eu but also in third countries. i therefore naturally endorse and voted in favour of the proposals concerning the need to encourage the participation of european companies, especially smes, in ppp projects, given the scale of investment and the opportunities provided by existing free trade agreements for this type of partnership. i also stress the proposals to include provisions on investment/access to public tenders, the need to establish positive reciprocity in opening up external markets, free of any barriers or protectionism and the assurance to investors that their long-term investment will benefit from sound and effective protection and legal certainty.
‒ public-private partnerships are today for many countries both a symptom of this model of capitalist integration and a cause of the current crisis. this model of european integration, with the single currency and all the budgetary constraints, leaves the states with no room to make the public investments necessary for development. they are becoming dependent on large companies not only for major transport infrastructure but also in such fundamental areas as health, energy and education. i could give many examples of political personalities who go from government to the boards of directors of large economic groups with which the state maintains ppps absolutely ruinous for the citizens. in portugal, ppp expenditure is growing exponentially, unlike all social expenditure. that is, austerity is for the few and not for the large economic groups, which are increasingly benefiting from public revenues. what is needed is to protect europe against the openness that ttip proposes. it is a question of combating, not extending, an instrument which has become a cancer on our democracy.
in writing. ‒ this report attributes a whole range of 'good' qualities to public private partnerships (ppps) and considers them to be 'successful'. the reality and the various experiences in the various member states contradict these statements. ppps have contributed to the dismantling of public services and their provision to the population. they have been a determining factor in the aggravation of regional asymmetries and have compromised the democratic nature of public services. this report aims to 'export' the model of ppps in the establishment of trade policies with third countries and for this reason we voted against it.
in writing. the successive reforms of the cap over the last 20 years have reduced the regulation of agricultural markets to almost nothing. the 'liberalisation' and 'market orientation' prevailed. this approach was also followed in the fruit and vegetables sector, where instruments such as minimum prices were abandoned. this process was accompanied by a policy of strengthening producer organisations (po), with very different results in the different member states, aimed at enabling farmers to act in defence of their interests, for example by selling their production collectively or increasing surplus value through agricultural processing. the amendments we have tabled reflect the reality of the sector and the need for public policies to support producers and national production. other proposals include the inclusion of economic and social criteria to increase support for small and medium-sized agricultural production while preserving the rural environment, and the defence of local marketing and consumption networks that promote social and regional cohesion. we also proposed that agricultural products be excluded from the ttip negotiations. we regret the rejection of these amendments by the majority. nevertheless, and falling clearly short of what is needed, the report reflects some legitimate concerns, pointing out real problems and needs in the sector.
in the light of the conclusions of the european council in brussels on the implementation of the reform of the common agricultural policy, the commission has decided to launch a new action programme on the reform of the common agricultural policy. the own-initiative report advocates simplifying the fruit and vegetable regime, improving the management of producer organisations, increasing the overall level of support to producer organisations and making better use of crisis prevention and management tools to help farmers protect themselves against large falls in incomes. i believe that increasing the organisation fee should remain a priority for the fruit and vegetable regime. it is also important to provide producer organisations with funds to hire capable managers, to continue to support all sectors suffering from the consequences of the russian embargo, to step up efforts to protect farmers from unfair trading practices by large retailers and to generationalise agriculture.
‒ this report on the fruit and vegetables (fph) scheme identifies a decline in the consumption of fph in the union, aggravated by the economic crisis. at the same time, the union has a trade deficit in hfp, in particular in fruit. in response to the liberalisation of the common agricultural policy, the union has implemented measures to create and strengthen producer organisations (po) and associations of producer organisations (paos). the number of pos and poa varies considerably between member states, so this paper calls for more incentives from the commission. reducing complexity and legal uncertainty are other elements that will make the ops and ppas more attractive, as well as creating more funds and operational programmes for investment in human capital, for the management, promotion, marketing and internationalisation of the ops. at the same time, the commission must do more to protect farmers from unfair trading practices by large retailers. this effort should be coordinated at union level and not lead to national protectionist measures. for the reasons i have outlined, i am in favour of adopting this own-initiative report.
‒ the commission presented a report in march 2014 on the implementation of the new rules of the fruit and vegetables regime (fph) to identify progress made while also highlighting existing problems. the rules of the pgi scheme establish a key vector aimed at the creation and development of producer organisations (po) in order to ensure production planning and promote concentration of supply and placing products on the market. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the implementation of the eu's external borders. the rapporteur believes that the solution to this problem lies in reducing the complexity of the current system. the rapporteur considers that, although operational programmes provide a modest leverage of the po's bargaining power in the distribution chain, the latter remains highly concentrated in the hands of retailers. the obvious solution is to increase cap support for the sector, which translates into an improvement in the 'human capital' of the op and, consequently, in a better supply of fruit and vegetables.
‒ this report analyses the situation in the fruit and vegetables sector since the 2007 reform and makes a number of recommendations to improve the current regime and protect farmers. support the simplification of the hff regime, the improvement of the management of producer organisations, the increase of the overall level of support to producer organisations and a better use of crisis prevention and management tools to help farmers protect themselves against large falls in incomes. i welcome the adoption of this report which also stresses the need to step up efforts to protect farmers against unfair trading practices by large retailers.
‒ portugal is a country rich in the diversity and quality of fruit and vegetables, and i welcome the proposal to simplify the system in this sector by improving the management of producer organisations, increasing the level of support to these organisations and making more effective use of crisis prevention and management instruments to protect producers from sharp falls in their incomes.
‒ this own-initiative report is the result of the european parliament's assessment of the commission's report on the implementation of the policy on the fruit and vegetables sector since the 2007 reform. eu policy in this sector has strengthened the role of producer organisations (po) to boost competitiveness, increase productivity, support research and innovation, improve promotion and marketing, prevent and manage market crises, improve the position of producers in the agri-food chain and encourage environmentally friendly practices. i agree with the rapporteur that the arrangements for fruit and vegetables need to be simplified, that the management of producer organisations needs to be improved, that the overall level of support for producer organisations needs to be increased, that crisis prevention and management instruments need to be better used to help farmers protect themselves against large and sharp falls in their incomes, and that the commission needs to step up its efforts to combat unfair trading practices by large retailers. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the organisation of production in the fruit and vegetables sector is essential to improve the trading position of producers vis-à-vis distribution and to integrate the process of adding value to products. this is particularly important in a context where the market is becoming less regulated and more vulnerable to crises caused by price or disease and pests. european incentives should be consistent with the aim of promoting producer organisations (po) and associations of po, thus enabling the role of producers to be strengthened, who are often placed in less favourable situations because of the need to dispose of their highly perishable products quickly. i support this report which sets these issues straight.
in writing. - the situation is paradoxical once again. we have a decline in the agricultural area used for fruit and vegetable production. we have a consumption that continues to fall and that is below the world health organization recommendations. we have a model in place where the big multinational food companies now determine the diet of our young people. producer organisations are key. the degree of organization has been increasing, but the picture varies greatly from country to country. we therefore continue to advocate greater flexibility in their recognition, depending on the specific situation of each region. more support is also needed, as is the extension of eligible expenditure to create conditions for sustainability. however, it is worth noting that we cannot entertain the illusion that it will be possible, with more ppps, to deal with the serious problems of the sector and, for example, the field of large-scale distribution. we are still very wary of this trend towards complete liberalization of the cap, which is still based on market solutions that will not bring any good to our farmers.
‒ we denounce that the decline in fruit and vegetable consumption in countries with austerity policies has led to the adoption of unhealthy diets that are low in essential nutrients by households. we are in favour of promoting traditional diets based on seasonal vegetables and fruits, we are against the limited use of funds by producer organisations, against the closure of farms which lead to the desertification of large areas of land, we are in favour of including criteria of economic and social value for small and medium-sized agricultural production, we are in favour of preserving the rural environment and we are in favour of local marketing and consumption networks which promote social and regional cohesion. we propose that agricultural products be excluded from the ttip negotiations. the report reflects some of our concerns and we have followed its analysis of the sector, its needs and the problems it has been facing since 2007.

budget with a high added value, i would even say a huge added value, given that 94% of the budget is for investment and only 6% of this budget corresponds to administrative and operating expenditure. in writing. tunisia has suffered a terrible terrorist attack that took the lives of 38 tourists in the coastal city of sousse. much has been said about the tunisian exception in the aftermath of the arab spring. however, despite progress in policy, the economy continues to deteriorate and most young people remain without prospects of employment and a better future. the tunisian democracy needs europe's help more than ever. but europe also needs tunisia: the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force, and it is also a political force, and it is a political force, and it is a political force. we have heard from several european leaders that, in addition to welcoming migrants from the maghreb and the levant, the causes of migration must be tackled in their countries of origin by promoting social and economic development. the diagnosis is correct europe can start applying the remedy in tunisia.
the european union and cuba must develop a strong strategic partnership, a partnership based on development cooperation, economic and trade relations and political dialogue. some ask: what does the eu have, what does the european union have to offer that can promote this opening of cuba to democratic values? we have, i would say in the difficult times we are going through, we still have and we want to continue to have a humanistic and people-centered development model, a model that combines social concerns and public service, something that cuba values, with the freedom of expression of civil society, individuals and institutions. we have the possibility of including cuba in the european system of trade preferences in order to encourage full respect for workers' rights and dialogue on human rights, but we need to act quickly, commissioner. it is urgent to repeal the european common position on cuba, an old, outdated position which limits the doors open to us for a constructive dialogue which has an impact not only on relations with cuba but also on the dialogue with latin america and central america, a dialogue so important for the sustainable development of globalisation and the planet. it is urgent to promote a profound dialogue with cuban civil society and its institutions, without compromising on values but also without prejudice or atavism in attitude. i express, on behalf of the socialists and democrats, our support and encouragement for the efforts of the high representative in this regard. we must be active partners in cuba's journey towards an inclusive, open democracy that creates the natural environment for free debate and the guarantee of fundamental freedoms. all this combined with sustainable development and the level of universal access to services that cuba offers is one of the best examples of the european social model. we must build bridges to a better world. in the troubled times we live in, this is an extraordinary challenge and it is a challenge we have an obligation to overcome.
mr president, the negotiations between the european union and cuba for the conclusion of a dialogue agreement are indeed positive. however, we believe that this agreement can only succeed if there is a de facto end to the european policy of interference in cuba's internal affairs. we do not see, for example, in this dialogue agreement the cuban government demanding from the european union that all people have the right to employment, health and quality education free of charge for all, as happens, for example, in cuba and not in the european union. we therefore hope that the dialogue will be conducted on a basis of reciprocity and cooperation and that it will be non-discriminatory. this should be the european union's position: respect for the self-determination of peoples and the charter of the united nations. with regard to the european union's common position on cuba, which has been hanging over the negotiations, i would like to ask the european commission whether it does not consider that a policy based on equality does not in fact presuppose, in the negotiating process, the immediate withdrawal of this common position on cuba.

‒ the eu-us transatlantic trade and investment partnership is a key element in reaching a win-win agreement for both blocs, providing an opportunity to cement commonly shared principles and values and establish a common vision and regulatory framework for trade, investment and related global issues. the complexity, interest and volume of opinions on the agreement, together with a negotiating process that was not always transparent, made it difficult for the ep to reach a common position. i support the lange report because i consider it to be balanced and expresses a set of concerns and recommendations which should be taken into account in the negotiating process. the only agreement that is good for europe is one that combines reciprocal access to markets and the reduction of barriers with respect for european norms and standards, without jeopardizing the quality of public services, respect for environmental standards, health, social protection, data protection, consumer protection and food safety. i welcome the agreement reached to replace the system of investor-state dispute settlement with a new system subject to democratic principles and control.
‒ this report is the first official position taken by the european parliament on the negotiations of the so-called transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the aim of ttip is to create even greater pressure on employment and wages by levelling down social and labour rights. the interests and profits of monopolies and transnational corporations are being placed above the public interest and respect for economic, social and labour rights, in particular by creating specific judicial mechanisms to safeguard these interests, limiting the sovereignty of states and, consequently, distorting democracy itself. overriding environmental sustainability and the safeguarding of public health, the search for new markets at any cost and enabling the advance of the market on the social functions of the states, destroying what remains of important public services. obviously, we voted against it. these are not manoeuvres which are designed, in response to public pressure, to ensure that something changes so that everything stays the same, which will alter the core and objectives of this treaty. only its rejection will secure the interests and rights of the peoples. the alternative is regulated trade, based on complementary rather than competitive relations between countries, producers and products, which respects and safeguards national sovereignty.
‒ i voted against this report because i believe that these recommendations do not safeguard the rights and interests of european citizens and call into question public services, democracy and sovereignty. the amendment on isds (state-investor dispute settlement) which has been adopted is nothing but a scheme to camouflage another form of isds and thus say that private arbitration has been put to an end, which is nothing but an attempt to manipulate public opinion. with the new isds, companies and multinationals will continue to have a veto over the legislative capacity of states, which is an attack on democracy that we cannot allow.
‒ this report contains the recommendations to the eu executive who is negotiating the agreement with the us partners on behalf of the eu. it aims to take stock of the eu-us talks since july 2013, indicating the european parliament's position on certain key issues. it has become clear that the eu-us trade and investment agreement should increase access to the us market, but without compromising eu standards or the right to regulate in the public interest. i therefore voted in favour.
‒ the european union and the united states of america are natural allies, historically cooperating in a number of thematic areas, ranging from the fight against terrorism to the promotion of human rights, freedom and democracy in third countries, and the dynamisation of trade relations. the transatlantic trade and investment partnership is of the utmost importance to both geographical blocks, as it aims to create a single market for trade and services, regulate the rules of world trade and eliminate remaining barriers and tariffs. in economic terms, the future creation of a market of 800 million citizens and the fact that trade contributes to the leverage of european gdp by 0.5% and that of the united states by 0.4% should be emphasized. i am fully in favour of this new transatlantic agreement which could put portugal and, in particular, the autonomous region of madeira, at the geostrategic centre of world trade.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of human rights, the european union is proposing to extend the scope of the convention to include the rights of minorities. i voted in favour of this report because it does not compromise the quality of public services and also insists on respect for environmental standards, health, social protection, data protection, consumer protection and food safety. i support a new mechanism for resolving disputes between investors and the reformed state, which is fully public and transparent, with impartial professional judges. portugal will be one of the first countries to benefit from ttip as national strategic sectors (such as footwear and textiles) face higher customs duties. as for my region, the autonomous region of the azores, gdp in the archipelago would increase by 0.35%, according to a study by the centre for economic policy research (cepr).
in writing. ‒ i am not comfortable with everything that will be included in this transatlantic trade and investment partnership agreement (ttip). the negotiation process should be more transparent. globalisation needs rules, but it needs to be safeguarded by workers' rights, public services, environmental rights, cultural diversity, data protection or a public court-based dispute settlement that guarantees equal rights for domestic and foreign investors. these are some of the points that cannot be negotiated. ttip cannot mean a compromise on the eu's social and moral standards, but must instead translate into more benefits for european citizens and businesses. it is clear that this was not a vote on ttip, but an attempt to show the commission the importance of including the european parliament's viewpoint and the s&d group's contributions.
in writing. ‒ in july 2013, the eu and the us launched negotiations for a comprehensive, ambitious, balanced and binding trade and investment agreement that would strengthen transatlantic ties from a regulatory, economic, financial and even geopolitical perspective. this resolution sets out a set of recommendations from the european parliament to the european commission on the negotiations of the 'transatlantic trade and investment partnership' (ttip) on the various chapters of the mandate: free market access for goods, services and investment, the elimination of non-tariff and regulatory barriers, access to public markets, the need to protect our geographical indications and the liberalisation of the energy market. after a record number of amendments tabled, lengthy debates and concessions on isds, an overall text was reached, reflecting the balanced and majority position of the european parliament. on a national level, i am sure that this agreement will bring a unique set of advantages and opportunities, especially in terms of exports and job creation, which will allow us to leverage various sectors of our economy, generating wealth and economic growth.
‒ the negotiations for a transatlantic partnership with the united states must be consistent with the policies of europe and its member states. the best levels of social, health and environmental protection should be the reference for progress in the talks between the parties, not the lowest common denominator. the farmers of the european union cannot be used as bargaining chips for the benefit of other sectors and it is therefore necessary to establish tariff quotas which represent adequate protection in this area. the protection of quality designations of european agricultural products, such as geographical indications, and european phytosanitary standards should also be ensured. the safeguard clause and an appropriate arbitration mechanism are also important.
in the light of the recent developments in the eu, the commission has decided to propose a new regulation on the free movement of goods and services. this addresses the concerns of many citizens, including respect for high standards of protection of social and labour rights, the environment, food safety and consumer rights; the defence of public services of general interest (such as water, health and education); respect for the privacy of personal data; the protection of european geographical indications; the transparency of negotiations and the end of the controversial private investor-state dispute settlement (isds) system. isds has allowed abuses and has raised legitimate concerns. the text adopted therefore excludes private arbitration from the ttip negotiations, requiring an entirely new, public and transparent system with professional judges appointed by states (instead of lawyers appointed by private investors) and a recourse mechanism. this report sends a clear message to the negotiators: ttip will only be possible if these demands of parliament and the citizens are respected. it is a very important step towards a good ttip and therefore deserves my vote in favour.
‒ this agreement, which has sparked a wave of protest and outrage in various european social and economic sectors, will have very serious impacts. the consequences for agriculture will be catastrophic for both producers and consumers. from an economic point of view, the conclusion of this agreement could mean the end of our family farming production model, which is considered to be the safest and most sustainable for food production in the world. but consumers will also be hit hard. while caution prevails in europe, only substances that are clearly harmful to public health are prohibited in the united states. finally, i conclude with the dispute settlement mechanisms provided for in these agreements, which provide for the creation of private arbitration tribunals to which multinational companies can appeal, ordering national states to pay large sums of compensation if they consider that they are maintaining any useless and harmful obstacles to free competition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the lange report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the european commission on the negotiations of the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) because i believe it is essential that there is a mandate from the european parliament to the european commission that strongly and explicitly translates the values of environmental, labour, human rights and consumer protection into the ttip negotiations. the report also makes clear recommendations on the need to abolish the system of private arbitration between states and private investors (isds) and replace it with a public, transparent and independent system where private interests cannot compromise the democracy of eu member states. the lange report also makes clear that ttip cannot be achieved at any cost and calls on the european commission to demand that the transatlantic partnership be a cornerstone in promoting european values for a fairer and more integrated globalisation.
‒ the aim of ttip is to create even greater pressure on employment and wages by levelling down social and labour rights. the adoption of this treaty implies not only the total liberalization of international trade between the two continents but also the opening to the market and competition of large sections of the so-called social functions of the state, with a view to their privatization and commodification. moreover, it is necessary to place the interests and profits of multinational companies above the public interest and respect for economic, social and labour rights, in particular by creating a dispute settlement mechanism above national legal institutions, which allows states to sue if multinational companies feel that their interests have been harmed, thus limiting the sovereignty of states and consequently distorting democracy itself. we voted against this report and will continue to demand the definitive rejection of this treaty in order to defend regulated trade, based on complementary rather than competitive relations between countries, producers and products, and on respect for and safeguarding national sovereignty.
‒ this is a technical document which seeks to include croatia, following its eu integration, as part of the protocol to the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) between the eu, its member states and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. the procedure itself does not alter the existing saa in any way, but makes some adjustments to the agricultural side, in particular to the conditions governing the movement of goods and their tariff quotas. we do not, however, disregard the broader framework of the said saa signed between the eu and the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, in particular particular aspects such as the creation of free trade areas, the imposition of economic, political, judicial, fiscal and public sector reforms, nor do we fail to keep in perspective the historical and political framework of this whole process (the dismemberment of yugoslavia and the role of the eu and nato powers, in particular in the conflict in the balkan region), as we have already expressed on other occasions. for the reasons stated, we abstained.

in writing. - i support the buzek report on the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation with india. in addition to updating the legal text of the international agreement to take account of the changes resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, this agreement was signed on 23 november 2001 and extended for a further five years, with a renewable period of five years. it is certainly in the interest of both the eu and india to intensify cooperation in science and technology in areas of common interest, not least because scientific knowledge leads to better market access opportunities. the agreement is based on the principles of mutual added value, reciprocal access to each other's programmes and actions, non-discrimination and effective protection of intellectual property.
‒ this report proposes the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india. the aim is to approve the continuation and financing of the agreement, which was initially established for a period of five years, renewable by agreement between the parties and after an evaluation during the year preceding its expiry. as a cooperation agreement, it aims at developing on both sides research and technological development capacity in various fields, including other activities that may promote the dissemination and/or exploitation of results of projects and coordination activities. we voted in favour. it is positive and desirable that cooperation in these areas can be established and deepened with a view to a joint approach to important social and environmental challenges in pursuit of the public interest. unquestionable mutual benefits can result. this does not prevent, however, but rather requires particular attention to the need for a fair and equitable distribution of the results of this cooperation and its benefits, from the outset between the different member states, combating tendencies towards a marked divergence, also in this area, and between them and india.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india.
‒ i subscribe to this recommendation on the draft council decision on the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india. the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india was signed in new delhi on 23 november 2001 and entered into force on 14 october 2002. the agreement was for five years and could be renewed by mutual agreement between the parties after the evaluation to be carried out during the last year of each successive period. in november 2006, at the meeting of the ec-india steering committee for c&t cooperation, both parties expressed their interest in renewing the agreement. i am voting in favour of the agreement because i am in favour of a rapid renewal of the agreement for a period of five years, because it is in the interest of both parties and because it maintains continuity in the scientific and technological relations between india and the european community.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation on the draft council decision on the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india. it is now more than ever in the interest of both sides not only to continue good relations in the scientific and technological fields but also to intensify this cooperation. in this connection, i support the renewal of the agreement with the government of the republic of india for a further five years.
‒ this is a simple renewal of the agreement (for another 5 years) with the government of the republic of india, and it is in the interest of both parties to continue good relations in the scientific and technological fields.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a recommendation on the draft council decision on the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india, signed in new delhi in november 2001. the agreement provides that it may be renewed by mutual agreement between the parties every five years, following an evaluation carried out during the last year of each successive period. by its decision 2009/501/ec of 19 january 2009, the council approved the renewal of the agreement for a further period of five years, until 17 may 2015. the renewal of the agreement for a further five years is objectively in the interest of the scientific and technological communities of both parties, because it allows the sharing of experience and projects. it should be noted that the assumptions and content of the agreement remain unchanged, with the exception of slight changes in terminology, due to the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. ‒ as a scientist, i have been involved in scientific and technological cooperation with india and i am very much in favour of this scientific and technological cooperation agreement. however, i have two concerns to share. on the one hand, i don't think the metric for monitoring is the most efficient. you can have countless joint projects and not produce a line of science or technology products. these are the results that are sought at the end of this cooperation. so i suggest that the follow-up metrics include, in the future, the number of publications and the number of patents generated. on the other hand, i consider that the direct investment figures are very low, not reaching eur 200 000 per year. the european union must make a greater effort and be more ambitious in its cooperation with india, which is a very advanced country in terms of science and technology.
‒ this document concerns the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india. it is part of the committee on industry, research and energy (itre). the document was not shadowed by the gue/ngl. the report was assigned to the chairman of the itre commission in accordance with the simplified procedure without amendments under article 50 (1). the report is designed to approve the continuation and financing of the scientific and technological cooperation agreement concluded between the european community and india in november 2001. the agreement provided for a five-year period, renewable by agreement between the parties and after an evaluation during the year preceding its expiry. this cooperation agreement aims at the development on both sides of rtd (research and technological development), including other activities promoting the dissemination and/or exploitation of project results and coordination activities. we support it.

in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 7 of horizon 2020, the specific terms and conditions for the participation of the faroe islands as a country associated to horizon 2020 framework programme are laid down in an international agreement. both parties shall demonstrate an interest in encouraging reciprocal access by their respective research organisations to research and development activities in the faroe islands and to the union's framework programmes for research and technological development. the importance of the ongoing scientific and technological cooperation between the faroe islands and the union strengthens the mutual interest in strengthening research and innovation in the context of the establishment of the european research area. with this recommendation we are helping to facilitate the free movement and residence of researchers participating in the activities, as well as the cross-border movement of goods intended for those activities.
‒ this report deals with the conclusion of the agreement on scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the faroe islands. in march 2014, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations on behalf of the european union with the faroe islands for an agreement associating the faroe islands to horizon 2020 - the framework programme for research and innovation (2014-2020). the faroe islands should participate as an associated country under the terms and conditions set out in horizon 2020 and in council decision 2013/743/eu. the cooperation agreement will include regular discussions on cooperation and development prospects, regular information on the implementation of research programmes and projects, meetings and visits with exchanges of views between researchers and technicians, participation of experts in seminars, symposia and workshops. an eu-faroe research and innovation committee should be set up, which should be composed of representatives of both parties. we voted in favour. it should be noted, however, that, while we have no objections in principle to the extension of the framework programme to other countries, we continue to denounce the very uneven distribution of resources under this programme, of which, please note, portugal was a net contributor in the period 2007-2013. we continue to demand action to change this situation.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the faroe islands, associating the faroe islands to horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation (2014-2020) (14014/2014).
in writing. ‒ horizon 2020 the community framework programme for research and innovation is the european community's largest instrument specifically geared to supporting research through the co-financing of research, innovation and demonstration projects, and has the overall objective of contributing to the creation of a knowledge-based and innovation-based economy, the creation of new job opportunities and sustainable economic growth in europe. in support of horizon 2020 cfp, which aims to ensure industrial leadership in the european union by 2020 and to contribute to the europe 2020 strategy focusing on smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, i approve this recommendation on the conclusion of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the faroe islands associating the faroe islands to horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation (2014-2020).
in writing. ‒ horizon 2020 the community framework programme for research and innovation, with an overall budget of over €77 billion for the period 2014-2020, is the european community's largest instrument specifically geared to supporting research, thus stimulating the dynamisation of the economy. i have approved the conclusion of this agreement with the faroe islands because i support the establishment of a research area without frontiers, in which scientific resources will be better used to increase employment and competitiveness in europe.
in writing. ‒ agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european union and the faroe islands, associating the faroe islands to horizon 2020 - the framework programme for research and innovation (2014-2020).
in writing. ‒ we are faced with a proposal for a recommendation aimed at concluding a scientific and technological cooperation agreement between the european union and the faroe islands, while associating the faroe islands to horizon 2020 - the framework programme for research and innovation (2014-2020). in addition to association with horizon 2020, cooperation may also include regular discussions on the guidelines and priorities of the research policies and plans of the faroe islands and the union, discussions on cooperation and development perspectives, visits and exchanges of researchers, engineers and technicians, participation of experts in seminars, symposia and workshops, among others. the draft agreement also lays down the conditions for the participation of the faroe islands in indirect actions and in the activities of the european commission research centre under the same conditions as those applicable to entities of the member states of the union. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of this proposal for a recommendation.
‒ horizon 2020 is a powerful tool for stimulating scientific research and, indirectly, for boosting the economy, protecting the environment and promoting the values we hold most dear in europe. the european union is devoting a lot of money to this programme and this will bring benefits in terms of competitiveness and quality of life for all. i therefore congratulate the faroe islands on becoming one of the regions benefiting from this instrument. however, i must emphasize that i am against the use of marine mammals that is being made in this territory. for this reason, i am concerned that european funds may be being used for any purpose including the persecution and killing of cetaceans. we cannot forget the sad images of the deaths that occur every year in the local communities of the faroe islands. as a corollary, i ask the european commission to be particularly careful in allocating and monitoring the use of funds under this agreement, ensuring that it does not contribute, directly or indirectly, to the death or suffering of species protected by international conventions to which it is a signatory.
