the rapporteur. madam president, a special greeting to commissioner vella. the second half of the 20th century was paradigmatic in terms of the management of the seas and oceans. the visionary united nations international law of the sea was agreed upon, based on such relevant values as the precautionary principle, peaceful development, the sharing of resources, the protection of biodiversity, sustainable development, the ecosystem vision, the idea of an ocean. but we also see, in spite of the law, overfishing and the collapse of wild springs. in conjunction with the decline in resources in traditional fisheries, some industrial fleets, many of them european, have migrated to the high seas and the deep sea. european countries have developed some of the largest long-distance fishing fleets and have concluded fisheries agreements with many acp countries. it should be noted that the international law of the sea requires that countries which do not use their renewable marine resources must make them available to third countries. fisheries cooperation agreements are thus ambassadors for the european union in maritime affairs. but fisheries agreements cannot be a backdoor to recover the ecological footprint we have left behind. they must be ambassadors for sustainable development cooperation and good fishing practices. unlike other fleets, european fleets today are subject to the constraints of legal frameworks based on environmental responsibility, based on the best scientific knowledge and an ecosystem approach. fisheries agreements are also better developed today than they were 40, 30, 20, 10 or even 5 years ago. they address issues such as the identification of living sources, respect for workers' rights, incentives for local fishing industries and respect for environmental constraints. in the event of failure - and there are failures - the different legal systems of the european countries tend, by very recent provisions, to be increasingly inflexible and efficient. as an example, i would remind you that one european government has increased the maximum penalties for non-compliance to eur 11 million. i am convinced that the fisheries agreement with madagascar, for which i am the rapporteur, can help to improve the conditions of a country in enormous difficulties and at the same time benefit european fleets. this partnership agreement is based on the rules established by the relevant fisheries organisations and includes fishing opportunities for 94 vessels. over 15 000 tonnes of fish are expected to be caught in the waters of the madagascar exclusive economic zone and, in return for using this area, the european union will finance madagascar and its fishing sector in particular with over eur 6 million over four years. in the case of the cape verde agreement, for which i am the shadow rapporteur, i am concerned about the level of uncertainty in the impact of fishing on shark populations, as my colleague mr van dalen has already said, but i welcome the provisions in the agreement for this subject to be studied in detail. the amendments to the report reinforce these aspects and i support them. although i am not directly responsible for the guinea-bissau report, i think we will have to be particularly careful in monitoring this agreement. the political instability in the country is worrying and this agreement should be another factor in bringing the authorities closer together and in the development of local communities, particularly fishing communities. it is therefore important that the commission monitors these agreements to ensure that they are free from negligence and corruption. i think that in the first place we must invest in inadequate infrastructure, which is in danger of being neglected or of being out of date and out of date. these are important questions. but small compared to the big problems of international fisheries. abuse of labour, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, including the use of flags of convenience and the use of environmentally untested technologies are gaps that need to be closed. i welcome the efforts made by the european commission, but i stress, with the same wisdom that has been used here, that much more needs to be done.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the main objective of fisheries partnership agreements is to provide european union member states with fishing opportunities in the waters of third countries with catch quotas within the limits of the available surplus and in compliance with the regulation on the common fisheries policy and the principles of good governance. the european union should use these agreements not only on the economic side but also to strengthen cooperation instruments and promote the development of these countries in the social and environmental fields. such cooperation instruments should therefore give priority to the fight against corruption of public office holders with responsibilities in the fisheries area, and the european union should suspend agreements when there are political changes that violate human rights or the principles of democracy. they should also implement programmes to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and the sustainable and responsible exploitation and monitoring of local resources. in short, fisheries partnership agreements naturally benefit the countries of the european union, but they also make a significant contribution to the development of the countries with which they are concluded and should therefore be supported and increased. the point is that they are not used as an incentive to fuel what the european union itself has been working to combat: illegal fishing and ocean degradation.

in writing. in the face of the world's largest refugee crisis, we must respond to the humanitarian emergency. unfortunately the council was unable to reach an agreement to distribute 40,000. the commission proposes to increase the number of refugees by 120,000 to be distributed among the 28 member states, while germany alone will receive 800,000 in one year. there are member states which are in solidarity, but others have blocked any solution and some speeches bring back racism and xenophobia. i fear that the council will once again fail to meet the challenge. we need a permanent resettlement mechanism with mandatory quotas. we need more funds for the member states. we need more resources for processing asylum applications. we need an effective return policy. we are protesting against the council's proposal to cut the budget appropriations which should have been increased. we must also look to the future: effectively combat the self-styled islamic state; humanitarian and development aid needs to be strengthened and strategically targeted (and we need to contribute to peace in syria, libya, among others); we need a truly european migration and asylum policy that includes better regulation of legal immigration and the fight against illegal immigration, and effectively tackling human traffickers.
the european union is facing serious economic and social difficulties, but above all humanitarian ones, due to the arrival of thousands of refugees fleeing the war in syria, iraq and egypt. this is one of the greatest challenges facing europe. we haven't seen an exodus of this magnitude since world war ii. we have a moral, civic and human obligation to temporarily host refugees, providing them with conditions that safeguard the primacy of respect and human dignity. it is important to ensure that all these citizens are registered and checked at the borders of the european union, and to use all the existing and necessary mechanisms to ensure the highest possible level of security. the year 2016 will also be full of economic challenges, with the key being to deepen the economic and monetary union, move towards the digital single market and complete the energy union. these three economic drivers, together with the conclusion of the eu-us international trade agreement, will make a decisive contribution to a new period of economic growth and job creation.
in writing. today we are faced with a dangerous scenario in the european union, one that reveals a weariness of the idea of a common space. the borders have been blurred. for whose benefit? the benefits of freedom of movement are most evident for businesses. but people have to come first. in the agricultural sector, there is a great asymmetry between farmers, who are tied to the land, and processing and distribution enterprises, which, in periods of financial contraction, crush the prices paid for production. in addition, these entities achieve efficiency gains also provided by the market. but without farmers there are no other links in the agri-food value chain, so it is vital to ensure that primary producers are fairly paid for their work. efficiency should not be the ultimate goal, but fair remuneration along the value chain and contribution to territorial balance. only then can there be equity in market share. it is unacceptable to allow cheaper, more efficiently produced products from anywhere in europe to compete with producers in my country to the extent that this would undermine the continuity of their economic activity. if we are not to grow tired of the common space, we must urgently moralize its rules.
in writing. let's talk about the recent news and the huge farmers' demonstration last monday. as reality shows, the cap and its market-oriented liberalising trend, with the gradual abandonment of all public regulatory instruments, most notably the abolition of milk quotas, has not benefited agriculture and farmers at all, leading only to a collapse in the prices paid for production and the bankruptcy of thousands of farms. it is therefore a matter of concern that the european governments, and in particular the portuguese government, which only a few months ago approved the end of milk quotas, are not able to accept the need for a thorough review of the cap and are simply approving in haste and under pressure from the struggle of european farmers a package of aid of 500 million euros which is far short of what is needed. it should be noted that this sum of eur 500 million of aid for the whole of the european union is equivalent to the cut portugal suffered in the financial envelope for aid to its agriculture, negotiated in 2013 for the 2014-2010 horizon.
the european union is facing enormous challenges. the challenge of global competitiveness, the challenge of sustainability and energy sovereignty, the challenge of leadership in combating climate change, the challenge of preserving its democratic, open and tolerant identity, the technological, economic and social challenge posed by the digital society, the challenge of poverty, asymmetries and inequalities. it faces all these challenges and it faces one challenge now that is of absolute urgency. the political and humanitarian challenge posed by the flows of political and economic refugees. there is a risk that the substantive and media force of the refugee crisis will eventually take the focus off all other issues in the state of the union debate. but there is also an opportunity to assess the state of the union by reference to its capacities and its inabilities to respond to the crisis. the response to the refugee crisis is a clear reflection of the state of the union and it is important to tackle europe's weaknesses in this case and also to strengthen the union as a project of peace, solidarity and development.
in writing. in his speech, the president of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, once again interfered in the political situation in greece, repeating the tone of blackmail towards the greek people in an attempt to condition the choice of the path they should take with regard to the future of their country. it is unacceptable to consider that all political forces should accept what he calls 'aid' but which in practice only means the continuation of the same policies that led greece to social and economic catastrophe. it is unacceptable that he should say that what is needed is to continue along the path of so-called budgetary consolidation when the greek people have expressed a different will in the last elections and in the last referendum. these statements are obviously all the more serious when we are a few days away from the next elections in greece. it 's further proof of what 's clearer today than ever - the eu does not mean respect for democracy and the will of the people, but rather the imposition of the policy that best serves big financial and economic capital. it is, and always has been, the "state of the union".

in writing. the procedures necessary for the signature of this new protocol had been suspended in 2012 as a result of the coup d'état in guinea-bissau and the european fleet ceased its activity because it was considered that its safety could not be guaranteed. following the elections in guinea-bissau in may 2014, a new protocol was signed between the parties in november. this new protocol to the eu-guinea-bissau fisheries agreement provides for fishing opportunities for vessels from spain, italy, portugal, france and greece. the protocol has a duration of three years and has been provisionally applied since 24 november 2014. under this protocol, portugal holds two licences for surface longlining and the possibility of fishing for shrimp trawls (1060 grt corresponding to about four vessels with the characteristics of the national fleet). with the suspension of the negotiations with mauritania, the eu-guinea-bissau fisheries agreement is of increased importance and can even be considered one of the most important currently in force, and i therefore support this recommendation for the signing of the agreement in question.
in writing. the new protocol to the eu-guinea-bissau fisheries agreement provides for fishing opportunities for vessels from spain, italy, portugal, france and greece. the protocol has a duration of three years and has been provisionally applied since 24 november 2014. the financial contribution is eur 9.2 million per year, of which eur 6.2 million is for access to resources in the guinea-bissau economic zone and eur 3 million is for support for the development of the guinean fisheries sector. the fishing opportunities allocated to the european fleet are: 3 700 grt for freezer trawls (shrimp) and 3 500 grt for freezer trawls (dermaids and cephalopods); 28 freezer and longliner tuna vessels and 12 reed tuna vessels. portugal holds under this protocol two licences for surface longlining and fishing opportunities for shrimp trawling (1060 tacs corresponding to about four vessels with the characteristics of the national fleet). i voted in favour.

‒ the first fisheries agreement concluded between the eec and guinea-bissau dates from 1980. since that date, fleets of the eec/eu member states have had access to fishing opportunities in the waters of that country. successive implementing protocols to the agreement have been in force since then and until 15 june 2012. i am voting in favour of this report which allows eu fishing fleets to catch 3 700 grt for freezer trawls (shrimp) and 3 500 grt for freezer trawls (demersals and cephalopods) and the free movement of 28 freezer trawlers and longliners and 12 tuna vessels with longlines. the eu will contribute €9.2 million per year, €6.2 million of which will be used to access resources in the guinea-bissau economic zone and €3 million to support the development of guinea-bissau's fisheries sector.
‒ guinea-bissau is among the least developed countries in the world and is heavily indebted. it also has one of the lowest gdp per capita in the world. this protocol, agreed between the eu and the republic of guinea-bissau, sets out the fishing opportunities and financial compensation (eur 9 200 000 per year) provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement in force between the two parties. the protocol aims to provide fishing opportunities for eu vessels in guinea-bissau waters, within the limits of the available surplus, and to strengthen cooperation between the eu and the republic of guinea-bissau in order to establish a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fishery resources in the guinea-bissau fishing zone. this agreement is of the utmost importance for guinea-bissau, not only from a financial point of view but also in terms of the rehabilitation of the fisheries sector and the development of local fisheries, including small-scale fishing. it's a serious contribution to the strengthening of the country's economy.
‒ the main objective of the protocol is to provide fishing opportunities for european union vessels in guinea-bissau waters, within the limits of the available surplus, and to strengthen cooperation between the eu and guinea-bissau, thereby creating a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the exclusive economic zone of guinea-bissau. the overall financial contribution provided for is eur 9,2 million per year, of which eur 6,2 million is for access to resources in the guinea-bissau economic zone and eur 3 million is for support for the development of the guinea-bissau fisheries sector. like the rapporteur, i believe that the adoption of this proposal should be completed as soon as possible, since this is a very important economic sector, particularly in the riverine areas (european and guinean). it is therefore imperative that the agreement promotes the effective sustainable development of the guinean fisheries sector and related industries and activities, increasing the added value that is left in the country as a result of the exploitation of its natural resources.

‒ the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of madagascar includes fishing opportunities for 94 vessels, 40 of which are purse seiners and 54 longliners of various sizes. a catch of 15 750 tonnes of fish is foreseen in the waters of the exclusive economic zone of the republic of madagascar. in return for the use of this fishing area, the european union will finance the fishing industry of the republic of madagascar with some eur 700 000 per year and a general contribution of some eur 866 250 for the first two years of the agreement and eur 787 500 for the last two years. in total, the agreement provides for the european union to pay the republic of madagascar eur 6 107 500 over the four years of its validity. since i consider that it deserves a generally positive assessment, while safeguarding the interests of the parties, i voted in favour of the conclusion of the protocol between the european union and the republic of madagascar setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of madagascar.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this protocol is to strengthen cooperation between the european union and madagascar by establishing a partnership framework for the development of a sustainable fisheries policy and the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in madagascar's fishing zone, in the interests of both parties. this is an opportunity to boost economic growth, improve the human rights situation and the conditions of workers, especially women, and eradicate illegal child labour in this field.
‒ the main objective of the protocol of agreement is to grant fishing opportunities to eu vessels in the fishing zone of the republic of madagascar. i believe that the strengthening of cooperation between the european union and the republic of madagascar through the creation of a partnership framework will make it possible to develop a sustainable fisheries policy and the rational exploitation of fishery resources in the interests of both parties, since it specifies the target species, the expected value of the fish, the amounts to be invested and the overall expected return. the protocol will also serve to develop the local fishing industry in partnership with eu vessels and to supply the eu market with quality fish products. the annual financial contribution shall be eur 1 566 250 for each of the first two years of the protocol and eur 1 487 500 for each of the following two years. this support meets the objectives of the national fisheries policy and in particular the needs of the republic of madagascar in the fight against illegal fishing. in this sense, and as in the other agreements voted on today, i cast my vote in favour.

‒ the trade facilitation agreement (tfa), concluded in december 2013, is the first multilateral agreement concluded since the wto was established in 1995. the tfa is a groundbreaking agreement. in addition to being the first multilateral agreement on the new standards ever negotiated since the establishment of the wto almost twenty years ago, it set a pioneering approach by allowing developing and least developed countries to categorize commitments and set a timetable for their implementation, by linking the application of some disciplines to the provision of technical assistance, by calling for joint action by wto member countries to support the implementation of some provisions of the agreement, and by incorporating a group of experts to assess a member's situation once the application periods expire. i agree that the tfa is notable for its recognition of differences between countries in the capacity to implement it, by asking developing and least-developed countries to define when they will implement the specific provisions contained in it and by linking the application of some disciplines to the provision of technical assistance by developed countries.
‒ after almost a decade of negotiations, the trade facilitation agreement (tfa) was finally concluded at the 9th wto ministerial conference in december 2013. this is a ground-breaking agreement, not only because it is the first multilateral agreement to be concluded since the establishment of the wto in 1995, but also because it is a pioneering approach to addressing the concerns of developing countries and the least developed countries in the wto. for this reason, and also taking into account the beneficial effects which the fta is intended to achieve in terms of improving and modernising customs regimes, increasing and speeding up trade and enhancing transparency and cooperation between customs authorities, i voted in favour of the conclusion of the protocol amending the marrakesh agreement establishing the world trade organisation.
‒ the wto trade facilitation agreement is the first multilateral agreement since the establishment of the wto 20 years ago and is considered the most important outcome of the doha development round, as it is seen as a breakthrough in the ability of the multilateral trading system to respond to the concerns of developing countries. this agreement, once implemented, will bring significant trade benefits worldwide and boost global economic growth by accelerating the cross-border movement of goods, ensuring fluidity and predictability of trade flows. it will also require greater transparency and cooperation between customs authorities. i would also like to highlight as a very positive aspect the removal of administrative barriers which will contribute not only to a reduction in costs but also to a better integration of developing countries and their companies in regional and global value chains, allowing them to benefit more from international trade. i am clearly in favour of this proposal and hope that this agreement will be ratified quickly by two-thirds of the 160 wto members so that it can enter into force.

in writing. ‒ at the 9th wto ministerial conference in december 2013, the 160 wto members concluded negotiations on the trade facilitation agreement, which is an important milestone as it is the first multilateral agreement since the establishment of the wto that sets a model for customs modernisation among the 161 wto members, providing benefits to developing countries and creating a more favourable environment for businesses, in particular smes. the implementation of this agreement will lead to the harmonisation and simplification of trade-related procedures, including in developing countries, by providing for special and differential treatment, whereby developing countries and least developed countries can decide in what circumstances the different provisions will be applied and which will require technical assistance. i support this report which is in line with what the european parliament and the eu have long advocated in promoting free, fair and open trade, which is balanced and mutually beneficial for all, and the wto is obviously the stage par excellence to pursue and reaffirm these principles.
‒ trade facilitation is primarily the responsibility of national authorities, but there is no doubt that in many areas multilateral cooperation can increase profits and reduce costs. the wto's trade facilitation agreement therefore needs to be ratified by two-thirds of wto members to enter into force. the benefits to developing countries of implementing this agreement, as it will help create a more favourable environment for business, in particular for smes, are clear and, if fully implemented, should reduce uncertainty about market entry conditions and trade costs by between 12.5% and 17.5%. i welcome the implementation of this agreement, particularly in developing countries, as it will lead to the harmonization and simplification of trade-related procedures.

‒ the eu is committed to promoting free trade, which is balanced and mutually beneficial for all. in this resolution, parliament welcomes the conclusion of the trade facilitation agreement at the 9th wto ministerial conference in december 2013. this agreement is an important milestone not only because it is the first multilateral agreement to be concluded since the establishment of the wto in 1995, but also because it will contribute to the modernisation of customs regimes and represent a step forward in the capacity of the multilateral trading system to respond to the concerns of developing and least developed countries. to this end, the agreement provides for special and differentiated treatment, allowing developing and least-developed countries to define autonomously the timetable for the phased implementation of the technical measures envisaged, and linking the application of certain provisions to the provision of technical assistance. they also contain some 40 provisions aimed at speeding up the movement of goods across borders, contributing to increased trade volumes, better fraud detection and enhanced efficiency of customs authorities, which is estimated to reduce trade costs by between 12.5% and 17.5%.

‒ the budapest convention contributes to the functioning of the internal market in transport by harmonising contracts and rules on inland navigation in europe. it is an agreement partially falling within the exclusive competence of the european union. however, the convention does not provide for the possibility of the union becoming a party. eleven member states are already parties to the budapest convention and fifteen member states have indicated that their inland waterways are not covered by the convention. austria and poland have expressed an interest in becoming parties to the convention and their participation will facilitate the wider application of this legal instrument for the benefit of citizens and businesses. belgium ratified the budapest convention on 5 august 2008. i agree with your accession to the budapest convention.
‒ the budapest convention was adopted by the diplomatic conference jointly organised by the central commission for the navigation of the rhine and the danube commission in collaboration with the united nations economic commission for europe (unece). the budapest convention, which entered into force on 1 april 2005, has proved to be a great success and contributes to the smooth functioning of the internal market in transport. it aims to harmonize contractual and inland navigation rules between european countries. by becoming party to this convention, acceding countries will benefit from the advantages of the convention. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways contributes to the functioning of the internal market in transport by harmonising contracts and rules on inland waterways in europe. i would stress that the eu cannot be a party to the convention and that its member states can only accede if duly authorised by the eu. i stress that the eu's external policy on judicial cooperation in civil and commercial matters is in no way affected by the fact that its member states have acceded to the convention. in view of the above and the expression of interest by austria and poland to become parties to the convention and the need for retroactive authorization to correct the ratification of belgium, i have nothing against this recommendation.
‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways, which entered into force on 1 april 2005, contributes to the functioning of the internal market in transport by harmonising contracts and rules on inland waterways in europe. partly covered by the exclusive competence of the eu, insofar as it allows the parties to choose the law applicable to the contract of carriage covered by the scope of the convention, this agreement cannot be ratified or acceded to by the member states without the union's authorisation (article 2 (1) tfeu). austria and poland have expressed an interest in becoming party to the convention. moreover, belgium ratified the budapest convention on 5 august 2008 and therefore a retroactive authorisation is necessary to correct the current irregular situation. this draft decision authorises belgium and poland to ratify and austria to accede to the budapest convention. i voted in favour of their approval.
‒ the purpose of this proposal for a recommendation is to authorise the kingdom of belgium and the republic of poland to ratify the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterway and the republic of austria to accede to the said convention, which is considered to be an important instrument for promoting inland navigation in europe. the budapest convention applies to any contract for the carriage of goods where the port of loading or the place of acceptance of the cargo and the port of unloading or the place of delivery of the goods are located in two different states, at least one of which is a state party to the convention. where the contract provides for a choice of several ports of landing or delivery places, the choice shall be determined by the port of landing or the delivery place to which the goods have actually been delivered. member states with inland waterways falling within the scope of the budapest convention should therefore be allowed to ratify or accede to this instrument. i agree, so i voted in favour.

in writing. the 962% increase in irregular migrants crossing the eu's borders compared to the same period last year has exacerbated the emergency situation in the countries of entry, particularly italy and greece. article 13 of regulation (eu) no 604/2013 assigns the responsibility for examining the application for protection to the first country of entry, which has consequently put a negative pressure on its migration and asylum systems. in order to alleviate the pressure on italy and greece, this legislative resolution lays down interim measures in the field of international protection for the temporary and exceptional relocation to other member states of 110 000 persons in clear need of international protection. given the shared responsibility of the member states in the reception of refugees and asylum seekers, and also taking into account the current emergency situation and the extraordinary demands it imposes - in terms of enhanced solidarity and responsibility - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution.

‒ i support the report by my colleague kerstin westphal on the urban dimension of eu policies. cities and functional urban areas are economic pillars and engines of job creation in the eu (since innovation and new economic activities often originate in the city), thus providing added value for the eu in its relations with other regions of the world. i support the commission's initiative to work towards a european urban agenda, and i consider its creation essential with the aim of seeking a better articulation between urban solutions and eu challenges, a better link between sectoral policies and levels of governance, a better targeting of eu funding to relevant local urban challenges and a better assessment of the territorial impact of sectoral policies. the urban agenda should promote the development of governance solutions that can best meet the challenges and objectives of sustainable, economically and socially inclusive development of europe's cities and functional urban areas.
‒ in 2014, half of the world's population and 72% of the european population lived in urban areas, and by 2050, almost 80% of the world's population will live in urban areas, which are a single polycentric structure built around large, medium and small cities and surrounding areas. in addition, some 70% of european policies and legislation are implemented at local and regional level, and better policy coordination between and with stakeholders and levels of government is needed, as the sectoral approach to eu policy can lead to policies and legislation that do not favour functional urban areas. i agree with the idea of creating a european urban agenda that better articulates urban solutions and eu challenges, a better link between sectoral policies and levels of governance, a better targeting of eu funding to relevant local urban challenges and a better assessment of the territorial impact of sectoral policies.
‒ i have voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the urban dimension of european union policies. given that 70% of european policies and legislation are implemented at local and regional level, it is also worth noting that cities, or large urban areas, play an important and fundamental role as economic pillars and engines of job creation. however, they are faced with less positive factors such as population ageing and decline, pollution, traffic congestion or social exclusion. in this sense, european policies play a crucial role for sustainable economic and social development.
‒ the creation of an eu urban agenda has been advocated for many years, with the aim of ensuring better coordination of policies and the integration of urban development objectives across a wide range of policy areas. i agree that the so-called 'european urban agenda' should, in order to be effective, adopt a shared conceptual model, which is regularly updated, and a thematic centralisation on a limited number of challenges within the wider context of the europe 2020 strategy objectives of smart, inclusive and sustainable growth. i believe that european union policies should support cities and their metropolitan areas, also known as functional urban areas, and enable them to demonstrate their key role as catalysts for economic growth, employment, social inclusion and sustainable development.
‒ the present own-initiative report addresses the challenges that urban policy poses to european union policy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in this context, it is important to develop an eu urban agenda that assesses policy coordination and ensures the integration of urban development objectives horizontally across the broad policy framework of the legislator. the aim is to ensure coherence in environmental, employment, transport and energy policies, which have an impact on urban areas. in view of the pace of urbanisation, which is projected to reach almost 80% of the world's population by 2050 and in view of the urgency of this coordinated action to provide eu citizens with progressively better living conditions, i voted in favour of the owninitiative report.
‒ i recognise the importance of a european urban agenda for sustainable, integrated and socially inclusive development. in 2014, the percentage of the eu population living in urban areas was 72% and could reach 78% by 2030, generating two thirds of gdp. it is therefore necessary to take account of the involvement of urban areas in the fulfilment of the eu employment targets and the 2020 cohesion policy objectives. i support the rapporteur's view that the european urban agenda should be compatible with the global urban agenda.
‒ 72% of europe's population lives in urban areas and this report draws attention to the urban dimension of european policies and the main features of a future eu urban agenda. it is proposed that cities should be more involved in the design and implementation of european policies, and that these should be adapted to urban realities, respecting the principle of subsidiarity and the limits of the european regulatory framework. the creation of an eu-wide urban agenda should help to improve the quality, efficiency and effectiveness of development policies for cities and the regions where they are located - sometimes rural areas with problems of desertification and depopulation, and is also a vehicle for promoting overall sustainability and development aid policies. it should also be ambitious and integrate european societal challenges of co2 reduction, adaptation to climate change and inclusion or demographic change. the role of local, regional, national and european authorities in defining, developing and implementing the agenda is of paramount importance, with a focus on strengthening coordination between the various sectoral policies. only through active participation and coordinated policy action can cities provide their inhabitants with sound living conditions.
‒ it is well known that the vast majority of europe's population lives in cities and that this trend will deepen in the medium to long term (80% of the population by 2050). the report takes a positive approach to the 'urban issue' as a driver of economic development and a space for socioeconomic inclusion. it therefore advocates the application of the principles of subsidiarity, better coordination between cities and urban management as a factor of participation and citizenship. we share the importance of the urban dimension of policies and are accompanied by the idea that many of today's social and political challenges can only be solved at the territorial level with policies directed at the city where the population is concentrated and an increasing share of economic activity. what we do not agree with is the attempt to tie the urban agenda to the objectives of strategy 2020, which we do not agree with and which is in conflict with the need to give social responses close to the populations.
‒ the report focuses on the development of the european urban context, emphasising that the vast majority of europe's population lives in cities and that this is a trend that will deepen in the medium/long term (80% of the population by 2050). the report takes a positive approach to the 'urban issue', ranking cities as engines of economic development and as spaces for socioeconomic inclusion. it therefore advocates the application of the principles of subsidiarity, better coordination between cities and urban management as a factor of participation and citizenship. it does, however, set out that the implementation of the european urban agenda should 'take the form of a shared and regularly updated conceptual framework, with a thematic concentration on a limited number of challenges in the broader context of the europe 2020 objectives', challenges that must meet certain criteria such as: being in line with the shared conceptual framework and not being able to be solved unilaterally by member states. we abstained because we were not in line with this strategy, which is dominated by market values and liberalization.

‒ the humanitarian refugee crisis facing europe is one of the greatest challenges the european project has ever faced. it is well known that most of the human beings who arrive today traumatised at the external borders of the european union qualify as asylum seekers, a fundamental right enshrined in international law. in this context, the only dignified attitude that is in line with the values and principles on which the eu is founded is to welcome these people. the discrepancy between the ec's plans and the willingness of the member states has caused great disappointment among most european citizens. while signs of a more generous approach are beginning to emerge, a number of measures are still needed to tackle the causes of refugees leaving their countries of origin, to establish an effective common asylum system to replace the inoperative dublin regulation, to establish humanitarian corridors or to combat hate speech. the present motion for a resolution takes these and other aspects constructively, and assertively calls for the european institutions to face the problem with vigour and courage, and that is why i feel that my vote is fully deserved.
‒ this refugee crisis poses challenges that test the limits of our project and whose solution will surely define our future in crucial ways. more than ever we need an ever closer union among the peoples of europe, concrete achievements that create, first of all, a de facto solidarity! europeans have been up to the challenge, and it is time that governments were too. this resolution makes that very clear. we must quickly deal with the drama at europe's borders, and relieve the pressure on italy, greece and hungary. and to do that we need to implement quickly the agreed measures, such as the redistribution mechanism, without prejudice to a permanent solution with mandatory quotas. in parallel, however, the union must begin to act quickly to resolve the problems at the root of this mass flight of people, which involves creating legal migration routes, a policy for targeted development, a strong external policy, a strengthening of the role of the fronte and easo, among others. parliament has long called for these measures and will no doubt continue to do so!
‒ the european parliament has called on the eu to base its response to the refugee crisis on solidarity and equitable sharing of responsibility. however, the council's position has been inconsistent and unacceptable because it is based on contradictions, in particular by cutting in the 2016 budget proposal the instruments that tackle the problems of migration and refugees: the european union has also cut its contribution to the preaccession assistance instrument by eur 119 million, the european neighbourhood instrument by eur 100 million and the development cooperation instrument by eur 143 million. solidarity does not live by proclamations. solidarity is done with action. europe must be a safe and legal place of access to the asylum system, advocating the establishment of a binding quota for the distribution of asylum seekers among all eu countries, as well as contributions to refugee resettlement programmes, strengthening cooperation with third countries and stronger measures against traffickers in human beings and criminal networks of smugglers.

in writing. ‒ social economy enterprises have proven to be more resilient to economic disruption and have been able to offer innovative solutions for social cohesion and inclusion as well as for job creation. in addition, social economy enterprises have a strong link with local and regional reality, enabling them to offer solutions adapted to specific needs. social entrepreneurship and social innovation are key to strengthening the development of the social economy, and therefore it is crucial to pay particular attention to education and training. the eu needs to instill this innovative and entrepreneurial spirit in young people from an early age.
‒ the social and solidarity economy provides jobs for more than 14 million people, which is equivalent to about 6.5% of the eu's workforce, considering that there are 2 million social and solidarity economy enterprises in the eu, which represent 10% of the union's enterprises. the commission will assess the impact of the aid on the beneficiaries and the beneficiaries' ability to pay the costs of the aid. these companies have been very important in the economic recovery and the fight against unemployment.
in writing. ‒ i would stress that, following the economic and financial crisis, poverty and social exclusion levels have increased, as have long-term unemployment, youth unemployment and social inequalities. the most affected by the crisis were the most excluded and disadvantaged groups in the labour market, such as people with disabilities, young people, the elderly, women, the long-term unemployed and disadvantaged workers. i agree that the economic and financial crisis must be seen as an opportunity to move towards a more sustainable economic model for the eu. i argue that the social entrepreneurship model often appeals to young people, giving them an opportunity to find innovative answers to today's economic, social and environmental challenges. i consider it important that social and solidarity-based economy enterprises should be better integrated by member states into the employment and social inclusion action plans and national reform programmes, with a view to capitalising on their potential for job creation and their contribution to the achievement of the broad objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
‒ the social economy model is inspired by common values such as solidarity, social cohesion, the primacy of the individual over capital, social responsibility, democratic management and, finally, a guiding principle that promotes social impact by secondaryising profits that, if they exist, are reinvested in the company and society. during the economic and financial crisis of recent years, this business model has shown exceptional resilience to economic shocks, giving it an advantage over traditional companies. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of hiv/aids and aids-related diseases, and calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of hiv/aids and aids. the report, which i support with my vote, calls on the member states to promote an entrepreneurial culture and the cooperative and social entrepreneurship model in education and training programmes - a promotion that seeks to lay the foundations for more sustainable economic growth.
‒ the report refers to companies and organisations in the 'third sector', the so-called social and solidarity economy. it proposes the establishment of incentives for 'social entrepreneurship', considered as a more just and structural response to the socioeconomic crisis, unemployment or exclusion. despite the positive work of the so-called social and solidarity economy organisations, their socioeconomic relevance and the recognition of the appropriate support and framework these organisations deserve, the report emphasises entrepreneurship (not only in this sector) as the absolute! solution to the problems of eu societies, and business creation as the answer to which all systems (economic, educational/training) should be oriented (inclusion in school curricula of entrepreneurship subjects, for example). it also places these organisations as substitutes for public services in a trend towards the discharge of the public sector from the (public, free and quality) services they are supposed to provide to the populations. we voted against it.
‒ in the aftermath of the european economic and financial crisis, unemployment remains one of the eu's biggest challenges, with high levels, especially among the youngest. ambitious labour market economic and social policies are therefore needed, alongside those already taken by the eu and member states, which foster smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and generate quality jobs and jobs. i support the dlabajová report for calling for careful attention to this problem, for pointing out the need to integrate young people, women and older people into the labour market, for stressing the importance of continuing education and training in achieving a competitive labour market that generates growth, for highlighting the importance of sharing best practices between member states and for stressing the importance of innovation and the digital transition. the importance of training and retraining programmes for the unemployed is emphasised, which should be designed and implemented in such a way as to better align the new skills of workers with the needs of the labour market.
‒ unemployment remains one of the biggest challenges in the eu, with a rate of 9.9% in december 2014, with very substantial disparities between member states (4.8% in germany, compared to 23.7% in spain). youth unemployment rates are more than double that, reaching 21.4% at eu level. on the other hand, there are some 2 million jobs in the eu that are not being filled, due to both the inadequacy of skills to labour market needs and the lack of worker mobility. to combat this problem, strong partnerships between governments and employers' and workers' representatives are needed to find the best solutions to address skills mismatches in all dimensions of the labour market. member states themselves should share and learn from best practice and support initiatives that foster their own job creation and entrepreneurship, with a particular focus on smes and micro-enterprises as the backbone of the eu labour market.
‒ ambitious economic and social policies and labour market reforms are needed to foster smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as well as to create more jobs and generate quality and sustainable jobs. there is also a need for sustainable social protection systems that include upgrading the skills of the unemployed, promoting the employability of people with no or very little qualifications, as well as incentives and job opportunities. that is why i am voting in favour.
‒ i argue that the evolution of the european labour market needs to be reflected in the skills of workers, as well as in initial and vocational training, as the demand for low-skilled workers is decreasing and the demand for highly skilled workers has increased considerably. i argue that economic and social policies and labour market reforms are urgently needed to foster smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as well as to create more quality and sustainable jobs. i stress the need for sustainable social protection systems, including updating the skills of the unemployed, promoting the employability of people with no or low qualifications, and providing incentives and job opportunities. i support the measures presented in the report, which are necessary to promote both the recruitment of young workers, including support for employers to organise in-house training, and the reintegration of older workers, with the establishment of vocational retraining facilities, updating of the skills of these workers and adequate preparation for the challenges presented by new jobs.
‒ eurostat estimates that 23.067 million men and women in the eu-28 were unemployed in july 2015. the causes of high unemployment rates are complex and diverse, but in a crisis scenario where the labour market is particularly subject to the adverse effects of economic cycles, it is also important to address the structural inefficiencies inherent in the labour market. the rapporteur takes account of the available statistical indicators, which point to significant distortions between the skills of workers and the needs of the labour market. only the establishment of strong partnerships between governments and employers' and workers' representatives can address this skills mismatch and help fill the 2 million jobs in the european union that have become available as a result of this disagreement. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution in question, which calls on the member states to promote the close and systematic involvement of the labour market players (trainers and employers) so that, in a joint effort, future skills needs can be anticipated.
‒ statistical manipulation around unemployment is widespread. behind many of the figures on the decline in unemployment rates are precarious employment, insecurity and the misery of many workers. in portugal it has been decided that the so-called "employed" are not part of the unemployment rates. we are talking about workers who, instead of having a contract of employment corresponding to their permanent post - often in public institutions - are workers who have a so-called 'employment-integration contract', who attend a training course or a vocational training course. in june last year, in portugal, these workers were already more than 150 000 workers in this type of precarious employment, about 50 000 of them under the so-called 'employment-insertion contract', under which workers earn less than the minimum wage. the eu itself funds this kind of labour exploitation. in the previous financial framework, more than €95 million from the european social fund went to these pseudo-contracts. it is certainly not by increasing the flexibility of industrial relations - as you have so often repeated - that a competitive labour market will be built which will improve the lives of workers.
‒ the report advocates the creation of what it considers to be greater labour competitiveness in the eu context. the reality is that in many eu countries the unemployment rate is very high, while there are vacancies to be filled (around 2 million). the report's response to ensure this 'competitiveness' is emphasised in the document in two ways: (1) the adaptation of education and training systems to labour market needs, in particular dual training, and the involvement of the 'business world' in curriculum design; (2) the promotion of labour mobility, adaptability and flexibility. the first subordinates the educational system (an individual right which must respond to the various needs of society) to the needs of the market, while the second perpetuates precariousness, with the common excuse of the need for "competitiveness". we voted against it.

in writing. ‒ this is a protocol to the forced labour convention, which is one of the eight international labour organisation conventions that form the core of international labour law instruments. this protocol in particular aims to address the problems, shortcomings and difficulties in the progress made in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as the protection and compensation of victims of this scourge. as this is a matter in which member states and the union share competence, the european parliament also needs to give its consent for the member states to ratify the protocol on behalf of the union. that's what you do with my support today.
‒ the ilo estimates that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are currently victims of forced labour and this draft resolution aims to eliminate disparities, develop the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation and protect and compensate victims of forced labour. with regard to victims, the protocol provides that effective measures are to be taken for their identification, release, protection, recovery and rehabilitation, as well as for other forms of assistance and support. the ratification of the protocol is therefore an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime throughout europe. its ratification by the member states will facilitate the fight against traffickers.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision authorising member states to ratify the ilo convention on forced labour in matters relating to cooperation in criminal matters. it is one of the eight core ilo labour conventions, and is inextricably linked to the protection of human rights. the new ilo protocol, adopted by the 103rd session of the international labour conference, aims to prevent the use of forced labour, particularly in the context of trafficking in human beings, by improving the protection of victims and providing for access to compensation.
‒ with the adoption of the convention in 1930, the international labour conference encouraged member countries to end the use of forced labour as soon as possible. more than 80 years later, the international labour organization estimates that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. the protocol aims to eliminate disparities in implementation, to develop the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation and to protect and compensate victims of forced labour. it is important to note that the 2014 protocol deals with fundamental rights, victims and the fight against trafficking in human beings, a crime that affects individuals but also society and the economy as a whole. i believe that ratification of the protocol will be decisive in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime throughout europe.

in writing. ‒ the substance 5(2aminopropyl) indole is a synthetic derivative of indole substituted in the phenyl part of the indole ring system. it appears to be a stimulant substance, which may also have hallucinogenic effects. the substance 5- ((2-aminopropyl) indole was mainly found in powder form, but also in the form of tablets and capsules. it was also detected in samples of a product sold similar to ecstasy tablets and is marketed on the internet. existing information and data suggest that the acute toxicity of 5(2aminopropyl) indole may cause adverse effects in humans such as tachycardia, hyperthermia, agitation and tremor. the specific physical effects of 5- ((2-aminopropyl) indole in humans are difficult to determine because there are no published studies assessing its acute and chronic toxicity, its psychological and behavioural effects, or the potential for dependence, and therefore there is little information and limited data available.
