‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to ensure rapid, effective and flexible assistance to the population of a member state and to countries negotiating its accession in the event of a major natural disaster. this fund complements public funds from member states in emergency situations, in particular for the urgent rehabilitation of infrastructure, temporary accommodation and emergency services to meet the immediate needs of the population, as well as for the cleaning up of the areas affected by the disaster. in 2015, bulgaria was affected by severe winter conditions that caused a 'large scale natural disaster' - and greece was affected by two catastrophes - floods in the evros river basin and in central regions of greece - considered 'regional disasters'. following the disasters, the countries concerned requested assistance from the european union solidarity fund. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 16 274 765 in commitment and payment appropriations from the european union solidarity fund to alleviate the pain, suffering and loss of those affected by these disasters.
‒ the european union solidarity fund (the 'fund') aims to enable the union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters, and the fund's intervention should not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 500 million. bulgaria submitted an application to mobilise the fund, following severe winter conditions. greece submitted two applications to mobilise the fund, following floods. i agree, therefore the fund should be mobilised in the amount of €16 274 765 to meet the requests made by bulgaria and greece.
‒ the eusf aims to provide a rapid, efficient and flexible response to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters. the eusf was requested to be mobilised to provide financial assistance following a disaster in bulgaria (severe winter conditions causing a 'large scale natural disaster' as defined by the eusf) and two disasters in greece (floods in the evros river basin and central regions of greece, considered 'regional disasters' as defined by the eusf). these storms caused considerable damage to public infrastructure, including dams, communication networks and roads, as well as to businesses, housing and private property (more than 300 buildings in burgas were flooded), and damaged the agricultural and forestry sectors in bulgaria, and caused damage to essential infrastructure, public buildings, private housing, businesses and the agricultural sector in greece, destroying agricultural infrastructure, warehouses and crops. i support the adoption of this report, since it meets the requirements.
‒ this is a report on the proposal to mobilise the eu solidarity fund for financial assistance following a disaster in bulgaria (severe winter conditions) and two disasters in greece (floods in the evros river basin and central regions of greece). the total amount of aid proposed was €16 274 765 (10% already advanced).
‒ this report concerns a proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund, totalling eur 16,3 million (in commitment and payment appropriations) eur 6,4 million for bulgaria and eur 9,9 million for greece as a financial response to the devastating natural disasters that occurred in those member states in early 2015. from the analysis of the report, the criteria for the mobilisation of the eusf are met and, being aware of the nature of the disasters, their scale and the profound impact these tragedies have had on local communities, i voted in favour of this mobilisation.
‒ in late january and early february 2015, large areas of bulgaria were hit by heavy rainfall, snow, flooding and landslides, with the south-eastern region being the most affected. these phenomena have caused considerable damage. in early february 2015, the regions of eastern macedonia and thrace were hit by widespread flooding, which caused damage to essential infrastructure, public buildings, private housing, businesses, as well as to the agricultural sector in greece, destroying agricultural infrastructure, warehouses and crops. in the same period, large areas of the central and western regions of greece were affected by another series of floods, which caused even greater damage, resulting in power cuts, the isolation of several mountain villages and the destruction of some greek cultural heritage assets. the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund (eusf) to provide financial assistance. we agree with this mobilisation, but we must also point out that the sectoral policies of the european union - such as the cap - contribute to an increase in the exposure of certain regions to the risk of disasters.
‒ a number of agricultural products (by origin or production by traditional methods) enjoy protection of geographical indications in the eu. it is desirable that such protection be extended to non-agricultural and traditional products such as handicrafts, embroidery and ceramics, which currently do not have a single system of protection, enjoying different levels of protection in the member states. in portugal, this will be the case, among others, of the arraiolos carpets or the handkerchiefs of the lovers of minho, so well defended by mr josé manuel fernandes. i fully support mrs rozière's report because it considers it vital to protect these traditional quality products based on traditional know-how and techniques which are part of the eu's cultural heritage and which generate activities directly related to local ways of life, especially in rural areas, helping to increase the attractiveness of these areas, to preserve local identities and to promote their specificity, with benefits for tourism, culture, employment and trade. in addition to the economic potential and the protection of their jobs, i would stress the benefits for citizens and consumers who are better protected and have more confidence in these products. i call on the european commission to come forward swiftly with the legislative proposal to create this system.
in writing. ‒ i believe that traditions strengthen our roots and promote development. portugal is very rich in handicrafts, embroidery and pottery. these products should benefit from a european system for the protection of geographical indications. in this way we protect the production method, tie the product to the site, preserve knowledge and jobs and give reliable information to the consumer. this legislation should promote innovation in traditional production processes and the creation of new businesses, as has been the case in portugal and, above all, in minho, as evidenced by the vila verde sweetheart scarves and the namorar portugal initiative. it should be noted that micro and small enterprises account for about 80% of typical local products. the viana embroidery, the guimarães embroidery and the vinhais mask are examples of products which could benefit from the legislation i am advocating. i therefore agree that the new rules could promote innovation in traditional production processes and the creation of new companies in the traditional products sector, and also contribute to the sustainability of jobs.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal on the possible extension of the protection afforded by european union geographical indications to non-agricultural products. it is essential that the quality of traditional european products be maintained and preserved. this proposal is intended to improve the fight against fraud by helping to abolish counterfeiting and, above all, to avoid unfair competition which misleads the consumer. non-agricultural products are part of our history, our identity and are also part of the cultural heritage of the member states.
‒ the european union does not currently have a single system for the protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products, unlike for agricultural and food products. i believe that this gap provides an inadequate european framework, as some member states do not have specific protection and others have established different definitions, procedures and levels of protection under national and local rules. it is important that producers, regional associations and the public authorities in madeira work together to preserve our culture and age-old traditions, such as tapestry, vimes or madeira embroidery. it is an opportunity to modernise, internationalise and safeguard these products. i fully support this document because the protection of non-agricultural products by geographical indications can highlight the eu's cultural heritage, preserve the economy of many regions of europe; support entrepreneurship at local and regional level, by promoting the maintenance of infrastructure and the creation of more skilled and local jobs; and have positive effects for consumers, producers and the whole european economic and social fabric.
‒ this report provides that non-agricultural products (crafts, ceramics, embroidery) benefit from a european system for the protection of geographical indications. as with agri-food products, this system must be visible to the consumer and must give him confidence in terms of quality, authenticity and transparency. i think it is advantageous, especially in terms of protecting micro and small enterprises (which account for about 80% of the production of these products). such legislation can also help to combat effectively counterfeiting and fraudulent use of geographical indications, practices which mislead the final consumer and are harmful to producers, most of whom still lack the legal or financial means to defend their interests.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of the protection of geographical indications, the commission proposes that the european parliament and the council adopt a resolution on the protection of geographical indications in the european union. such a measure will have a very positive impact at local level by providing protection for the unique characteristics of these products and ensuring their quality (and traceability), providing consumers with reliable information on the place and method of production, promoting process innovation and the creation of new businesses in the traditional products sector. it could also boost tourism, ensuring the safeguarding and sustainability of jobs in areas where employment is scarce. a harmonised european legislation on this subject, extended to non-agricultural products, will not only help to combat counterfeiting but also strengthen the system of protection of geographical indications in bilateral and multilateral trade negotiations. i welcome the opportunity of this proposal, which makes a significant contribution to the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the regions and to the european cultural heritage, with the ultimate aim of providing a high level of protection for all traditional european products, whether agricultural or not, outside the eu.
in writing. ‒ the system of geographical indications (gi) as a quality designation can be an added value for products that meet the requirements to benefit from it. this added value can be translated into consumer information and preference, both inside and outside the european union, which is all the more relevant in a context of erosion of our trade borders and closer ties with other regional partners. current experience with gi for agricultural products reveals that there is widespread consumer ignorance of gi, which may counteract the intended effect. it is important to take account of this experience, where relevant, and to draw lessons from it in order to lay the foundations for a good strategy for non-agricultural products. this must be done in a cost-benefit logic, without losing sight of the intended objectives: to strengthen the territorial role of european production, which in this case can only be achieved if this system has a clear impact from the point of view of consumer recognition and preference.
the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide system of geographical indications for non-agricultural products, taking into account the traditional european quality products based on traditional know-how and techniques which are an integral part of the eu's cultural heritage and which must be preserved. protection of gi's could act as an incentive to preserve cultural heritage and traditional know-how, and could help to prevent depopulation and destruction of rural areas and to halt the exodus of young people leaving these areas, by ensuring fair remuneration for producers. good legislation can help to combat counterfeiting effectively, to promote and facilitate access to the common market and to markets outside the eu, and to stimulate economic development at regional and local level.
‒ the objective of this report is to increase the level of initial pre-financing of the programmes of greece's cohesion policy under the investment for growth and jobs goal and the programmes under the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) for the period 2014-2020 and, on the other hand, to increase to 100% the maximum co-financing rates of the operational programmes under the convergence objective and the regional competitiveness and employment objective. these measures are designed to address a serious lack of liquidity in the greek economy and to provide an immediate and desired stimulus to investment. in order to ensure that the additional initial pre-financing amount is used effectively and reaches the beneficiaries of the esf, the cohesion fund and the emff as quickly as possible, the additional pre-financing amount should be reimbursed to the commission if it is not followed by an appropriate level of payment requests within a given time-frame. for all these reasons, i support the mihaylova report.
in writing. ‒ this proposal strengthens solidarity - but the european union's budgetary solidarity has been in existence for many decades. i would remind you that the european social fund has actually been in existence since 1958. but this is a strengthening of solidarity which will relieve greece, which is in financial difficulty, a liquidity difficulty, and will therefore be able to use the funds with less financial effort on its part. this lesser financial effort, this greater solidarity, requires greater vigilance, requires additional responsibility. the 100% cofinancing amounts, the prefinancing rates correspond to about 2 billion euros, require that these amounts be used for projects that are sustainable. we want intelligent solidarity, which contributes to greece's growth, which contributes to the strengthening of greece's competitiveness, which brings more jobs, and therefore these funds, in addition to social cohesion, in addition to economic cohesion, owe greater wealth to greece. i hope that greece, the greek authorities, will seize this opportunity which they cannot afford to lose.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal amending regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 of the european parliament and of the council laying down common provisions on the european structural and investment funds, which provides for specific measures for greece. it is essential that the lack of liquidity and public funds resulting from the severe financial crisis in greece does not hamper investment under those programmes, which is essential for the economic recovery of the country.
in writing. - i support this report in the face of the pressing financial situation in greece, a member state beset by liquidity problems and a lack of public funds. i agree that it is essential that this lack of liquidity and public funds in greece does not prevent investment under programmes supported by the european regional development fund, the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). given the exceptional nature of the situation, i believe that the european union should try to intervene with specific measures, simplified procedures and effective as soon as possible, in order to contribute to the overall effort to help greece. i support the amendments to the common provisions regulation contained in this report, given their objective of making up for the lack of liquidity in the greek economy and of boosting investment in the short term by enabling the speedy launch of a greater number of projects.
‒ the austerity policies have had terrible impacts on the lives of the individuals, families, companies and countries affected by the troika. austerity has only created more misery, more poverty, more bankruptcies, more fear, more emigration, more flight from the top, more depression and suicide. this happened in greece, but also in portugal. for four years we felt the hardness of being europe's youngest son. greece was severely punished during these years. at the same time, hundreds of refugees are arriving in greece every day, and we are almost 'demanding' that the greek government deal with the matter, simply because greece should be one of the gateways to this europe which should be united. we now have the opportunity to help greece by adopting this package of specific measures through european funds. it's not about "giving more money" to greece. this is to anticipate the financing of operational programmes to promote growth and employment. we know that cohesion policies have been and are fundamental for the countries most affected by the crisis. just as there has been technical assistance from the european institutions in implementing austerity measures, so there should be now when we talk about investment.
‒ having been hit by the consequences of the financial crisis in a unique way, greece is now facing liquidity problems and a lack of public funds available for the investments needed to foster a sustainable economic recovery, and therefore lacks additional pre-financing for the operational programmes of the cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. this is an exceptional situation requiring exceptional measures, and therefore additional pre-financing is provided for the 2014-2020 cohesion policy operational programmes under the investment for growth and jobs goal and for programmes financed by the european maritime and fisheries fund; the proposal also provides for a ceiling of 100% for the cumulative total of prefinancing and interim payments, increasing to 100% the co-financing rate for the 2007-13 operational programmes under the convergence, regional competitiveness and employment objectives in this country. it should be noted that this solution, which i voted for, requires a serious commitment effort from greece, which involves accelerating the pace of its payment requests for the programmes concerned before the end of 2016, or else repay the additional initial pre-financing.
‒ the measures concern the release of the funds under the 2007-2013 framework, amounting to 800 million, financed at 100%, allowing the closure of the projects that were applied for under this framework. the commission notes that the greek authorities have not provided any evidence that the aid granted to the beneficiary is compatible with the internal market. it is understood that this aid is positive and may alleviate the suffering of many people. however, this is only a palliative. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the greek economy is restored to a sound basis and in accordance with the will of the greek people. the situation in greece confirms our second analysis, namely that it is urgent to open a comprehensive process of renegotiation of sovereign debts at european union level and to hold an intergovernmental conference to review the treaties, in particular the budgetary treaty, and to remove the monetary buffer that blocks any possibility of alternative and sovereign development. this position and the coherence it requires, which justified a vote in favour of the above amendments, must not interfere with the sense of solidarity which the greek people deserve from us, and it is not our intention to block the allocation of eu funds.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of its main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 6 958 623 for germany to support the 2 881 workers made redundant at adam opel ag and a supplier company.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (the fund) aims to enable the union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters, and the fund's intervention should not exceed a maximum annual amount of eur 500 million. germany submitted a request following redundancies at adam opel ag and a supplier company in germany. i therefore agree that a financial contribution of eur 6 958 623 should be mobilised to meet the request made by germany.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, application egf/2015/002 de/adam opel. according to the commission, the measures described constitute active labour market measures falling within the eligible actions defined in article 7 of the egf regulation. these actions do not replace passive social protection measures. it should be noted that the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. this is an application that meets the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation.
‒ the egf was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. in the present case, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of germany to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in adam opel ag, nace revision 2, division 29 (manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers) and in a supplier company. the source of the redundancies is the total closure of the adam opel ag production plant in bochum, due to the 25% decrease between 2007 and 2013 in the number of new cars registered in the eu and efta member states. i agree with the importance of improving the employability of all dismissed workers through adapted training and the recognition of qualifications and skills acquired throughout their working career, and it is vital that the training offered is adapted not only to the needs of dismissed workers but also to the real environment of companies. i therefore support the adoption of this report.
‒ the european union has set up legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers who have been affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns (globalisation) or the global economic and financial crisis, and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. germany submitted this application on the basis of the sharp decline in sales of cars by adam opel ag. 2826 workers were made redundant (plus 55 workers made redundant in suppliers and producers of adam opel ag). eur 6 958 623 was mobilised for assistance. germany submitted this application on the basis of a criterion of the european globalisation adjustment fund which defines at least 500 workers made redundant in an enterprise in a member state in a reference period of 4 months. without calling into question the general principle, it seems, however, to be a criterion tailored to large companies.

‒ regulation (ec) no 861/2007 establishes a european small claims procedure with the aim of simplifying and speeding up small claims in cross-border cases and reducing the costs involved. the experience gained during its existence shows that, although the european small claims procedure has proved to be a useful instrument, recourse to the courts remains low. i support the increase in the limit for using the european small claims procedure from eur 2 000 to eur 10 000, which will be a considerable improvement for smes. the organisation of videoconferencing hearings will help to reduce costs and increase the use of such actions, as it will not be necessary to travel to the court. the obligation for member states to set up means of distance payment will allow applicants to save between eur 400 and eur 800 in payment costs when travelling. with these proposals we are helping to improve the functioning of the european small claims procedure.
in writing. ‒ this report amends regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 1896/2006 establishing a european small claims procedure and a european order for payment procedure, applicable to disputed and uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters the value of which does not exceed eur 2 000. these regulations ensured that decisions given in the context of such proceedings were enforceable without intermediate proceedings, in particular without the need for a declaration of enforceability in the member state of enforcement (abolition of the exequatur). the general objective was to improve access to justice by reducing costs and speeding up civil proceedings in respect of claims falling within its scope, both for consumers and for businesses. it has been recognised that the european small claims procedure has facilitated the settlement of cross-border cases concerning such actions in the eu. however, obstacles to the full application of this procedure for the benefit of consumers and businesses, in particular smes, are identified, which relate to the low threshold provided for in the current regulation which deprives many potential claimants of the use of a simplified procedure in cross-border disputes. the amendments proposed here deal with this aspect of course. in general, the report deserves our agreement.
‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 11 july 2007 establishing a european small claims procedure and regulation (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 12 december 2006 establishing a european order for payment procedure. after five years of application, the european small claims procedure has proved to be an extremely useful instrument, simplifying and speeding up small claims in cross-border cases and reducing the related costs. however, there was still room to strengthen the application of that regulation in order to encourage its application and use.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of 11 july 2007 establishes the european small claims procedure with the aim of simplifying such actions in cross-border cases, thus reducing the costs of litigation. access to justice is the main objective, making it a useful procedure to facilitate such access for consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the limit for small claims should be revised and court costs should be proportionate to the value of the cases, with the aim of increasing the use of this procedure in some member states where small claims are significantly low in value. flexible dispute resolution conditions should be provided for, through distance communication methods, the abolition of language barriers and the transparency of procedures. i am in favour of this proposal, which meets the need for swift and simplified justice, providing consumers and businesses with fair and immediate solutions.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the european small claims procedure and a new european order for payment procedure. this regulation will bring about uniform law throughout the community in the settlement of crossborder disputes and also disputes involving another crossborder element, so that union citizens can benefit from more simplified and less costly access to justice. with regard to the full development of the single market in the european union, it is also essential that consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises also benefit from a secure, transparent and useful legal system, and can thus bring actions without fear of legal costs disproportionate to the amount of the action, or proceedings whose length of time undermines confidence in justice and, consequently, in the single market. in order to remedy the shortcomings in the application of the regulation, five years after its entry into force, amendments are proposed to extend the scope of the procedure, limit legal costs, make payment methods more flexible and modernise the communication channels. i voted in favour.
‒ the adoption of this report has a significant practical effect for european citizens. claiming back the money spent on a defective product is not always easy, involving bureaucracy, large expenses and even trips to the country of origin, if this involves a court decision. oftentimes, the injured consumer gives up because the work and expense involved in the complaint is not justified. the aim of this decision is to simplify and speed up small claims in crossborder cases and to reduce the costs of small claims (by making them proportionate to the amounts claimed). the main objective is to help consumers and smes bring their cases and thus ensure access to justice. the use of small claims courts remains low and efforts need to be stepped up in terms of legal certainty, language barriers and transparency of proceedings.
in writing. ‒ this report seeks to amend regulations (ec) no 861/2007 and (ec) no 1896/2006, as it has been found that the application of these instruments, five years after their entry into force, has proved to be very useful, although it is possible and desirable to extend and strengthen their scope, since the use of small claims courts in european terms remains significantly low and efforts need to be intensified in relation to legal certainty, language barriers and the transparency of proceedings. in this respect, i support this proposal to raise the limit for small claims from € 2000 to € 10 000, and to extend the definition of what constitutes a crossborder case to include other elements than domicile in the member state, such as the place where the contract is executed or the place where the harmful event occurred. on the procedural side, the idea of equalising the means of service, the use of videoconferencing for hearings, the setting of a ceiling on legal costs and the reduction of the length of proceedings are also positive. for all these reasons, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report amends regulations (ec) no 861/2007 and (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council and establishes a european small claims procedure. it establishes a european order for payment procedure applicable to disputed and uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters the value of which does not exceed eur 2 000. those regulations also ensured that decisions given in the context of that procedure were enforceable without intermediate proceedings, in particular without a declaration of enforceability being required in the member state of enforcement. the general objective of these regulations was to improve access to justice, reduce costs and speed up civil proceedings in respect of claims falling within their scope, both for consumers and for businesses. we have, however, reservations about the possibility of dealing with matters of labour law, since in portugal we have the labour courts which judge these matters.
‒ the purpose of this report is to amend regulations (ec) no 861/2007 and (ec) no 1896/2006 of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european small claims procedure and a european order for payment procedure, applicable to contested and uncontested claims in civil and commercial matters the value of which does not exceed eur 2 000. these regulations had the express objective of improving access to justice, reducing costs and speeding up civil proceedings in respect of claims falling within their scope, both for consumers and for businesses. the amendments now introduced, among other things, raise the maximum amount concerned to eur 5000, extending the scope to the concept of matrimonial property regimes and maintenance obligations. we believe that these measures can facilitate the feasibility of this type of crossborder judicial proceedings, improving access to and speed of justice.
‒ medium combustion plants are a major source of emissions of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter (fine dust) and are used for a wide range of purposes, such as electricity generation, domestic/residential heating and cooling, and the production of heat and/or steam for industrial processes. emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants (unlike small and large plants) are not normally regulated at eu level. this proposal is designed to fill this gap. in the eu there are about 150 000 medium combustion plants, i.e. plants with a thermal output of between 1 and 50 mw. the proposal sets emission limits for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. the commission's original proposal has been amended several times and we are generally in agreement with it. we supported the proposed exceptions for the archipelagos of madeira and the azores, which we consider to be fully justified, taking into account their nature and specific situation, and there should be another framework.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, particularly as regards the azores and madeira, because i believe that the poorest regions cannot be subject to higher levels of pollution simply because they do not have the means. i understand, of course, the argument of the lack of resources, but i think that the derogation from the limits is a contradiction in terms of its results and would in fact imply a double penalty for these regions, which remain poorer and would be more polluted by this derogation. the solution to this equation is necessarily the eu's response to help and equip the regions with the means to meet the limits.
‒ the report on the proposal for a directive is presented as an important instrument for improving air quality, and i therefore voted in favour of limiting emissions of certain pollutants into the atmosphere, which is the central issue under discussion. the aim is to establish a more coherent and ambitious regulatory framework within the union, closing important gaps that have been identified so far, without imposing unjustified burdens.
‒ the control of emissions of pollutants into the atmosphere from medium combustion plants is not regulated at eu level. as such, there is an urgent need to close this gap, as we are faced with an issue in the field of the protection of human health and the environment. the aim is to set minimum requirements for new and existing plants by setting emission limit values for pollutants, introducing aggregation rules for new combustion plants and obliging member states to apply limit values in areas outside eu air quality standards. this proposal is in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and also with the new air quality framework for action set out in the eu thematic strategy on air pollution. the environment and the citizens of the eu need to be protected by measures that contribute to that end, and therefore i vote in favour of this proposal for a directive.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment. it should be noted that, as a general rule, emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants are not regulated at eu level and only this proposal will make it possible to set limit values for existing and future plants in line with the community's emission reduction obligations. i voted in favour of the proposed amendments because i consider that the compromise solution between the burden on society and the economy and the quality of air is fair, as defined in the proposal.
in writing. ‒ we all agree on the harmful effects of air pollution on public health and the environment. if we want effective results we have to go to the source of pollution. this directive lays down provisions for medium combustion plants (150 000 in the eu), setting limit values for new and existing plants, together with a simple registration system, to ensure compliance by member states with the reduction of polluting emissions. an eu climate policy will only be credible at global level if it is combined with a competitive industrial strategy but with a strong emphasis on sustainability and innovation. as is clear, i voted in favour of this report, with the exception of two points in an amendment (87) tabled by the envi committee which provides for the exception to the directive for the canary islands, madeira, the azores and the french islands. the argument put forward for the exception is based exclusively on the increase in financial burdens and the logistical difficulties inherent in an island which, if true, cannot prevail over the quality of life of the population. air quality must be guaranteed in all european regions, whether or not they are the outermost regions. there are no first-class citizens and no second-class citizens.
‒ the fight against the atmospheric emissions of certain pollutants from medium combustion plants is at the heart of this proposal for a directive. in fact, there is a gap in this area, arising from the absence of any specific regulation at european level applying to emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants, which needs to be filled not only to bring about greater legislative coherence but also to reduce the harmful impacts on the environment and, not least, to combat the harmful effects these emissions have on human health. another important aspect that will be addressed by regulation in this area is the significant contribution that the reduction of emissions from medium combustion plants will make to the achievement of the eu's climate and energy objectives by reducing greenhouse gases, improving energy efficiency and promoting renewable energy. the adoption of these measures will send a clear signal in favour of new investment, creating more incentives for research and innovation in cutting-edge technologies, and allowing european companies to take a leading position in green innovation. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour.

‒ the proposal for a directive sets emission limits for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from medium combustion plants. on 23 june 2015, the european parliament and the council reached a provisional agreement on the proposal. about 75% of medium combustion plants are run by smes. care must be taken not to impose an excessive administrative burden. on the other hand, it is important to look at the context in which they operate, either because of the climate or because of their geographical location, with particular emphasis on the island territories of the eu countries.

‒ it is proposed to approximate the laws of the member states concerning certain caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption, taking into account other legislation adopted in the meantime, in particular in the food sector, and harmonising the compositional requirements for food caseins with the relevant international standard (codex alimentarius). the products covered by the proposal are not intended for sale to the final consumer but are used for the preparation of foodstuffs and are therefore traded between companies in the sector. it is important that food business operators have the information necessary for the labelling of final products, in particular when allergens are involved. for this reason, the proposal provides for provisions on the labelling of caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. if the mandatory information provided for therein is not provided on the packaging, containers or labels, those products may not be placed on the market as food caseins and caseinates or used for the preparation of foodstuffs. the alignment of the requirements on the composition of food casein with codex alimentarius will ensure a level playing field for food business operators. the rapporteur temporarily limits the commission's power to adopt delegated acts and suggests some technical amendments to ensure consistency with codex alimentarius. we voted in favour.
‒ i have tabled my vote in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to certain caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. the aim is to ensure that the information which is exchanged between companies for the preparation of foodstuffs is appropriate for the labelling of the final products, particularly as regards allergens.
‒ in the context of certain lactoproteins (caseins and caseinates), the aim is to approximate the laws of the member states with a view to consolidating european legislation in the food sector by repealing directive 83/417/eec. the aim is to separate the powers of the commission and to harmonise the compositional requirements for food caseins with international standards, in particular the codex alimentarius standard. the repeal of directive 83/417/eec is necessary to the extent that the current legislation concerns foodstuffs. in addition, with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, there is a need to establish a distinction between the powers of the commission to adopt non-legislative acts and to adopt implementing acts. the proposal establishes the compositional and quality requirements for casein products referred to in the codex alimentarius standard. i am in favour of the adoption of this new directive, thus creating a level playing field for food business operators and consumers alike.
‒ this report on a proposal from the council and the european parliament is intended only to introduce specifications to harmonise legislation and ensure transparency in the member states as regards certain lactoproteins (caseins and caseinates) intended for human consumption. the report also calls for the introduction of a european standardisation body to ensure that the standards are complied with.
‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to certain caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption, as i considered that it would be prudent to harmonise this matter with international standards on general food law, which would allow the free movement of safe, wholesome foodstuffs that contribute to the health and well-being of european citizens. i would stress the provisions on the labelling of caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption as mandatory information to be included on packaging, containers and labels, enabling consumers to make informed decisions regarding food allergies and intolerances.
in addition to the technical nature of this text which we voted on, one of the aspects of particular relevance has to do with the best possible information for the consumer. it is essential to have a system which allows the clear identification of potentially allergenic substances, which means that they must be labelled. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
‒ as regards harmonisation with international standards (codex alimentarius), it is proposed to set the parameters for the maximum moisture content of casein in foodstuffs at 12% (instead of the 10% previously provided) and the maximum milk fat content of casein in acid foodstuffs at 2% (instead of the 2,25%). in order to allow for the rapid adaptation of annexes i to iii (standards for food casein, food casein obtained from coal and food caseinates with regard to their composition, contamination, process aids used, etc.) to international standards and future technical progress, the commission also suggests the adoption of delegated acts. it is suggested that the power to adopt delegated acts to adapt the annexes should not be conferred on the commission for an unlimited period of time, but only for 5 years, and it is proposed that a date be set for the application of this directive in the member states.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption, as i considered it important to approximate the laws of the member states concerning certain lactoproteins (caseins and caseinates) intended for human consumption by repealing the current european council directive 83/417/eec. the european commission's proposal to replace the current directive should be considered in the context of general food law, which aims to allow the free movement of safe and wholesome foodstuffs, thus contributing significantly to the health and well-being of citizens. in this respect, although the products covered by the proposal (caseins and caseinates) are not intended for sale to the final consumer but only between companies for the preparation of food products, the proposal is important in that it implements the need for food business operators to have the necessary information on the labelling of final products and for the compositional requirements for food caseins to be harmonised with international standards.

‒ the universal abolition of the death penalty is one of the eu's key human rights objectives. the death penalty is incompatible with the values on which the eu is founded and in this regard it is important to leave here a testimony of the strong condemnation that its application arouses and an appeal to the european institutions and the member states to remain vigilant to developments in this field and to continue with determination their fight to abolish the use of the death penalty, strongly supporting the moratorium as a step towards such abolition, and urging those countries that still use the death penalty to comply with international minimum standards, reduce its scope and use and publish accurate and unambiguous data on the number of convictions and executions. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ 10 october is world day against the death penalty. the global abolition of the death penalty remains a key objective of eu human rights policy. in 2014, at least 2,466 people in 55 countries were sentenced to death (an increase of 23% from 2013), not including china, which sentences more than all other countries combined. the eu continues to condemn the use of the death penalty, which is incompatible with the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, equality and democracy which underpin its constitution. this proposal encourages us all, and in particular the member states, not to give up and to make every effort to put an end to this practice with third countries.
in writing. ‒ over the past 12 months, there has been a worldwide resurgence in the use of the death penalty for drug-related crimes, with some states (such as iran and saudi arabia) experiencing a significant increase in the number of executions for these crimes. other states are seeking to reintroduce the death penalty for drug-related offences (such as oman), and some states have ended the long-standing moratorium on the death penalty (such as indonesia and pakistan). of the 14 countries that carry out the death penalty for drug-related offences, 12 are asian or middle eastern countries. in 2015, 14 people were executed in indonesia for drug trafficking, including 12 foreigners. dozens of people are awaiting execution on death row, including european citizens, such as frenchman serge atlaoui. at a time when we are commemorating the european day against the death penalty, it is time to express our opposition to this practice, which is an affront to human dignity, and to hope that these recent trends will not call into question the progress made over the last century in this regard.
‒ we condemn the death penalty and call for its abolition. we regret that the death penalty is still applied in at least 55 countries and we note with concern the growing tendency to promote discussion of reversing the abolition of the death penalty by some countries, particularly in europe. we are in general agreement with the content of the resolution. we cannot, however, fail to note elements of the usual hypocrisy imposed by the majority of the european parliament in the considerations made with traces of interference and in the discrepancy in the analysis, where, for example, the maintenance of capital punishment in countries such as the usa and china is not treated in the same way, or when the european external action service is put forward as an instrument in the fight against capital punishment, the same instrument that promotes aggressive interventions in third countries responsible for the death of hundreds of people. in spite of these remarks, we voted in favour of the resolution.
‒ the rupture of a waste reservoir in hungary spilled almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red sludge and flooded several villages, killing ten people, injuring around 150 and polluting vast areas, including four natura 2000 sites. it was the most serious industrial disaster in hungary and i pay tribute to the victims on the fifth anniversary of this tragic event. the eu has to take action and it is urgent that eu legislation and international conventions be respected.
in writing. a reservoir of toxic sludge from an aluminum oxide factory has burst, contaminating several towns and cities in hungary. ten people were killed, 150 were injured. this accident exposed the weak enforcement and loopholes in environmental legislation on industrial toxic waste in the eu. it was not the first time accidents of this kind had happened. this was the biggest. the resolution calls for efforts to understand the current situation of waste from mines, its management and treatment. more investment is needed in research and development on the prevention and treatment of this type of toxic waste. it calls for compliance with the polluter-pays principle (we emphasize: in its original meaning, without the distortions that were subsequently introduced, seeking to transmute it into a separate user-pays principle). the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of environmental inspections, which would be more effective and more efficient. regular information to the public on pollution levels and the degree of threat to ecosystems and public health is advocated. although we had some doubts about some of the proposals put forward (such as the suggested risk-sharing instrument), we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ five years after the accident in hungary, there is still a poor implementation of eu legislation and relevant international conventions, as well as poor control. it is essential that lessons be drawn from the disasters that have occurred and that greater prevention and monitoring be implemented.
‒ the red mud catastrophe in hungary in 2010 highlights a serious environmental situation, which calls for cooperation and solidarity at eu level. red sludge is a hazardous waste until proven otherwise in accordance with commission decision 2014/955/eu and may be incorrectly classified in other member states, causing danger to the european community and giving rise to improper authorisations. it is essential to take preventive measures to avoid further industrial disasters by correctly applying european environmental legislation and international conventions. progress is also needed in developing monitoring and inspection instruments in this area at eu level. member states should take steps to ensure that the 'polluter pays' principle is respected. i am in favour of this motion for a resolution, stressing the need to close the gaps in european legislation and calling for cooperation by all member states in preventing environmental disasters and sharing financial risks.
in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2010, the rupture of a waste reservoir in hungary spilled almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red sludge and flooded several villages, killing ten people, injuring around 150 and polluting vast areas, including four natura 2000 sites. five years on, it is important to pay tribute to the victims. it is also important to take stock of the situation regarding the development of the prevention of such disasters. parliament expressed concern that in practice the lessons drawn from this tragic event had not been learned, as none of the gaps in eu legislation had been closed and weak enforcement of eu legislation and relevant international conventions and weaknesses in controls continued. the commission and the member states must therefore intensify their efforts to ensure the prevention of pollution and the treatment of hazardous waste. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2010, the rupture of a waste reservoir in hungary spilled almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red sludge and flooded several villages, killing ten people, injuring around 150 and polluting vast areas. commission decision 2014/955/eu states that red sludge is to be classified as hazardous waste. there is a risk that these have been classified as non-hazardous waste in other member states. the proposal warns of this situation and expresses concern that no lessons have been learned in the last five years. the implementation of eu legislation and relevant international conventions remains weak, coupled with successive weaknesses in controls. we are calling in a clear way for the member states to strengthen their national environmental inspection bodies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the most serious industrial disaster in hungary, caused by the rupture of a waste reservoir, which spilled almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red sludge and flooded several villages, killing ten people and injuring about 150. five years after the tragic accident, i pay a simple tribute to all the victims, and i commend those who, with great effort, intervened quickly and effectively in the resolution of this event, trying to find the best solutions to eliminate and reduce damage. this incident also served to show that there is still a weak and incorrect implementation of european legislation, so it is essential to develop work not only at the level of correct application of legislation, but also at the level of inspections, controls and prevention of future disasters, so that serious incidents like these do not happen again in the future.
‒ the importance of proper treatment of hazardous waste is unquestionable. hungary has been a sad witness to this. i take this opportunity to supplement my statements in the plenary by reiterating that i consider it essential to find solutions for the proper management of this waste and that these have two approaches. on the one hand, we must create the conditions for hazardous waste to be effectively treated, by giving it economic value and by creating extraordinary guarantees to compensate for losses caused by accidents. at the same time, i believe that transparency must accompany the whole process of handling hazardous waste. this process must start at the planning level of its use up to its final destination and includes a possible remediation phase, which is not expected to be necessary. these are some of the reasons why i voted in favour of this resolution.
‒ this accident, which occurred five years ago and is reported here, exposed the poor enforcement and loopholes in eu environmental laws on industrial toxic waste. it revealed the fragility of the inspection system, which is either non-existent or ineffective, and its failure to be complied with by both the member states and the industrialists who own the factories. sadly, this disaster is not unique. we all remember similar events in spain or romania. this resolution calls for lessons to be learned and efforts to be made to understand the current situation of mine waste, its management and treatment, five years after this major accident in hungary. the commission is asked to invest and give greater emphasis to research and development in the prevention and treatment of this type of toxic waste. the real and effective prevention of pollution and environmental risks from extractive industries, among others, requires stricter environmental rules for environmental inspections, which implies allocating more resources to the national bodies responsible for these inspections. more transparency is needed, with the responsible authorities regularly informing the public about the state of pollution and the possible impacts on fauna and flora, as well as on the health of local populations.
‒ the explosion of a toxic sludge reservoir from an aluminium oxide plant has contaminated several towns and cities in hungary. ten people were killed, 150 were injured. this accident exposed the weak enforcement and loopholes in environmental legislation on industrial toxic waste in the eu. the resolution calls for efforts to understand the current situation of waste from mines, its management and treatment. more investment is needed in research and development on the prevention and treatment of this type of toxic waste. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of environmental inspections, which would be more effective and more efficient. regular information to the public on pollution levels and the degree of threat to ecosystems and public health is advocated. we voted yes.
‒ the european union has promoted gender equality and has sought to ensure that the gender dimension is mainstreamed in all its actions. however, progress towards gender equality and women's empowerment has been slow and uneven. progress is reported in all countries. according to the latest figures, around 800 women die every day worldwide from complications during pregnancy and childbirth; some 222 million women in developing countries do not have access to safe and modern methods of family planning; the majority of the world's poor are women and women-led households; 62 million girls worldwide are out of school. i therefore agree that the action plan should develop specific actions to strengthen the rights of different groups of women, paying particular attention to young people, migrants, women and people with disabilities.
in writing. the resolution states that progress towards gender equality and women's empowerment, as well as maternal health, has been slow and uneven. no country in the world has fully bridged the gender gap. it is noted that the percentage of development aid allocated to family planning in relation to total world aid allocated to health has decreased. the report calls for a significant change in eu action on gender equality and women's empowerment and points to measures. the use of qualitative and quantitative gender-sensitive indicators and the collection of gender-disaggregated data in a timely and systematic manner are emphasised and, to this end, member states are invited to set up gender-sensitive monitoring systems. the need for the eu to ensure sufficient human and financial resources to meet its commitments in this area is underlined. the resolution recommends that very concrete measures be included in the second gender action plan. among others: the call for the guarantee of the rights of different groups of women (young people, migrants, hiv-infected patients, lgbti and disabled); the recognition of the importance of universal access to sexual and reproductive health care and rights; the recognition of the urgency of eliminating social and legal barriers. we voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that member states take the opportunity to simplify and update their legislation on equal opportunities and equal treatment between men and women in areas related to employment and occupation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that the member states work together in an articulated way to promote greater equality of opportunity in all areas related to employment.
‒ equality between men and women is one of the fundamental principles on which the eu is founded. gender equality and the empowerment of women are a precondition for achieving the sustainable development goals and the eu should ensure their promotion and mainstreaming in all its policies and actions. the truth, however, is that progress towards gender equality and women's empowerment has been slow, and these goals remain largely unfulfilled. in this respect, and as the commission is currently working on the new gender action plan (gap2), it is important to ensure a radical change in eu action on gender issues and a renewed political commitment that can bring greater effectiveness to the results achieved. the resolution makes a number of recommendations on the main aspects to be addressed by the gsp2. i voted in favour.
‒ the evaluation of the gender action plan 1 (gap 1) revealed the need for a radical change in gender equality and women's empowerment. this is why this gap 2 has emerged, which advocates gender equality (ge) as a central element of the activities of the european union institutions, seeking to ensure that in future ge issues are included in the annual reports of all commission directorates-general involved in external action. it clearly highlights several areas of intervention: violence against women, rape as a weapon of war, sexual and reproductive rights, equal pay, motherhood and reconciliation of work and family life, the role of formal and informal education, the vulnerability of migrant, refugee and asylum-seeking women, among many others.
‒ the plan which ran from 2010 to 2015 contributed to the development of a set of new policies in the field of cooperation and development. however, there are still a number of situations which need to be intensified and others which merit more tailored treatment or even new approaches. the plan to be implemented between 2016 and 2020 should be ambitious and coherent. it is intended to promote a cultural change at the level of the institutions. it should embrace the social and political objectives of the european union and align them with our role in the world. the promotion of gender equality, also in other geographies, should be a key component of this new plan. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ unfortunately, and despite all the talk about the subject, the majority of the world's poor are women and households run by women. worse still, the vulnerability of marginalized women is increasing. worldwide, 62 million girls are out of school. one in three women in the world will be a victim of physical and sexual violence at some point in her life. although the eu has committed itself to respecting the right of all individuals to have full control over their sexuality and sexual and reproductive health and to decide freely and responsibly on these matters, without discrimination, coercion and violence, we are again debating this issue with the crude figures that demonstrate the failure of the gender action plan. more action and more resources are needed. and we must not isolate this problem, which is real and concrete, but which is not detached from the neoliberal orientations which guide eu policies and which promote the concentration of wealth and the spread of poverty.
‒ the resolution states that progress towards gender equality and women's empowerment, as well as maternal health, has been slow and uneven. no country in the world has fully bridged the gender gap. it is noted that the percentage of development aid allocated to family planning in relation to total world aid allocated to health has decreased. the need for the eu to ensure sufficient human and financial resources to meet its commitments in this area is underlined. the resolution recommends that very concrete measures be included in the second gender action plan. among others: the call for the guarantee of the rights of different groups of women (young people, migrants, hiv-infected patients, lgbti and disabled); the recognition of the importance of universal access to sexual and reproductive health care and rights; the recognition of the urgency of eliminating social and legal barriers. it is a positive resolution.
in writing. directive 2006/54/ec consolidated a set of community instruments on gender equality in employment and occupation. although gender equality is in the dna of the union itself, little progress has been made. this report, which i support and vote for, acknowledges that progress has been made, but as parliament has consistently argued, more effective measures are needed. the main objective of the directive is to combat the gender pay gap, but also indirect discrimination in the context of workplace assessment, recruitment systems and pension schemes. without regulatory excesses or bureaucratic red tape, all measures should be considered and cooperation and exchange of best practices between member states encouraged. it is true, however, that listed companies should be subject to stricter regulation than a micro-enterprise. for the most part, public bodies are required to have a flawless record.
‒ all women, regardless of age, education or social status, are potential victims of discrimination in the workplace, whether direct or indirect. the impact of employment inequality cannot be underestimated. in fact, equal pay for men and women is a matter of fairness and motivation. at the same time, it can also be understood as a family-related issue. in europe, the welfare of many families depends on women's earnings. most mothers participate in the labour market and many even bear the primary responsibility for supporting their families as the sole or main source of livelihood. however, over the last decade the gender pay gap, as an important indicator of gender inequality in the labour market, has almost stagnated, from 17,5% in 2008 to 16,4% in 2012. i agree with the need to review the directive on this matter.
‒ equal treatment and the principle of non-discrimination are principles enshrined in eu primary legislation. however, by action - by virtue of their policies - and by omission, we are far from seeing them in the eu. over the past decade, the gender pay gap has almost stagnated, going from 17.5% in 2008 to 16.4% in 2012. this own-initiative report is important. among other aspects, labour policies aimed at ending the principle and practice of collective bargaining and favouring individual wage negotiation are noteworthy. the level of occupational and sectoral segregation between men and women in different types of employment remains high, with some occupational categories predominantly occupied by women, and these sectors and professions are less well paid or valued. income disparities between men and women increase after retirement, with women's pensions on average 39% lower than men's; the role of trade unions and employers and civil society organisations in promoting equal treatment and the concept of equal pay in employment is highlighted. the report makes a number of positive recommendations and its scope is satisfactory, so we voted in favour.
‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of directive 2006/54/ec on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation. the report drawn up by the rapporteur departs from what should be its main purpose: the defence of equal treatment between men and women. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that member states take the opportunity to simplify and update their legislation on equal opportunities and equal treatment between men and women in areas related to employment and occupation. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that the member states work together in an articulated way to promote greater equality of opportunity in all areas related to employment. i voted against the introduction of quotas in listed companies and in politics because i believe that women should be in these positions because of their competence, ability to work and prestige rather than just because of a numerical categorisation in terms of board of directors or political activity.
‒ equality between men and women is one of the fundamental principles on which the eu is founded. this resolution addresses the issue of gender equality in the context of employment and occupation. in this respect, it is worrisome to note that, although the principle of equal pay has been enshrined in eu law since 1957, the gender pay, pension and employment gaps persist. in this regard, and given that greater equality between men and women is not only a matter of fairness and justice but also brings numerous benefits to the economy and society and is essential to promoting growth, competitiveness and economic recovery, it is important that the eu and its member states implement measures to ensure the effective implementation of the provisions on equal pay and equal treatment. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, in agreement with the rapporteur's recommendations in this respect in general.
‒ the rapporteur considers that the current directive 2006/54/ec needs to be updated. the report focuses on the gender pay gap, work-life balance, discrimination in pension schemes, the concept of equal work, pay transparency and access to justice, among other relevant and important issues. i would like to stress the issue of equal pay. ten years after the introduction of an eu law aimed at ensuring equal pay for equal work for men and women, women still receive on average 16% less (a fact exacerbated by the economic crisis). one of the reasons for this discrepancy was the lack of sanctions for companies that persistently treat men and women unequally. this is a situation that the report's report attempts to address by providing for sanctions for some companies (those listed on eu stock exchanges) if they choose not to meet their responsibilities with regard to gender pay equality. it also suggests that member states do the same with publicly funded companies. it was a courageous and decisive step toward justice.
‒ in the global gender gap index of the world economic forum, portugal was ranked 39th in 2014. here are some figures: 31% of the seats in the national parliament are held by women, 21% of ministerial posts are held by women and there are only 12% of women on company boards. a portuguese man earns on average 30% more than a portuguese woman. for these reasons, i find it very positive that this report explicitly states that member states should legislate to ensure a balanced representation of women and men on boards.
‒ equal treatment and the principle of non-discrimination are an important part of eu primary legislation. however, over the past decade, the gender pay gap has almost stagnated, going from 17.5% in 2008 to 16.4% in 2012. the current directive 2006/54/ec (recast) has thus reached its limits and needs to be updated. amongst many things, it is intended to introduce mandatory pay audits for listed companies in the member states, with the exception of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), and the possibility of applying sanctions in case of non-compliance, or the need for the country-specific recommendations, within the framework of the european semester, to include targets to reduce the gender pay gap, discrimination and the risk of poverty of older women and to apply in fact the principles of equal treatment. these are positive ideas. however, this issue cannot be dissociated from a wider context which has to do with the fight against exploitation and the general backsliding of which all workers, and particularly women, are victims.
in writing. ‒ this report has very positive aspects, including the defence of the role played by trade unions in promoting equal treatment and the concept of equal pay in employment; the need for vocational assessment and classification systems to be based, preferably, on collective bargaining; the assumption that ms should guarantee maternity-related rights, in particular the prevention of unfair dismissal of female workers during pregnancy or when they return to work after maternity leave; the finding that data protection cannot be invoked as an excuse for not publishing annual information on wages at the workplace. the report also advocates the need to strengthen public labour inspection mechanisms and for member states to take the necessary measures to ensure that the burden of proof is reversed, ensuring that it is always the employer's responsibility to prove that differences in treatment are not the result of any factor of discrimination. if we could put these positions into practice, we would be on the right track.
