answer under the 'blue card' procedure. i appreciate your question, but the answer is obvious: the united kingdom already controls its borders, and it controls them within the rules it has accepted, which are the rules of free movement. of course if the uk wants to be in the european union without freedom of movement, it cannot be in the european union - there is no alternative. the free movement of persons is an essential freedom of the european union and it cannot be called into question. so the uk controls its borders. if you want to be in the european union you have to guarantee freedom of movement for european citizens, not for others.
in writing. in the last month, ministers and heads of government met a total of seven times. but even so, member states failed to do enough to respond to the humanitarian emergency, taking too little and too late. i am referring to the relocation mechanism, which still faces resistance and problems on the ground and is clearly insufficient. i am referring to the provision of more human and operational resources to the european agencies, which is so necessary for the operationalisation of hotspots; i am referring to financial support for reception centres, which take time to arrive. i hope therefore that tomorrow the member states will be able to give a clear political impetus to the implementation of these and other measures, and that the humanitarian emergency will indeed be dealt with. clearly, we must not ignore the root cause of this emergency. the diagnosis has been made long ago and the solutions have been put forward long ago. now, it is totally illogical that the political momentum of tomorrow is for the long term when we have not yet been able to solve the present. we don't need catapult measures or media pirouettes to simulate movement. we need to act!
eu leaders will meet on 15 october 2015 in the context of europe's migration and refugee crisis. this will be the fourth european council in six months to focus on the response to the so-called refugee crisis. once again we hear a chorus of good intentions. but in the face of such passivity, we ask where are the values of democracy and human rights that are being preached in all directions by this european union which always boasts of its right to give lessons to the world. the eu is complicit in the crises in libya, syria and iraq. just days ago, we heard the united states lamenting the russian bombing of the terrorist units that the cia had worked so hard to create and train. the eu has therefore a moral duty, not only in the face of its responsibilities in the refugee influx, but also in the name of the values it insists on proclaiming, to welcome all refugees with dignity and to create humanitarian corridors that will put an end to all these perfectly avoidable deaths that wound our consciences.
madam president, commissioner, i would like to greet dr manuela eanes in the gallery, who was awarded the european citizen prize today. we are only a few weeks away from the paris conference, where an ambitious and binding agreement is to be reached at global level. as we approach this, the pressure from some quarters to tone down the level of ambition of a possible agreement is higher than ever. we are concerned about the recent exclusion from the outline conclusions of the conference of co2 emission reduction targets for the shipping and aviation sectors. if progress at icau and imo has been manifestly insufficient so far, the absence of a reference in terms of objectives for these sectors in paris would be simply irresponsible and would constitute political endorsement for the absence of a shared and balanced effort to reduce co2 emissions. maritime and aviation transport together account for about 8% of global emissions and are on the rise. it is not fair to require additional efforts from other sectors, such as energy or industry, which are also struggling to be competitive and whose contribution to reducing emissions is already clear. we must ensure that ambition is maintained in the paris climate agreement.
in writing. at the moment, few issues are as pressing as the increase in climate change on planet earth. if we are not effective in mitigating the effects and reversing the consequences, this will be the last problem that humanity will have to deal with. it's as serious as that. this report, by proposing a very significant increase in renewable energy and by setting out a roadmap for the states, makes an effective contribution to reducing climate change. however, in this statement i want to attach particular importance to the proposal to end subsidies to petroleum products. this option has a deeper content than simply ending a support. with this option we are, in fact, changing the paradigm, giving priority to environmentally friendly energy and putting an early end to passive dependence on fossil fuels. europe takes the lead and contributes to a better world.
the paris summit focuses on climate change control, but underlying this theme is the need to change the principles on which the current process of economic and social globalisation is based. the ep report sets out a proper path and a holistic approach to the problem. it is important that an ambitious and legally ambitious global agreement be defined at the paris summit. it is also important that the european policy for the decarbonisation of the economy and for the technical and social transition should be an example for the world, and that it should be possible to set up a fund to support developing countries which will have to make a greater effort to adapt their growth strategies to the new objectives of sustainability of the planet.
in writing. the ruling by the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) on 6 december, declaring decision 2000/520/ec of the european commission, known as the safe harbour agreement, invalid, has obvious implications for changing the rules on the transfer of personal data from the eu to the us. one consequence of this decision is that transfers of personal data to the usa under the safe harbour are now prohibited in principle, as the principles of this agreement are considered not to ensure an adequate and sufficient level of protection of personal data. it is therefore imperative that measures be taken to put an end to this procedure, ensuring the protection of individual data and thus the fundamental guarantees.
‒ this council implementing decision aims to allow continued access to the vis by national police forces for the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist acts and serious crime. this access is the result of a concerted strategy to combat these phenomena. the vis is a european visa database, created to enter data on applicants and visas issued. this makes the whole procedure quicker, the visa safer and the so-called "visa shopping" is combated. the legal basis for this access had already been granted by amending the regulation on the basis of its creation and of which i was rapporteur. this decision - to which parliament must give its assent - merely approves the date of its entry into force and technical elements.
in writing. ‒ decision 2008/633/jha on access for consultation of the visa information system (vis) by designated authorities of the member states and by europol for the purposes of the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and of other serious criminal offences provides for its taking effect from a date to be determined by the council, when the commission has informed it that regulation (ec) no 767/2008 of the european parliament and of the council has entered into force and is fully applicable. whereas the commission informed the council by letter of 2 july 2013 that that regulation had entered into force and was fully applicable as from 27 september 2011, the conditions triggering the exercise by the council of the implementing powers provided for in decision 2008/633/jha are fulfilled, the present commission proposal aims precisely to fix the date from which decision 2008/633/jha takes effect. in order to ensure continuity of access to the vis for consultation, that proposal, now submitted for consultation by parliament, maintained the date of 1 september 2013 set out in the previous decision 2013/392/eu, which was annulled by the cjeu. i voted in favour.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data in the context of the processing of personal data by europol. the adoption of this measure aims to establish a uniform strategy capable of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist acts and other serious criminal offences. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. there was broad agreement from all the political groups on this matter and there were no grounds for not approving this report, so i voted in favour.
‒ this is a council implementing decision fixing the date from which decision 2008/633/jha on access for consultation of the visa information system (vis) by the designated authorities of the member states and by europol for the purposes of the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and of other serious criminal offences takes effect.
‒ this document is only intended to fix the date of entry into force of decision 2008/633/jha on access for consultation of the visa information system (vis) by the designated authorities of the member states and by europol for the purposes of the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and of other serious criminal offences. the establishment of a visa information system (vis) is part of the schengen information system (sis) and eurodac, within the framework of the communityisation of the so-called 'third pillar', namely justice and home affairs, and seeks to remove central competences from the member states. the vis is intended to be a system for the exchange of visa data between member states. we have always spoken out against the system of surveillance and securitisation of companies set up by the eu, often under the pretext of the security of citizens but in reality against their fundamental freedoms and guarantees, so we voted against this report.
‒ following the multiple measures presented by the commission to deal with the refugee crisis, it was necessary to make budgetary provisions for them. since the money is needed as quickly as possible, this parliament has used the urgency procedure and approved this amendment to the budget in record time. a eur 100 million increase in the asylum, migration and integration fund, a total increase of 120 staff for frontex, the european asylum support office and europol, and a contribution of eur 300 million to the syria support fund are approved. these measures are not sufficient and must be part of the broader migration strategy. it is also part of a strategy of using unused resources and of anticipating funds, which necessarily has an impact on the multiannual financial framework. the council must therefore not only fulfil its promises to provide extra budgetary contributions to deal with this crisis, but - in the short term - make up for this advance by avoiding that it is used today and then not used tomorrow.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a new regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and social policy. compared to the initial 2015 budget, national gni-based budget contributions could be reduced by eur 2,26 billion, thanks to traditional own resources (i.e. customs duties and sugar levies) revenues exceeding the forecasts by eur 1133,5 million. this technical adjustment on the revenue side of the union budget is soundly based on the latest statistical developments and in line with the agreed distribution among member states. none of the elements of draft amending budget no 6/2015 have an impact on the expenditure side of the 2015 budget and their impact on the revenue side is limited to a change in the distribution of contributions between member states
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 6/2015 covers a revision of the estimates of traditional own resources, the vat and gni bases, the budgeting of the corresponding corrections in favour of the united kingdom, as well as their financing, which result in the change in the distribution of contributions to the eu budget between the member states. it also includes the creation of two new budget lines for support expenditure for trust funds managed by the european commission in the 'development and cooperation' and 'enlargement' policy areas, as well as a change in the staff of the berec office, without any changes in the total number of posts or in its budget. however, considering that none of the elements of draft amending budget no 6/2015 have an impact on the expenditure side of the 2015 budget and that its impact on the revenue side is limited to a change in the distribution of contributions between member states, and based on the report of the committee on budgets, i voted in favour.
‒ this proposal seeks to present a draft amending budget to the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015, covering a revision of the traditional own resources forecast, a revision of the vat and gni bases, the budgeting of the corrections in favour of the united kingdom and their financing. to that extent, such corrections result in a change in the distribution of the member states' contributions to the general budget of the european union. two new budget lines are also created for support expenditure for trust funds managed by the european commission, intended to compensate for management costs related to the union trust funds for external action. i would stress that none of the elements of this draft amending budget have an impact on the expenditure side of the 2015 budget, although the effects on the revenue side are limited to a change in the distribution of contributions between the member states, and i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ article 11 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 provides for the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, up to an annual ceiling of eur 471 million (2011 prices), to allow the financing of specifically identified expenditure which could not be financed within the available ceilings of one or more of the other headings. after an analysis of all possibilities for reallocating appropriations within the expenditure ceiling of heading 3 (security and citizenship), it appears necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument to supplement the financing of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015 with eur 66,1 million to finance measures in the field of migration. in this connection, and on the basis of the report of the committee on budgets, i voted in favour of the decision to mobilise the flexibility instrument to provide immediate budgetary measures under the european agenda on migration.
‒ this european parliament resolution concerns the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to provide immediate budgetary measures under the european agenda on migration. the commission proposal aims to mobilise this flexibility instrument by an amount above the mff ceilings, to supplement the financing of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015 with an additional eur 66,1 million in commitment appropriations to finance measures to manage the refugee and migration crisis and the allocation of the corresponding payment appropriations of eur 52,9 million in 2016 and eur 13,2 million in 2017. as one of the many positive measures put forward by the commission to deal with the refugee crisis, it deserves my approval and my vote in favour.
‒ the flexibility instrument is mobilised to provide eur 66.1 million in commitment appropriations to finance measures to manage the refugee crisis. in view of the crisis and the urgent need for measures to deal with the arrival of these thousands of refugees, we voted in favour.
‒ after examining all possibilities for reallocating commitment appropriations under heading 3 of the 2015 budget, it became necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument for commitment appropriations, amounting to eur 66,1 million in commitment appropriations, once again highlighting the need for the european union budget to be more flexible and larger. the commission then proposed to mobilise the flexibility instrument above the mff ceilings in order to supplement the financing of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015 with an additional eur 66,1 million in commitment appropriations to finance measures to manage the refugee and migration crisis. the corresponding payment appropriations of eur 52,9 million in 2016 and eur 13,2 million in 2017 are also proposed. we voted in favour of this mobilisation in order to speed up and accelerate this process so that the funds reach where they are needed.
‒ the union must practice internal and external solidarity in the refugee crisis. additional efforts are needed in the reception and further action for the stabilisation of countries of origin. the funds, programmes, instruments and agencies involved should be strengthened and better coordinated. i therefore agree to the increase in emergency assistance provided under the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf) to a total of eur 100 million; to the increase in the number of posts on the frontex, easo and europol establishment plans (120 in total) and the corresponding appropriations for salaries until the end of the year to eur 1.3 million in commitments and payments; to the additional funding for the european neighbourhood instrument (totalling eur 300 million); to the increase in the humanitarian aid payment appropriations by eur 55.7 million and finally to the budgetary provision for immediate measures under the european agenda on migration to the amount of eur 66.1 million.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 7/2015 aims to increase the union's resources for managing the current migrant and refugee crisis, thus addressing the current funding shortfall in categories 3 and 4. in this regard, it provides for: an increase in emergency assistance provided under the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf) totalling eur 100 million in commitment appropriations, while maintaining the necessary resources, as well as other programmes financed under amif; an increase in the number of posts in the frontex, easo and europol establishment plans (120 in total), as well as the corresponding appropriations for salaries until the end of the year, amounting to eur 1.3 million in commitments and payments; additional funding for the european neighbourhood instrument (eur 300 million); and an increase of eur 55.7 million in payment appropriations for humanitarian aid through reallocation. considering the need to provide a comprehensive response to the current migrant and refugee crisis, i voted in favour of this resolution, which endorses the council's position on draft amending budget no 7/2015.
‒ europe's humanitarian legacy is rooted in the principle of solidarity between peoples. the eu's assistance to migration must be based on technical and financial support capable of mitigating the negative effects of this wave of refugees, and the funds, programmes, instruments and agencies involved in these actions must be strengthened and better coordinated so that in the near future we can have a truly comprehensive and coherent european policy on asylum, refugees and migration. in this respect, i am in favour of the present commission proposal to increase emergency assistance provided under the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf) by a total of eur 100 million, and to increase the total staffing of frontex, the european asylum support office and europol by 120 staff, as well as to increase the payment appropriations for humanitarian aid by eur 55.7 million and to make available immediate budgetary measures under the european agenda on migration by eur 66.1 million.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 7/2015 provides for an increase in the number of posts in the establishment plans of frontex, easo and europol (120 in total) and the corresponding appropriations for salaries until the end of the year, amounting to eur 1,3 million in commitments and payments. this is a positive element. however, because we do not agree with all aspects of european refugee policy and in particular the common european asylum system, we abstained in the vote on this amending budget. we also believe that the union should make greater efforts to manage the current migrant and refugee crisis and contribute to the stabilisation of the countries of origin by assisting the countries of transit, since the proposed measures will certainly not be sufficient, given the seriousness of the problem.
in writing. ‒ this draft amending budget no 7/2015 provides for an increase in the emergency assistance provided under the asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) and the internal security fund (isf) totalling eur 100 million in commitment appropriations as well as in other programmes financed under the amif. it also provides for additional funding for the european neighbourhood instrument (a total of eur 300 million) and an increase of eur 55.7 million in appropriations for payments for humanitarian aid by reallocation. this draft amending budget is accompanied by a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to provide immediate budgetary measures under the european agenda on migration amounting to eur 66,1 million. unfortunately, it insists on the response by militarizing humanitarian aid, while also providing for an increase in the number of posts in the frontex, easo and europol agencies (120 in total). the report considers that the union should make more efforts in managing the current migrant and refugee crisis by 'contributing to the stabilisation of the countries of origin', and never refers to eu efforts to destabilise them.

‒ climate change requires an urgent, responsible and global response based on solidarity from the international community. climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing humanity for sustainable development, global health and the global economy. the european union and its member states are committed to jointly adhering to a binding target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels. however, i believe that we must have more ambitious targets and the european parliament should advocate a reduction of greenhouse gases by 50% by 2030 compared to 1990 and increase the share of renewable energy to 45% of the energy mix, achieving 40% energy savings. i support the need for the paris agreement to be global, ambitious and legally binding in order to provide a long-term response to the challenges of climate change. the european union should also complete the ratification process of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol as soon as possible and encourage the other parties to do the same so that it can enter into force as soon as possible. i therefore support the report by mr gilles pargneaux.
‒ i also agree with the need to reach an ambitious and legally binding global agreement at the paris climate conference, calling for a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of at least 40% by 2030, an increase in energy efficiency of 40% and renewable energy sources of 30%. a stable climate system is essential for food security, energy production, water and sanitation, infrastructure, as well as the preservation of biodiversity and terrestrial and marine ecosystems, peace and prosperity in the world. it recalls that climate change is accelerating the loss of biodiversity. it is noted that between 2008 and 2013, 166 million people were forced to leave their homes due to floods, storms, earthquakes or other disasters, adding that climate-related developments in some parts of africa may contribute to exacerbating the refugee crisis in the mediterranean.
‒ climate change is now an unavoidable reality and represents one of the main threats to the sustainable development of our planet. for this reason, the european union is committed to reaching an ambitious and legally binding global agreement, which includes concrete targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% by 2030 (compared to 1990), increasing energy efficiency to 40% and increasing renewable energy sources to 30%. like the rapporteur, i stress the importance for the eu and its member states to complete the ratification process of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol by the end of this year, so that it can enter into force as soon as possible. finally, i stress the need for this international climate agreement to be binding, capable of responding to the challenges posed by climate change in the long term, so that we can contribute to a stable climate system that preserves the biodiversity of ecosystems and human health. in view of these considerations, i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i think it is very important that the european parliament, which represents all the citizens of the european union, sends a clear message of urgency to cop21 in paris with regard to the intensification of global climate change. this report, by proposing a very significant increase in renewable energy and by setting out a roadmap for the states, makes an effective contribution to reducing climate change. however, in this statement i want to attach particular importance to the proposal to end subsidies to petroleum products. this option has a deeper content than simply ending a support. with this option we are, in fact, changing the paradigm, giving priority to environmentally friendly energy and putting an early end to passive dependence on fossil fuels. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ climate change poses an urgent and potentially irreversible global threat to human societies and the biosphere. according to the scientific data of 2014, there is no doubt about the warming of the climate system. human activities are the main cause of the observed warming since the middle of the 20th century. we note that the eu reduced emissions by 19% between 1990 and 2013 under the kyoto protocol, and increased its gdp by over 45%. unfortunately, between 1990 and 2013, global ghg emissions increased by more than 50%, with the global monthly average concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere exceeding the 400 parts per million threshold for the first time in march 2015. we therefore have the greatest doubts about the ability of emission trading systems to solve this problem, insofar as they treat equally companies with large developmental differences.
‒ the environmental problems facing humanity today are manifold and diverse, and are so serious that they threaten the very existence of life on earth as we know it. this resolution is intended to set out guidelines for the eu's mandate at cop 21 and, while we agree on some points, we strongly disagree on others. a consistent approach to climate change should focus, for example, on reducing dependence on fossil fuels. the world's major economic powers seem more interested in using climate as a pretext for lucrative business opportunities than in achieving real emission reduction targets, without necessarily challenging the current dominant economic and social organisation on a global scale, insisting on the main instrument proposed by the eu to contain climate change, which not only does not contribute to alleviating this dependence but is even an obstacle to the necessary energy paradigm shift. the difficulties and contradictions of these climate change conferences stem largely from the failure of the major industrial powers, including of course the eu, to understand the true and profound meaning of the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibility', and not from a lack of diplomacy or a voice speaking for 28 sovereign countries.
we would like to draw your attention to a situation which we consider to be of the greatest gravity, and which has to do with the absurd interference of the services which you direct in the matter of the intervention of members, by limiting that intervention. i am talking about the situation with the written questions and the new interpretation given to it by the committee on constitutional affairs. the point is that the justifications which are being put forward by members - justifications of urgency - are being called into question by the services. it is important that we understand who is making this decision and on what basis they decide whether or not the justification for urgency put forward by a member is legitimate. we need to know who's making these decisions, and on what principles they're making them.
the committee on budgets madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur and thanking him for the spirit of commitment he has shown in his collective work on this matter in the european parliament. later today, in the special committee on taxation, which was set up after the luxleaks scandal, we shall also vote on another report and we hope that the spirit of compromise will also prevail. it is a year since the luxleaks scandal and the problem of information exchange is just one of those that needs to be dealt with urgently and seriously, through a commitment not only within parliament but also in the form of an interinstitutional agreement, including the commission and also the council, so as to introduce into european culture a new approach to taxation. it is in this sense that i would like to begin by congratulating the commission on the number of initiatives that have already been brought to light by the debate, and i would ask the european commission not to give up this fight. it is essential that there should be a strong position of this parliament, which we are building. the european commission's strong position is essential. but there must also be a credible position on the part of the council. and in this respect i also agree with what my colleague mr ferber has just said about the disappointment of the ecofin council decisions of 6 october, not only with regard to the date of entry into force of the new procedures, but also at three other levels. firstly, it is unacceptable that the agreement on the exchange of information on hitherto secret agreements, which give preference to multinationals in tax matters, allows these to be adopted and exchanged between member states without assigning to the european commission the role it has to perform. the european commission must be the platform where this exchange of information takes place, so as to prevent what has been the outline of all the commitments between states that have existed so far from continuing to be the european norm. the european commission must be the platform for exchange. secondly, it is unacceptable that governments have limited this exchange of information to rulings issued in the last 5 years, when the european commission's proposal was 10 years old, as there are numerous agreements which are still in force and which therefore have to be made accessible to tax administrations, whatever the period in which they started or at least all those which are still in force are the subject of this exchange of information. finally, i would also like to mention the fact that all rulings, all exchanges, all agreements have to be transmitted, because in the internal market, advantages granted to a multinational in one member state automatically have an impact on the collectible in all other states. and so it makes no sense to limit the obligation to exchange information to exchanges between states when, in fact, the agreement ends up creating, in the internal market with free movement of capital, a risk of tax loss for all other states. in short, there is a new european agenda on this matter. parliament is working in good faith. the commission is working very hard and we want it to continue. but the council must act with loyalty and determination to correct the situation of fiscal injustice in europe and to restore the confidence of europeans, of the citizens, who are the taxpayers, in the seriousness of the work of the integrated project in which we all believe.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, i come from a country where 19 out of 20 listed companies pay taxes in other countries. tax competition and laws to eliminate so-called double taxation generate a race to the bottom which will only end when taxation of capital gains is equal to zero. the legislation we are discussing here today does not solve this, but it could at least lead to minimum conditions of loyalty between member states and help governments and citizens to become aware of the scale and gravity of this phenomenon. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information provided by the member states is not used for the purposes of the taxation of profits. the tax abuse by multinationals results in a loss of tax revenue or taxes, estimated at between eur 50 and 70 billion. if we add other issues, such as the amount for tax avoidance and special agreements, this amount could be as high as 160 to 190 billion euros. this fraud results in an overburden of taxation on other national economic actors, in particular workers, in the non-fulfilment of corporate civic and social responsibility, while depriving sovereign states of key resources to implement their social policies, combat poverty and social inequality and promote economic development. all of this increases economic and social inequality. one of the main dimensions of transparency is the free access to information by the general public, and that is why i call on my colleagues to support the amendments we are putting forward to allow for civic and democratic scrutiny. as for the report by mrs scott cato, i fully support it.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the current rules on package holidays are obsolete in the face of the changing paradigm in the travel market and the new realities of the digital age, where consumers increasingly book personalised trips over the internet, either from one operator or from several operators linked commercially. european consumers are thus less protected because the existing rules were designed for traditional package tours, where everything was pre-arranged by the travel agency. now, for us, consumers must be at the centre of the internal market. the scattered legislation of some member states to fill this legal void and the wide margin of manoeuvre that has been given to the transposition of the directive are also not a solution. there is a fragmentation of the internal market, there is a need for harmonisation and that is why it was so important to amend the package travel directive. the commission, parliament and the council were right to agree to modernise this important sector of the european economy. a word of praise for the work done by my colleague, birgit collin-langen, as rapporteur, which has enabled the european parliament and the council to reach agreement on this dossier, striking the necessary balance between a high level of consumer protection and the protection of a free, borderless area for the movement of goods and services and the freedom of establishment.
mr president, the fight against torture and the death penalty is a decisive battle for the european union and humanist culture, and it must be fought on all fronts, including the european union's trade policy. it is our duty not only to ensure that the marketing of products intended for torture and execution is effectively prohibited, but also to control so-called dual-use products which can be misused, either for torture or for execution. this proposal for a regulation is a positive initiative which deserves the clear and constructive political support of the european parliament. updating the lists of products subject to special authorization, creating a general export authorization for countries that respect international commitments, but also creating a general clause making the authorization dependent on the absence of reasonable grounds to suspect that these goods are being misused, would be important steps and a good opportunity for a trade policy that is more faithful to the european commitment to human rights.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has been a pioneer in introducing rules aimed at preventing and eradicating torture and ill-treatment, and in abolishing the death penalty worldwide. in this respect, i am pleased that portugal was the second european nation to abolish capital punishment in 1867. the european union is now strengthening the legal framework it already has, by expanding and updating the list of prohibited products and technologies, to prevent our companies from promoting, brokering and providing technical training in the use of devices and technologies for torture, execution or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. i hope that this effort will make a real contribution to the abolition of the death penalty in the countries which still apply it and to the reduction of torture practices throughout the world, particularly in relation to the violation of human rights and freedom of expression. and because this is a forum of citizenship par excellence, i end by urging the angolan government to immediately and unconditionally release luaty beirão and the other human rights activists who are illegally detained in angola. freedom now!

mr president, we have seen inflamed professions of faith in the liberalization of various sectors of economic activity before. the truth is that the single market in electronic communications, as life and practice have shown in other sectors of activity, is tailor-made for the great powers and their monopolies. they lose the workers, they lose the consumers, who never see the wonderful promises come true. monopolistic concentration is on the rise, private appropriation of public goods, such as spectrum or the internet, is on the rise, and the neutrality of these is being jeopardized to satisfy the business perspective of some of the giants of the industry. even the one that is touted as the great benefit of this regulation, the end of roaming charges, in the realm of the multinational domain, is not without potential harmful effects. only a few weeks ago, the chairman of the body which brings together the 28 national regulatory bodies in the telecommunications sector said that the southern countries would be disadvantaged by the dominant tourist flows in europe. it will be the non-roaming populations of these countries who will have to bear the costs associated with the elimination of roaming charges through an increase in their own charges. we still have no convincing response to these alerts.
the digital single market for electronic communications regulation is an essential pillar for the achievement of the digital union. the regulation adopted is the result of a compromise between the european parliament and the council. it is true that more could have been done on some points, in particular on consolidating the concept of net neutrality, but the agreement reached is a synthesis that allows future work to continue in the right direction. i note that this agreement will allow for the reduction of roaming charges from 30 april 2016 and the abolition of these charges on 15 june 2017. the agreement also guarantees open access to the internet and prohibits the practice of paying for priority access to the network. the role of national regulators in ensuring the application of the regulation is also strengthened. for these reasons, it is a positive regulation, but one which must be monitored at all times, both to ensure its effective application and to introduce improvements and corrections arising from the experience of its application.

‒ certain legislative acts adopted in recent decades are no longer relevant today, either because their content has been taken up by subsequent acts or because of their temporary nature. union legislation should therefore be updated and reduced by deleting acts that are no longer applied in order to improve transparency and legal certainty. the aim of this report is to amend the addition of a reference to article 114 tfeu which 'is intended to ensure consistency with the dual legal basis (agricultural policy and internal market policy) used for the adoption of directive 76/621/eec on the fixing of the maximum level of erucic acid in oils and fats'. i voted in favour.
‒ this proposal is intended to object to council directive 76/621/eec on the fixing of maximum levels of erucic acid in oils and fats and to council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 establishing a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar industry, since some of the legal acts adopted in recent decades have become irrelevant, either because their content has been adopted by other subsequent legal acts or because some of them are temporary. following the interinstitutional agreement on simplifying and improving eu legislation, this legislation should be updated and condensed, removing legal acts that are no longer applicable, in order to improve transparency and trust. the commission proposal does not give it the power to declare legal acts adopted by the council obsolete. the acts listed in the commission proposal should therefore be repealed by a decision of the european parliament. those delegated acts have become obsolete since the content of council directive 76/621/eec has been repealed by regulation 1881/2006 and regulation 320/2006 only establishes a temporary scheme which is no longer applicable. the proposal is not problematic and we voted in favour of it.
‒ i have tabled my vote in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on the repeal of obsolete acts in the framework of the common agricultural policy. the commission proposal aims to repeal council directive 76/621/eec and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006, which no longer have any effect and remain only technically in force. the need for legal certainty and security requires that obsolete acts be repealed. the commission also proposes to add article 114 tfeu to the legal basis for the approximation of the laws on the establishment and functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the common agricultural policy, council directive 76/621/eec on the fixing of maximum levels of erucic acid in oils and fats and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 establish a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar industry, which have exhausted their legal effects and no longer correspond to the original purposes for which they were created. the elimination of obsolete acts is an element of the 'better lawmaking' strategy put in place by the european institutions, and there is no justification for keeping these acts in the current legislative order. the content of directive 76/621/eec is reproduced in commission regulation (ec) no 1881/2006 setting maximum levels for certain contaminants in foodstuffs, and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 would only apply under a temporary scheme of restructuring of the sugar industry, ending in the 2009/2010 marketing year. i am in favour of this proposal, since it must safeguard legal certainty and transparency by repealing obsolete acts which are only formally in force.

‒ on 27 may 2015, the european union and switzerland signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, aimed at improving tax cooperation and compliance with international tax obligations. this is important progress in the context of the efforts being made to combat tax fraud and evasion. from 2018, the eu and switzerland will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of residents of the other party. the aim is to prevent situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which no tax has been paid. it also contains provisions to limit the possibilities for taxpayers to avoid disclosure of their information to the tax authorities by transferring assets or investing in products that fall outside the scope of the agreement. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2004, the council decided to conclude the agreement between the eu and the swiss confederation to ensure that the latter adopts measures equivalent to those to be applied in the eu to ensure effective taxation of savings income in the form of interest (directive 2003/48/ec). the agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information, signed on 27 may 2015, which aims to improve international tax cooperation, represents an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement. however, there are several limitations to this proposal: the lack of a requirement for full and detailed information on account holders, in line with the effort to achieve full transparency and full disclosure of information as a mandatory requirement; the fact that the original deadline for the automatic exchange of information is inadequate, requiring the reporting cycle to be tightened from an annual basis to a quarterly basis; the existence of an exemption from disclosure, which is too broad and ambiguous. the agreement, the content of which the european parliament cannot alter, is thus clearly not up to the task. that is why we abstained.

in writing. ‒ in 2003, the savings taxation directive was adopted as a measure to ensure that taxes on savings are paid in the form of interest. following the 2008 evaluation, the commission proposed a review to address certain gaps, which was definitively adopted in 2014 and should apply from 1 january 2016. however, the 2011 administrative cooperation directive was revised, aligned with the oecd global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information for tax purposes and adopted in 2014. it should also apply from 1 january 2016. the commission proposed, in its tax transparency package of march 2015, the repeal of the 2003 savings tax directive, so that member states do not have to apply the provisions of both directives and can thus avoid the difficulties caused by dual information collection and reporting systems. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ directive 2003/48/ec is on taxation of savings income in the form of interest generated by credits and was implemented with the aim of ensuring the payment of taxes on savings in the form of interest. that directive will be repealed so that member states do not have to apply the provisions of the 2003 and 2011 directives (relating to taxation of savings and administrative cooperation respectively) and can avoid the difficulties caused by dual reporting systems. this report proposes that the european commission draw up a report on the results of the repeal. it also proposes that the european commission submit legislative proposals to ensure that any gaps that may exist are closed. it also regrets that no specific cost-benefit analysis of a dual communication system or of a transition period between the two standards has been carried out. i'm not objecting.

in writing. ‒ according to decision 2008/615/jha on the stepping up of crossborder cooperation in combating terrorism and crime, the provision of personal data cannot take place until the general provisions on data protection have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states concerned. the council's proposals are designed to authorise poland, belgium and sweden to receive and supply personal data in accordance with the abovementioned decision. these three reports relate to the prüm convention, which was signed in may 2005 in prüm, germany, by seven member states: austria, belgium, france, germany, luxembourg, spain and the netherlands. it has been criticised for being negotiated and adopted in a very opaque way and without being subject to effective democratic control. the purpose of the prüm decision is to intensify and accelerate the exchange of information between authorities, for example by making it possible to compare a given dna profile with profiles recorded in automated databases in the member states. our vote is inseparable from our more general consideration of the fight against terrorism and the role the eu is playing in this.

in writing. ‒ decision 2008/615/jha on the strengthening of crossborder cooperation substantially incorporates the prüm treaty into the community legal order, while maintaining the objective of encouraging greater cooperation between member states' security forces, in particular through greater exchange of information. as i have said on several occasions, this exchange of information is essential in the field of security, as is the requirement for a result of greater mutual trust. certain requirements must therefore be met, in particular the principles of necessity and proportionality and respect for fundamental rights. therefore, in order to allow for the automated exchange of dactyloscopic data, each member state should ensure that data protection standards are implemented. this council decision rightly authorises the start of the automated exchange, since belgium has successfully implemented it.
‒ the deepening of crossborder cooperation, in particular in the field of combating terrorism and crossborder crime, is one of the most important issues in preventing terrorist acts against citizens of the european union. the exchange of information between countries is a crucial factor in minimizing these attacks. however, data sharing should be done in line with and with the agreement of the different countries. in the present report, these aspects are duly safeguarded and therefore deserve my approval.
in writing. ‒ according to decision 2008/615/jha on the stepping up of crossborder cooperation in combating terrorism and crime, the provision of personal data cannot take place until the general provisions on data protection have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states concerned. the council's proposals are designed to authorise poland, belgium and sweden to receive and supply personal data in accordance with the abovementioned decision. these three reports relate to the prüm convention, which was signed in may 2005 in prüm, germany, by seven member states: austria, belgium, france, germany, luxembourg, spain and the netherlands. it has been criticised for being negotiated and adopted in a very opaque way and without being subject to effective democratic control. the purpose of the prüm decision is to intensify and accelerate the exchange of information between authorities, for example by making it possible to compare a given dna profile with profiles recorded in automated databases in the member states. our vote is inseparable from our more general consideration of the fight against terrorism and the role the eu is playing in this.
‒ with a view to deepening crossborder cooperation, particularly in the fight against terrorism and organised crime, i have tabled my vote in favour of the report on the draft council implementing decision on the launch of the automated data exchange system in belgium. cross-border comparison of data reflects a new dimension in the fight against crime. the information obtained by comparing data plays a crucial role in supporting the judicial and law enforcement authorities of the member states.
‒ i believe that the effectiveness of the fight against terrorism and crossborder crime depends on efficient and close cooperation between member states. the transfer of personal data pursuant to decision 2008/615/jha may only take place when the general provisions on data protection laid down in chapter 6 of that decision have been incorporated into the national legislation of the territory of the member states participating in that transfer. the verification of compliance with this condition for automated data exchange should be carried out on the basis of an evaluation report, which in turn is based on a questionnaire, an evaluation visit and a pilot run. given that belgium has fulfilled the requirements of decision 2008/615/jha and has successfully conducted a pilot run with france and luxembourg, this report deserves my vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of the idea that cooperation and the exchange of information are decisive factors in strengthening the fight against terrorism and crossborder crime.
the european parliament, the council and the commission have adopted a number of resolutions on the future of the european union, including the european council resolution of 17 december 2006 on the future of the european union and the european council resolution of 17 december 2006 on the future of the european union. like the report on sweden and poland on the same subject, belgium has been found to have responded positively to the questionnaires on data protection and on the exchange of datalink data, and has also successfully completed the pilot experiment with france and luxembourg on this exchange, so there are no reasons why this report, which is of an eminently technical nature, should not be adopted, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ in december 2008, the european commission presented a proposal for the creation of the 'eurodac' fingerprint comparison system for the effective application of the dublin convention. this proposal is currently part of the 'asylum' package. eurodac is a common personal data processing system, which has been in use since 15 january 2003 and includes an automatic fingerprint recognition system. the purpose of this processing is to determine which member state is responsible under the dublin convention for examining an asylum application lodged in one of the eu states. this draft council implementing decision on the launch of the automated data exchange system is part of this logic.
