‒ cepol, the european police college, is responsible for training security forces throughout europe. the amendment proposed by the commission is essentially to align the legal basis with the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon and to give the agency the task of implementing the european training programme for the security forces, which are very welcome and go against what parliament has repeatedly called for. this report, which i clearly support, introduces changes along three lines: to focus the agency's activity on european and crossborder areas, in line with the european security strategy; to strengthen the coordinating role of ecpol, without prejudice to the support provided to the training bodies of the member states; to make its administrative structure more efficient, as was the case with europol. the new responsibilities mean that adequate funding is needed for the next financial year. i have been an early advocate of the agency's autonomy and i believe that the training of national police has contributed to greater mutual trust and, consequently, cooperation.
‒ cepol is not a training institute in the traditional sense: the courses take place throughout the eu, mainly by a network of national police training institutes, and it has a rather modest budget (around €8.5 million) and a simple staff (a total of about 40 people, including officials/temporary agents, contract agents and contingent agents). in 2013, some 8 250 police officers participated in some 100 cepol activities (courses, seminars, conferences and webinars). in addition, some 450 police officers, trainers and researchers from 25 countries have used cepol's european police exchange programme erasmus to spend time in the police force of another country. the proposal for a regulation updates the legal basis of cepol, adapts it to the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon and entrusts cepol with the implementation of the principles of the new police training programme, as set out in the commission communication referred to above. i voted in favour.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposed regulation should be amended to take account of the changes introduced by the treaty of lisbon (including the role of the european parliament and national parliaments) and to give cepol the task of implementing the principles of the new police training programme, as set out in the european commission's communication. the new legal framework now proposed is intended to enable cepol to implement a police training programme for all european law enforcement officers. in march 2015, the european commission put forward a proposal to update the legal framework of europol (european police office), where, among other changes, it already proposed the merger of cepol and europol in order to bring together synergies between law enforcement operationalization and officer training. under the pretext of 'guaranteeing the security of european citizens', this is nothing more than an attempt to create the conditions for the establishment of a supranational policing structure, outside the democratic control of the member states and therefore outside their constitutions, that is, it is another step in the intention of federalizing the eu in an area that goes to the heart of the sovereignty functions of the states. we voted against it.
‒ in the face of the continuous evolution of the eu's internal security needs, it is important that the training of police authorities is adapted to the constant challenges to citizens' security. the proposal for a regulation updates the legal basis of cepol, strengthening its role and entrusting it with the principles of the new vocational training programme as set out by the european commission.
‒ the european union plays a relevant role in the security of european citizens and as such, the simplification and improvement of the european union agency for police training (cepol) aims to provide high quality training for law enforcement officers, an essential factor in combating the growing threat of transnational organised crime. the cooperation between cepol and the member states is linked to the need to improve the organisation and coordination of police training activities at european level where cepol will act as a platform to support the internal security of the european union. the protection of fundamental rights and human rights should be the basis of all their training activities, with regard to topics such as data protection, support and protection of victims, privacy, among others. i am voting in favour of this proposal, taking into account the growing needs of society to deal with conflicts and the increasing organized crime through modernising police training and cooperation between member states and the european union.
‒ cepol is an agency of the european union (eu) tasked with training national police authorities to promote crossborder cooperation. without a training institute in the traditional sense, cepol uses a network of national police training academies to effectively deliver the courses. the role of this agency in training on organised and transnational crime, with particular emphasis on eu-related issues, should be noted. the european parliament, taking into account the eu's internal security needs and the consequent need to adapt its agencies to them, is called upon to adopt the proposal for a regulation updating the legal basis of cepol at first reading. the amendments requested by the present report establish a new legal basis, adapting the agency's legislation to the proposals contained in the commission's communication on the european police training programme. in this way, the target group for training is broadened, new tasks are assigned to the agency and the competences in the areas of research are extended to training, allowing a forward-looking approach in the construction of curricula. i voted in favour of the proposal subject to the conditions set out.
‒ the constantly evolving needs of europe's internal security place increasing demands on security forces and police officers, requiring them to be appropriately qualified to face new and complex challenges and to ensure the security of european citizens. the european police academy is the agency responsible for police training and, although not a training institute in the traditional sense of the term, it is the body responsible for training police officers throughout the eu, mainly through the national police training institutes. the amendment proposed by the commission aims, on the one hand, to update the legal basis of the academy, adapting it to the changes resulting from the lisbon treaty, and, on the other, to instruct it to adopt the principles of the new police training programme. i enthusiastically support this report, which aims to make cepol more effective by strengthening its coordinating role and making its administrative structure more efficient, and to implement the european police training programme more consistently and rigorously by focusing more on the european and crossborder areas, in line with the european security strategy.

the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a regulation on the european police force. the new legal framework proposed is intended to enable cepol to implement a police training programme for all european law enforcement officers. on 27 march 2015, the commission put forward a proposal to update the legal framework of europol (european police office), where among other changes it already proposed the merger of cepol and europol in order to bring together synergies between law enforcement operationalization and officer training. under the pretext of 'guaranteeing the security of european citizens', it is simply a matter of creating the conditions for the establishment of a supranational police structure, outside the democratic control of the member states and therefore outside their constitutions, that is, it is another step in the intention of federalising the european union, by taking away the sovereignty of the member states in matters so sensitive to the freedoms and guarantees of individuals. we voted against it.
‒ this regulation responds to the need to enhance the transparency of securities financing markets and, therefore, of the financial system. in order to ensure a level playing field and international convergence, this regulation follows the recommendations made by the efc. it establishes a union-wide framework under which information on ofifas can be provided efficiently to trade repositories and investors. regulators and supervisors may therefore face less transparency in relation to those activities, preventing them from obtaining an adequate overview of the risks associated with securities financing transactions. this would only exacerbate the already well-established links between the regulated banking sector and the shadow banking system in certain markets.
in writing. the stated objective of this proposal for a regulation is to increase the transparency and monitoring of financial activities outside the traditional banking sector, i.e. the shadow banking sector. it was this type of financial product that was behind the bankruptcy of lehman brothers and therefore the financial crisis of 2007/2008. it was not a lack of transparency or notification that triggered the crisis, but the very nature of the 'products'. on the other hand, all the changes to legislation since then to increase the level of regulation, or which are still in the pipeline, will always remain insufficient. the solution is to ban securities financing. it should either prohibit commercial banks from selling the loans they grant to companies and individuals (the possibility of selling the credit leads to the lowest risk analysis and, on the other hand, the lender is the one who knows the implicit risk best with successive sales, the information is lost); or prohibit securitisation of the credit (post-securitisation rating is done by the rating agencies, to which investment banks pay the good ratings). and in any case, a separation of commercial and investment banking should be promoted. we voted against it.
‒ problems have been identified with respect to securities financing operations and, in order to minimise risks and increase transparency of such operations, the proposed regulation introduces certain measures. there is a need to improve transparency in the monitoring of the build-up of systemic risks associated with securities financing transactions in the financial system and the disclosure of information on such transactions to investors. i cast my vote in favour.
‒ the need to enhance the transparency of securities financing markets has led to the creation of this regulation in order to ensure a level playing field in terms of competition and international convergence. the assessment and monitoring of banking risks and the level of interconnectedness of the financial system by investors, regulators and supervisors can only be effective if there is transparency in the course of operations. this measure will enhance the efficiency and the provision of specific information on securities financing transactions (sfo), i.e. repurchase transactions, securities or commodities lending, securities or commodities borrowing, buy/sell or sell/buy-back transactions, liquidity swaps and collateral swaps. i am voting in favour of this regulation because it responds to the need for supervision and the establishment of transparent markets, by providing a more robust banking system, capable of avoiding situations of financial instability and promoting the proper functioning of the internal market in the member states.
‒ securities financing transactions are essentially a form of collateralised financing which allows the exchange of assets, temporarily, as collateral for the financing of securities lending or repurchase transactions. in view of the so-called 'shadow banking system' in which non-bank credit activities with scale and expression are carried out to contaminate the regulated financial sector, and also in view of the specific risks posed by securities financing operations (which intensify indebtedness and pro-cyclical nature and interdependence in financial markets), it is essential to ensure transparency of operations, the analysis of which will allow the development of effective and efficient policy instruments to prevent systemic risks. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation, considering that every effort must be made to prevent excessive leverage of the financial system leading to another major financial crisis.
‒ the relevant regulation of the parliament and of the council integrates the structural reforms of the eu banking sector and was published in the proposal of 29.01.2014 on structural reform of banking. the aim of the regulation is to increase transparency and monitoring of financial activities outside the traditional banking sector, at a time when so-called 'shadow banking' is again growing disproportionately, once again endangering the entire stability of the financial system. we're not going there with regulations. the solution lies in public control of the financial system and the separation between retail banking and investment banking. abandoning the financial system to a mere logic of profit accumulation will only lead to increased speculation to the detriment of financing the real economy which today needs capital as if it were bread to eat.

‒ this resolution follows many of the recommendations made in the original 2014 document, particularly with regard to data protection, democratic scrutiny, the issue of whistleblower protection such as the snowden case in june 2013 and net neutrality. it goes further, proposing the status of 'whistleblower and human rights defender' and consequently its protection as such, and demands that the united states of america put an end to the espionage it has been carrying out. however, this resolution expressly condemns the united kingdom, the netherlands and france for their recent legislation in this area, and in paragraph 21 goes so far as to state that 'the european union and its member states need a common definition of 'national security' in order to ensure legal certainty', which is a huge contradiction with the stated defence of democratic control and national constitutions. it is one of the many contradictions in the report. for the foregoing, our vote is abstention.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the large-scale electronic surveillance of eu citizens. i urge the commission to respond to the calls made by successive resolutions of the european parliament. the us-eu relationship is essential for both sides. the surveillance revelations have jeopardised this relationship and it is therefore essential that steps are taken to ensure that this trust is restored, taking into account cooperation on a wide range of issues of common interest.
‒ i believe that data and information flows, which dominate our daily lives and are part of the integrity of every person, must be protected and secure. data protection and privacy are fundamental rights. it is important to stress that security measures, such as counter-terrorism measures, should be applied in accordance with the rule of law and be subordinated to fundamental rights obligations. i am concerned about the rapporteur's view that the fundamental rights of eu citizens continue to be in danger and that little has been done to ensure the full protection of those rights in the event of large-scale electronic surveillance, and i also regret the little progress made towards ensuring the protection of whistleblowers and journalists. i agree that there should be strict monitoring and follow-up of large-scale electronic surveillance of eu citizens by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs.
in its resolution of 12 march 2014, parliament drafted, on its own initiative, a number of observations addressed to the council and the commission in order to clarify certain key issues relating to the surveillance programmes and bodies of the united states of america and several member states and their impact on the fundamental rights of citizens of the european union (eu). parliament called on the commission to give its opinion on the follow-up to the report and to report on the progress made in promoting and protecting the right of eu citizens to freedom of opinion and expression. in a climate of large-scale surveillance, it is important that the european commission, as the 'guardian of the treaties', step up its efforts to respond to the challenges of the legal framework on data protection. the recommendations made by the rapporteur are a decisive contribution to ensuring that eu personal data continue to enjoy the necessary adequate protection, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ since 2007, due to the economic crisis affecting europe, long-term unemployment has doubled, accounting for half of total unemployment, i.e. more than 12 million people. long-term unemployment often leads to poverty, inequality, social exclusion and progressively isolates people from the labour market through deterioration of skills, loss of contact with professional networks and loss of work rhythm. i support this motion for a resolution because i believe that it is essential, in order to combat longterm unemployment, to significantly improve the registration of longterm unemployed with the employment services; to assess the employment potential, individual needs and preferences of longterm unemployed before they reach 18 months of unemployment and to facilitate a 'job integration agreement' between the longterm unemployed and the services concerned. i am in favour of the creation of one-stop shops where the unemployed person benefits from the presence of a professional who is responsible for his case. member states should integrate eu funds into their national policies in order to use adequate national funding to fight long-term unemployment.
‒ due to the economic crisis and its consequences, long-term unemployment has doubled since 2007 and now accounts for half of total unemployment, i.e. more than 12 million people, which is 5% of the eu's working population. in 2014, more than 60% of the long-term unemployed had been out of work for at least two consecutive years. the longterm unemployment rate varies considerably between member states, ranging from 1.5% in austria to 19.5% in greece, with the member states with the highest longterm unemployment rates being italy, portugal, slovakia, croatia, spain and greece. i therefore consider it necessary to significantly improve the registration of longterm unemployed with the employment services, with a view to comprehensive coverage, to assess the employment potential, individual needs and preferences of longterm unemployed before they reach 18 months of unemployment and to provide for an adapted, balanced and intelligible 'employment integration agreement' between the longterm unemployed and the services concerned within a maximum of 18 months after the start of the period of unemployment.
‒ longterm unemployed workers are an easy target for labour devaluation policies aimed at increasing exploitation. the aim is to make labour cheaper, to increase the extraction of surplus value, unpaid labour time, i.e. exploitation. it is urgent to boost job creation. it is urgent to stimulate sectors of the economy, such as industry, where these jobs can be created. there is an urgent need to boost public employment by addressing serious shortcomings, particularly in public services. the state itself, in its capacity as producer (and not merely as 'regulator'), can and must make a direct contribution to this. but it is also necessary to respect the principle that a permanent job corresponds to a real employment relationship and that the various forms of precarious work should be converted into real contracts when they meet permanent needs. it is therefore urgent that the strategies to be adopted by the council do not repeat the false solutions of creating vocational training programmes or pseudo-contracts for temporary insertion into the labour market, which only increase the exploitation of workers without giving them a viable and dignified solution to their lives.

‒ tourism is one of the areas with the greatest growth potential in the european economy, generating more than 10% of eu gdp, if tourism-related sectors are included, employing 13 million workers directly and therefore accounting for at least 12% of eu employment. europe is the world's leading tourist destination with a 52% market share, and the number of international tourists arriving in the eu is expected to increase by 140 million per year by 2025. the sector employs 3.2 million people, mostly young people aged 16 to 35. i believe that the european commission should continue and improve the joint promotion of europe as the world's number one tourist destination and implement the 'destination europe 2020' strategy, which includes a set of marketing actions, a branding strategy and the promotion of europe as a tourist destination.
in writing. the report is based on a logic of promoting a scale of tourism that is 'continental', stressing that a very significant percentage of world tourism (52%) is in europe. while the report does contain some relevant and interesting recommendations, there are several aspects that we do not fully follow, at least in the wording adopted here, such as the insistence on a mythified 'european identity' and an alleged 'common cultural heritage', along with the subsidiary theses of creating a 'european brand' and 'pan-european products'. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'tourist' in the definition of tourist activities. but the report is concerned about the so-called unstable situation in the neighbouring countries, and it is based on considerations which are not immune from slipping into a xenophobic and neo-colonial logic (from facilitating entry for companies operating in the field of tourism in developing countries to refusing to take in refugees on grounds of 'sanitising' tourist spots) which, however, are not explained in these terms. one of the positive aspects to be highlighted is the reference, in several places, to decent working conditions as a factor of quality and tourist enhancement.

‒ the european commission has set up a programme on interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2), which enable data exchange within their administrations and between their administrations and the eu institutions. the decision taken, which i agree with, not only follows the path followed, but also opens a new cycle which takes account of technological developments, the new needs of administrations and civil society and the new opportunities offered by cloud computing. interoperability increasingly promotes the potential quality of public services and creates a context of increased competitiveness for businesses and increased satisfaction for citizens, contributes to the achievement of the digital single market and to the implementation of an ambitious, globally leading and socially inclusive european digital agenda. the programme shall enter into force on 1 january 2016 and shall mobilise funding of eur 131 million for a period of five years.

‒ interoperability of public administrations-citizens-businesses within the eu maximises the economic and even social potential of information and communication technologies and it is to this extent that this report is a relevant step towards the creation of a programme on interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens, within the framework of the european digital agenda. the interoperability solutions programme for european public administrations (isa) has proved to be key to the coherent development and implementation of global and sectoral strategies to overcome electronic barriers in the union and to improve efficient and effective cross-border or cross-sector electronic interaction between european public administrations and between businesses and citizens. with the isa programme ending at the end of this year, it is necessary to establish a new eu programme for 2016-2020, which promotes the reduction of cross-border administrative costs, barriers and burdens, and deepens the internal market and freedom of movement in the eu. in this respect, i agree overall with the objectives set out in this report and support the need to provide for an increase in financial allocations for interoperability solutions between eu public administrations, which is consistent with the current multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
‒ since 1995, the european commission has been promoting with the member states interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens, and mechanisms that allow data exchange within their administrations and between their administrations and the eu institutions. we are supporting all measures aimed at modernising the various services of the public administration, and in particular those aimed at dematerializing part of the documentation. however, access to and the universality of these services should be safeguarded by combating any form of exclusion, particularly in relation to those who have difficulties with new technologies and the internet. we also believe that these developments should not, under any circumstances, jeopardize the existence of local services, particularly in regions which are socially, economically and demographically depressed.
in writing. ‒ this report is about the programme for interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens - isa2 and aims to continue the inter-administration data exchange programme ida - launched in 1995 with the aim of promoting with the member states solutions that allow for the exchange of data within their administrations and between them and the eu institutions. the document is essentially an important sign of progress towards modernising and interoperability of the public sector so that it can respond more effectively and efficiently to current needs, particularly in the field of new technologies and cloud computing. although this is an important step in updating and adapting the programme, it is stressed that the necessary data protection safeguards must be taken and that therefore computer resources, among other things, should remain the exclusive domain of public administrations. moreover, the necessary progress in this field should not call into question other measures and other means of supporting the provision of public services to the population throughout the territory of the member states and should be complementary. we voted yes.
‒ the deepening of european democracy that has been taking place over the last decades has one of its major expressions and causes in the election by universal suffrage of the european parliament. although the possibility had been enshrined since 1957, it was not until the so-called "electoral act" of 1976 that universal suffrage was put into practice. in 2002 the first - and so far only - reform was carried out. over the years, parliament has progressively reflected its increased democratic legitimacy through an increase in its powers, being now co-legislator - with the council of ministers - on almost all matters. we are left with 28 national elections to the european parliament, but we must bring europeans closer to the only institution that directly represents them. many factors are involved, including a better electoral law. i therefore support the report on the reform of eu electoral law in general, although i disagree with some of the points which deserve further reflection, such as the immediate creation of a european circle and the right to vote at the age of 16.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the right to vote and to stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament. the reform of the electoral act of 1976 requires member states to allow electronic voting and the internet in elections to the european parliament. the vote by mail should also be allowed in the european elections. the amendment aims to increase participation and facilitate voting for all citizens, especially people with reduced mobility and people working or living abroad. the current european electoral legislation allows for a non-binding limit of up to 5% of the votes cast for european elections. in the smaller member states and in those member states which have subdivided their territory into constituencies, although there is no limit, the de facto limit remains above 3%.
in writing. ‒ we need greater citizen participation in european elections to make the work of the european parliament even more legitimate and to enhance the effectiveness of our decisions. if the aim is to involve more and more citizens in political decisions at european level, it is essential to consider harmonizing the minimum voting age to 16, as is already the case in austria, for example. many young people are studying or doing an internship in other eu countries, and many citizens are working in member states other than their own. i therefore believe that it is increasingly important to introduce electronic voting as a key means of promoting and facilitating greater participation in the electoral process. it should also be stressed that the european parliament advocates the adoption of open and transparent procedures for the selection of candidates in order to strengthen the democratic legitimacy of representatives at european level. the resolution adopted today also advocates the choice of a common day for the 28 member states for the elections to the european parliament, the closing of the polls at the same time (20h00 portugal) and a common deadline for finalising the electoral rolls (8 weeks).
‒ elections are the main instrument of democratic participation and, in this sense, i welcome, in particular, the solutions to introduce the right to vote in european elections for all citizens of the union residing outside the eu and the possibility of electronic voting, via the internet or by post, as a way of promoting greater participation and electoral fairness by citizens, reinforcing the concept of citizenship of the union and improving the functioning of the european parliament and the governance of the institutions. the amendments to the proposed amendment to the electoral act 1976 contain controversial aspects such as the introduction of a mandatory minimum threshold of between 3% and 5% for the allocation of mandates, the harmonisation of the minimum voting age to 16, the introduction of alternate (gender) lists on ballot papers and the creation of a transnational list. i generally regard the solutions put forward as positive. however, i did not support the proposal to harmonise the minimum voting age to 16, considering it more important to preserve the traditions of each member state (the principle of subsidiarity), nor the creation of a common electoral constituency which is not based on a subsequent council decision.
‒ i voted in favour of the hübner/leinen report on the reform of the electoral law for the european elections because its proposals represent, in general, a significant advance in the functioning of european democracy and a strengthening of the democratic legitimacy of the union's institutions. in particular, the visibility of european political parties on ballot papers and campaign materials greatly enhances transparency so that citizens know who they are voting for. furthermore, greater harmonisation of electoral rules, now largely regulated by different national laws, promotes the unity of the electoral act, voter participation and equality between european citizens. although i have reservations about the proposal to create a common european electoral area based on a transnational list, a complex issue which would require further development, my final vote in favour took into account that this proposal is part of the overall, very positive commitment reached between various political groups in the european parliament and that its implementation is still dependent on a unanimous decision by the council.
‒ this reform of the electoral law is yet another manifestation of pure hypocrisy. the eu preaches democracy but continues to armor up all its instruments and mechanisms for imposing its neoliberal policy and its unique thinking on citizens and nation states. so it was in referendums, so it is in economic governance and so it is at the level of the ecb that continues to determine what states should or should not do under penalty of cutting access to credit. if there is any doubt, look at greece. the fact that we are in agreement with european parties or with measures to standardize electoral practices in each member state does not mask this reality. we no longer support this attempt to federalize the process of electing the european parliament and we reject the attempt to impose criteria which are linked to the practice and experience of each national state. nor do we recognise any legitimacy for the eu to give lessons in democracy to anyone.
in writing. ‒ under the guise of increasing transparency, increasing democracy, strengthening the concept of 'european citizenship' and harmonising the process of elections to the ep, what is proposed in this report is the deepening of federalism. the report advocates the inclusion of the names and logos of european political parties on ballot papers and their use on posters and other material used in campaigns for elections to the ep; encouraging member states to facilitate the participation of european political parties in electoral campaigns; the creation of an eu electoral circle (25 meps); the creation of a european electoral authority. it also proposes that 'national' parties should 'elect their candidates for the ep elections in a 'democratic' way, which means imposing ways of functioning on the parties. the report argues that meps have become representatives of the eu's citizens. all these positions seek to deepen federalism, to remove the sovereignty of the member states and to unify the thinking of meps who, in this light, must no longer be representatives of the people who elect them, but must be subordinated to the logic of the eu and the parties to which they belong. it's an attack on democracy. we voted against it.
‒ the air transport sector represents a huge market at european level, representing a considerable value in european gdp and providing a large number of jobs. the commission will present a package on aviation by the end of 2015 to identify and address the challenges facing the eu aviation sector. it is important to stress that the measures adopted will ensure the sustainability and competitiveness of the sector (threatened by competition both on the internal and external markets) on the one hand, and high safety, labour and environmental standards on the other. i share the concern that this new package should be consistent with passenger rights legislation, so as to create a clear and easy-to-understand body of legislation for both consumers and air carriers.
in europe, the economy of the air transport sector directly contributed to 2.6 million jobs and accounted for more than 2.4% of eu gdp, and in 2014 849.4 million passengers were transported by air in the eu, an increase of 4.4% compared to 2013 and 16.9% compared to 2009. however, the environment around the companies areas is changing rapidly, which has already led to the elimination of more than 20 000 jobs. against this background, the presentation of an aviation package aimed at identifying and responding to the challenges facing the eu aviation sector is of the utmost importance, including in order to strengthen its sustainability and competitiveness, consolidate european airlines, airports and the aviation industry, ensure a level playing field in the global market and define a long-term strategy for the european aviation sector.
‒ european airports are easily undervalued over other international airports for reasons ranging from the lack of regulation of air transport to the lack of subsidies. it is therefore important to establish comprehensive aviation agreements with the european union's most important trading partners as a strategic objective, allowing european airlines to be relieved of national and community burdens, thus strengthening the competitiveness of this important sector at european level. in this way we are also contributing to greater cohesion of the regions as a strategic pillar for growth and employment and for increased turnover. improving the competitiveness and ensuring the sustainability of the sector, which is expected to double air traffic by 2030, is an important basis for employment growth in the european union, as the report in question argues. for these reasons, i support the report for a resolution on aviation in and out of the european airspace.
‒ unsurprisingly, this european parliament resolution remains in line with the previous packages on aviation and the single european sky. in other words, they end up supporting the commission's positions and its proposals for the liberalisation and outsourcing of airport services. the resolution states in particular that: urges the commission and the member states to accelerate the implementation of the single european sky by adopting the ses2+ package because the current fragmentation of european airspace places additional burdens on european airlines; that is why we are voting against it.
the resolution calls for a set of measures to be included in the future aviation package. in general, the measures focus on increasing the competitiveness of eu aviation systems in the face of other realities (notably in the middle east) for which the development of a number of areas, based on the deepening of the single european sky, would be key. the single european sky project is, from its inception, inseparable from the intention of liberalising the air transport sector. the underlying vision is not the development of the sector according to a logic of the prevalence of the public interest, but rather the alignment of airspace management with the interests of the large airlines and the monopolistic concentration in progress. the arguments that have been advanced over the years in favour of the 'single european sky' are subsidiary to this objective and are without foundation. we voted against it.

madam president, i would first of all like to welcome the conclusion of the free trade agreement with vietnam, which is an important partner of the european union in the context of south-east asia. this is the first new generation trade agreement with a developing country and can therefore be a model for future agreements with asean countries. but trade is not an end in itself, and the union's own trade and investment strategy underlines the need for trade agreements to promote european values and, in particular, human rights. we have good reason to be concerned about the respect for human rights in vietnam, in particular freedom of expression. and this house insisted that the european commission apply an approach based on conditionality in its trade agreements. i would therefore like to ask the commissioner what progress has been made in vietnam on human rights since the start of the trade negotiations and what lessons we should learn from this process. can we consider, can the commission consider that this agreement with vietnam has in fact respected the principle of human rights conditionality in a trade agenda?
madam president, how far should we go in terms of animal welfare legislation? it is a question that has been based on a compromise between improving the physical and psychological health of the animals and the financial impact on the producers. with the intensification of production, we can never give up on the objectives of continuously improving animal welfare. as regards the welfare of aquatic animals, it is necessary to ensure that aquaculture production, and especially intensive aquaculture production, has the appropriate conditions. we know that some of the conditions of stabilization are questionable to say the least. i therefore ask the commission to indicate the results of scientific research carried out under the 2012-2015 strategy. there are also issues related to animal suffering during the fishing process. i would point out that this issue was omitted in the 2012 commission and it was worth starting its reflection for the future.
the attacks on animal welfare are a consequence of an agriculture increasingly subject to the logic of profit in an increasingly competitive global market. the absurd levels of production intensity we have in the european union, whether in the case of piglets or intensive pig, poultry or rabbit production, are not the result of any whim on the part of our farmers. this is a contingency which forces them to maximise animal productivity, otherwise they simply cannot guarantee the profitability of their farms. it's this contingency that's unresolved. a contradiction between an increasingly liberal, market-oriented cap that pushes farmers towards productivist models where profit is put above animal welfare, and also all the scientific evidence that warns us every day of the need to stop this madness. stop in the name of animal welfare, biodiversity and public health. so it's important to extend our agricultural equation to other social and environmental variables, in the name of our planet's survival.
the rapporteur. - madam president, in the european union today more than one in four children live at risk of poverty or social exclusion. in 2013, 26.5 million children in the european union were at risk of falling into poverty and social exclusion. these are dramatic numbers. the policies that have impoverished families in the european union are the same ones that have pushed children into poverty by denying them many of the rights enshrined in the convention on the rights of the child, including the rights to health, education and social protection. in this report we have made very clear what the various studies pointed out, but what seems to have been ignored by those who insisted on austerity policies, so-called fiscal consolidation. the main factors contributing to child poverty are policies of redistribution of wealth, the effectiveness of government intervention through income support. it is clear that increasing employment is the most effective instrument in the fight against poverty. it is clear that the degradation of wage policies and social protection systems at national level is increasing child poverty. but the job itself is not enough. the tragedy of today is that the risk of child poverty persists in families with a high work intensity, as is the case in romania, lithuania, portugal, spain and others. it is now known that working parents who do not have access to childcare are often forced to leave their children in the care of another child or to resort to paid and uncertified informal care networks, which puts the safety and well-being of children at risk. in this report, we therefore recommend that member states introduce labour laws that guarantee social rights, including an appropriate mandatory minimum wage that respects national practices and collective agreements and that provides greater security for families and combats precarious ties by promoting work with social rights. in this report we therefore urge the european commission to refrain from recommending reforms and cuts in the public administration of the member states, from promoting the flexibilization of labour relations and the privatization of public services, which have unequivocally led to the weakening of children's social rights. but there is a fundamental perspective in this report: that effective poverty prevention policies are those that ensure universal and free access to public services, not those that are only concerned with compensating children already in child poverty. it is the studies that conclude that universal support policies offer better protection against child poverty. in this report, therefore, we advocate high-quality, free, universal public services, particularly in the areas of childcare, education, health, housing and leisure activities. we therefore advocate universal social subsidies for children as their own and intrinsic right. we encourage legislation that protects or increases maternity and paternity rights, safeguards women's return to work after pregnancy and maternity leave and supports single-parent families, which are predominantly female. in our report we consider not only monetary poverty but also multidimensional deprivation, and therefore we advocate statistical methods that integrate multidimensional indicators. we also believe that the european union's structural funds should be used more effectively to combat child poverty. we will vote against the parties included in the report who believe that this tragedy can be resolved through the european semester or the rules of economic and monetary union, because we believe that what is largely causing the problem must be tackled and cannot be part of the solution. finally, we would like to thank all those who contributed to the preparation of this report, in particular the various portuguese and international organisations that fight against child poverty on a daily basis.

mr president, commissioner, on the eve of the paris climate summit, the energy union is moving forward and on its way. this is in itself excellent news and a reason to press on with even greater vigour. the european union and the world need a robust and credible energy union. we therefore need to move forward on all the strategic dimensions of the agenda and we need to engage european citizens in a debate that will lead to concrete actions that have a concrete impact on their lives. this involvement needs clear and transparent information. the public debate on the renewables directive has to be based on open access to all relevant information on the direct and indirect costs of the various options. the improvement in information on statistics, prices, the provision of relevant information on energy security, nuclear safety, oil reserves, energy efficiency and consumption trends is also important. we need, to lead the energy transition, political intelligence, to mobilize citizens, to mobilize businesses, to have regulatory flexibility, convergence of efforts among the 28 countries and the ability to attract investment. and here, commissioner, we are going to have to be able to mobilise the strategic investment fund, the european strategic investment fund. and the response will have to be unequivocal, swift and appropriate to the responsibilities. it is also very important to have interconnections, because without them there will be energy islands, and without a single energy market there will be no energy union.
the european union is facing a triple energy challenge. with few reserves and highly dependent on imports in this area, it seeks to ensure the security of its supplies. rising energy prices pose another challenge. finally, climate change requires a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. the eu imports more than 60% of its gas and more than 80% of its oil. if no other solutions are adopted, dependence on energy imports could reach 70% in 20 or 30 years from 53% today. however, this eu intends to solve this serious structural problem through the market, by privatising the sector, by preventing governments from intervening directly or indirectly, or even, astonishingly, by forcing the existence of a carbon market which, in practice, has never worked. we remain convinced that only public control of the key sectors of the energy sector can lead to lasting solutions.

‒ the instruments of the so-called area of freedom, security and justice, in particular as regards the schengen acquis, were initially incorporated into the union legal order by the treaty of amsterdam. gradually, many have been updated, reformulated, strengthened, and in some cases have simply become obsolete. this regulation is intended to ensure the repeal of such acts and to ensure that in certain cases a transitional period is ensured.
‒ this report takes account of the results of the evaluation of the schengen acquis and legal instruments in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. several acts have been deemed obsolete, either because their content has been incorporated into subsequent acts or because of their temporary nature. the proposal repeals 11 decisions of the schengen executive committee, as their content was taken up in subsequent acts, and council regulation (ec) no 189/2008 of 18 february 2008 on the testing of the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii), which ceased to have legal effects when sis ii became operational on 9 april 2013. i agree with the motion for a resolution tabled.
‒ the committee on civil liberties of the european parliament has decided to place this report under the simplified procedure rule 50 (2) of the rules of procedure. the report is part of a set of three on the repeal of acts of the schengen acquis and acts in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. several acts belonging to the schengen acquis have ceased to be relevant because of their temporary nature or because their content has been taken up by subsequent acts, although they have not been repealed, rendering them obsolete. this report is therefore of an eminently technical nature. the fact is that, in practical terms, there are no substantial improvements between the obsolete acts and those which replace them, and so, despite the above, we reaffirm our fundamental critical position on schengen and its acquis. and so it is with regard to police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. these are areas where we have been critical of the eu approach and attempts at deeper federalism, with added limitations on the member states' decision-making capacity in areas that go to the heart of the sovereignty of the states.
‒ the european commission has carried out an evaluation of the schengen acquis and of the existing legal instruments in the field of judicial and police cooperation in criminal matters, taking into account protocol no 36 on transitional provisions annexed to the treaties. since these are obsolete provisions - either because they are purely temporary or because their content has been changed by subsequent acts - with a view to simplifying legislation, with gains in legal certainty and security, better lawmaking means repealing these same acts. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council decision repealing certain acts in the field of freedom, security and justice.
‒ in accordance with the european strategy 'legislate better', which requires greater transparency of union law and whose main objective is to simplify and make european regulation more effective, all acts which become obsolete both because of their content and their temporary nature should be repealed. in this way, certain acts in the area of freedom, security and justice have become obsolete - within the framework of the schengen acquis. the content of 11 decisions of the schengen executive committee has been taken up in subsequent acts and council regulation (ec) no 189/2008 of 18 february 2008 on the testing of the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii) ceased to have legal effects when the sis ii became effectively operational. in view of the various amendments, it has become necessary to change the type of decision to regulation, as the latter is binding and directly applicable to the member states, thus better suiting the purpose of the report in question. i am voting in favour of this proposal, since its adoption meets the objectives of clarity and legal certainty to be achieved in the framework of european union legislation.
‒ this commission proposal provides for the repeal of a number of acts belonging to the schengen acquis which have become obsolete, either because their content has been incorporated into subsequent acts or because of their temporary nature. in this particular case, the case concerns the repeal of eleven decisions of the schengen executive committee and regulation (ec) no 189/2008 of 18 february 2008 on the testing of the second generation of the schengen information system. in view of the end of the transitional period laid down in protocol no 36 annexed to the treaties and in view of the objectives of simplification and reduction of the volume of legislation set out in the strategy 'better regulation', i voted in favour.

‒ the european commission has carried out an evaluation of the schengen acquis and of the existing legal instruments in the field of judicial and police cooperation in criminal matters, taking into account protocol no 36 on transitional provisions annexed to the treaties. since these are obsolete provisions - either because they are purely temporary or because their content has been changed by subsequent acts - with a view to simplifying legislation, with gains in legal certainty and security, better legislation means repealing these same acts. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council decision repealing certain acts in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters.

‒ the convention for the conservation of southern tuna is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of southern tuna in all its distribution areas and has been in force since 20 may 1994. since the united nations convention on the law of the sea in 1982, the eu has pursued a very active policy of participation in all rfmos with the aim of contributing to the efficient, rational and sustainable management of marine resources and to the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. this proposal is intended to authorise an exchange of letters between the european union and the enlarged commission of the ccsbt, of which it has been a non-cooperating member since 2006. the conclusion of this agreement will allow the eu to become a full member of the enlarged commission of the ccsbt and thus to participate fully in its work. the ccsbt was only open to states, but the october 2013 amendment has allowed regional economic integration organisations, such as the eu, who wish to become members of this committee. i am in favour of concluding the agreement so that the eu becomes a full member of the ccsbt.
‒ the commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) responsible for the management of southern bluefin tuna (sbf) in all its areas of distribution. the convention for the conservation of southern tuna entered into force on 20 may 1994. the european union has been a non-cooperating member of the enlarged board of the ccsbt since 2006. the non-cooperating members shall participate fully in the activities of the ccsbt but shall not have voting rights. in october 2013, the scctb amended the resolution governing the enlarged committee to allow regional economic integration organisations that wish to become members of the committee (previously only eligible for non-cooperating membership) by means of an exchange of letters in which the applicant organisation must state to the scctb its firm commitment to respect the provisions of the convention and to abide by the decisions of the scctb enlarged committee. the purpose of this proposal is precisely to allow an exchange of letters between the eu and the enlarged ccsbt committee. the signature of this international instrument will thus allow the eu to become a full member of the enlarged commission of the btwc. i voted in favour.

‒ the key elements of the recast insurance mediation directive are to, inter alia, extend the scope of application to all distribution channels such as car rental; clarify some concepts and the powers of home and host supervisory authorities; identify, manage and mitigate conflicts of interest; increase the level of harmonisation of administrative measures and penalties; improve the adequacy and objectivity of consumer advice. although the recast aims at harmonising national provisions, coordinating rules and ensuring a level playing field for consumer protection and competition for distributors, it should be noted that this should not prevent member states from maintaining or introducing more stringent provisions to protect customers. we also welcome all improvements in consumer information, along with the guarantee of continuing training and professional development for workers. however, we believe that the directive will still not provide the desired level of transparency in the insurance sector as a whole. we also do not welcome the concern to promote an internal market for life and non-life insurance products and services, since this will only benefit the interests of the large financial companies.

‒ all children should have the right to education, health services, housing, protection, participation in decisions affecting them, leisure and free time, a balanced diet and care in the family environment, as stipulated in the un convention on the rights of the child. unfortunately, the eu is still far from fully complying with the convention. a comprehensive policy framework is therefore needed to address child poverty and promote child welfare based on three pillars, namely access to adequate resources under the european social fund, access to inclusive and quality services and children's participation in society and decision-making, recognising children as rights holders. in using the financial resources of the european structural and investment funds (esif) and in defining social policies, member states should pay greater attention to ways of protecting families with children with health problems from poverty. child support policies should be strongly marked by prevention, containing long-term strategies to combat social inequalities.
‒ child poverty is a reality in the eu: 1 in 4 children lives at risk of poverty and social exclusion. according to the united nations convention on the rights of the child, all children have the right to education, health care, housing, recreation, and a balanced diet. according to eurostat, in 2014, some 26 million children and young people were at risk of poverty and social exclusion, i.e. 27,7% of all children living in the eu. there are children at risk of poverty in all member states. the countries with the highest percentage of children at risk of poverty are romania (51%), bulgaria (45.2%) and hungary (41.4%). the countries with the lowest percentages are denmark (14.5%), finland (15.6%) and sweden (16.7%). malnutrition is also increasing among european children. according to unicef, in estonia, greece and italy, the percentage of children who cannot afford to eat meat or fish every other day has doubled since 2008. member states must therefore ensure that children and their families have access to education, health and social security, and it is necessary to tackle unemployment, promote job security and parental, educational and social networks, balanced nutrition and adequate housing. i voted for the report.
‒ more than a quarter of children in the eu live at risk of poverty or social exclusion. in 2013, 26.5 million children were at risk of falling into poverty and social exclusion. the policies that have impoverished families are the same ones that are pushing children into poverty by denying them rights enshrined in the convention on the rights of the child, namely the rights to health, education and social protection. the report recommends that member states introduce labour laws that guarantee social rights, including an appropriate mandatory minimum wage that respects national practices and collective agreements and that provides greater security for families and combats precarious ties by promoting work with social rights. the european commission is urged to refrain from recommending reforms and cuts in the public administration of the member states, from promoting the flexibilization of labour relations and the privatization of public services, which have unequivocally led to the weakening of children's social rights. the report argues that poverty prevention policies should ensure universal and free access to public services, particularly in childcare, education, health, housing and leisure activities. it advocates universal social subsidies for children as their own and intrinsic right. this report is to be enforced.
‒ the number of children in poverty and social exclusion was already a major problem in the eu even in the years of economic growth, with high employment rates, even before the recession and austerity programmes began. already in 2007, child poverty figures reached 26.3% and in 2011 26.9%. i agree with the need to develop policies to combat child poverty, but also to provide specific social emergency support, whether in the context of raising the lowest pensions or in the context of actually creating jobs and reducing unemployment. i abstained on this report because i disagree with the way in which the rapporteur has drafted it, which has departed from the main objective of the report.
‒ the european reality points to an increase in child poverty and social exclusion, in contradiction with the provisions of the un convention on the rights of the child, which states that all children should be guaranteed the right to education, health care, housing, protection, leisure and free time, balanced nutrition and care in a family environment. europe is currently facing a serious economic crisis which is affecting families and especially children. the existing inequalities go beyond the lack of basic needs, including also access to education and health services, as well as the possibility of integrating cultural, sports and leisure activities. the definition of public policy objectives and policies that reduce child poverty should be a priority, and measures should be implemented in the context of the european union as well as in the respective member states, such as ensuring access to education. i therefore vote in favour of this report, since i consider it essential to protect children's rights by setting targets for reducing child poverty and social exclusion.
‒ according to the un convention on the rights of the child, all children should be guaranteed the rights to education, health services, housing, protection, participation in decisions affecting them, leisure and free time, a balanced diet and care in the family environment. however, even within the eu, the convention is far from being fully complied with. indeed, the reports point to an increase in child poverty in europe. this report analyses the causes of child poverty and proposes some measures to combat it. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ according to unicef, between 2008 and 2013, an additional 1.6 million children in 30 european countries were living in severe material deprivation. child poverty is growing along with increasing social inequalities. the negative effects of poverty and social exclusion on children last a lifetime. it is in the early years of life that cognitive and socioeconomic skills are formed, which means that negative policy measures taken today will have irreversible negative impacts on these people's lives and on society. it is relative poverty that perpetuates social inequalities. it is essential that member states increase the amounts and effectiveness of social support for children and parents and promote labour legislation that guarantees social rights and security for families. the figures are clear in the portuguese case: one in four children in portugal lives in a household with material deprivation; more than half a million have lost their right to family allowance; state support for families is below the oecd average. there is no doubt that we need other policies for our country and for the union.
‒ based on the un convention on the rights of the child, every child has the right to education, health care, housing, protection, access to sports, leisure and culture, among others. however, these rights are not yet fully respected throughout the eu. the increase in child poverty is unfortunately a growing fact and as such the problems associated with it at an early age have an impact on the way future generations will develop. i therefore support the measures contained in the report concerning the need to stop children being exposed to poverty and social exclusion and the measures envisaged to minimise the consequences of this real social scourge. i also believe that identifying the root causes of child poverty and tackling them effectively and relentlessly, by promoting and ensuring education and the most basic rights of children in the eu, should be the aim of the union and, on a wider scale, the aim of all governments worldwide, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ an estimated one billion children live in conflict-affected areas; a quarter of these children are under five and are denied the right to education. these are un numbers. it is also estimated that 65 million children are affected by emergencies and protracted crises and that approximately 37 million children of primary and lower secondary school age are not in school. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. while welcoming the call for member states to contribute to increasing humanitarian funds for the education of children in emergency situations to 4% of the humanitarian aid provided for in the eu budget, we argue that these funds should be channelled towards promoting universal access to free, quality public education at all levels of education.
‒ the policies that have impoverished eu families are the same ones that have pushed children into poverty, denying them many of the rights enshrined in the convention on the rights of the child, including the rights to health, education and social protection. in this report, we therefore recommend that member states introduce labour laws that guarantee social rights, including an appropriate mandatory minimum wage that respects national practices and collective agreements and that provides greater security for families and combats precarious ties by promoting work with social rights. we therefore advocate universal social subsidies for children as their own and intrinsic right. we encourage legislation that protects or increases maternity and paternity rights, safeguards women's return to work after pregnancy and maternity leave and supports single-parent families, which are predominantly female. we voted against the parties included in the report who believe that this tragedy can be resolved through the european semester or the rules of economic and monetary union, because we believe that what causes much of the problem must be fought and cannot be part of the solution.
‒ the eu's cohesion policy aims to strengthen economic, social and territorial cohesion by reducing social disparities and situations of poverty and exclusion, which implies preventing segregation and promoting equal access and opportunities for all citizens, including the most marginalised communities. the effects of the economic crisis and austerity measures have reduced the availability of municipalities and entities providing treatment and support to the most marginalised groups, and may increase their exclusion when they are barred or refused participation in social and political processes essential for their social integration. i support the reintke report because i think it is important to use the union funds for the inclusion of these communities and the recommendations suggested are an opportunity to promote and support greater cohesion of the different european societies.
‒ the use of eu funds for the inclusion of marginalised communities can become a major opportunity to promote and support greater cohesion of european societies. cohesion policy is one of the strongest instruments the european union has at its disposal to combat inequalities and support territorial and social cohesion in its regions. in all european societies there are groups and communities facing structural exclusion and segregation from the majority of society and lacking even access to basic public infrastructure and services. however, in many cases, marginalised communities do not benefit from european cohesion policy and are not included in the decision-making structures or in the processes of project implementation and monitoring. i voted in favour.
‒ the report advocates greater use of eu cohesion funds to support marginalised communities. this support would be provided through the promotion and development of public health, education and social security services, the promotion of employability, cultural inclusion, gender equality and the participation of these communities in the definition of policies that affect them (political inclusion, participation and partnership with representative organisations). we generally support the report and its objectives, although there are some shortcomings and limitations. the big issue that the report fails to highlight is the eu budget's tightness in terms of cohesion, along with the dynamic of divergence that the capitalist nature of the integration process generates and drives. more than two decades ago, the then president of the european commission, jacques delors, said that to effectively implement the principle of cohesion, the community budget would have to be at least doubled. since then, there have been successive enlargements (to countries with levels of development below the eu average), while the budget has been shrinking. without eggs, there are no omelets. cohesion will thus be nothing more than a dead letter in the treaties. and in well-intentioned reports like this one.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and marginalised communities. the relevant role of cohesion policy in supporting the economic and social inclusion of marginalised communities and combating inequalities by promoting greater cohesion of european societies is underlined.
‒ the economic crisis has had a major negative impact on the territorial and social cohesion of the regions of the european union, due to public spending constraints in the member states, especially affecting marginalised communities. in response, cohesion policy plays a major role in the establishment of social equality, aiming to combat social exclusion and the most recurrent problems such as poverty, employment and health problems. accessibility to public infrastructure or lack of livability conditions may also emerge as some of the problems affecting marginalised communities, which include various groups of people such as disadvantaged neighbourhoods, people in need, people at risk of poverty, among others. there is a growing need to create actions and programmes at european level that intervene in this area, using european union funds, playing a key role in cohesion policy. i am in favour of the recommendations in this report, as it benefits marginalised communities by improving their living conditions, by tackling social inequalities and by promoting european social cohesion.
‒ cohesion policy is one of the strongest instruments the european union has at its disposal to combat inequalities and support territorial and social cohesion in its regions. in all european societies, there are groups and communities facing structural exclusion and segregation from the majority of society and lacking even access to basic public infrastructure and services. while the primary responsibility for changing the situation of marginalised communities lies with the member states, the objective of social cohesion requires european intervention in policies to include marginalised communities. indeed, cohesion policy can play an important role in changing the situation, not only by overcoming challenges in housing or access to public infrastructure, as is already the case under the erdf, but also by taking an integrated approach to tackling all forms of discrimination faced by marginalised communities. the point is that the necessary adjustments are made and monitoring and qualitative evaluation mechanisms are introduced so that interventions can achieve sustainable and long-term results. i voted in favour.
‒ strong cuts in public spending during the crisis have led to a worsening of existing problems in the member states, such as unemployment, lack of social security, difficult housing situation and lack of public health services. the crisis has had a direct negative impact on members of marginalized communities. many municipalities continue to face serious budgetary constraints that prevent them from adequately addressing social marginalisation. cohesion policy can play an essential role in changing this situation, not only by overcoming challenges in housing or access to public infrastructure, but also by taking an integrated approach to tackling all forms of discrimination faced by marginalised communities.
‒ cohesion policy has played a very important role for the regions of the european union in recent decades, in particular in strengthening the instruments at its disposal to combat asymmetries and in supporting the territorial, economic and social cohesion of its regions. however, many groups and communities are still subject to social exclusion resulting from the denial of access to basic infrastructure and services such as housing, education, employment, social security or health services. this reality is the result of a complex set of circumstances which have accentuated existing social and economic problems, particularly in the most disadvantaged and socially deprived communities (and unfortunately prevalent in many european regions). in view of these facts, this report argues that cohesion policy should therefore also provide for measures to include these marginalised communities. i therefore voted in favour of this report because i believe that concrete measures at european level are needed to meet this need.
in writing. ‒ the focus of this report is on a greater use of eu cohesion funds to support marginalised communities. this support would be provided through the promotion and development of public health, education and social security services, the promotion of employability, cultural inclusion, gender equality and the participation of these communities in the definition of policies that affect them (political inclusion, participation and partnership with representative organisations). it is noted that the report shows a tendency to seek a broad definition (in the eu context) of the concept of marginalised community, which presupposes a standardisation. the report also focuses on the use of the structural funds and is in line with eu objectives. these references to federalisation and the application of the 'one size fits all' recipe are not, however, comprehensive in the report.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on a greater use of eu cohesion funds to support marginalised communities. this support would be provided through the promotion and development of public health, education and social security services, the promotion of employability, cultural inclusion, gender equality and the participation of these communities in the formulation of policies that affect them. we voted yes.
‒ the united nations system is the world's leading forum for global governance and a stage par excellence for promoting the values and interests of the european union and its member states. the new challenges and problems of the union are inextricably linked to the wishes and system of the un, insofar as they lack global answers, and global problems also lack european answers. the eu's security instability (conflicts in ukraine, syria, the expansion of is), development and humanitarian aid problems, environmental and climate change challenges cannot be solved by themselves without a global response, with the support of the international community, under the auspices of the un. however, the eu's place as a major international actor is not properly recognised in the un system of governance and it should be sought to strengthen and increase its own influence and that of its member states. reforms in the rationalization of its structures, working methods, budget and even the power of its security council must be carried out, and its blockage in situations of genocide and crimes against humanity is regrettable. to stress the importance of increased cooperation between the eu and un humanitarian agencies.
‒ the european union's vision is linked to peace, security, development and human rights on a global scale, and the challenges it faces lack global responses which, in turn, lack european action. the eu promotes an international system based on enhanced multilateral cooperation and good global governance and is committed to genuine multilateralism, with the united nations at its core. this commitment is based on the conviction that, in order to respond effectively to global crises, challenges and threats, the international community needs an effective multilateral system, based on universal rights and values. to better achieve its foreign policy objectives, the eu must aim to strengthen global governance within the un system and to increase its own and its member states' influence within the un system. i voted in favour.
in writing. - this report is unacceptable, both in its content and in its objectives. only a very biased reading of the un charter can lead one to believe that the european union shares its values and principles, as this report does. what, then, of direct participation in military aggressions against sovereign countries, violating their independence and territorial integrity, as has happened in the cases of iraq, libya or syria, among others? this report carries an unacceptable view of how the eu should act within the un and, in particular, within its general assembly - a body of which the eu should not even be a part, given the nature of both the body and the eu itself. we cannot accept the proposal that the eu should be a member of the security council, nor that changes should be made in the un institutional framework in general to align it with the eu's (i.e. the powers that command it) interests in foreign policy. the attempt to force the submission of sovereign states to the eu's pre-determined positions in the un discussions is unacceptable. this report is an example of the most unbridled federalist impulses within the eu. we obviously voted against it.
