the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. in this respect, the eu needs global partners to achieve its foreign policy objectives, notably on peace and security, terrorism, organised crime, regional conflicts, state collapse and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. the united nations system is the world's main forum for improving global governance and as such represents the best forum for promoting the values and interests of the eu. this framework requires that, in order to achieve its objectives as enshrined in the treaty, the eu should aim to strengthen global governance within the un system and to increase its own and its member states' influence. the position adopted in this report reaffirms the importance of revitalizing the work of the general assembly in general and the work of the eu under the auspices of the united nations in particular. in view of the above, i voted in favour.
‒ as a major global actor, the eu has a highly relevant role to play within multilateral organisations and should therefore contribute to ensuring peace, security, development and the respect of human rights worldwide. the eu's problems lack global answers just as much as global problems lack concrete european action. the eu and the un have been working together to address key issues that not only secure the present but also protect future generations. examples include the strengthening of work in developing countries and of various international companies that also contribute in this respect, the fight against violence, gender equality, the fight against corruption, climate change and the proper management of refugee flows. however, i also agree with the rapporteur's view that the general assembly must be revitalised and the un security council reformed. i therefore consider it essential to maintain and strengthen dialogue and cooperation between the eu and the un so that the objectives set by the union in terms of foreign policy can be achieved and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
‒ this report is based on a principle which is, to say the least, dubious, namely that the european union shares the values and principles of the united nations charter. but what about the military aggressions actively promoted and carried out against sovereign countries, violating their independence and territorial integrity, as happened in the cases of iraq, libya or syria, among others? the report does not, however, address key issues where the eu could play a relevant role in the united nations. let us take two examples. first, the discussion on the establishment of a multilateral framework for the renegotiation of sovereign debts, a matter of the utmost importance for several eu member states. what does the eu do? boycott the discussion and its outcome. secondly, the resolution on the right to water and sanitation, which is regarded as a human right. what does the eu do? it boycotts the resolution and persists on the path of water privatisation, which is being pursued in several countries, in some cases as a result of eu impositions.
‒ the eu's imperialist bent and aspirations to play a dominant role in the world political context are clearly evident in this report. in a most abject way, the eu's principles and values are being collated with those of the united nations. the pursuit of peace is proclaimed, ignoring the aggressive and warmongering character that the eu and many of its member states have assumed, promoting war in countries such as iraq, libya, syria or afghanistan. the contribution to poverty eradication and the promotion of democracy is proclaimed, when we know well that the support is often consecrated in a framework of imperative alignment, that is, imposition, with the political strategies and 'democratic' values of the eu. it is unashamedly proposed that the eu should have a greater preponderance as a body within the united nations, its influence and role in global governance within the un system, in particular in the general assembly, and take its place in the security council, which we reject. the document sets out, in essence, a strategy to take the united nations by storm and to make this organisation an instrument of the eu's foreign policy. we voted against it.
the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, if i were to tell you now that you would only have to pay 5% income tax this year, none of you would believe it, even though we are so close to christmas. well, that is the reality of most of the large multinational companies operating in europe, which pay effective taxes of 5%, sometimes even less, even in countries where the nominal tax rate is 30% and above. this situation has very serious consequences. the first is that the tax burden that fuels our collective expenditure on health, education, unemployment support, infrastructure, falls almost exclusively on two types of taxpayers: small and mediumsized enterprises and individuals, that is, the ordinary citizen. the second consequence is that in a period when so many exceptional sacrifices are being asked of the populations, which include giving up public services and social benefits, including some that have been solemnly contracted with the state, such as pensions, while the tax burden is rising to impossible levels, this situation is totally unfair. an injustice that becomes unbearable. how do you explain this? strangely enough, although the rules of the internal market and the single currency have evolved to create a level playing field throughout europe, the european union has always maintained the key principle in direct taxation that any member state can oppose this and any development in this area can be immediately blocked. this situation would perhaps have been tolerated at the time of the founding of the european union, when the three big countries, france, germany and italy, turned a blind eye to more or less open tax competition on the part of the three small benelux countries. but today, with the european union extended to 28 countries, and when the movement of capital is more important than the movement of goods, the distortion of competition in the internal market, coupled with this principle of unanimity, forces us to make a very serious reassessment of how we work together. one year after the lux leaks scandal, the european parliament is now producing its first major report on direct taxation in europe. this report must be a factor capable of triggering the structural change that is needed. we have all worked hard and seriously, we have listened to hundreds of people, and we hope that our conclusions will enable this parliament to take a strong and solid stand against the council and the commission in defence of the interests of the citizens, who are also taxpayers. our proposals, it should be noted, are not about tax harmonization in the union, but about ensuring that direct taxes on company profits are calculated according to common methods, that multinational companies publicly report essential information in each of the countries in which they operate, that tax administrations, and in particular the european commission, will have access to the terms of advance tax agreements between administrations and large companies, that there is a much greater transparency regime at european level on how these matters are handled at member state level, particularly in the framework of the code of conduct. we also need to move towards a european definition of tax havens, with zero tolerance for them, and to create clear rules to protect whistleblowers. it is also necessary to manage the conflicts of interest of those who give tax advice to multinationals and at the same time advise the states and the european institutions. i would like to leave one last note, and i'll finish right away, madam president, and this note is that this work is not finished. we have to keep working and getting the information we haven't gotten so far, but that doesn't mean we have to keep going backwards. we must move quickly, as soon as this week, with a continuation of our work, with a clear mandate to achieve what we have not achieved so far, but to move forward in monitoring the commission and the council in implementing what we are now going to recommend.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a real pleasure for me to be here today to present the final report of the taxe committee. it is a good report and i want to give credit to the two rapporteurs, mrs ferreira and mr theurer, and to all the participants in this committee. i want to take the time to congratulate them on their work. we both want to make taxation more transparent, fairer and more efficient. this is a priority for the european commission. our citizens expect it. it is one of the main lines of my action. i already wanted to move forward fast and strong in 2015 and i want to keep this momentum going in 2016 with the support of the european parliament. you know the two fundamental principles that guide my action and which are rooted in the most basic sense of justice. first, taxes must be collected where the profits are made. this is known as the principle of effective taxation. secondly, everyone, including multinational firms, must pay their fair share. this is an ambition which, i know, is shared by the committee on taxation, which supplies the report and explains why, in fact, on many points our views converge. i shall now return to some of them, but i shall also return to the quality of our cooperation with the committee on taxation. i noted what mr theurer said at the end of his speech: the need for information. we have tried to find pragmatic arrangements to allow the various groups access to as many documents as possible. there is still progress to be made. you know the limits that exist. they do not come from the commission. i mean that very strongly. this year, the commission presented two major initiatives to change the corporate tax regime in europe: the tax transparency package - this was last march - and the action plan on corporate taxation in june. these are two initiatives that lay the foundations for a substantial reform of the corporate tax framework, covering a very wide spectrum, from transfer pricing to preferential regimes, to advance tax agreements, tax havens, dispute resolution and code of conduct reform. several of these initiatives are the subject of specific recommendations by your committee. i want to quickly go back to the main ones. first, we heard the message from the european parliament on country-by-country reporting. i had the opportunity to say this at one of my hearings, because i have had two in front of you, that the commission is keeping up with this initiative. we will complete our impact study in the first half of 2016, accompanied by an initiative, which we will calibrate. you know my personal preferences, but we must also take into account, in defining the target audience, the need to preserve the investment. that is where the commission will set its sights. it is in the commission's work programme for next year, which gives you a measure of our commitment. i'm sure my staff is very good at this. as regards the proposed common consolidated corporate tax base accis , the commission wants to revive this dossier, which has been stuck in the council for too long. this will was clearly stated, again, in the commission's 2016 work programme. we are withdrawing the current proposal, not because it is bad, but because it is blocked. we will replace it with proposals for a two-stage approach, starting with an agreement on a mandatory tax base. this will improve the single market for businesses while closing the gaps and ensuring that each business pays its fair share of tax. this is the key element in the overhaul of corporate taxation so that it is finally in line with the european dimension. i would like to say, however, that i am not giving up on consolidation. i know that is what is expected, but it seems to me that the way to convince those who are reluctant is to proceed first to the creation of a common platform and, i regret, to move towards consolidation. i am glad to see that we have agreed on these key instruments in the fight against tax evasion and the establishment of a fair taxation system in the european union. as far as the work of the oecd is concerned, the commission is in full agreement with your recommendation. now that the g20 meeting in antalya a few days ago has approved the final measures for the beps project, this must become the de facto rule of the european union. it must be implemented in a manner compatible with the treaties. a patchwork of national approaches would fragment our single market, hinder the freedoms guaranteed by the treaty, and weaken member states' efforts to combat tax evasion. therefore, a coordinated approach to beps is essential and the union has already taken the lead in this regard. for example, the commission's proposal to increase transparency on the advance decision process in tax matters was adopted in record time, only seven months after it was proposed, and i had the opportunity to come and defend this proposal for a directive. i would like to congratulate the european parliament on the very high quality of its work. i would have liked, as you would, ladies and gentlemen, to go a little further, but i think that the compromise we have reached is, let us say, of a high quality. we must do so more quickly if we are to protect the tax bases of all member states and safeguard our common competitiveness. we must also ensure that our own instruments are consistent. parliament asks us, and i quote, 'to deal in depth with the problems of corporate taxation, including harmful practices and their impact in the case of the european semester'. the commission is of course prepared to continue to use all the instruments at its disposal to combat tax evasion, including in the framework of the european semester. i therefore answer in the affirmative. where rules and practices that make tax systems vulnerable to aggressive tax optimisation are already being examined, they need to be examined more. as regards the external dimension of tax evasion, the commission fully shares the view of the taxe committee that the union must raise its playing field. we published a pan-european list of third countries identified for tax purposes last june. it was the first time. this is an important step towards a more coherent approach towards these countries in terms of good tax governance. i'm aware of the criticisms that may have come here or there. it was a potpourri or a best of. we must now move towards a much more coherent and common strategy. we must have a real external tax strategy, based on a common mechanism within the european union, to deal with external threats to the tax bases of the member states. on this point, again, our views converge. the commission also shares the european parliament's expectations regarding the fight against the misuse of legal structures such as companies and trusts. we will therefore pay particular attention to the implementation by the member states of their obligations under the fourth anti-money laundering directive. as regards tax advice, i would like to stress that new rules, which are already being implemented in the european union and which apply to the auditing of the accounts of certain entities, will make it possible, in particular, to regulate the joint provision of audit services and tax advice in order to limit, as you wish, the risks of conflict of interest. they shall apply from june 2016. finally, a word on the control of state aid in the tax field. the commission thanks the european parliament for its support on this obviously important subject. the control of aid is an important instrument in combating the unlawful advantages granted to undertakings by member states and contributes to strengthening the fiscal equity of our union. as my colleague, margrethe vestager, has said, with whom i work under the best conditions, each in his own field and of course respecting the other's competences, legislation on the one hand, implementation on the other, she is pursuing the investigations on behalf of the commission, in particular through the procedures at her disposal. it is making progress in its analysis of the information received from all the member states on the report on tax returns and you know that it has been forced to take quite courageous measures with the college, which i fully support, as do you. ladies and gentlemen, when i was appointed, with this house, as commissioner for taxation just over a year ago, i promised to make fair and efficient corporate taxation a major priority. the pace and scope of the commission's initiatives on corporate tax reform presented this year are proof, beyond my personal commitment, of the commission's commitment to go faster, stronger, further than any commission has done so far. but 2015 is coming to an end, and my work in this area has barely begun. of course, it will continue at the same pace and with the same ambition in 2016 and beyond. i want to say that i share the conviction of the commission and its president that the european parliament has a crucial role to play. that role is that of deliberation. it is also, let us say, to maintain political pressure because you and i both know what the rule is in tax matters. it is constraining, difficult and even limiting. it's the unanimous rule, twenty-eight. it is therefore also necessary to be able to turn to the member states. i do it, you do it, we do it together. i am sure that our institutions will continue to work hand in hand to advance these joint initiatives and i think that this report and the work of your contribution are a very important contribution to this.

on behalf of the s&d group. - madam president, commissioner, this report could not be more relevant after the horrific terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november. it is the result of intensive collective work, in cooperation with the author, rachida dati, whom i salute. thousands of young europeans have left for syria and iraq to fight in the ranks of daesh, which is neither a state nor an islamic state. but it is not, as some people wish to tell us, that closing borders or a directive on the pnr will stop their radicalisation and recruitment. the fight is also political and ideological, and it is waged right here in europe, within our societies, because the attackers in paris in january, as in november, were europeans, french and belgians. and so it is essential that we return to tackling the inequalities, discrimination and social exclusion felt particularly acutely by migrant communities in neighbourhoods that we have allowed to become ghettos of despair and resentment, with 60% unemployment, like molenbeek in the heart of europe, brussels today besieged by fear. our collective security requires an end to the destructive policy of blind austerity, which also explains why instead of having human resources and other reinforced means, police, intelligence services and magistrates are struggling with incapacities, and explains why prisons have become centres of radicalization instead of rehabilitation for criminals. we need unity in the fight against the transnational terrorist threat. we need political union, where our states share security information and police and judicial cooperation, and make joint planning and joint security risk assessment. we need a common foreign policy, european security and a common security and defence policy, as syria, iraq and libya have shown. the member states of the european union must coordinate and tackle arms trafficking, terrorist financing and organised crime, associated with the capacity of organisations such as daesh and al-qaeda, and cannot continue to operate in a business as usual way vis-à-vis governments and states where daesh and al-qaeda have found financiers and facilitators. international trade, including arms and oil, cannot be worth our silence. the lesson to be drawn from the paris attacks is that our governments must coordinate to stop the terrorist threat and understand that this requires a coherent european strategy. and that it will not be at the expense of fundamental rights and freedoms that we will defeat terrorism. without rights, we will never have security. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover all the member states, and to extend it to cover all the member states, and to extend it to cover all the member states. and that is our moral strength not to bow to the terrorists and not to play into their hands, who want to destroy freedoms and democracy. (the speaker accepts to answer a question on a blue card in accordance with rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure.)
blue-card answer.– no, we do not oppose pnr. we voted for pnr. but pnr is only a tool and not the ‘magic bullet’ that will solve the problem. yes – and also in reply to mrs dati – we are in favour of border controls, but we are not in favour of the abuse of controls to allow racial profiling and ethnic profiling in order to prevent migrants and refugees from coming into europe. i recall that, when we had borders, more than a million of the citizens of my country, portugal, crossed those borders illegally to work in france.
mr president, there are a number of positive aspects to this report. for example, it refers to the harmful effects on health and safety at work of precarious employment or that precarious employment excludes workers from access to training and occupational health and safety services, and is also associated with mental stress. all this would be even more positive if the european union always acted consistently and in accordance with the principles set out in the strategy. for example, it was important to understand what kind of work the european union funds under the youth guarantee programme, when it is now known that a large proportion of jobs covered by this type of programme are forms of labour exploitation of young people. for example, it would be important to see whether the european union does not finance companies that violate these rights, particularly in the field of safety and health at work, with structural and cohesion funds. because we hear every day of many companies that do that and have already received funding.
mr president, in order for this strategic framework to have the desired effect, we need to achieve five objectives. more social dialogue is a key element for the development, adaptation and implementation of occupational health and safety policies, both at national and european union level, because only a genuine commitment between all the parties involved will guarantee success in local implementation. more tools to support businesses. certain sectors have specific needs and we cannot ignore the particular case of smes. in this regard, it is urgent to develop practical instruments and guidelines to support, facilitate and improve compliance by them and their workers with occupational health and safety requirements. increased effort and coordination at the level of the european union and its member states. the european commission should set up a database of national health and safety organisations to facilitate access to national plans, encourage the sharing of good practice and help fill policy gaps in this area. increased capacity to adapt to new occupational safety and health challenges. new emerging risks in the workplace, such as psychosocial risks and burnout, among others, require a rapid and appropriate response. finally, greater awareness among workers and employers of the benefits of implementing these measures. for example, reducing error, motivation, greater individual and collective well-being, contributing to increased worker productivity and reduced risk for companies.
mr president, there is no better preventive measure to prevent gender discrimination in pensions than to close the gender pay gap. and to do this, collective bargaining must be respected, and wages must not be negotiated individually. it is necessary that women workers should not be afraid to report discrimination and therefore be protected by the law. it is necessary to provide the labour inspection authorities with adequate means. sanctions must be applied to companies that do not comply with the law. the rights of mothers must be defended so that women are not penalised for having been mothers during their working lives. these are some of the measures, but their implementation, together with the defence of public, supportive and universal social security systems, will safeguard a dignified ageing for women.
mr president, the paris attacks were not just an attack on france. they were an attack on all of europe. it was the values of the western democracies, which france embodies, that were hit, and people from many countries, including portugal, were murdered. we are at war, a hidden, cowardly war, without the classic rules, but no less lethal. terrorism is not fought with romantic proclamations. it's not enough to say we won't give in to fear. we need to act. we must fight to eliminate extremism that attacks our values, our way of life, our very existence. we can't feel like we're being held hostage in our own home. the first solidarity of the european leaders, without forgetting the others, must be with our peoples, whom we cannot put at risk by our decisions. everything must be considered: r&amp;d, smart borders, detection and elimination of funding sources, monitoring of social networks and other modern forms of communication, use of all military forces, closure of indoctrination sites in europe, reassessment of conditions of assignment and loss of nationality, if necessary, and of course... we have just said, mr president, that europe is old, but it does not have to be weak. europe must face medieval madness and win. we will win.
jihadist terrorism has a precise target: liberal-democratic institutionalism that favours the affirmation of critical thinking. the attacks in paris a few days ago show that this is the case. the terrorists know that fear is a silent poison that can dissolve the foundations of this model of political and social organization: they want to inoculate it through these horrible acts. the european union, which has among its aims the protection and promotion of human rights, must react with vigour and intelligence to this threat: the european union must work towards improving its repressive response capacity, both internally and externally. this will mean increased cooperation between member states in the fields of security and defence policies, which will also mean increased sharing of sovereignty.
in writing. we live in fear today, as if our safety has been called into question. and it was. and our values are under attack. and they were. we must therefore act. but freedom and security are not opposite concepts. strictly speaking, there is no freedom without security, and no security without freedom. when we are in emergency situations, exceptional measures are necessary, but only for the period strictly necessary to neutralize the threat. in the long term we must look for the necessary and proportionate measures to combat the threat. on a sensitive issue such as the fight against terrorism, a united front is called for. the extremes are already trying to polarize the discussion. it is therefore up to the moderates not to take the easy way out and to fight these criminals effectively while preserving our essential values, such as fundamental rights or the schengen area. in january of this year i said that we need new instruments or the strengthening of existing ones if their future is the same as that of those we have approved so far: little or no use? in the heat of the moment, it's up to the decision-makers to act with balance and not forget the reason why they're attacking us: we are free. to compromise our core values would be to grant a victory to the terrorists.
in writing. the paris attacks show that we need more europe to keep our citizens safe: less europe has facilitated the terrorist killing spree. it is up to governments to take the political lead in establishing european coordination of intelligence services, police and judicial cooperation, which need to be strengthened in means and capacity and not be further reduced by the disastrous austerity policies which also feed the ghettos from which the terrorists have sprung. we need to work for peace and security in the neighborhood - it's the conflicts that get us in the door! we need a common security and defence policy within the framework of a coherent common foreign and security policy. and we need consistency: to say that we are at war is to give the terrorists political status, to play into their hands. we must attack the sources of terrorist financing: arms trafficking, oil, money laundering, by holding all financiers and facilitators accountable, many of them playing a double game, such as saudi arabia, qatar and turkey. finally, mr weber's accusation that the socialists tried to introduce amendments to the pnr in the dati report yesterday is false. it's a dirty coup against the convergence we need to fight terrorism.
the recent terrorist attacks in france demonstrate the urgent need to build an international force capable of fighting and defeating the self-proclaimed islamic state. for the first time in the history of the lisbon treaty, france has invoked article 42 (7), which provides for a solidarity clause in the event of aggression against an eu country. it is an article which has never been used before in the history of our union. i understand that in addition to attacking strategic targets, countries have to stop funding the islamic state, stop acquiring oil resources from isis and try to build a real economic blockade so that they have no resources to finance their activities. the european union must take a leading role on the international political stage, building the necessary bridges with the us and russia to defeat isis, as well as improving the education of our young people in schools, preventing the radicalisation of young people and improving control and surveillance systems at the eu's borders.
‒ as a result of the adjustment of a set of indicators, this draft amending budget revises downwards the contributions for the financial year 2015. in total, around eur 9.4 billion will be reimbursed to member states and thus withdrawn from the union budget. at a time when the union is facing a refugee crisis which requires a strong mobilisation of funds, particularly by the union, i find it regrettable that it has not been possible to reach an agreement in the negotiations with the council. instead of using these to meet commitments under the migration agenda outside the community budget (such as the trust funds for syria and africa or the united nations world food programme), member states decided to receive the money and leave a decision for later.
in writing. ‒ member states have committed eur 2.3 billion to the trust fund for africa and the trust fund for syria. these commitments are not being met. this corrective draft translates into a reduction in national contributions of eur 9.4 billion, of which eur 2.3 billion correspond to fines and a surplus over the revenue from customs duties. these revenues are from the eu budget. the member states were to hand over the surplus of eur 2.3 billion for commitments they had made in respect of the trust funds, which was coincidentally the same amount. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this draft budgetary correction no 8/2015 concerns the revision of the estimate of traditional own resources (customs duties), the budgeting of the missing vat and gni (gross national income) balances for 2014 and the vat and gni balances for 2015. this results in a decrease of eur 9.4 billion in member states' contributions to the eu budget, based on their gni. the draft amending budget also aims to update the forecast for other revenue sources. it also provides for a reduction of eur 123 474 in both the commitment and payment appropriations of the european data protection supervisor. we have argued that if such arrangements are made, the money should not be returned to the member states - which is mainly to the benefit of the wealthier countries - but should remain in the eu budget, reinforcing the (small) cohesion funds. in this case, parliament proposed that the money be allocated to trust funds for africa and syria, as well as to refugee support agencies. the european commission and the council have not accepted it, and this report regrets that. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have not yet adopted the euro.
‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution approving the council's position on draft amending budget no 8/2015.
in the light of the above, the commission is proposing to extend the scope of the programme to include the following areas: i regret that the financial commitments made by member states for the trust fund for africa, the trust fund for syria and the un agencies providing support to refugees have not yet been implemented, resulting in a backlog of eur 2,3 billion at the beginning of november 2015, according to commission figures. it is essential that member states honour the commitments they have previously made. i advocate additional financial support to provide humanitarian assistance along the transit routes and to manage the challenges posed by the reception of unprecedented numbers of refugees in europe's cities and regions.
i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that it is necessary to strengthen the means in view of the current refugee crisis.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to present draft amending budget no 8 to the general budget for 2015, which concerns a revision of the estimate of traditional own resources (customs duties), the budgeting of the 2014 vat and gni balance sheets missing, the 2015 vat and gni balance sheets missing and an update of the estimate for other revenue. the overall revenue impact is a €9.4 billion reduction in member states' contributions to the european financial cake. there is also a reduction of eur 123 474 in both the commitment and payment appropriations of the european data protection supervisor. in this case, where there is a need for budgetary adjustments, i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need for more financial resources to deal with the current refugee crisis and the urgency of allocating the €2.3 million in transfers of funds for this crisis which are overdue. to regret the lack of commitment in conciliation. however, member states are expected to be able to honour the commitments they have made.
in writing. ‒ draft budgetary correction no 8/2015 concerns the revision of the estimate of traditional own resources (customs duties), the budgeting of the missing vat and gni balances for 2014 and the vat and gni balances for 2015, resulting in a decrease of eur 9,4 billion from member states' contributions based on their gni. it also intends to update the forecast for other revenue sources. in addition, this draft amendment provides for a reduction of eur 123 474. we abstained.
in writing. ‒ as i have argued from the outset, the european response to the refugee crisis has - essentially - had two levels of approach: one, immediate, which addresses the humanitarian emergency, and another, which looks at the root problems. in this context, a set of immediate measures was adopted, such as the reinforcement of the operational and human resources of the frontex and easo agencies and the temporary relocation mechanism. on a proposal from parliament, the financial support to member states will be the same for all refugees relocated. as the report points out, the difficulty in making funds available to respond to this crisis, as well as the mortgaging of funds for the coming years should we be faced with another unexpected event, highlights the lack of flexibility of the budget and the need for a larger community budget. the measures adopted and the improvements introduced by parliament are commendable, but here too we see that the union does not yet have all the tools it needs to face the challenges posed by this crisis.
in the light of the conclusions of the european council in brussels on the situation in the middle east, the european council called on the eu to take all necessary steps to ensure that the situation in the middle east is resolved as soon as possible. we are thus strengthening the agencies dealing with migration and refugees, the funds and programmes supporting the response and reception mechanisms for refugees arriving in europe, and the funds and programmes to tackle the root causes of the problem and to combat its causes. we have increased the budget for these objectives from eur 2 billion to eur 4 billion in the 2016 budget. the european union is thus in a position to support the refugees it receives internally and at the same time to act at the root of this problematic phenomenon, i.e. externally, by focusing on prevention and strengthening humanitarian aid and development and cooperation instruments. i voted in favour.
‒ the flexibility instrument is designed to ensure greater flexibility in the multiannual financial framework in order to respond to unforeseen circumstances that justify exceeding the ceilings for budgetary appropriations, with a maximum annual amount of eur 471 million (2011 prices). this proposal replaces the european commission's proposal to mobilise eur 123 966 698 for title 3 (security and citizenship) of the eu budget to support measures to respond to the refugee crisis. it is therefore proposed to mobilise eur 1504 million from this instrument to allow the title 3 ceilings to be exceeded by the same amount, using for this purpose funds not used in the previous years 2014 and 2015. the payments will be made until 2019 (eur 710 million in 2016, eur 652,9 million in 2017, eur 82,7 million in 2018 and eur 58,5 million in 2019). we voted in favour.
in the light of the above, the commission proposes that the council adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the republic of moldova on the participation of the republic of moldova in the union programme for research and technological development. in view of the urgent need to mobilise additional funds to finance the cost of measures to manage the refugee crisis, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ article 11 of regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 provides for the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument up to an annual ceiling of eur 471 million (2011 values) to allow for the financing of specifically identified expenditure which could not be financed within the available ceilings of one or more headings. given the urgent need to address the migration and refugee crisis, it is essential to mobilise additional funding to finance support measures. i agree with the rapporteur's position on the mobilisation of this instrument, that it is crucial that the union budget should be more flexible. this additional appropriation is only possible thanks to the carry-over of unused amounts from the flexibility instrument for the financial years 2014 and 2015. the report contains a number of important points, and i would like to stress that the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets.
‒ the current refugee crisis requires adequate funding for the urgent measures provided for under the european agenda on migration. however, the expenditure ceilings under category 3 (security and citizenship) and category 4 (global europe) do not allow to address the external dimension of the challenges. it is therefore necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument to supplement the financing of the general budget of the union for the financial year 2016, beyond the ceilings, by more than eur 1506 million for category 3 and by more than eur 24 million for category 4. the additional appropriations will be made possible by the carry-over of unused amounts from the flexibility instruments for the financial years 2014 and 2015. the european commission proposes to reallocate commitment appropriations over several years, estimated at eur 734,2 million in 2016, eur 654,2 million in 2017, eur 83,0 million in 2018 and eur 58,6 million in 2019. it should be noted that this reallocation allows the financing of the measures adopted, as provided for in article 11 of the mff regulation. in the light of the foregoing, i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument.
‒ the solidarity instrument is mobilised to make available the amounts of eur 1 506 million in category 3 (security and citizenship) and eur 24 million in category 4 (global europe), to be used to finance measures to manage the refugee crisis. it also adds the proposal for the allocation of payment appropriations of eur 734,2 million in 2016, eur 654,2 million in 2017, eur 83 million in 2018 and eur 58,6 million in 2019.
‒ europe has been experiencing, particularly over the last year, a long and difficult challenge with the continuing wave of migrants/refugees, who are looking to the old continent for a new lease of life. however, this situation has in some cases led to tragic outcomes and for this reason the european union has sought to respond by using the instruments at its disposal. in this respect, the eu has adopted a model for financing urgent measures in the field of migration, which was proposed by the european commission, through the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument. the proposal was to increase the allocation of payment appropriations by a further eur 1506 million (for the heading 'security and citizenship') and eur 24 million for the heading 'global europe', which constitutes additional, basic and indispensable aid in view of the dramatic development of this situation. i therefore believe that using this instrument to finance measures to manage the refugee crisis is a necessary and justifiable decision to activate this extra procedure, and i therefore vote in favour of this report.

‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to ensure rapid, effective and flexible assistance to the population of a member state and to countries negotiating its accession in the event of a major natural disaster. the current proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council is not linked to a specific disaster. it aims to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances in an efficient and timely manner in the event of a disaster in the coming year. this is the direct result of a new provision in the 2014 amending regulation, strongly supported by the european parliament, which aims to accelerate the disbursement of aid to affected countries by paying an advance before the final decision on aid is taken, enhancing the effectiveness of the fund. i support this report because the eusf, in addition to providing assistance to the affected citizens, also contributes to sending a clear political message of solidarity. a rapid response capability, including the payment of an advance, will help the union to achieve these objectives.
‒ the european union solidarity fund is intended to enable the union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters, and the fund's intervention should not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 500 million. however, this proposal is not linked to a specific disaster and aims to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances in order to respond in an efficient and timely manner should a disaster occur in the next year. i voted in favour.
‒ this proposal seeks to include in the 2016 budget the advance payment of eur 50 000 000 in payment and commitment appropriations through the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the compensation for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2015. o-a.this proposal is not linked to any specific disaster; it will only serve to mobilise the eu solidarity fund in advance of the formal and final decision to mobilise and allocate aid, so as to respond in a timely and more effective manner to a potential catastrophic event that occurs during 2016. we have long argued for the need to speed up the procedures associated with the mobilisation of the solidarity fund. the urgency of responding to disasters is not compatible with complex, time-consuming and, above all, avoidable bureaucratic procedures. this report is intended to welcome and to some extent respond to this concern and we have therefore voted in favour.
‒ the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund is not linked to a particular disaster. it aims to allow the entry in the general budget of the european union for 2016 of an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the timely payment of advances in the event of a disaster in the following year. this is a preventive measure in the budget. i voted in favour.
‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the european union to cope with emergencies caused by large-scale natural disasters and to show european solidarity to the affected regions of europe. i support the current proposal for a decision of the european parliament and the council, stressing that it is not linked to a specific disaster. this proposal aims to allocate in the general budget of the union for 2016 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances in an efficient and timely manner in the event of a disaster in the coming year. i believe that this measure is necessary because it will speed up the disbursement of aid to the countries concerned by paying an advance before the final decision on aid is taken, thus enhancing the effectiveness of the eusf. i agree with the rapporteur that the eusf is not just another form of eu financial support, but also a clear political message of solidarity, providing the necessary assistance to the citizens affected.

‒ this process has developed extremely positively, respecting all the political priorities defined by parliament, in particular as regards support for the promotion of employment, the dynamisation of the economy, the valorisation of knowledge and research in the growth strategy and the strengthening of the european union's capacity for internal and external solidarity. the overall eu budget for 2016 is eur 155.004,2 billion in commitment appropriations and eur 143.885,3 million in payment appropriations. these amounts represent an increase in the planned appropriations, compared with the initial budget proposed by the european commission, of more than eur 2.8 billion in commitment appropriations and eur 2.15 billion in payment appropriations. the budget was pushed to the limit, using all available resources and the entire flexibility instrument to meet the challenge of promoting employment and helping refugees, and all budgetary margins for the headings relating to employment, social and territorial cohesion and internal and external solidarity were exhausted.
‒ this report assumes the validation and approval of the joint text agreed in the conciliation committee, which concerns the eu budget for 2016. the agreement, as one would expect, does not change the underlying meaning of the criticisms we have made of the eu budget, which justified our vote against it at second reading and which now justifies that same vote against it. this joint text allows, for example, for a reduction of eur 11 075 000 in title 3 of the multiannual financial framework from the budget lines for the protection, detection and control of plant and animal pests and from the fund for emergency measures relating to animal and plant health. despite the increase in commitments for horizon 2020, the cosme programme and the erasmus+ programme, payment appropriations were cut by eur 460 100 000. cuts were made in the total of budget lines for the promotion of sustainable rural development (eur 87 000 000), in the european regional development fund (erdf) (eur 127 259 355), in the cohesion funds (eur 43 693 564) and in rural development programmes (eur 33 000 000). the european parliament is committed to cutting some 179 jobs by 2019, down from 60 in 2016.

‒ this legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft common budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 was adopted by the conciliation committee in the framework of the budgetary procedure. i am in favour of the adoption of this report, which approves the 2016 budget and the amounts of the eu contributions in commitment appropriations and payment appropriations for the decentralised agencies and the executive agencies. i would also like to highlight as a positive point the approval of the overall package of 89 pilot projects/preparatory actions, totalling eur 64.9 million, as proposed by parliament, as well as the amount of eur 50.8 billion for economic, social and territorial cohesion (1/3 of the total union budget), of which eur 46.6 billion (92%) will be allocated to investment in growth and jobs, one of the eu's political priorities.
in writing. ‒ in a context of strong budgetary constraints on national contributions to the union budget, some concerns should be noted. first of all, we draw attention to the cut of eur 11 million which will directly affect the budget lines devoted to the protection, detection and control of plant and animal pests. this cut, in a context where climate change is leading to the emergence of several epidemic crises, leaves us at least apprehensive. there is talk of a significant increase in programmes for youth employment, but we must realise that the erasmus+ programme represents a minimal portion of the budget and that therefore the 30% increase will unfortunately not have a great impact. we also note that the european parliament is committed to cutting some 179 jobs by 2019, with 60 jobs expected to be eliminated in 2016. finally, a final word on the increase in funding for emigration. it could be positive, if it were not for the deliberate aim of promoting persecutory solutions which will help to perpetuate the problem, rather than resolve it with a genuine policy of solidarity and support for development.
‒ in a context of major budgetary constraints on national contributions to the eu budget, we note here the cut of eur 11 million, which will directly affect the budget lines dedicated to the protection, detection and control of plant and animal pests. there is talk of a significant increase in programmes dedicated to youth employment, but given that the erasmus+ programme represents a minimal portion of the eu budget, a 30% increase in this programme will not have much impact. the european parliament commits to cutting some 179 jobs by 2019 and 60 jobs by 2016, which means more redundancies and a decline in the quality of services. this is not a fairer budget, with higher contributions from the wealthier member states, but a restrictive budget.
‒ dehp has been included in the list of 553 candidate substances in chemical category i that have been shown to have harmful endocrine effects in at least one species using intact animals. it was also one of the first six compounds to be phased out under the reach regulation. however, dehp should be identified as a substance of very high concern as it is a substance with endocrine disrupting properties for which there is scientific evidence that it is likely to cause serious effects on human health. i therefore agree to a new draft rejection of the applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled flexible pvc containing dehp.
‒ phthalates are a family of industrial chemicals used to make pvc plastic flexible and as solvents in cosmetics and other consumer products. studies indicate that these chemicals can affect the liver, kidneys, lungs, hormonal and reproductive systems of mammals and are therefore included in the reach regulation due to their classification as toxic to reproduction. this draft objection concerns the draft commission implementing decision granting an authorisation for uses of bis (2-ethyl-hexyl) phthalate (dehp). this implementing act implies a wider authorisation for the use and formulation of recycled pvc containing dehp. this would lead to a continued presence of hazardous substances in products made from recycled material, thus perpetuating the use of hazardous substances through recycling rather than their replacement. the objection further considers that the draft commission implementing decision, which proposes to authorise the use of these products for a further 7 years, exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006, and requests the commission to withdraw its draft decision by submitting a draft rejection of the applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled flexible pvc containing dehp. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on draft commission implementing decision xxx granting an authorisation for uses of bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (dehp) under regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. dehp should be identified as a substance of very high concern. dehp meets the criteria of article 57 (f) of the reach regulation as a substance with endocrine disrupting properties for which there is scientific evidence that it is likely to cause serious effects on human health. it is extremely important that eu citizens are aware of the dangers of these substances.
in the light of the above, the commission considers that the proposed amendments to the draft directive should be adopted by the council in accordance with the procedure provided for in article 189b of the ec treaty. dehp is known to be part of the list of industrial chemicals used in plastics, cosmetics and other types of consumer products and is considered a toxic substance capable of causing problems for human health. i therefore agree with the adoption of this draft objection concerning the use of this substance, not only because of its toxicity but also because it formally goes beyond the scope of the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006, and i therefore support the rapporteur's position to withdraw the draft commission decision and to submit a new draft rejection of the applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled flexible pvc containing deph.
‒ i voted in favour of the objection raised by the rapporteurs because i do not think it is fair to allocate the use of deph to a small number of recyclers, which will have a negative impact on european recyclers, will harm innovation and competitiveness in europe and will result in the loss of credibility that the recycling sector presents. dehp is known to be a well-known toxic substance. dehp is widely used, and both eu citizens and the environment are exposed. however, there are safe alternatives. the applicants did not fulfil all the conditions for the authorisation to be granted and 90% of the application dossier was classified as confidential by the applicants with the consent of the european chemicals agency. although i understand the interest of industrial secrecy in exceptional situations, i consider it a priority and a determining factor that industry should act in a clear and transparent manner.
‒ dehp is a toxic substance well known, among other things, for its endocrine disrupting effects. unfortunately, dehp is widely used putting citizens at high risk of its toxicity. we have doubts about the evaluation of the european chemicals agency (echa) as 90% of the application process was classified as confidential by the applicants. this context implies that relevant information, such as details on exposure and production volumes, has not been disclosed. we therefore do not understand the commission's implementing decision, which proposes to authorize the use of these products for another seven years, and we propose instead to suspend the application for authorization.

‒ a fair tax system based on the principle of taxation in the member state where profits are generated, the presentation of country-by-country financial information by multinationals, the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, the creation of a common eu definition of tax havens and the protection of whistleblowers are some of the actions proposed by the european parliament. most large multinational companies operating in europe pay effective rates of 5%, sometimes lower, even in countries where the nominal tax rate is 30% and above. the european parliament wants multinational companies in all sectors to disclose in their financial statements, broken down by member state and by third country in which they have establishments, a range of aggregated information, including profit or loss before tax, taxes on profit or loss, the number of employees, assets held and basic information on tax rulings (reporting by country). this information shall be made available to the public, possibly in the form of a central register at eu level.
in writing. ‒ we have always said that the free movement of capital would lead to increased tax evasion and avoidance and would facilitate the transfer of profits, which would harm public coffers. the creation of the single market has proved to be beneficial for multinationals and detrimental to workers and smes. in the name of competitiveness and attracting foreign investment, member states compete with each other. the multinationals, in their relentless pursuit of profit, assisted by big consultancies and with the connivance of policy makers, dictate the rules of the game. luxleaks and the taxe commission's investigations have shown that while governments designed tax decisions and legislation that allowed multinationals to minimise their tax rate and encouraged them to shift profits, in the name of complying with the sgp and complaining about the need for tax revenues, stability and tranquility in financial markets, they dictated so-called austerity policies (increasing taxes on labour, decreasing the viability of direct taxes and progressive cuts in public spending). the report voted on today is wrong in that it does not make public the tax decisions that have been taken in advance, in that it does not quantify the size of these decisions, their impact on the tax revenues of the different member states and in that it is soft on those who are politically responsible for these decisions.
‒ one of the main priorities of tax policy at eu level should be to promote greater cooperation between tax administrations in the control and fight against fraud and harmful tax competition. i voted in favour of the report on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect, which provides, among other measures, for the strengthening of the exchange of information (when a tax agreement is concluded between a country and a company, it is automatically communicated to the european commission and the other countries).
‒ the globalisation and digitalisation of the economy have radically changed the global value chain and the way markets work, with most large companies now having a transnational structure that needs to go beyond national tax rules. i am voting in favour of this report, which calls for new financial rules for transnational trade, greater control of national tax systems and new rules to prevent certain member states from making available lower taxation but which could generate more profits. i also understand that tackling aggressive tax planning by multinational companies has been high on the political agenda of the member states, the eu, the oecd and the g20, and it is essential to adopt the position of principle that a company must pay taxes where it operates and not where it has its tax headquarters, thus avoiding legal but unethical financial shenanigans by companies.
‒ this is a report calling on member states and the eu institutions, which share political responsibility for the current situation, to put an end to harmful tax competition and to cooperate fully in order to eliminate both disparities between tax systems and all measures that create the conditions for large-scale tax avoidance by many multinational companies. for many years, large multinationals have been able to reduce their tax contributions through advantageous negotiations with different member states. as a result, the tax bill for health and education, for example, is borne mostly by smes and the average citizen, who are excluded from these unfair tax offers. these are not isolated cases, but a systematic and organized practice that is at least tolerated by the states. this vicious circle must be broken by strengthening transparency, control and sanctions. one year after the luxleaks scandal, the european parliament approves a report that aims to put an end to an unacceptable and unfair practice towards all honest taxpayers, a timely decision at a time when budget cuts are being called for in social services.
‒ the tax practices in some eu member states are highly controversial and have sparked debate on their nature and legitimacy at european level. that is why a temporary special committee on taxation decisions was set up in the european parliament a few months ago and other measures were adopted to put an end to unfair tax practices and to combat tax evasion in europe. i also think it is important to stress, among other measures mentioned in the report, that taxes on company profits will now be calculated using common methods, in order to avoid repeating past situations and to avoid new controversial cases. i voted in favour of the report because i consider the measures contained in it to be generally positive.
‒ these practices, which are designed to circumvent national tax authorities by draining profits to territories where they are not taxed, such as tax havens, are closely linked to the current process of european integration, which has as one of its main features the free movement of capital and as its main consequence globalisation. if it were not for the disclosure of successive tax scandals at a time when the people of europe are suffering the effects of austerity policies, we would probably still be living with these crimes with total impunity. it was therefore public outrage that was the real engine that propelled this whole well-intentioned plan. the report under discussion today is still incomplete. we have fought against many obstacles in these months. we still have no access to documents of great importance for a proper assessment and ascertainment of the facts. every day new elements emerge involving senior european officials and which have necessitated an extension of the mandate of the taxe committee. as this report is incomplete, we abstained, in the conviction that the work will continue, confronting the european institutions with their responsibilities, but also with their action plan announced last june, which has made little or no progress.
‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on tax rulings and other measures of a similar nature or effect (2015/20667ini), because it includes very significant progress in the crucial fight against aggressive taxation, which undermines the single market, competitive transparency and the financing of the european social model. the report highlights the excellent work carried out by the special committee on tax agreements and other measures similar in nature or effect, and in particular by its co-rapporteurs, elisa ferreira and michael theurer. it also identified that, more than the non-harmonisation of rates, it is the non-harmonisation of criteria for the calculation of taxable items and the absence of exchange of information between member states on these items that create the conditions for intolerable tax avoidance and aggressive competitiveness between member states, resulting in a negative-sum game for the union's interest. i also believe that the work of this committee should be continued, particularly in view of the information which was not available during its term of office.
‒ tax fraud and tax evasion, which are designed to circumvent national tax authorities in order to divert profits to non-taxed territories such as tax havens, are deeply linked to the process of european integration, which has the free movement of capital as one of its main pillars and globalisation as its main consequence. if it were not for the disclosure of successive tax scandals at a time when the people of europe are suffering the effects of austerity policies, we would probably still be living with these crimes with total impunity. as this is an incomplete report, we abstained.
in writing. ‒ it is now clear that the fight against terrorism cannot be based solely on military and police retaliation and increased security measures. it is also imperative to tackle the deep-rooted and complex causes that lead to the radicalisation of european citizens, the overwhelming majority of whom are young people. the european union must therefore pay particular attention to the marginalisation and uprooting of these young people, in order to give them back the horizon of expectations that they feel they are deprived of today. this will require the involvement of society as a whole and of various fields of knowledge and action. it is also an ideological battle against fear and for the values we hold most dear. in parallel, the eu must have more effective legislation to combat online radicalisation and to allow better coordination and exchange of information between our police and intelligence services.
‒ this report, which is a result of the attacks in paris earlier this year, has been given added weight by the recent criminal acts in paris. it deals with one of the most important issues in the fight against terrorism, which requires a comprehensive set of measures, both repressive and preventive. it is prudent not to legislate in response to events, let alone to give in to securities derivatives. to compromise our core values would be to grant a victory to the terrorists. as regards radicalisation, this report provides a good diagnosis and a set of valid solutions which should be pursued, including, among others, preventive measures in prisons and schools or a harmonisation of the penal framework. the emphasis on action at local level, on proximity, and not just on european level and coordinated action between states, is particularly important. i voted in favour of this report despite disagreeing with some of the points which i consider excessive.
the report also calls for the eu to take action to prevent the radicalization and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations such as the islamic state or daesh. more than 5000 european citizens have joined terrorist organisations and other military formations, including the ranks of the self-proclaimed islamic state/daesh, jabhat al-nusra and other formations outside the eu, in particular in the middle east and north africa region. the fight against terrorism remains essentially a matter for member states, but 'european cooperation is essential for the effective and efficient exchange of information between police forces' in an area of free movement of persons. a strategy to combat terrorism, radicalisation and terrorist recruitment in the eu can only be effective if it is developed in parallel with a strategy for social integration and inclusion. i voted in favour.
‒ this report proposes a number of measures, supposedly in the name of combating terrorism, which deliberately avoid the root of the problem, without contributing to its solution, to the increase of the security of citizens or to a coherent strategy of cooperation between states to combat and above all prevent terrorism. on the contrary, this report endorses the curtailment of individual freedoms, insisting on the peregrine thesis of the false dichotomy of freedom and security, and supports a militaristic vision of the alleged fight against terrorism which, instead of weakening, strengthens the logic of hatred, war and terrorism. measures such as the drafting of a directive on indiscriminate passenger identification registers, the strengthening and centralisation of the powers of europol, eurojust, cepol and the various eu information systems, the obligation for member states to make certain information and data available, the criminalisation of internet companies, the weakening of computer encryption systems are aspects of concern in this document and therefore constitute a restriction of fundamental rights, freedoms and guarantees. we voted against it. the response to terrorism must necessarily be to combat its root causes - political, economic and social - and to defend and affirm the values of freedom, peace, democracy, the sovereignty and independence of states and solidarity between peoples.
‒ concerted action at european level is essential to prevent the radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations. but this prevention also requires stronger cooperation, more effective control and the existence of instruments to combat terrorism. the european union needs a passenger identification register (pnr), it needs the regulation of smart borders, which will allow for more effective and rigorous control, it needs to coordinate efforts in the exchange of information between national authorities and it needs to monitor the proliferation of social networks and the recruitment of european citizens that is developed through this channel. it's not enough to say we won't give in to fear. we need to act. we must fight to eliminate extremism that attacks our values, our way of life, our existence. we can't be kidnapped in our own home.
the european union is also committed to the protection of the rights of the child, and to the protection of the rights of the child. the attacks in mali and tunisia show that insecurity is a global problem. it is therefore necessary for the union to act in a coordinated and joint manner with member states and other organisations in preventing the recruitment of european citizens into the ranks of terrorist organisations such as daesh. it is estimated that more than 5000 europeans have already joined, mainly from belgium and france. this document serves as a recommendation for the future european strategy on this subject. the need for the authorities to ensure stricter control over the internet and websites that incite hatred is mentioned, as well as the need to promote a preventive role among the prison population, the role of education and school, the sharing of information between intelligence services, the control of external borders to prevent and anticipate the return of recruited citizens and the proper follow-up of these citizens. i voted in favour because i believe in the need for intercultural dialogue and greater coordination, because terrorism is not a religion, it is not a civilization or a nationality.
‒ the fight against the radicalisation of european citizens who are recruited by terrorist organisations is primarily a matter for the member states. however, the effectiveness of the strategy in this fight lacks a concerted european approach anchored in prevention. in this particular case, prevention of terrorism involves preventing radicalisation in prisons, on the internet and in public spaces in general, through education and social inclusion, which promotes critical thinking and the promotion of non-discrimination in schools and, outside schools, reduces the risk of economic and geographical marginalisation, which are key factors in the radicalisation of alienated and excluded young people. on the other hand, the exchange of information on terrorist radicalisation in europe is also a vital tool for combating the radicalisation of european citizens. however, some member states still stubbornly refuse to cooperate in sensitive areas such as the exchange of information and strategic intelligence. i voted in favour of this report in the hope that the strategy against the radicalisation of citizens will be strengthened.
‒ the fight against the radicalisation of european citizens remains a matter for the member states. however, a concerted european approach is needed to effectively combat the threat posed by radicalised european citizens who can move freely within europe. it is estimated that over 5000 european citizens have left to fight for terrorist organisations in iraq and syria. the aim of this report is to make recommendations for a european strategy to prevent the radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens. some of the measures include preventing violent extremism and terrorist radicalisation in prisons and on the internet, prevention through education and social inclusion, enhancing the exchange of information and best practices at various levels, or dismantling terrorist networks. respect for the fundamental rights and freedoms of european citizens will nevertheless always be a concern of the european parliament.
‒ the unspeakably barbaric acts of terrorism that have taken place in europe in recent months have led to a consequent increase in security measures. but these attacks have not only served to raise the real alarm about the current terrorism, but also to remind us of the importance of continuing to strengthen and speed up measures to prevent acts such as those that recently took place in paris. with the ultimate aim of eradicating the problem of terrorism, the european union has taken important steps in this direction. the report aims to strengthen certain preventive measures both in relation to the radicalisation of european citizens and in relation to the speeding up of european cooperation processes between member states. unfortunately, more than 5000 european citizens have defected to countries such as syria or iraq to join the ranks of terrorist groups. cooperation and exchange of information at european level is therefore essential to prevent the free movement of such citizens, between their countries of origin and the other member states, whose motive is to commit terrorist acts. european concertation on such a sensitive subject is therefore needed more than ever , which is why i am voting in favour of this report.
‒ we live in times of great anxiety and with an almost universal feeling of insecurity. to prevent perpetual loss of freedom, action must be taken now and rules must be understood as temporary. it is with this in mind that i voted in favour of this report. we must act now to achieve normalcy in terms of individual freedoms and clarity of action as quickly as possible. the future of europe depends on encouraging whistleblowing or the use of 'blacklists'. unfortunately, in the present, we will have to deal momentarily with these types of instruments.
‒ the report proposes a set of measures which are purportedly in the name of combating terrorism, but which deliberately circumvent the root of the problem, without contributing to its solution, to the increase of citizens' security or to a coherent strategy of cooperation between states to combat and, above all, prevent terrorism. on the contrary, this report supports the eu's deliberate strategy of curtailing democratic freedom and individual freedoms, insisting on the pilgrim thesis of the false freedom-security dichotomy and supporting a militaristic vision of the alleged fight against terrorism which, instead of weakening, strengthens the logic of hatred and war. horrible crimes such as those committed in paris, or those which have been perpetrated for years in various places around the world, call for a policy of peace in international relations and respect for international law, which puts an end to interference and aggression against sovereign states, particularly in the middle east region, which have led to the resurgence of terrorist groups.
