in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers die as a result of work-related accidents, and the number of fatal occupational diseases is over 150 000 per year. good working conditions that safeguard good physical and mental health are a fundamental right of workers and, despite considerable progress in the field of health and safety at work over the years, important risks to the health and safety of workers persist. i believe it is vital to develop specific european strategies covering all forms of employment, and national strategies for health and safety at work should follow up on the progress made in these areas in other member states. on the other hand, we must continue to improve the implementation of these rules and be demanding on the compliance of the labour authorities with the rules, and the work of the national labour inspectorates is essential. particular attention should be paid to new forms of employment as well as to new technologies which pose new challenges to health and safety at work.
in writing. ‒ every year more than 4,000 workers die as a result of work-related accidents and the number of fatal occupational diseases is over 150,000 per year. the ageing workforce in many member states and demographic changes in europe point to the need to promote a safe and healthy working environment for all workers throughout the entire life cycle. in the eu strategic framework for 2014-2020 on health and safety at work, the commission identifies several important challenges facing european employers and workers in the field of health and safety at work. effective management of health and safety at work remains a challenge for micro and small enterprises. action is therefore essential to promote compliance and effective management of health and safety at work by these companies. i voted in favour.
‒ the report stresses the strategic importance of the development of occupational safety and health (osh) policies for the period 2014-2020. despite some more negative aspects, which we do not follow, such as the association of this strategic framework with the neoliberal eu 2020 strategy, the report contains other undoubtedly positive and important aspects. the definition of osh policies is advocated and encouraged, linking them to undeclared work and false self-employment, gender equality and the fight against harassment, the need for a 'balanced' working time, or access to public health services to issues of the highest relevance. in addition to promoting these measures, there is the promotion of appropriate training and worker representation in the formulation and monitoring of osh policies. these are reasons for our vote in favour.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategic framework for health and safety at work 2014-2020. the number of workers who die each year as a result of accidents at work and the number of occupational diseases with fatal outcome is extremely worrying. the economic and social costs of accidents at work and occupational diseases require immediate action at eu level.
‒ health and safety at work are essential for society, and are seen as beneficial investments in the productivity and competitiveness of companies, as well as improving the sustainability of social security systems and enabling people to enjoy good health until retirement age. i agree that the prevention of occupational hazards, the promotion of health and safety and the protection of workers at work are essential factors for improving working conditions and, consequently, for protecting the health of workers, which in turn benefits workers and society in general socially and economically. the european union, in accordance with article 153 tfeu, shall support and complement the action of the member states in improving the working environment in order to protect the health and safety of workers. i believe that national strategies for health and safety at work, which should be in line with eu guidelines, are fundamental and contribute to progress in this area in the member states. unfortunately, the economic crisis has caused some instability in employment and reduced company revenues, and this cannot put the importance of health and safety on the back burner.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4,000 workers die as a result of work-related accidents and the number of fatal occupational diseases is over 150,000 per year. despite all the progress made, much remains to be done. having identified several important challenges facing european employers and workers in the field of occupational health and safety, it is now time to move forward with legislative proposals aimed at raising the level of occupational health and safety across the eu. in addition to a substantial set of proposed measures, this report does not forget the increase in precarious work (and its impact on workers' mental health) and the new forms of employment linked to new technologies, which have posed new challenges to occupational health and safety that need to be addressed.
‒ issues of health and safety at work are of great concern and require coordinated work by the european institutions. some 4,000 workers die each year in work-related accidents and 150,000 suffer from work-related diseases. precarious work, new technologies and the ageing of european workers have been some of the factors driving change in our workforce. these are challenges that lack urgent and effective solutions to halt the scourge. to this end, preventive measures should be strengthened and supervision tightened. examples such as productivity, labour participation and the sustainability of the social security system itself are the positive results of a set of measures and policies in health and safety at work that are re-thought and implemented. i therefore feel it is important to give my full support to this own-initiative report on the eu strategic framework for occupational health and safety 2014-2020, so that positive and more effective measures are put in place for a safer and more predictable future for europe's workplace.
‒ we note the importance of the definition of occupational safety and health (osh) policies as a strategic eu definition for the period 2014-2020. we do not follow the report in its federalist perspective, with references to the union's capacity to support and complement the action of the states, or in the relation of this strategy to the europe 2020 objectives or the need to implement european-wide legislation and strategic guidelines, in particular the sst strategic framework. despite these issues, the report refers to and encourages the development of osh policies, linking it to undeclared work and false self-employment, gender equality and the fight against harassment, the need for 'balanced' working hours, or access to public health services. in addition to promoting these measures, there is the promotion of appropriate training and worker representation in the formulation and monitoring of osh policies.

the european union is committed to the promotion of gender equality in all its policies and activities. the scale of the problem was highlighted in a survey carried out by the european agency for fundamental rights in 2014, which surveyed 42 000 women in 28 member states. the results of the survey are revealing: some 13 million women were victims of physical violence in the previous 12 months, and 3.7 million were victims of sexual violence. the urgency of this matter is therefore beyond doubt. violence against women constitutes an attack on one of the most basic human rights, it is an attack on fundamental rights, on individual freedom. a european union which believes in the full development of the personality of its citizens cannot but intervene so that this kind of attitude may in time become a thing of the past.
mr president, since we have been talking here mainly about the valletta summit, i think it is worthwhile to focus some attention on the g20 group and, in particular, on the approach taken by the g20 meeting in antalya to the question of terrorism, since it took place immediately after the paris attacks of 13 november. what i wanted to make clear here is that the fight against terrorism by european countries and, in particular, by the european union must be a fight without a truce. we must give a clear response on the external front, with military action and military cooperation with france, the united states, the coalition countries and the islamic state, and we must also take some measures, such as the approval of the pnr at the internal level, and others, such as strengthening the external borders of schengen in the context of the european union. i also think it is very important that we have here a great opportunity to strengthen european cooperation and to strengthen the european union's presence in security and defence matters. in particular, i believe it is essential that we move from the frontex and other programmes towards the creation of a genuine european border guard, which can protect the external borders of schengen and the external borders of the european union, with a membership of all european countries. it is essential to take this step because without it, we will not have effective control, we will not have effective defence of our security and we will be vulnerable, we will be exposed to terrorist attacks. there are no economic, social or sociological explanations for terrorism. terrorism must be fought without any fail on our part.

our aid can help unleash such potential. the commission is doing its share, and we will keep pushing for national governments to follow up on their commitments. i would encourage you all to pass on this message that you have voiced here today, also back home. secondly, many of you rightly highlighted that saving lives must remain our focus in implementing valletta. i completely agree. protection is and remains a key element of our partnership with africa, both in terms of supporting the huge effort of african partners in offering humanitarian relief to refugees and the internally displaced in africa, and in terms of a wider and more consistent effort from the eu in terms of resettlement, in close cooperation with unhcr. yes, this is a crucial part of our effort to save lives and avoid hazardous journeys. another key component of our discussion in valletta has indeed been legal mobility: opening legal, regulated ways and facilitating mobility for bona fide travellers, starting from students, researchers, academics and business operators. it is part of our commitments in the action plan and we will make it happen. this is very important, as you know. as federica mogherini said in her introduction, helping africa’s growth and development is in our own interests. if we disinvested from the continent’s future, we would be hurting our own future. it would be against our values and our interests. this is not an idealistic approach, it is a very pragmatic approach. we need a strong cooperation with africa, which addresses europe’s interests and african interests at once. there is no ‘horse-trading’; we are redrawing our partnership on new bases. this includes how we deal with migration, but also our cooperation on peace and security, on development and on counter-terrorism. this leads me another point, raised by mr verhofstadt. yes, a new partnership with africa is not just about managing mobility, but also tackling the root causes of forced displacement. and yes, investment, industrialisation, opportunities for private actors to engage in a partnership for development in african remains very important. next, the security aspect of our cooperation. as many of you said, recent events only confirm that we cannot underestimate the threats we are facing. but let us also be clear on something: of course we must improve the checks on our external borders – it is obvious. but, as the attacks in paris demonstrate, the threat to our own security mostly originates within our own borders. on the external side, the call for more cooperation on security comes directly from our african partners. cooperating with africa on security is consistent with our interests: think of the work we can do to control their borders, to fight international criminal networks and to investigate terrorist suspects. finally, let me thank you once again for this debate and let me assure you that we count on the cooperation of this parliament and on its support in shaping not only migration but at the same time a new partnership with africa.

madam president, we are going to vote on three urgent motions for resolutions and we are going to vote on them, in particular, by roll-call votes which are recorded. we are being denied the right to make written statements, to explain why we voted in a certain way, and this is unacceptable, so we ask that the rules be changed immediately so that a member can normally give his explanation of vote on these matters.
‒ the 10th ministerial conference of the world trade organisation will be held in kenya in december. since its creation in 1995, the world trade organisation (wto) has played a significant role in creating a rules-based international trading system. since 2001, wto members have engaged in a broad round of multilateral trade negotiations, the doha round, which seeks to further liberalise trade, focusing on development, strengthening the capacity of developing countries to benefit from international trade, and helping them to fight poverty. in this respect, i welcome the trade facilitation agreement ratified on 5 october by the eu and i hope that this new ministerial conference will reach a political agreement that will advance the doha development agenda, while ensuring the principle of special and differential treatment. i agree with the need to accompany economic growth and sustainable development with appropriate accompanying macroeconomic and microeconomic policies, including budgetary transparency, tax equity, administrative simplification, education, training, social policies and institutional reforms.
‒ the doha round was launched in 2001 with the aim of creating new trade opportunities, strengthening multilateral trade rules and addressing current imbalances in the trading system, putting the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular least developed countries, at the centre of the negotiations. open and fair multilateral trade is more restricted by various non-tariff barriers than by customs duties, which are being substantially phased out as globalisation advances. i therefore support the enduring value of multilateralism and an agenda for trade based on free and fair trade for the benefit of all and whose process is focused on development. i voted in favour.
‒ this resolution insists on the neoliberal vision of the doha development agenda (ddd) launched in 2001. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's trade policy is not distorted. the 10th wto ministerial conference (cm10) will be held in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015 in nairobi. it will be the first wto ministerial conference ever held in an african country. it will show the further progress towards liberalization and deregulation of world trade. the crisis of the profitability of capital and its unprecedented degree of centralization and concentration of wealth leads it to seek new forms of exploitation, creating agreements of neo-colonial character, in which developed countries dictate what developing countries should or should not do in areas such as fiscal and tax policies, administrative organization, education and training, institutional reforms and social policies, while exploiting their natural resources with irreversible consequences for the environment, and attacking progress and social achievements such as public services and the right to fair employment. we therefore reaffirm the urgent need to suspend the doha round. we obviously voted against it.
‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the current state of the doha development agenda with a view to the 10th wto ministerial conference. in view of the fact that the doha round aims to create new trade opportunities, strengthen multilateral trade rules and address current imbalances in the trading system, and given the proximity of the 10th wto ministerial conference to be held in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015, this motion for a resolution makes perfect sense. this motion for a resolution reinforces and defends an agenda based on free and fair trade for the benefit of those whose process is focused on development and also the need for structural reform of the wto.
‒ i advocate a multilateral, regulated and stable strategy for trade, recognising that bilateral, regional and plurilateral agreements also promote trade openness and economic development and support the multilateral system, provided they are compatible with world trade organisation rules. it is essential to advocate a trade agenda based on free and fair trade for the benefit of all and with a development-centred process. trade liberalisation is an essential tool for ensuring sustainable economic growth and development, which should be accompanied by macro- and microeconomic measures such as fiscal transparency, fiscal policies, tax equity, administrative simplification, education and training, institutional reforms and social policies. i recommend that the european union should continue to play a leading role with a view to achieving progress in the ongoing wto negotiations with a view to the full conclusion of the doha development round in the near term, as well as ensuring the participation of the least developed countries in world trade.
‒ the doha round negotiations, launched in 2001, aim to improve multilateral trade through rules agreed by consensus between the counterparts. these trade policies must be developed along two lines: the reduction of protectionist trade barriers which impede free trade, on the one hand, and the establishment of rules governing the maintenance of trade barriers, on the other. article 207 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) establishes the common commercial policy as an exclusive competence of the european union. accordingly, the european commission (ec) has been exercising its mandate by putting the needs and interests of developing countries at the centre of the negotiations. in this particular case, the principle of special and differential treatment must be an integral part of the negotiations, ensuring the sustainable economic growth and development of the least developed countries, the main victims of the imbalances in the trading system. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the doha development round, which is a report on the implementation of the doha development round.
‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which comes just before the 10th wto ministerial conference in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015. i fully support the need for greater liberalisation of world trade, based on a multilateral system based on fairer and more equitable rules, which will make it possible to contribute to trade opportunities that promote the development and sustainable and sustained growth of the least developed countries, bearing in mind the principle of special and differential treatment, which must underlie this type of negotiation. this was the aim of the 2001 doha round, which should now be revised in order to achieve, in a more realistic way, the concrete and more balanced results sought for the world economy in trade terms. i am also in favour of structural reform of the wto to better ensure an open, fair and non-discriminatory trading system that takes account of the heterogeneous roles and interests of economic operators, smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups. it is therefore important that all wto members study viable solutions to conclude the doha round negotiations and ratify the trade facilitation agreement swiftly, which will increase transparency and legal certainty, reduce administrative costs and reduce the duration of customs formalities.
‒ the doha round was launched in 2001 with the aim of creating new trade opportunities, strengthening multilateral trade rules and addressing current imbalances in the trading system, putting the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular least developed countries (ldcs), at the centre of the negotiations. this objective is based on the conviction that a multilateral system based on fairer and more equitable rules can contribute to fair and free trade, to the economic development of all continents and to poverty reduction. it is based on the fundamental premises of free trade and the presentation of supposedly neutral rules, which do not take into account the profound inequalities in the development of countries. in this sense, this model is the antithesis of the model we propose, based on relations of complementarity and respect for national sovereignty and their right to produce and to guarantee minimum levels of self-sufficiency.

in writing. the first major flaw in this resolution is the lack of recognition of the great contradiction between the increasingly liberal, market-oriented common agricultural policy, which pushes farmers towards intensive production models where profit is overridden by animal welfare and health, and all the scientific evidence that warns us of the need to defend ecological balances, animal welfare, biodiversity and public health. it could and should have gone further, criticizing and rejecting the productivism of the present cap and advocating a different agricultural policy. we believe that there is a need for a legal framework that reflects the concerns of the general public with regard to safeguarding animal welfare, but we have not followed all the amendments that have been tabled. before condemning or prohibiting more or less traditional practices, we should advocate the need to ensure that staff carry out inspections, and other specialised staff are on the ground supporting producers, such as public veterinarians and other animal health professionals. another of the failures is that there is not a proper focus on the reasons for the failure of the previous animal welfare strategy. despite its shortcomings and limitations, we recognize the positive aspects of this resolution.

‒ the attacks on animal welfare are a consequence of an agriculture increasingly subject to the logic of profit in an increasingly competitive global market. the absurd levels of production intensity we have in the european union, whether in the case of piglets or intensive pig, poultry or rabbit production, are not the result of any whim on the part of our farmers. this is a contingency which obliges them to maximise animal productivity, otherwise they simply cannot guarantee the profitability of their farms. it is this contradiction that is unresolved. a contradiction between an increasingly liberal, market-oriented cap that pushes farmers towards productivist models where profit is put above animal welfare, and all the scientific evidence that warns us every day of the need to stop this madness. stop in the name of animal welfare, biodiversity and public health. it is therefore important to extend our agricultural equation to other social and environmental variables in the name of our planet's survival.

madam president, commissioner vella, one of the objectives of implementing and strengthening the circular economy is to reduce the amount of waste that flows into the seas. the impact of plastic waste at sea is extremely serious, holistic and perennial and is identified by several international bodies and is one of the priorities of the g7. plastics and especially microplastics are a problem for the physical, chemical and molecular contamination of marine organisms' food chains. plastics contain persistent organic pollutants that contaminate the animals that ingest them and cause hormonal problems that lead to changes in growth and reproduction rates. acting as hormone disruptors, they have been responsible for reproductive failures in marine mammals, fish and birds to name just three examples. one of the solutions to minimize this problem is to provide the tools associated with the circular economy, thus ensuring at least not the solution but the urgent mitigation of the problem. the circular economy is inevitable, it's not enough, but it can be a step forward.

in writing. ‒ directive 2003/48/ec is limited to the taxation of savings income in the form of interest on loans, excluding matters relating to the taxation of pensions and insurance benefits. the agreement signed this year on the automatic exchange of financial account information, which aims to improve international tax cooperation, is a step in the right direction in the ongoing efforts to fight tax fraud and tax evasion. however, the report falls short of what is needed and is flawed in several respects, such as: (a) the lack of efforts to achieve absolute transparency and full disclosure of information between the parties and the presence of legal constraints in the agreement; (b) the existence of an exemption from disclosure of information, which is an overly broad and ambiguous conditionality; (c) conditions for the exchange of information based on prior approval by the competent authorities. moreover, as was the case with the eu-switzerland agreement, the european parliament was not consulted until after the agreement had been ratified, and it was practically impossible to introduce any improvements. that is why we abstained.

in writing. ‒ the european union and the principality of liechtenstein signed an agreement on 28 october 2015 on the automatic exchange of financial account information with the aim of improving tax cooperation and the enforcement of international tax obligations. this agreement provides that the european union and the principality of liechtenstein shall exchange automatically information on the financial accounts of residents of the other party as from 2017. the purpose of this agreement is to prevent a taxpayer from attempting to conceal the capital corresponding to income or assets in respect of which taxes have not been paid. in advocating greater cooperation, transparency and the sharing of tax information with the aim of reducing fraud and evasion, this report and the approval of the agreement deserve my vote in favour.
‒ this draft legislative resolution of the european parliament approves the conclusion of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of liechtenstein, adapting it to the enhanced measures equivalent to the eu directive, updated in march 2014. the amendments to the protocol provide that, in the context of exchanges of information on the financial accounts of residents of the other party, the exchange of information is to be facilitated not only on income such as interest and dividends but also on account balances and the proceeds of the sale of financial assets. the agreement allows for the prevention of situations where a taxpayer tries to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which no tax has been paid, and the prevention of tax evasion limits the negative consequences for economic development and therefore the negative impact on the achievement of solidarity and prosperity as laid down in the letter of the treaties. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in october 2015, the eu and liechtenstein agreed to automatically exchange financial account information to improve tax cooperation and enable compliance with international tax obligations. the main objective of this agreement is to combat tax fraud and evasion, also updating the 2004 agreement which allowed this country to apply measures similar to those provided for in the eu directive on taxation of savings income. one of the improvements implemented concerns the possibility of automatic exchange of information on the financial accounts of residents of the other party from 2017, thus helping to prevent potential situations of taxpayers concealing financial capital corresponding to income or assets on which taxes have not been paid. in addition, it is also envisaged that the global standards (established in 2014 by the oecd) regarding the requirement for automatic exchange of information on financial accounts will be followed. these reinforcement measures to the equivalents of the eu directive updated in march 2014 will make for a fairer and more transparent system, and i therefore supported this report by voting in favour.
‒ the agreement can represent an important step forward in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and updates the 2004 agreement which ensured that the principality of liechtenstein would apply measures equivalent to those provided for in the eu directive on taxation of savings income. the eu and the principality of liechtenstein will thus exchange automatically information on the financial accounts of residents of the other party as from 2017. the aim is to prevent situations where a taxpayer attempts to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets for which no tax has been paid. unfortunately, history shows that it is not for lack of agreements or regulations that tax fraud and evasion continue to exist. it is important to monitor compliance with this agreement, avoiding the usual traps of these agreements which often serve only to mislead public opinion.

in writing. this report follows the special report of the european ombudsman following the inquiry into the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex). in the face of what has become a flagrant failure, it is intended to set up a system for reporting incidents and drawing up codes of conduct, as well as the establishment of a consultative forum on fundamental rights and a fundamental rights officer. it also establishes a mechanism for complaints (which did not exist) concerning breaches of fundamental rights, including the rights of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. the first point to be made is the unequivocal recognition of the human rights violations by frontex. this agency is increasingly becoming a supranational police force which is undermining the territorial sovereignty of the member states and acts as a repressive force against defenceless citizens, in particular refugees and asylum seekers from north africa and the middle east, who arrive in europe every day and suffer its repulsive xenophobic effects. complaints come and go. the mechanism now proposed does not meet, by any means, the requirements.
in writing. ‒ firstly, i welcome the special report by the european ombudsman following the own-initiative inquiry into frontex. the european ombudsman recommended to frontex that a mechanism should be established to deal with complaints about violations of fundamental rights in all joint operations with the frontex chancellor. the mechanism should receive complaints from persons who claim to have been personally affected or who wish to complain for reasons of public interest. this function could be assigned to the fundamental rights officer, who would be provided with the resources necessary for the exercise of this function. the eu frontex regulation requires the agency to ensure full respect for fundamental rights and the rights of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers, and frontex should therefore set up an appropriate complaints mechanism. i share the rapporteur's view that the mechanism for dealing with individual complaints must be efficient and transparent. i cast my vote in favour.
‒ the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union should ensure full respect for the fundamental rights and the rights of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. it should be noted that frontex's mission is to ensure the effective implementation of the common rules on the control and surveillance of the external borders as regards fundamental rights and that these actions therefore have human rights implications. i agree with the recommendation of the european ombudsman that frontex should deal with each individual complaint concerning violations of fundamental rights in the course of its operations and should provide appropriate administrative support to this end. this individual complaint mechanism will provide individuals with an opportunity to exercise their right to an effective remedy in the event of a breach of fundamental rights, and will have as a corollary the increase of transparency and respect for fundamental rights. the implementation of this right should be the subject of an information campaign, disseminated in the official languages of the eu and in languages that asylum seekers and migrants understand or are reasonably supposed to understand.
‒ following the own-initiative inquiry into the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the union (frontex), the european ombudsman published a special report which insisted on the implementation of an individual complaint mechanism. the ombudsman advocates the creation of an incident reporting system and the development of codes of conduct, as well as the establishment of a consultative forum on fundamental rights and a fundamental rights officer. these mechanisms are all the more relevant in the context of frontex's operational cooperation with the competent authorities of the partner countries, which is carried out through operational agreements which are not legally binding and do not fall within the scope of international law. considering that frontex, like any eu body or agency, must observe the charter of fundamental rights in the exercise of its activities, and that this obligation is enshrined in the tfeu, and considering further that the implementation of the mechanism proposed by the ombudsman is the indispensable guarantee of frontex's compliance with fundamental rights obligations, i voted in favour of the report.

‒ the concept of urban mobility is highly relevant and topical today. soon, 80% of europe's citizens will live in cities, which is a paradigm shift in terms of accessibility and mobility for europe's citizens, and places urban centres in front of social, quality of life and sustainable development challenges. i believe that it is urgent to establish sustainable urban mobility plans that include all citizens, in particular people with reduced mobility, and that involve reducing the dependency on cars in cities, which is responsible for serious health, ecological and congestion problems, and redesigning the way we move around in cities (both in transporting people and goods). i share the concerns raised in the delli report and the suggestions for solutions put forward by the committee on transport and tourism.
in writing. ‒ soon, 80% of europe's citizens will live in cities. mobility should therefore promote access for all, including persons with reduced mobility, to school, work, culture, recreation and healthcare. the dependence on the car and its corollary, road congestion, whose cost to all european cities is estimated at €80 billion, makes city dwellers prisoners of a mobility supported rather than chosen. while certain sectors, such as agriculture and industry, have reduced their greenhouse gas emissions, the transport sector shows an increase of 30% since 1990. while the major cities of the european union are living at the peak of pollution, some 400 000 premature deaths are caused annually by particulate matter emitted by the european car fleet. it is also recorded that 38% of road deaths occur in urban areas. to this end, the european union should set ambitious targets so that member states and regional and local authorities can jointly implement this new model of sustainable urban mobility, giving priority to electric mobility plans, non-polluting modes of transport: electric, cable cars, bicycles and car sharing.
in writing. the report stresses the importance of developing sustainable urban mobility policies that do not inhibit the development of cities, regions and countries, while ensuring the reduction of the environmental impacts of the transport sector, better urban planning, improved health indicators and social inclusion. relevant goals. the impact of transport on societies (especially urban ones, which by 2050 will comprise 85% of the eu population) is significant. the organisation of urban mobility gives priority to the car 50% of citizens in the eu use their own car on a daily basis, while only 16% use public transport and 12% use the bicycle. the transport sector is thus the only one that has not reduced its greenhouse gas emissions. the report emphasises the promotion of quality and affordable public transport (including as a means of boosting urban economies and helping to combat poverty and social exclusion), the need to promote mobility plans, the use of alternative fuels, the improvement of pollution situations and their impact on human health (air pollutant emissions and noise pollution) and the reduction of accidents. a 'bottom-up' approach is advocated, as opposed to the imposition of guidelines by the european institutions. despite some shortcomings, we voted in favour.

madam president, technical measures and multiannual plans are useful tools with potential in fisheries management. the multiannual plans have the advantage in general terms of allowing some stability and predictability to a sector that is hardly affected by major instability, but these plans must be part of a local management system that involves the sector and in which the member states have a leading role. the institutional framework in force since the lisbon treaty, which enshrines the management of living marine resources as an exclusive competence of the european union, imposes a centralised management of fisheries that is far removed from reality, which does not take into account the enormous diversity that characterises the sector at the level of resources, fleets, fishing gear and fisheries, making local management unfeasible. it is this proximity management that best meets the objectives of a fisheries policy: to ensure the public supply of fish, to ensure a decent income for fishermen, to promote the development of coastal communities and to do all this while ensuring good conservation of resources.

blue-card answer.– mr etheridge, i agree with your identification of choices, but i believe my choices are different from yours, because i really think that the solution for us europeans is to move forward quickly in completing and rebalancing the economic and monetary union. i really believe there is a future for all members of the euro area.
mr president, this debate is extremely important. the three presidents who co-signed the five presidents’ report are here and we are, for the first time, discussing in plenary the stance and functioning of the eurozone. so this moment is very welcome indeed. the truth is that, more than seven years after the 2008 crisis, in spite of the welcome massive quantitative easing by the european central bank and also in spite of a more intelligent application of the governance rules by the commission, the eurozone economy is stagnant. it is basically flat with strong internal divergences and alarming levels of poverty and unemployment. the reality confirms what we have repeatedly been saying here and what president draghi said in 2014, which is that in a recessive economic environment, monetary union alone is not enough to boost the economy. in a zero lower bound interest rate and stagnant economy, investment projects are hardly viable, thus limiting the potential to increase competitiveness and create new jobs, while non-performing loans jeopardise the viability of banks and other lenders. so the commission and council urgently need to acknowledge that the policies which have been imposed until now need urgent change. in 2015, gdp per head and the level of productive investment in the euro area remain below the levels in 2007. the future of the eu – and in particular the future of the eurozone and its acceptance by its citizens – depends on this policy change. change means that the eurozone cannot, in 2016, pursue a neutral aggregate fiscal stance as, once again, is being proposed by the commission and the council. it is suicidal to ignore the facts and to persist in this neutral stance. the aggregate fiscal stance should instead be expansionist, clearly countercyclical, protect productive investment and limit internal divergent trends. but what instruments do we have? until now, only pre-crisis external deficit countries have adjusted, whereas external surplus countries continue to increase their current account surpluses. the surplus largely reflects excess domestic savings over investment, which leaves the eurozone without a stimulus. this asymmetric adjustment, incapable of generating internal investment or conception, is further reducing the viability of the common currency. apart from interpreting the existing rules in a wiser way, we need immediately to prepare for the next phase of the 2015 five presidents’ report, which is already a diluted version of the 2012 van rompuy report. but we need to prepare immediately for the establishment of conditions to create a fiscal capacity for the eurozone. without a reinforced budget, monetary union cannot function. european institutions also need to respect and comply with all the promises made, on the banking union in particular, by urgently providing an indispensable permanent credible backstop to the single resolution mechanism, by accelerating the common guarantee of deposits, and by allowing the esm to directly recapitalise banks. i recall that this element is included in the first phase of the five presidents’ report. i do not think that this can be a trade—off for anything else. it is just finishing what has been promised. this is essential for mutual trust and the belief of citizens.
we are talking about a further step in the deepening of the process of economic governance, seeking to respond to the proven failure of the european semester. the stability pact has been joined by the six pack, the two pack and the euro+ pact. we are now discussing more rules and more procedures with this proposal from the five presidents, all of whom are seeking to respond to a social and economic crisis and to tighten up the budgetary policy of the national states even further. the failure to comply with the recommendations by country is mentioned, but its timeliness or applicability is not disputed. instead, it is preferable to impose more expert bodies which, under the guise of an allegedly infallible scientificity, will only cause more confusion and deepen the anti-democratic character of economic governance. but as political as the report is, it still fails to resolve this irreconcilable contradiction of having a system in which countries that need to invest cannot and those that can do so do not because they lack the capacity to consume. the persistence of external imbalances is now being noted. countries accumulate surpluses at the expense of others. the report now proposes that the process of economic governance should encourage governments with surpluses to spend more in the interests of all, that is, it seeks to resolve, in an administrative way, a balance that was ensured through the money market that existed before the euro. it's a pity.

‒ this agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on the modalities of its participation in the european asylum support office (easa) is essentially intended to allow switzerland to participate in the work of the easa and to receive support from it, as well as the possibility of having an observer on the agency's management board. the situation of refugees who have moved to europe in recent months raises serious humanitarian concerns. the large number of refugees arriving requires the creation of conditions for assistance, which are far from guaranteed. the european union has not been able to cope with the problem, nor with the responsibility it has and is at the origin of this scourge. the establishment of this agreement may be a positive step, but it is only a drop in a huge ocean of problems that urgently need to be addressed in order to ensure effective protection and reception for the thousands of refugees - children and adults - who arrive every day fleeing war and persecution in their countries of origin.

‒ to cross the external border of the european union, third-country nationals need to be in possession of a visa, in this case for a short stay. however, many countries are already exempt from this obligation, as they meet a set of criteria approved in 2001 and 2014 by the european parliament and the council, including respect for fundamental rights, security of the visa system or risk of illegal immigration. the visa waiver goes far beyond benefits for european and third country tourists. it can promote rapprochement and dialogue between cultures, economic growth and has also helped to consolidate democratic regimes. so it is with pleasure that i see dominica on the list of countries exempt from visa requirements for short stays.
‒ this recommendation concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the community of dominica on the short-stay visa waiver. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and dominican nationals to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (common, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders), regardless of the purpose of stay, except for the pursuit of a paid activity. the agreement facilitates travel, which is in itself a positive. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the commonwealth of dominica on the short-stay visa waiver. i share the rapporteur's view that this agreement is the result of the deepening of relations between the european union and the dominican community, and is an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations, but also of deepening political debate and dialogue on a number of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms.
‒ the european commission has established an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for citizens of the european union and dominican community nationals travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period, which requires the approval of the european parliament. visa facilitation brings people closer together and strengthens economic, cultural and political relations between the european union and the dominican community, reinforcing the political importance of the cotonou agreement, a partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific states and the european union and its member states. several categories of persons, irrespective of the purpose of their visit, are covered by this visa facilitation agreement, except in the case of gainful employment. i am voting in favour of this agreement because i consider it essential to establish relations between the european union and other communities which will bring benefits to both sides in the economic, political and social fields and will give a boost to bilateral cooperation dialogues.
in writing. ‒ as part of the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, the community of dominica was transferred to annex ii, which establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the external borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation, the council authorised the commission on 9 october 2014 to open negotiations for the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the union and the community of dominica. the negotiations were concluded on 9 december 2014 and the agreement was signed on 28 may 2015. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and dominican nationals to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. i voted in favour of the agreement because i consider it to be an important agreement to strengthen economic and cultural relations and to intensify political dialogue between the european union and the dominican community.
‒ this agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations between the eu and the dominican community, and is of high political importance, and is also an additional means to strengthen economic and cultural relations, as well as to intensify political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms.
‒ i have decided to support the proposal for a recommendation on the conclusion of an agreement between the eu and dominica on the short-stay visa waiver. as in the other visa waivers voted on today, the strengthening of economic and cultural relations and the enormous political importance of the cotonou agreement were essential to this strengthening of bilateral cooperation and to the facilitation and conclusion of this agreement. dominica has an economy predominantly focused on the agricultural sector. however, it has made numerous efforts to boost growth in the tourism sector and geothermal energy production. the agreement will not only boost tourism but also strengthen trade and investment links by simplifying travel conditions, thereby promoting links between businesses and entrepreneurs, both in terms of new investment and consumer-supplier relations. as dominica is a democratically stable country with significant progress in the defence of human rights, it is essential to continue to ensure and expand this path of democratic dialogue. as the eu is the main promoter of fundamental rights in the dominican republic, this agreement is expected to be a plus for both co-signatories, which is why i supported the recommendation to conclude this agreement.

‒ the european commission has established an agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for citizens of the european union and the democratic republic of timor-leste when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period, which requires the approval of the european parliament. visa facilitation brings people closer together and strengthens economic, cultural and political relations between the european union and the democratic republic of timor-leste, reinforcing the political importance of the cotonou agreement, a partnership agreement between the african, caribbean and pacific states and the european union and its member states, which timor-leste acceded to shortly after its independence. several categories of persons, irrespective of the purpose of their visit, are covered by this visa facilitation agreement, except in the case of gainful employment. i am voting in favour of this agreement because i consider it essential to establish relations between the european union and other communities which will bring benefits to both sides in the economic, political and social fields and will give a boost to bilateral cooperation dialogues.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, the democratic republic of timor was transferred to annex ii, which establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the external borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation, the council authorised the commission on 9 october 2014 to open negotiations for the conclusion of a bilateral agreement between the union and the democratic republic of timor. the negotiations were concluded on 15 december 2014 and the agreement was signed on 26 may 2015. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the european union and the democratic republic of timor to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. i voted in favour of the agreement because i consider it to be an important agreement to strengthen economic and cultural relations and to intensify political dialogue between the european union and the democratic republic of timor.
‒ this agreement is the culmination of the deepening of relations between the eu and timor, and is of high political importance, as well as being an additional means to strengthen economic and cultural relations and to intensify political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms.

in writing. ‒ under decision 2002/187/jha, eurojust may conclude cooperation agreements or arrangements with the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies established by or on the basis of the treaties. such cooperation agreements or arrangements may in particular concern the exchange of information, including personal data, and the secondment of liaison officers to eurojust. eurojust has negotiated with the office for harmonization in the internal market the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market and eurojust. i welcome the peculiarity of article 3 (5) of the memorandum, which stipulates that the exchange of information and experience does not include the transmission of operational information, in particular data relating to an identified or identifiable person. i support the report in question because i consider the agreement reached to be fruitful and legitimate and to contribute to a better performance of the functions of these two bodies.
‒ the objective of the memorandum of understanding is to foster cooperation between eurojust and the institute for harmonisation in the internal market (ihmi), in accordance with their respective mandates, by strengthening the fight against certain crimes, in particular counterfeiting of products. it provides for the exchange of 'technical and strategic' information, but does not include the transmission of 'operational information, in particular data relating to an identified or identifiable person'. the rapporteur considers it legitimate to conclude that eurojust and the ohim recognise that the terms of the memorandum contribute to the better performance of their respective functions. it follows that, as it stands, the memorandum is in the common interest of eurojust and the ohim. although the report focuses on a number of technical aspects and the issues of personal data are duly safeguarded, in the assessment of this report we have taken into account our positions of principle with regard to the two institutions in question and the known reservations about their tasks.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on the draft council implementing decision approving the conclusion by eurojust of the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market and eurojust. the objective of this memorandum is to develop strategic cooperation, taking into account the functions of eurojust and the ohim.
‒ the proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 207/2009 and the proposal to amend directive 2008/95/ec, concerning the community trade mark, aim to harmonise the trade mark registration systems existing in all the member states of the european union and to ensure the coexistence and complementarity between the community trade mark system and the national trade mark systems. i support this amendment in order to make trademark systems more efficient for companies, reducing their costs, bureaucracy and the complexity of procedures, and ensuring greater speed, predictability and legal certainty. so i am sure that there will be a substantial increase in innovation and economic growth. it is important to stress the need to extend the community acquis on the protection of geographical indications at union level to include, through a future eu legislative act, geographical indications for goods other than agricultural and foodstuffs, wines and spirits.
‒ i voted in favour of this draft council decision concerning the conclusion of the memorandum of understanding between the institute for harmonisation in the internal market (ihmi) and eurojust. this is a memorandum designed to foster strategic cooperation between eurojust and ohim and can thus contribute to better performance by both parties. i believe that the conditions are right for the council to adopt such an instrument.
in writing. this legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council regulation on the methods and procedure for making available the traditional own resources and own resources based on vat and gni and on measures to meet the needs of the treasury, which i voted in favour of, is part of the new legislative package on own resources which will enter into force at the beginning of 2016 (with retroactive effect from 01/01/2014). this highly technical regulation contains practical provisions on such matters as the establishment of traditional own resources, the retention of supporting documents, the rate applicable to own resources based on gni, and the making of adjustments and other provisions relating to the management of cash and amounts outstanding. i also think it is important to take account of the need to establish effective rules on the provision of contributions to the union budget by the member states, in order to enable the commission to properly manage its treasury operations. the report also stresses that the union's own resources system is too complex and 'needs to be thoroughly reformed in the next multiannual financial framework', a statement with which i agree.
‒ the memorandum of understanding fosters cooperation between eurojust and the ihmi, in accordance with their respective mandates, by strengthening the fight against serious crime, in particular counterfeiting of products. eurojust and the ohim recognise that the terms of the memorandum, including article 6 thereof, contribute to the better performance of their tasks. we have followed the advantages of such a memorandum and noted that personal data is safeguarded.
‒ the draft implementing decision under examination formalises the conclusion by eurojust of the memorandum of understanding between the institute for harmonisation in the internal market (ihmi), for which the committee on legal affairs is competent under annex vi to the rules of procedure of the european parliament, and eurojust. the objective of this memorandum of understanding is to foster cooperation between eurojust and the ihmi, in accordance with their respective mandates, in the areas of the fight against serious crime, in particular counterfeiting. given our strong objections both to the harmonization processes within the framework of the internal market policy and to eurojust, which means the withdrawal of national competences from the justice systems of each country, we voted against.
‒ this report concerns the amendment of the regulation defining the member states' contributions to the eu budget, in particular those based on vat and gni. the proposed amendments are designed to speed up and make available resources in a timely manner, while avoiding as significant a posteriori adjustments as those seen in recent years. the amendments clarify more technical aspects and increase transparency and accuracy in the calculation of national contributions. although this is generally a positive sentiment, we have long advocated a more substantive change in national contributions to the eu budget, with a substantial increase in the latter, guaranteed by national contributions that take account of each country's relative wealth (based on its gni), with a substantial increase in contributions from the countries with the highest gni those that have benefited most from the single market and eu policies. the community budget should have a redistributive role and should give priority to real convergence and the promotion of economic and social cohesion, and the own resources ceiling should therefore be raised. the current budget is far from allowing it. this is not the subject of this report, but only of some very technical adjustments to the present system. we abstained.
‒ the report on the proposal for a council regulation amending council regulation (eu, euratom) no 609/2014 on the methods and procedure for making available the traditional own resources and own resources based on vat and gni and on measures to meet the needs of the treasury approved the commission proposal as amended. the need to establish clear and effective rules on the timely provision of contributions to the union budget by the member states, so that the european commission can manage its treasury operations properly, is one of the points highlighted in this report, a position which i also share. i voted in favour.
‒ i agree with the rapporteur that the provision and adjustment of member states' contributions to the union budget should not be the subject of political negotiation but should be a technical process to meet the treasury needs. i support the need to establish effective rules on the timely provision of contributions to the union budget by the member states in order to enable the commission to properly manage its treasury operations. it should be noted that most member states are paying, without significant delay, the full amount of their gni-based and vat-based contributions to the union budget. the rapporteur has said that this proposal deserves my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a council regulation aims to amend regulation no 609/2014. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the compensation for the costs of the measures in question. it contains technical provisions on the clearance of traditional own resources, the retention of supporting documents, administrative cooperation, the rate applicable to own resources based on gni, the drawing up of own resources accounts and the timetable for their making available and the introduction of adjustments, as well as provisions on cash management and amounts not recoverable. those rules will now be subject to a review which, among other adjustments - such as the guarantee that the own resources accounts are free from negative charges and interest and the possibility of advancing twelfths of a month - aims to streamline the annual adjustments to the own resources based on vat and gni in the light of the experience gained in the 2014 adjustments made under an amendment to regulation no 1150/2000, which will now cease to apply when regulation no 609/2014 enters into force. i voted in favour.
‒ this report speeds up the application of resources and proposes that the annual calculation of member states' contributions to the eu budget be made mandatory not only for the member states but also for the european parliament. we believe that a fair own resources system must be in line with the relative wealth of each country (based on its gni), so that the effort in the budgetary contribution is similar for all citizens in the different eu member states, and there are still exceptions for some countries in the calculation of their contribution. the community budget should therefore play a redistributive role and give priority to real convergence and the promotion of economic and social cohesion, and the own resources ceiling should therefore be raised.
‒ this report concerns the amendment to the regulation laying down the rules by which member states make own resources available to the commission for the budget of the european union, in particular those based on vat and gni. the proposed changes are aimed at streamlining and making resources available in a timely manner, after what happened during 2014 when the adjustments for the years 1995-2013 were very high. the proposed amendments also clarify interest rates and other more technical aspects, and increase transparency and accuracy by reporting adjustments, in a timely and regular manner, to the calculation process and to vat/gni data. we believe that a fair system of own resources must be in line with the relative wealth of each country (based on its gni), so that the effort in the budgetary contribution is similar for all citizens of the different eu member states, and there are still exceptions for some countries in the calculation of their contribution. the community budget should therefore play a redistributive role and give priority to real convergence and the promotion of economic and social cohesion, and the own resources ceiling should therefore be raised.
‒ the report under consideration concerns the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of georgios kyrtsos, which the public prosecutor's office has requested from the supreme court of greece, in the context of a possible legal action relating to an alleged offence. the mp is accused of not paying part of the salary of a former employee. the accusation concerns part of the 2013 salary of a former employee of two newspaper publishing companies, of which georgios kyrtsos was a manager at the time. considering that the alleged infringement has no connection with georgios kyrtsos's term of office as a member of the european parliament, but rather with his previous position as manager of two newspaper publishing companies; that the judicial procedure does not concern opinions or votes expressed in the course of the member's term of office (in dispute for the purposes of article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union) and that there is no reason to suspect that the intention underlying the judicial action is to prejudice the member's political activity (fumus persecutionis), given that the proceedings began some years before the member's term of office began, we voted in favour of the lifting of georgios kyrtsos' parliamentary immunity.

in writing. ‒ on 21 july 2015, the public prosecutor's office at the supreme court of greece requested the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of georgios kyrtsos in a legal action in which the member of the european parliament is accused of failing to pay part of the salary of a former employee. in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. according to the report of the committee on legal affairs, article 8 of the protocol does not apply in this case, as the alleged infringement has no relation to georgios kyrtsos' mandate as a member of parliament, but rather to his previous position as manager of two newspaper publishing companies. in these terms, and on the basis of the juri report, i voted in favour of this decision to waive the immunity of georgios kyrtsos.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of its main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 2 623 200 for finland to support the 1603 workers made redundant in 69 companies in the consultancy and computer programming sector.
in writing. the application concerns 1 603 redundant workers in the consulting and computer programming sector in finland. the redundancies occurred in 69 companies, with microsoft mobile accounting for almost half (778). in recent years, employment in the ict sector has declined sharply in the eu as companies and services move to countries such as china, india, taiwan and other destinations outside europe. these effects were particularly felt in finland where the entire electronics industry was severely affected. in total, 69 companies in the software industry ended up laying off workers during the fall of 2014 and spring of 2015. northern ostrobothnia is a region with a high unemployment rate (above the national average). the redundancies also affect workers over the age of 50, a group who have difficulty finding new jobs. we supported the mobilisation of this aid for the workers made redundant. however, this fund is only limited support for those affected by the liberalization of world trade. measures are needed to stop the course of the neoliberal policies which have once again led to this outcome.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund, which was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of structural change in world trade patterns, can be mobilised if an application is assessed positively. i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the egf for finland, since the finnish authorities have provided all the guarantees necessary for the procedure in question.
‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 6 november 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of finland in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant in 69 enterprises operating in the economic sector classified under nace revision 2 division 62 (consulting and related computer programming) in several nuts level 2 regions covering the whole of finland. i am voting in favour of this proposal for the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 2 623 200 from the egf for finland. this concerns 1 200 of the 1 603 workers made redundant.
in writing. recent developments affecting nokia in recent years, including the relocation of nokia's mobile phone operating system development and design functions to countries outside europe, have had a strong impact on the finnish economy, especially in the important information and communication technology sector. as a result of these problems at nokia, 1 603 workers were made redundant from a universe of 69 companies operating in the economic sector of consultancy and computer programming activities. to address this high level of redundancies in this sector, finland has applied for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund totalling € 2 623 200 to support the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market. as this application fulfils the conditions for the mobilisation of the fund and as the fund is channelled in its entirety towards support for newly unemployed people - in particular coaching, employment services and enterprises, training, recruitment subsidies and entrepreneurship - i am voting in favour of this report.
‒ the redundancies are located in the regions of länsi-suomi, helsinki-uusimaa, etelä-suomi and pohjois-ja itäsuomi. in recent years, the distribution of ict employment between the eu and other economies has developed negatively for the eu as companies and services have been transferred to countries such as china, india, taiwan and other destinations outside europe. these effects were especially felt in finland where the entire electronics industry was severely affected, culminating in the nokia announcement in 2011. in these circumstances, the consultancy and related computer programming activities sector continued to struggle to remain competitive at world level, even though the main recipient of its services had disappeared. the redundancies also affect workers over 50 years of age, a group that has difficulty finding new jobs, and it may be that by june 2016 more than 50% of these workers will be long-term unemployed.
‒ the application concerns 1 603 redundant workers in the consulting and related computer programming sector. the redundancies are located in the regions of länsi-suomi, helsinki-uusimaa, etelä-suomi and pohjois-ja itäsuomi. the redundancies occurred in 69 companies, with microsoft mobile accounting for almost half (778). northern ostrobothnia is a region with a high unemployment rate (above the national average). in uusimaa, at the end of february 2015, the unemployed accounted for 11% of the labour force. in the period under review, 49 software companies in the uusimaa region resorted to cooperation negotiations, with the estimated need for 1 681 job cuts. the total contribution requested from the egf amounts to eur 2 623 200 (60% of the total costs). we agree with the mobilisation of this aid, but we still insist that this fund represents only limited support for the main targets with the consequences of the liberalisation of world trade, and that measures are needed to stop the course of the neoliberal policies which have once again led to this outcome.
‒ the european parliament voted on 25 february 2014 on the proposal for a regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 207/2009 on the community trade mark, which aims to simplify and update trade mark legislation at both national and eu level and to make the registration of trade marks in the eu less burdensome, faster, more reliable and more predictable, thus further increasing legal certainty for trade mark proprietors. this proposal is a regulatory package comprising a recast of directive 2008/95/ec, which approximates the laws of the member states relating to trade marks, a revision of regulation (ec) no 207/2009, which also contains provisions on the office for harmonization in the internal market, and a revision of regulation (ec) no 2869/95 on fees payable to the office for harmonization in the internal market. i support this report which approves the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the community trade mark regulation, thus following up the long-awaited review of the trade mark system in europe.
in writing. the purpose of these reports is to revise the regulation on community trade marks and the directive relating to the trade mark legislation of the member states. they are part of a package of renewal of the whole brand system at european level. the basic operation of the marking system is as follows: a producer of a good or service who intends to protect the name and general characteristics of his product must register his trademarks at both national and european levels. to do this, you have to register your trademark in national and european registers, defining the name and essential characteristics of your product. each product type is assigned to a 'class' of products. this register protects the producer or company against copying, counterfeiting, unauthorised or unlawful use. the report aims in particular to harmonize, by means of a regulation, the way in which trade marks are registered and protected at european level. among other things, it is expected to significantly reduce the cost of online registration fees for trade marks. the report contains positive aspects, but also others that give rise to reservations, such as the blocking system (which does not exclude generic medicines).
‒ i have tabled my vote in favour of the recommendation for second reading of the council's position at first reading on the community trade mark regulation. the community trade mark system and the ohim have been in existence for more than 15 years and it is therefore necessary to review the existing rules in order to adapt them to the current reality.
‒ i am in favour of reducing the differences in the trade mark system in europe and of the eu trade mark system and national trade mark systems coexisting in a complementary relationship. i think it is essential to ensure that registered trade marks enjoy the same protection under the legal systems of all the member states. in line with the broad protection afforded to eu trade marks which enjoy a reputation in the union, broad protection at national level should also be granted to all trade marks which enjoy a reputation in the member state concerned. i stress that it will be necessary to modernise trade mark systems in the union in order to meet the increased demands of those concerned for faster, better and more rational trade mark registration systems. by making the trademark systems more efficient, we will be reducing costs, red tape and complexity for businesses, which could mean increased innovation and economic growth.
‒ the trade mark system serves to protect branded products. to this end, a mechanism is being set up which allows companies and member states to block, by means of tailor-made tools and the implementation of tailor-made procedures, the transit of goods from third countries which are allegedly counterfeit. the possibilities for such application are strengthened in this proposal. this can be seen as a positive development for european industries. however, one of our concerns is that generic medicines are not clearly excluded from this possibility, despite the mobilization of associations such as msf.
‒ the purpose of the report is to reformulate the regulation on registered community trade marks and the directive relating to the trade mark legislation of the member states. the express objective is to modernize the procedures for the registration of trade marks and to move from a community approach to the eu approach (in accordance with the implementation of the lisbon treaty) . in principle, this reform will facilitate changes to the nomenclature of the office for harmonization in the internal market, simplify procedures, strengthen the fight against counterfeiting and clarify the form of registration of trademarks. for example, it will reduce the cost of online registration fees for trade marks from eur 950 to eur 850 at eu level. we therefore voted against the rejection of the council's position.
