‒ this agreement provides for strategic cooperation between europol and the united arab emirates. a strategic agreement of this nature excludes the exchange of personal data, so that the issue of data protection is not relevant in the present case. the information exchanged may include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on both criminal investigation processes and crime prevention methods, training activities, provision of advice and support in certain criminal investigations. according to europol, the uae is of increasing importance in the fight against organised crime as it is increasingly becoming a platform for economic and financial crime.
‒ the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the united arab emirates provides for an increased exchange of information that can integrate expertise on issues important for the fight against organised crime. europol's joint work with the united arab emirates (uae) is key to tackling global economic and financial crime, which, while it does not choose countries or borders, prefers the fastest growing economies and where liquidity levels are highest, such as the uae, as its initial gateway into the system. i therefore think it is important to support this legislative resolution, since this agreement should make a direct contribution to the fight against financial fraud and to the promotion of international cooperation in the field of economic and financial investigation and other relevant criminal matters.

‒ european energy policy must ensure the functioning of the energy market, security of energy supply, promote energy efficiency and energy savings, develop renewable energies and promote the interconnection of energy networks. the existence of 28 energy hubs, the high level of total energy imports (53%), especially oil and natural gas, and the dependence of some states on a single supplier place the eu in a position of vulnerability and supply disruptions to the taste of political and trade divergences. i support the gróbarczyk report for its view that there is an urgent need to create a true resilient energy union, with a forward-looking climate change policy based on the transition to an efficient sustainable energy system, with smart and interconnected infrastructure, with renewable energy and better use of europe's energy resources. special attention should be paid to decarbonising our economy and setting binding climate and energy targets by 2030, as well as to a strong focus on research and innovation so that we can take the lead in energy technologies. putting citizens at the heart of the energy union means giving them safe, sustainable and affordable energy sources!

in writing. ‒ the so-called 'european energy union' is a tailor-made project for the major european monopolies in the sector, and it is certainly not out of proportion to say that documents such as this report are, in essence, their specifications. the energy sector is liberalised and privatised in the various member states, and then it is said that energy must be accessible to all and that energy poverty must be tackled. is there a greater contradiction? the liberalization of this sector within the single market has led to the creation of transnational private monopolies which colonize markets and accumulate prodigious profits, while energy prices for consumers and micro, small and mediumsized enterprises reach unbearable levels. the disparity in energy access and prices is growing. only a publicly owned and managed energy sector can guarantee affordable energy prices for the population and maintain sovereignty in the definition of national energy strategies. the appropriate response to energy efficiency improvements, diversification of sources, progress towards renewables, and the fight against energy poverty, among other challenges, requires public, democratic planning and control of the energy sector, energy production and distribution. something this report cannot and will not reflect. on the contrary, i did. we voted against it.

‒ in accordance with article 194 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, european energy policy shall ensure the functioning of the energy market, the security of energy supply, and the promotion of energy efficiency and energy savings. i am voting in favour of this report, which aims to increase energy security by reducing dependence on russia, to improve energy efficiency by focusing heavily on renewable energy and to deepen the european energy interconnection market, in particular by improving the iberian links to france. we must therefore diversify sources of supply, established routes and types of energy production and support people and businesses in providing their homes or businesses with better environmental conditions, as well as effectively investing in electric cars and innovative methods of electricity production.

‒ the so-called 'european energy union' is based on the privatisation and liberalisation of national energy sectors. we are well aware of the consequences of the liberalization of this sector in the single market, with the creation of transnational monopolies that exploit the energy consumption markets and accumulate prodigious profits, while energy prices for consumers and for micro, small and mediumsized enterprises reach unbearable levels that increasingly limit the existing disparity in access to and prices for energy. only a state-owned and managed public energy sector will ensure affordable energy prices for the population and the maintenance of sovereignty in the definition of national energy strategies. the response to energy efficiency improvements, the diversification of sources, progress towards renewable energy, the appropriate use of each country's endogenous potential, security of supply, the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, among others, require public, democratic planning and control of the energy sector, energy production and distribution.
‒ i voted in favour of the report 'towards a european energy union' because i consider that its current absence reflects the fragmentation of the union's energy markets and is extremely damaging to europe's competitiveness and security. as such, i believe that the political and legislative package on which the creation of a european energy union is based will be important for the development of a european energy market, which will have as its central priorities the focus on renewable energy, the guarantee and diversification of the union's energy supply, the strengthening of energy sovereignty, the increase in energy efficiency and the progressive decarbonisation of the economy and social organisation models and the focus on innovation and research to put the union at the forefront of the energy transition. however, for the eu to continue to lead the energy transition, it needs political intelligence, the mobilisation of citizens and businesses, regulatory flexibility, convergence of efforts among the 28 member states and the ability to attract investment. only then will we be able to establish a robust and credible european energy market, which is less dependent, innovative and in line with the planet's sustainability challenges.

‒ the existence of an internal market for the free movement of energy and the increase in renewable sources and energy and an optimal level of energy efficiency are key requirements for the eu to have a stable, secure, dependent energy system in the framework of a sustainable and future-oriented wealth-creating economy. electricity interconnection is one of the essential preconditions for the completion of an integrated internal energy market which goes beyond any purely economic and geopolitical vision but is embodied in a strategic principle of a more resilient and robust network, environmentally friendly and able to cope with all types of disturbances. i support the eriksson report because it considers it important to achieve the 10% target by 2020 and that, in addition to the quantitative target, progress is made in the free access and availability of interconnections, which are indispensable for the elimination of the remaining obstacles to the functioning of the market. i deplore the behaviour of some member states in pursuing these principles, blocking the interconnection of networks for reasons of protectionism on their market, thus creating energy islands, as in the case of the iberian peninsula, whose capacity with continental europe is too small and the current projects of common interest are not sufficient to achieve the interconnection target by 2020.
‒ it is imperative to reach 10% of installed generation capacity in the short term and 15% by 2030 as a minimum interconnection target. this priority was agreed by the european commission, the council and this parliament in the previous legislature. i am therefore sorry that the eriksson report under discussion today seems to call this priority into question. we are constantly witnessing the persistence of what is a market failure, and we have an obligation to engage politically in resolving it, without giving in to the vested interests which for years, or even decades, have prevented a proper integration of the energy market. failure to do so would condemn several member states to their peripheral position, not only in energy terms but also economically. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments which point to ways of strengthening that objective.
‒ the advantages of interconnecting electricity networks to enable interoperability between the various member states are important for all the potential reasons outlined in this resolution. however, as a significant part of the costs of interconnections and the systems associated with them in each state is borne by consumers in those states, it is essential to ensure that the potential benefits are realised and outweigh the potential disadvantages. it is therefore necessary that, once the objectives have been set, the effects of the resulting actions be carefully weighed. these are questions which, unfortunately, are not dealt with in this report. portugal, which has been diligently implementing the eu energy guidelines, has borne and bears the heavy costs of this implementation, but still fails to see the benefits claimed, especially in the price of electricity it costs, which has a severe impact on households and businesses, especially smes. it would be important to correct the distortions observed and to ensure the protection of consumers and economies, especially those most in need of stimulus. it will be necessary to ensure that interconnections and market mechanisms do not render investment in renewable energy useless (the surpluses of french nuclear will certainly be more competitive) and that national consumers do not heavily subsidize these renewable energies in order to make them competitive on the european market.
‒ electricity interconnection is one of the essential preconditions for the completion of an integrated internal energy market. in this context, it is essential to strengthen the interconnection between the iberian peninsula and the rest of europe, allowing the region to participate fully in the internal electricity market. i would also stress the important role that the iberian peninsula region can play in the establishment and creation of a genuine european energy union, particularly through the key role of the development of renewable energies. i voted in favour.

‒ in 2010, the european union set up the european progress microfinance facility with the aim of ensuring that socially and economically disadvantaged people have an opportunity to build a decent income. progress is an important and effective tool for achieving the eu's employment and social policy objectives under the europe 2020 strategy: a significant number of new jobs are created by newly created companies. almost 85% of these jobs are created by micro enterprises. thus, there is a strong demand for microcredit by people who cannot obtain a loan in the traditional banking sector. progress helps to unlock entrepreneurial potential, to find new skills through training and mentoring, and to enable people to return to the labour market and live with dignity and autonomy. microcredit should be seen as a social policy instrument to give an opportunity to people in difficult social situations. the maximum amounts of microcredit/loans that can be accessed should be reconsidered, as they may not be sufficient in all eu countries. i therefore support this report.
‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because of the positive effects of the granting of microcredit under the progress microfinance facility, which ends in 2016. progress is the only eu financial instrument that is based solely on the social conditions of applicants rather than promoting entrepreneurship and innovation in the european business fabric, focusing on supporting socially and economically disadvantaged people in europe (unemployed, young, elderly) by helping them to get out of their situation by granting micro-credit to enable them to set up their own businesses. in view of the positive results of a key instrument for eu employment and social policy, and in view of the fact that a new microfinance programme for the 2014-2020 cycle (easi microfinance axis) was established based on the positive experience of progress, it can be concluded that the programme has met its objectives and therefore received my vote in favour.
‒ microfinance is the set of financial services for individuals and smes with limited access to bank credit and associated services. in the eu this instrument has been used in policies for job creation, social inclusion and gender equality. this report assesses the implementation of progress (launched in 2010) and its impact. the use of microcredit has been limited, with a high number of projects not approved; information on this mechanism does not reach its potential beneficiaries; their effectiveness in the context of territorial cohesion is questionable. the report seeks to address these weaknesses. training of those involved, greater territorial dispersion and a greater focus on cohesion, project information and programme evaluation processes are some of the issues addressed. the emphasis on solutions such as micro-credit, entrepreneurship, etc., as a way of solving unemployment, exclusion, inequality and the economic crisis is fallacious and dangerous, because it removes the responsibility of the states. this does not mean that there can be no support for the creation or revitalisation of enterprises, but it does not limit real solutions to social problems. the report does not emphasize microfinance as an absolute solution. we have therefore voted in favour.
‒ the european progress microfinance facility aims to ensure that economically and socially disadvantaged people in europe have an opportunity, whether it is to set up new businesses, to promote new jobs or to ensure that the unemployed and micro-enterprises can access finance. this european instrument is important for achieving the union's objectives in the field of employment and social policy, and i therefore voted in favour of this report on its implementation.
‒ the european microfinance facility progress was set up in 2010 with the aim of ensuring that socially and economically disadvantaged people in europe have an opportunity to build a decent income. it is important to stress that progress has a social dimension and facilitates access to microcredit for the creation or support of micro-enterprises and is an important and effective instrument for achieving the european union's employment and social policy objectives under the europe 2020 strategy. i would highlight the social benefits that progress provides, namely helping people to (re) enter the labour market, unlocking entrepreneurial potential, finding new skills through the training and supervision provided and enabling people to live with dignity and autonomy. i advocate the continuation of progress, its availability in all member states, and that the initiatives and funding available for the provision of micro-credit to innovative youth-led startups should be doubled in order to support young entrepreneurship and technological innovation.
‒ the objective of this instrument is to increase access to and availability of microfinance for people who have lost or are at risk of losing their jobs, for people who have difficulties entering or re-entering the labour market, as well as for those who face the threat of social exclusion or are in a vulnerable or disadvantaged situation with regard to access to the conventional credit market and who wish to set up or continue to develop their own micro-enterprises, including self-employment. this is an essential instrument to increase the access to and availability of microfinance for microenterprises and thus to boost the social economy.
‒ after identifying the positive effects on the local economy of micro-credit to combat poverty in developing countries, the eu set up the european microfinance facility progress in 2010, with the main objective of ensuring that the most economically and socially disadvantaged citizens have an opportunity to create their own source of income. this financing, which is not intended to support micro-enterprises directly but intermediaries, is intended to increase their access to loans through improved guarantees. this not only helps to make potential entrepreneurs viable, but also contributes to the development of new skills through training/support for these citizens. the instrument is aimed at unemployed people, citizens claiming social security benefits, immigrants and people who cannot obtain conventional bank loans, and it is an important socio-political instrument, since it grants loans of up to eur 25 000. this report on the implementation of 'progress', which i voted for, shows that it is an important and effective instrument for achieving the eu's employment and social policy objectives, but as described in the report, it lacks greater visibility and more detailed implementation reports from the commission.
in writing. ‒ we value this programme and are in favour of strengthening this microfinance mechanism. unfortunately, the potential of this programme is not being properly exploited. this is largely due to a common problem in eu programmes - the lack of information and ways of supporting those concerned. it is often those who are least excluded who have the information and end up benefiting from this possibility of applying for microcredit. we agree with the logic of the report, which does not emphasize the solution of microfinance as an absolute solution to solve social and economic problems, as many emphasize. this logic is fallacious and dangerous - it puts social equity and development policies in the hands of the greater or lesser success of individuals, while relieving states of their responsibilities. microfinance yes, but without replacing the social functions of the states.
‒ microfinance is the set of financial services for individuals and smes with limited access to bank credit and associated services. in developed countries, especially in the eu, this instrument has been used in policies for job creation, social inclusion and gender equality, notably through the european progress microfinance instrument, launched in 2010, which funds credit intermediaries to increase the number of projects and improve the conditions under which those accessing credit can obtain these loans. this instrument aims to distribute 46000 microcredits by 2020, with a total budget of eur 500 million. this report assesses the implementation of progress and its impact in the eu. the use of microcredit has been limited, with a high number of projects not being approved; information on this mechanism does not reach its potential beneficiaries; its effectiveness in the context of territorial cohesion is questionable, when the instrument covers only 20 countries; there are many sectors that are part of the exclusion map that do not use this mechanism. we agree with this assessment and have therefore voted in favour of the report.
‒ we generally support proposals aimed at simplifying legislation, involving fishermen in the definition of fisheries policies, particularly at regional level, improving fishing gear by increasing its selectivity, and a sustainable approach to stock management. technical measures and multiannual plans are useful tools with potential in fisheries management. the multiannual plans have the advantage, in general terms, of allowing some stability and predictability to a sector that is hardly affected by any major instability. but these plans must be part of a local management system which involves the sector and in which the member states play a leading role. the strict alignment and submission of these plans to the constraints imposed by the common fisheries policy (cfp) compromises much of their potential and accentuates limitations and disadvantages. this happens to be the dominant view throughout this report - the advocacy of strict submission to the new cfp. we, for our part, believe that a fundamental change must be made to the existing institutional framework, which, since the treaty of lisbon, has enshrined the management of living marine resources as an exclusive competence of the eu. the disastrous results of this centralized management are in sight. that is why we abstained.
‒ since 2009, there has been almost no progress in the legislative processes on technical measures and multiannual plans, which are very important instruments for achieving the objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy. i have voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on this subject.
in writing. the new common fisheries policy entered into force on 1 january 2014 following the green paper on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) presented in april 2009. the new cfp aims to ensure optimal exploitation of the species caught - at least at levels that can produce the maximum sustainable yield (msy) - by implementing an ecosystem approach that ensures minimal negative impacts of fishing activity on the marine ecosystem itself. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, shows that, in the context of the practical implementation of the new cfp, there is an objective need to apply technical measures in a coherent, simplified and geared to the type of fisheries and the region on the one hand, and on the other hand, the absolute need to 'enhance the involvement of stakeholders through the advisory councils and in all decisions concerning [their] regionalisation' when defining and implementing the multiannual plans. it also recalls that the landing obligation is a rather radical change for the fisheries sector, which requires an adaptation of technical measures to allow its effective application (e.g. granting greater flexibility to nets, as described in the report).
‒ i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr gabriel mato, on the work he has done on this report. we may not agree with some of the details in this report, but we are in complete agreement with the need to preserve the sustainability of fishermen, marine resources and marine ecosystems. as the report argues, fisheries management in europe must follow the new common fisheries policy and must accommodate the marine strategy framework directive. this is a particularly important and repeatedly disregarded subject. at the same time, i disagree with the report that says that all catches must be landed in port in 2019, because that is not true. only catches of species with defined quotas shall be obliged to land in port.
‒ the advantage of multiannual plans in general terms is that they allow some stability and predictability to a sector that is hardly affected by any major instability. unfortunately, the institutional framework in force since the lisbon treaty, which enshrines the management of living marine resources as an exclusive competence of the european union, imposes a centralised management of fisheries policy, far removed from reality, which does not take into account the enormous diversity of the sector (in terms of resources, fleets, fishing gear and fisheries) and makes local management unfeasible, thus taking away much of the advantages that such multiannual plans could bring to the sector.

madam president, commissioner avramopoulos, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate the european commission on what seems to be another courageous proposal. europe's response to this refugee crisis has been slow and below what is needed. much of it is the council's fault. the consequences of this inaction were many, even tragic, but one of the most obvious was that it called into question one of the greatest successes of european integration: the schengen area. i have said from the beginning that we had to respond to the humanitarian emergency and find solutions to the underlying problems. we need instruments to deal with crises, but also to better ensure the integrity of the schengen area. and we cannot forget that all of this is based on mutual trust. those who ignore european solidarity and express nationalist sentiments, but also those who think that the solution lies in ignoring the involvement of the member states, are doomed to failure. mutual trust is what we need, because we need a union that can respond to challenges. with pragmatism and with a will to act.

the european union's reaction is most shameful. in fact, it's very much in keeping with his nature. you don't want to save and welcome immigrants, among whom are refugees, of course! they just worry about putting up more barriers and walls. what is the difference between this policy and that of orban? this proposal simply wants to strengthen the mechanisms for expulsion, to give frontex faster access to data on migrants so that it can expel them more quickly, to put its agents everywhere, even without the permission of the member states, to take corrective action, whatever that is. on the other hand, it takes away from the member states even more of their sovereignty and the possibility of managing their borders in a more humane way. it is this policy and this supremacy complex of the european union that is fuelling xenophobia and racism. social integration is the best weapon to fight them.
madam president, commissioner, i welcome the agreement on global warming reached in paris, which limits global warming to two degrees with a view to not exceeding 1.5 degrees. this represents a crucial step for humanity and for the planet. this is a landmark achievement, covering 195 countries for the first time. i congratulate the commissioner on his excellent work, as does our president la via. that said, it is true that the agreement could and should be more ambitious. scientific data indicates that we need to decarbonise our economy as early as 2050, and yet quantitative targets for emissions reductions have been removed from the agreement. it is also regrettable that no reference is made to the maritime and aviation sectors, whose emissions are expected to increase in the coming years. we must now make a serious effort to implement this agreement and the transparency of this process and the periodic review mechanism are essential. i hope that each nation can now step up its national contribution to the immediate move away from coal-fired electricity generation and to the promotion of electric mobility and energy efficiency. the fight against global warming is a race against time, and the paris treaty was just a starting gun.
mr president, at the time of the adoption of the paris agreement, the conditions were not met which would allow us to assume that its objectives could be achieved. far from it. however ambitious these objectives may seem, without reliable means of achieving them, they cannot be taken seriously. this is one of the great failures of paris. despite the insistence of several countries, particularly in latin america, on criticism of market mechanisms and so-called flexibility mechanisms, these are at the heart of this agreement. these are mechanisms which have proved perverse and ineffective in achieving emission reductions, but which serve the business prospects of some. this is what it's all about, gentlemen, business, not environmental goals! as for the financing of adaptation and mitigation, another handful of nothing. the unwillingness to lift barriers such as intellectual property rights shows where the millions from the green fund will go in the name of so-called technology transfer. the enthusiasm surrounding the outcome of cop 21 must therefore be tempered by reality.
mr president, we should welcome the decisive commitment made at cop 21, an ambitious approach to the security of the planet. we had to wait about 65 years when, for the first time, an oceanographer said that we were subjecting the planet to a geophysical experiment of releasing sequestered carbon, the results of which would be disastrous. finally, we have the recognition of an ambitious and binding agreement. the objective of limiting the temperature increase to 1.5° is indicative of this determination. monitoring of the efforts of individual states to reduce greenhouse gases is essential. let's not forget that there are still economic and corporate interests out there who see short-term opportunities in global warming. some applaud the melting as an opportunity for more natural resources, including fossils. the central issue is urgent mitigation. we must therefore keep the flame of this difficult global agreement burning. this is the last chance for us to work together to make the adoption process work.

‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when europe is facing a financial, economic and social crisis, with unemployment as one of its main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to respond, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i therefore supported this report on the mobilisation of eur 442 293 for ireland to support the 108 workers made redundant at pwa international ltd (pwai).
‒ ireland has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) following 108 redundancies at pwa international ltd (pwai), established in 1989 in rathcoole, a joint purchase between united technologies corporation and lufthansa technik airmotive, which operated in the machinery equipment repair and installation sector. the recent trend towards the relocation of activities in the maintenance, repair and overhaul (mro) sector, for example to asia, has been a factor which has seriously affected this sector and ireland. this application does not fulfil all the traditional eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation in terms of the number of redundancies, invoking a derogation for exceptional circumstances, as redundancies have a serious impact on employment and the local, regional or national economy. ireland has also decided to provide personalised services co-financed by the egf to 108 young people who are not in employment, education or training (neets). almost 80% of the workers made redundant are aged between 30 and 54 years, and all 108 of the workers made redundant are skilled workers in the 'repair and installation of machinery and equipment' sector, more specifically in the aviation engine sector. each new egf mobilisation is a libel against eu policies.

in writing. in accordance with the invasive exotic species regulation on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive species, the commission is to submit a list of such species by january 2016. the detailed criteria for the construction of this list are set out in the regulation. the list presented consists of 36 species. this draft objection considers that the list is incompatible with the provisions of the regulation, since no harmful or rapidly spreading species (animals and plants) have been included. in addition, the procedures for drawing up this list were not respected, in particular the european parliament was not informed about the elements and methodologies of the impact studies. in short, the decision on the species included in the list appears to take into account criteria of a political or economic nature, without a scientific basis, and was weighed in its final configuration by a set of pressures put forward by some member states. some of these pressures are known. as regards portugal, the importance of the inclusion of the water hyacinth in the list is underlined, despite the opposition of member states with a commercial interest in this species. given that the next revision of this list is scheduled for six years from now, the shortcomings of this proposal must be corrected now, which is why we voted in favour of the objection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation adopting a list of invasive alien species of union concern. this is a subject to which i have always devoted much attention. it is of the utmost importance that priority be given to the identification of all invasive alien species causing damage in the eu. by combating invasive species we are simultaneously protecting the native biodiversity of each member state. the commission's initial list ignores species that are among the most harmful invasive alien species in europe.
in writing. ‒ the commission shall adopt a list of invasive alien species of union concern, under the criteria of article 4 (3) of regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council. whereas the commission has not specified the type of evidence that is acceptable and has not provided a detailed description of the application of article 5 (1) (a) to (h) of the regulation, including the methodology to be applied in risk assessments, nor has it ensured that the methodology and application of risk assessments are the same for all member states when proposing to include a species in the union list. i think it is important that the inclusion of species in the list is based on a risk assessment and a standardised methodology and not based on the political will of the member states. it should be noted that the commission's initial list has been criticised by several national authorities and stakeholders, raising serious doubts as to the effectiveness of the ias regulation, mainly because many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not listed, while some species that are not likely to cause significant adverse impacts on biodiversity, human health or the economy are included.
‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the objection to the draft commission implementing regulation adopting a list of invasive alien species of union concern, as i consider that this regulation exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (eu) no 1143/2014, as stated in paragraph 1 of the report. the commission is therefore asked to submit a new draft, which is in line with the regulatory provisions and which brings together in a single document the identification of the group of invasive alien species which are of legitimate concern in a number of member states of the european union. in this way, we will be able to adopt specific uniform measures to minimise the adverse effects that these species may have on the preservation of european biodiversity and related ecosystem systems, as well as on the economy and human health.
‒ in accordance with regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive species, the european commission has until january 2016 to present a list of these species based on criteria defined in the regulation. although it is a fairly comprehensive legislative document, one important element is missing, namely which species should be targeted and controlled, which is why articles 3 and 4 set out detailed criteria for the construction of the list. the list presented by the commission consists of 36 species, which, according to the rapporteur of the objection, is incompatible with the provisions of the regulation, since the most harmful or the most rapidly spreading species of plants and animals have not been included. in addition, the procedures for drawing up this list were not respected, in particular the european parliament was not informed about the elements and methodologies of the impact studies, and the decision on the species included in the list appears to be political or economic and not based on scientific grounds.
‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation adopting a list of invasive alien species of union concern in accordance with regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council (d041932/01 2015/3010 ((rsp)) mainly because i agree that the draft list proposed by the ec does not address the problem of invasive alien species in a comprehensive way, does not take care to protect native biodiversity and ecosystem services, and does not minimise and mitigate the impacts that these species may have on human health or the economy. it also weighed in my vote the fact that the text calls for the withdrawal of this draft implementing regulation and the submission of a new one. the new commission proposal should include the water hyacinth, an invasive species which is posing a serious threat to the alqueva river basin.
‒ in accordance with the invasive exotic species regulation, on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive species, the european commission is to present a list of these species by january 2016. the detailed criteria for the construction of this list are set out in the regulation. the decision on the species included in the list appears to take account of political or economic criteria, without any scientific basis, and was shaped by a set of pressures from some member states. some of these pressures are known. as regards portugal, the importance of the inclusion of the water hyacinth in the list is underlined, despite the opposition of member states with a commercial interest in this species. given that the next revision of this list is scheduled for six years from now, the shortcomings of this proposal must be corrected now, which is why we voted in favour of the objection.
‒ this objection aims to reject any authorisation for the placing on the market, either for trade or for animal feed, of genetically modified organisms (gmos), as the procedures are being reviewed and there is a clear inadequacy and inadequacy of the current eu legislation. in the present case, the authorisation of the use of the genetically modified maize nk603xt25, which is resistant to glyphosate, requested by the multinational monsanto, is rejected. this herbicide (along with another, ammonium gluosine-to), has been classified as probably carcinogenic to humans by the world health organization's cancer agency. nevertheless, the european food safety authority declared that the herbicide was unlikely to pose a danger. symptomatic of the lack of credibility of this entity, whose promiscuous links to industry have been pointed out several times. since the current gmo authorisation process came into force, authorisation decisions have been adopted by the european commission without the support of a qualified majority of member states. the european commission is asked to present, as promised by its president but not yet implemented, a new legislative proposal to amend the current legislative framework on gmos, which is considered to be insufficient to address concerns associated with food safety, public health and the environment. we voted in favour.
‒ i have some reservations about the text of this resolution, particularly as regards the scientific assessment of the risks and possible impacts on humans. i believe that there should be a more thorough debate on this matter, which merits some caution, and that is why i have decided to vote against the motion for a resolution authorizing the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 x t25.
‒ i am in favour of reducing the differences in the trade mark system in europe and of the eu trade mark system and national trade mark systems coexisting in a complementary relationship. i think it is essential to ensure that registered trade marks enjoy the same protection under the legal systems of all the member states. in line with the broad protection afforded to eu trade marks which enjoy a reputation in the union, broad protection should also be granted at national level to all trade marks which enjoy a reputation in the member state concerned. i stress that it will be necessary to modernise trade mark systems in the union in order to meet the increased demands of those concerned for faster, better and more rational trade mark registration systems. by making the trademark systems more efficient, we will be reducing costs, red tape and complexity for businesses, which could mean increased innovation and economic growth.
‒ this motion for a resolution concerns the objection to the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 x t25, on the grounds that the commission's implementing decision on this matter exceeds its implementing powers under regulation (ec) no 1829/2005, and is not in accordance with union law. i therefore believe that there should be a re-examination of the situation to see whether the commission's implementing decision should be suspended or not until a new regulation is adopted, so that it complies with the provisions of the acquis communautaire. because it is a question of the need to provide a high level of protection for human life and health, animal health and welfare, environmental protection itself and the need for consumers to be properly informed, and because there are still doubts about the safeguarding of these rights, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ a few days after the european parliament's environment committee raised an objection to the authorisation of monsanto's genetically modified maize nk603xt25, the european commission, in the absence of consensus among member states, decides to authorise the placing on the market of this same gm maize. this is an undemocratic decision. moreover, its concrete content takes on the greatest gravity. this is a genetically modified corn to tolerate two herbicides glyphosate and glyphosate. the first is classified by the european union itself as toxic to reproduction. the second is classified by the world health organization as potentially carcinogenic. the total discredit of the current gmo authorization mechanism requires the immediate suspension of the issuing of authorizations until the president of the european commission fulfils his promise and proposes a new mechanism.
‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled pursuant to rule 106 on commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 of 4 december 2015 authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified maize, as i consider that any implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified organisms (gmos) in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 should be suspended until a new regulation is adopted. the current version of the regulation lacks functionality and an effective system for the approval of genetically modified food and feed. moreover, the commission's final decision on such authorisations, which has become the norm, should be only an exception in the whole procedure. i therefore consider that the commission implementing decision is not compatible with the purpose of the regulation to ensure a high level of protection of human life and health, animal health and welfare, the environment and consumer interests.

‒ the luxleaks scandal and subsequent investigations have shown that tax fraud and evasion are widespread in most member states, with the knowledge of their governments. this report proposes to address ways of 'ensuring transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate taxation policies in the eu'. the report contains positive recommendations, such as, among others:- mandatory and public country-by-country reporting by multinational companies for all sectors;- countermeasures against companies using tax havens;- - adaptation of the definition of permanent establishment so that companies cannot artificially avoid having a taxable presence in the member states where they carry out an economic activity; - improvement of the transfer pricing framework in the eu. the proposal to introduce a common consolidated corporate tax base can help to combat profit shifting. but the application of this measure will not solve the problem by itself. the report leaves the door open to tax harmonization with proposals which, in the name of combating tax evasion and profit shifting, are intended to give the impetus to the loss of yet another economic policy mechanism, this time fiscal policy. we abstained.
‒ i voted in favour of the report on ensuring transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate taxation policies in the union. in the debates held by the european parliament's taxe committee, it became clear that aggressive tax planning practices are not limited to luxembourg but are quite widespread throughout the eu. according to a study commissioned by the european parliament, the eu loses around €50-70 million a year through corporate tax avoidance and profit shifting. it is of the utmost importance that legislative measures are adopted at eu level in order to improve the transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate taxation policies in the union.
‒ 'aggressive tax planning' practices are quite widespread throughout the eu. this phenomenon consists of taking advantage of the technical aspects of a tax system in order to reduce tax liabilities. while not the same as tax fraud and tax evasion, which are illegal activities, in essence, all three practices reduce the collectible, undermining trust in governments and businesses. the eu loses around €70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance, simply through profit shifting. these practices are never acceptable, especially in difficult economic circumstances such as those facing europe today. if some multinational companies do not contribute, then there is no longer a level playing field and smaller national companies have difficulty in competing, which is completely contrary to the principle of the single market. recent experience shows that member states cannot act individually in the fight against aggressive tax planning. respecting the sovereignty of the member states in matters of tax policy, it is necessary to adopt legislative measures at eu level in order to improve the transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate taxation policies in the union.
‒ aggressive tax practices in some eu member states have caused a lot of controversy and controversy, and even more so since the widely publicized lux leaks case (11/2014). in february this year, the european parliament set up a special committee on aggressive tax practices to 'find out about practices in relation to the application of eu tax and state aid law to decisions of the tax court and other measures of the same nature or effect taken by member states, where such practices constitute an act of a member state or the commission', as the text of the decision establishing it said. the committee on economic and monetary affairs has also decided to draw up its own own initiative report proposing legislative action on this subject, which i voted in favour of. among the proposals in this report, which are divided into four areas, namely transparency, coordination, convergence and other measures, i would only highlight the preparation of public reports describing the situation in each of the member states, the creation of a common and convincing definition of 'tax havens' and the improvement of the exchange of information between tax administrations.
‒ this issue has been heightened following the luxleaks revelations by a consortium of journalists in november 2014, which revealed that many multinational companies had entered into secret agreements with the luxembourg authorities, allowing them to reduce their tax obligations, in some cases to almost 1%, creating very little or no economic activity in the country. these 'aggressive tax planning' practices are by no means limited to luxembourg, but are in fact quite widespread throughout the eu. according to available studies, the eu loses around €50-70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance, simply through profit shifting. this amounts to around eur 160-190 billion if account is taken of special tax arrangements, inefficiencies in collection and other similar elements. these practices are never acceptable, especially in difficult economic circumstances such as those facing europe today. this scandal deeply affects the credibility of the european institutions, as it directly implicates the presidents of the european commission and the eurogroup. it shows who this eu serves with its model of neoliberal integration based on the free movement of capital and the sacralization of financial markets.
‒ the luxleaks scandal and other investigations that followed showed that tax fraud and evasion is a widespread practice in most member states with the knowledge of their governments for decades. in the light of the findings, the ep authorised in december 2014 the drafting of a legislative own-initiative report on ways to 'ensure transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate taxation policies in the european union'. the report makes some recommendations which we consider to be quite positive, such as the submission of mandatory and public country reports by multinational companies for all sectors, the creation of a common and strict definition of tax havens or of countermeasures against companies using tax havens. the report leaves the door wide open to tax harmonization through proposals which, in the name of combating tax evasion and profit shifting, seek to give the impetus to the loss of sovereignty in tax policy. we abstained.
‒ this report is marked, on the one hand, by the eu's manifest interest in investment and trade issues with china and its determination to gain access to larger slices of the chinese internal market and, on the other hand, by its insistence on interference in china's internal affairs at every level, arrogating to itself the right to set parameters for a wide range of chinese policies (from the economy to religious policy, from diplomacy to defence, to human rights and civil society). the report never affirms the principles of respect for sovereignty and non-interference, mutual interest, equality of conditions, progress and social welfare. the issue of human rights is omnipresent throughout the document, although it also deserves a specific chapter, always from an inquiry and superiority perspective on the part of the eu. whether it is on security, terrorism, the rights of national minorities, etc., the text is full of hypocrisy, which could be summed up in one sentence: "don't look at what i do, do what i nail". full of pressure, prescriptions and remarks which amount to a flagrant and gross crime of meddling and interference expressing the view and interests of the eu - this report can only be rejected.
‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on eu-china relations. the eu and china are engaged in a number of ongoing sectoral dialogues, including on environment, regional policy, employment and social affairs and civil society. the identification of common interests such as global and regional security, the fight against terrorism, the fight against organised crime, cybersecurity, weapons of mass destruction and nuclear non-proliferation, energy security, global financial and market regulation, climate change and sustainable development, adds enormous value to this strategic partnership.

‒ the last global discussions on the humanitarian action framework took place almost 25 years ago. since then, the conditions for humanitarian assistance have changed significantly, notably with a steady increase in the number, scale and persistence of humanitarian emergencies resulting from both man-made conflicts and natural disasters, and exacerbated by global issues such as climate change. i support the salom report because i believe it is important that global actors, and in particular the eu as the main donor, should play a leading role in reshaping the humanitarian architecture to make it more inclusive, effective, transparent and responsive to the increased humanitarian needs related to the current challenges such as the wave of displacement of people. i believe that in the context of the summit, the eu should build on the european consensus on humanitarian aid to guide its contribution to the process and use it as a regional model to promote. finally, given the nature of the current emergency situations, new financing is urgently needed, and parliament has already stressed the importance of maintaining the same payment and commitment appropriations in the humanitarian aid chapter and in the reserve for emergency aid.
‒ this report is about the world humanitarian summit (whs) and aims to contribute to a common eu position at this summit. it is noted that the objectives of the chm will shift from reshaping the humanitarian system to adapting it to a rapidly changing emergency scenario, in order to make humanitarian action more efficient and prepared. it calls for closer cooperation between humanitarian aid communities and for the focus of action to shift from response to prevention and anticipation. the world is facing humanitarian crises unprecedented in both their number, scale and persistence. the year 2014 saw a dramatic increase in forced displacement caused by war and conflict, reaching the highest level in recent history. many of these situations are a painful demonstration of the inhuman, exploitative and aggressive character of the capitalist system and have their causes and culprits: the processes of destabilization in various parts of the globe and the imperialist wars of aggression, the policy of economic domination and the plundering of natural resources. the report calls on member states to integrate business into their national emergency plans and advocates enhanced cooperation with the private sector in humanitarian action. a view which we do not share, which is why we did not vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the preparation of the world humanitarian summit: challenges and opportunities for humanitarian aid. the world is currently facing humanitarian crises unprecedented in both their number, scale and persistence. the recurring natural disasters, the level 3 emergencies in syria, iraq, yemen, south sudan and the central african republic and the ebola outbreak in west africa have exponentially increased the number of people in need of humanitarian assistance. the world humanitarian summit, to be held in istanbul in may 2016, should seek to reshape the humanitarian system and adapt it to new scenarios, such as the current refugee crisis. only in this way can we hope to make humanitarian action more efficient and future-proof. the eu has the responsibility and the capacity to take a leading role in finding more efficient and effective ways of meeting the needs of victims of conflict and disasters.
‒ humanitarian crises have grown in recent years in terms of scale and frequency. the number of people forced to move has reached its highest level since world war ii. we're talking about over 60 million people, 40 million of whom are internally displaced, and over half of the world's refugees are children. this document is intended to be a contribution to the first world humanitarian summit to be held in may next year in istanbul. i agree with the inclusion of a five-year action plan to make operational the political actions and commitments undertaken, and with the necessary complementarity between humanitarian aid and development aid to deal with the numerous obstacles and the lack of coordination between these two policies. i am also in favour of the need to review the geneva convention on refugees and the kampala convention in order to adapt them to the problems of our world today. i also agree with the need to look at the issue of climate refugees, which is now the reason for the internal displacement of thousands of people. i believe that we can and must do more for the most vulnerable groups, and i therefore vote in favour of this report.
‒ this is a real call for member states to support the world humanitarian summit and adopt sound conclusions at council level with specific commitments and priority areas of intervention, ensuring operational efficiency, common quality standards, better coordination and partnerships with emerging donors, based on politically non-biased aid, as well as a common understanding and application of the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence and in compliance with their obligations under international humanitarian law.
‒ the eu has been proactively involved in resolving/minimizing the effects of a growing number of humanitarian crises that have been increasing in scale, severity and persistence and that require a coordinated, firm and adequate response at the global level. the first world humanitarian summit will take place in may 2016, and as such the eu will need to draw up a concrete development and operationalization plan in the face of the political commitments it will make and the humanitarian catastrophes that have arisen. i also believe that it is essential to increase the financial resources for humanitarian aid through global solutions adopted multilaterally and on a world scale. the key challenges we face today require innovative solutions, linking thematic areas such as humanitarian effectiveness, vulnerability reduction, or risk management. i therefore vote in favour of this report, which suggests a set of preparatory measures for this summit, where it is urgent to adopt effective and efficient measures to minimise or eliminate the humanitarian disasters which have occurred in recent years and which require an immediate and definitive response.

‒ the world is currently facing unprecedented humanitarian crises. the continuing and protracted conflicts caused by imperial strategies of interference in the internal affairs of various countries and continents are accompanied by recurring natural disasters and epidemics, such as the recent ebola case. there are now more refugees and internally displaced persons than there were after world war ii. one consequence of this has been the disproportionate increase in people attempting to seek refuge by undertaking life-threatening sea journeys. the chronic needs arising from these conflicts and disasters, the fruit of selfishness in western nations and in particular in the eu, are pushing the humanitarian response system to its limits. in this context, the un secretary-general, ban ki-moon, has called for the first-ever world humanitarian summit (whs) to be held in istanbul in may 2016. we do not deny the urgent need to respond to situations requiring immediate humanitarian aid. what is also needed, but unfortunately absent from the debate, is a diagnosis of the root causes of this phenomenon, as well as policy changes that can address this problem at the root.

in writing. the decrease in capacity and employment in the european steel industry is partly due to the drop in demand. in 2014, it decreased by 40 million tonnes compared to 2007. but this decline is mainly the result of decades of divestment and dismantling of this sector, as exemplified by the case of portugal, which has involved dependence and the loss of specialised industrial know-how, which is reflected in downstream sectors. the report states the urgency of increasing the development of the base metals industry - iron, aluminium, copper, etc. - and the need to adapt it to new technological/environmental paradigms, with a view to its international reassertment. some of the recommendations in this report are positive. but the approach taken is incomplete and inconsistent. we also do not follow up on the considerations of exploitation and ownership, i.e. the accumulation of capital by large multinationals which will ultimately continue to appropriate the resources and wealth creation of this sector. a new impetus for industrial policy must continue the process of technological, energy and environmental modernisation, and to this end it must create more jobs and have the necessary instruments and means, which will not be possible without strategic public control of the base metal industries.
in the light of the above, the commission has decided to propose to the council that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the conclusion of the agreement on the european economic area. the commission also found that the union industry had a significant market share in the union market. the eu cannot and must not lose the industrial know-how it has acquired over many decades. the idea that the eu could become dependent on a sector which has made numerous technological achievements is very worrying. investment in this sector should be promoted and the eu should launch a european industrial policy in the raw materials and base metals sector.
‒ the base metals sector is of strategic importance for the union, but in particular for some regions. this report is in line with the union's objective of reindustrialising the european continent by promoting investment and creating a favourable and fair international environment. this industry has to adapt to the union's climate and energy policies, but the union must also protect this market against dumping. the price of energy, the relocation of industry, dumping and export subsidies by third countries are some of the threats to this sector. i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the approach adopted will have positive consequences for the restoration of the economic potential of this industry.
‒ the metal industry is extremely important for the eu, as it is the basis for many other industries that have a strong impact on the european economy, such as automotive, aerospace, energy production and civil construction. to ensure the competitiveness of the base metals industry, the report suggests that the eu should build on the redefinition of its current emissions trading system. energy-intensive industry should reduce co2 emissions, allowing the eu to ensure industrial competitiveness while meeting its objectives. supporting the base metal industry - which is so special and vulnerable to external competitiveness and to eu energy and environment policy - should have as its ultimate aim the fight against the increasing loss of competitiveness of various base material industries such as steel or aluminium. the eu needs to help (re) build an efficient framework for these sectors in order to strengthen economic potential and, above all, to re-industrialize europe through innovation and promoting a level playing field in the sector at international level. for these reasons, and because i consider it essential to support the european base metal industry, i voted in favour of this report.
‒ the financialisation of the economy and the long process of deindustrialisation associated with it are eloquently illustrated in this report. the commission also found that the union industry was not able to fully benefit from the measures in force. this capacity adjustment has been so significant that any recovery in european demand will result in the creation of a historic trade deficit in europe, which in turn will lead to dependence and losses of industrial know-how that will not fail to have an impact on the downstream sectors of the automotive, construction and low-carbon technologies sectors. any industrial policy that is implemented and that seeks to break with this situation of impoverishment and dependence will not be possible without a strategic public control of its base metal industries by creating all the necessary instruments and means to cope with an increase in the price of carbon and to draw up a strategy compatible with the environmental objectives that we have set ourselves to respect.
‒ i voted in favour of the report 'developing a sustainable european base metals industry' because i believe that europe, already dependent on raw materials, cannot allow a new dependence on base metals to develop, an industry which is currently facing a significant drop in demand and investment, driven mainly by energy prices and comparatively high carbon costs compared to third countries. despite the difficult situation in which it finds itself, the base metals industry must at the same time pursue a policy of energy and environmental modernisation in accordance with existing european rules and equip itself with the necessary instruments to make this transition a success. as such, to ensure the competitiveness of this industry, a reformulation of the current eu emissions trading system is urgently needed, complementing it with other energy and environmental innovative instruments and strategies for effective emission reduction, as well as a focus on the reuse of base metals and the development of a circular economy. investment in research and development is also needed if europe is to remain a centre of excellence for the production of base metals.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in hungary. the policy pursued by prime minister orbán raises a number of questions in terms of fundamental rights in hungary. the eventual reintroduction of the death penalty in the country, and a controversial public consultation on immigration, has triggered an eu reaction. the european commission has stated that the reintroduction of the death penalty would be contrary to the values enshrined in article 2 of the treaty on european union and would lead to the application of article 7, which allows, in the event of a serious and persistent breach of eu values, the suspension of certain rights of the member state concerned, including the right to vote of the representative of the government of that member state in the council. it is extremely important that the commission continue to monitor the situation in hungary closely.
‒ in june this year, a motion for a resolution was adopted on the need for all member states to fully respect eu law, its common basic values, including democratic principles, the rule of law and fundamental rights themselves. in this respect, this proposal adds nothing substantive or new to the proposal previously submitted on measures to protect the rule of law and european values. hungary has made an effort to fulfil and respect fundamental rights and other obligations under eu law. i think it is important that the commission continues to monitor all the member states on an equal footing and without any duality of criteria as regards migration, democratic principles and fundamental rights, and the need to promote greater cooperation and unity between member states at this time of crisis and the need to strengthen the rule of law. however, i do not share the restrictive view of this joint motion for a resolution by the political groups: alde, gue/ngl and greens/efa (which is not part of the epp motion for a resolution, which was rejected earlier during this voting period - before the vote on this joint motion), which is why i voted against it.
‒ the actions of the hungarian government have over the years led to a serious deterioration in the situation of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. as regards the treatment of asylum seekers, refugees and hostile actions and hate speech directed at groups such as roma, jews, the lgbti community, migrants, the homeless and other poor people, the need for a position to condemn these practices that undermine the values of human dignity is emerging. the hasty measures adopted in recent months, which have made access to international protection extremely difficult, have unjustifiably criminalised migrants and asylum seekers, as well as the increasing use of detention of asylum seekers and xenophobic rhetoric linking migrants to social problems or security risks, reach the limits of the tolerable and cannot be tolerated. however, it is also important to denounce the hypocrisy of the eu in this matter, which has been building a policy for migration that, in practice, is based on repressive measures that end up being at the root of all this humanitarian drama that the world is witnessing and that require measures that the eu clearly does not have the political will to take.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the situation in hungary, as i consider that member states must fully respect eu law. it is based on respect for human dignity, human rights, freedom, democracy, equality and the rule of law, values which are universal and common to all full eu member states. in the light of recent developments and measures taken over the past few years in hungary, especially with regard to restrictions on freedom of expression, the human rights of migrants, asylum seekers and refugees, freedom of assembly and association, restrictions on the activities of civil society organisations, the right to equal treatment and minority rights, i see hungary as a test for the eu to demonstrate its capacity and political commitment to respond to threats and cases of violation of its own fundamental values by a member state, and as such i consider the commission's infringement procedure against hungary of 10 december to be important in order to ensure that hungary or any other member state complies with its obligations under eu law and respects its underlying values by using the procedures of the regulation to revoke the emergency measures adopted.

mr president, the working conditions of human rights activists accused and persecuted for terrorism or restricted by legislation on the registration and funding of ngos are worsening all over the world. the european union and its member states continue to pursue contradictory, inconsistent, counterproductive policies and fail to speak with one voice. the special representative for human rights must be able to speak publicly on behalf of the union. european union delegations and embassies must resist political interference and intimidation by local authorities in human rights programmes. this was not the case with mrs concetta tirzi, who was expelled by the angolan authorities with the inadmissible complicity of the european union for having arranged meetings with activists such as luati beirão and other prisoners who were subjected to sham trials. the european union delegations shamefully censor themselves, as in ethiopia, where the regime is repressing and killing oromo students and the delegation remains mute and buries its head in the sand.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european union, despite all its limitations, which have been widely acknowledged here, continues to play an irreplaceable and leading role in monitoring, reporting and intervening in the field of human rights. i would therefore like to stress the importance of the annual discussion of this report and, in the specific case of the one now under discussion, the comprehensive and constructive way in which it has been drawn up, covering all areas of human rights. as we know, these have suffered very worrying setbacks in recent years in various parts of the world, as a result of wars, terrorism and the persecution of minorities, which are directly linked to the current exodus of migrants, with tragic consequences on european soil. there is, however, one question i would like to raise which i think should be dealt with in greater depth in this report and which has to do with the link between our trade policy and our policy of promoting human rights. as we know today, the trade agreements we have with other regions of the world are absolutely essential for the integration of human rights clauses for the promotion of human rights worldwide.
in writing. the same european union which, internally and externally, tramples on democracy and human rights, claims the right to give lessons in democracy and human rights to the rest of the world, as this debate once again attests. the universal declaration of human rights lists rights and principles aimed at ensuring respect for life and human dignity, including, inter alia, freedom, the rights of expression, opinion, religion and participation in the life of communities, equality at birth regardless of social class and race, equality before the law and justice, the right of everyone to access to health, education, social security, work and a reasonable wage to ensure that all families have a decent life, clothing, decent housing and food, equal pay for equivalent work, including equality between the sexes, the right to privacy, advocating the elimination of all forms of discrimination. the impoverishment of democracy is always linked to the non-fulfilment of some fundamental human rights. we feel it today as never before in the eu. it is the defence of these rights - won and now threatened - that is the pulse of the struggle of the workers and peoples of europe and the world.

in writing. the humanitarian refugee crisis has several dimensions. this debate has exposed a pattern which has been recurring in the various member states which are receiving this flow of refugees, namely the arbitrary detention and use of force, simply because one is an asylum seeker. the right to seek asylum is a human right enshrined in the geneva convention for refugees. therefore, detention should only be used as a last resort and within a limited period of time. the conditions for the detention of asylum seekers pending the examination of their application are described in the directive on the reception conditions for asylum seekers. it should be noted that unaccompanied minors may only be detained in exceptional circumstances and must be held in accommodation suited to their needs and separated from adults. therefore, if member states do not comply with these conditions, the european commission should initiate infringement proceedings against the member states concerned. in a humanitarian situation of this magnitude, member states and the competent authorities should be aware of the vulnerabilities and marks that these people carry with them. we must ensure that existing instruments are respected.

design of member state governments. it is urgent to set up an independent monitoring authority and a reporting mechanism and a standardised reporting for all member states with sanctions for infringements of the common position. it is essential that governments provide detailed accounts of exports, including quantities, values and destinations. it is the security of our citizens, our neighbourhood and the world that is at stake, as demonstrated by the recent terrorist attacks in paris, carried out with weapons and explosives produced and easily acquired here in europe. it is
